1033-1055 华盛顿街 (Washington St) 的项目范围发展计划(PDA), 是用于两座生命科学办公大楼的混合开发用途，
底层为零售/餐厅和社区/非营利空间使用。 PDF项目位于南端(South End) 邻里区以北的经济开发区，东面为华盛
顿街 (Washington St), 而西为所物街 (Shawmut Avenue)。
拟议的生命科学发展项目, 将会给予提供设施，为不同收入水平的人, 创造新的就业机会等的好处。
• 创造就业机会/提升经济效益：400 个建筑⼯作岗位； 900 个永久性⼯作岗位。
• ⼤约 $400 万美元的 RE 税收
• 连锁⾦⼤约 $750 万美元
o 住房贡献供款
o 就业贡献补助⾦
有助于 南端(South End) 的整体发展复兴愿景• 兴建从华盛顿街到所物街 (Shawmut Avenue), ⽅便⾏⼈的庭院连接,•
提供负担得起的/社区⾮营利使⽤空间；• 涌⼊私⼈投资, 利⽤现有公共基础设施, 和便利的公共交通地点。
项⽬将以公共交通为发展导向, 开发为商业和零售⽤途的例⼦;
邻近有多种公共交通服务, 提供服务的交通枢纽地带，包括:
MBTA 银线、橙线、红线、绿线和当地的巴⼠路线, 和通勤
铁路线 (弗雷明汉市 [Framingham]/ 伍斯特市 [Worcester]、富兰克林市 [Franklin]/ 福克斯堡市 [Foxboro]、尼德姆市
[Needham] 和普罗维登斯市 [Providence]/ 斯托顿市[Stoughton], 以及美国国铁 (Amtrak) , 这⼀切将会形成, 更⼴泛及
更多的公交出⾏使⽤⽐例, ⽽不是使⽤⻋辆出⾏。
项⽬现址由于本身与 I-93 的连接, 享有优良的本地和区域性的道路⽹络联系。
项⽬现址的⻋辆停⻋需求, 将会容纳 353 个现场停⻋位（299 个全新现址停⻋位), ⽽⾃⾏⻋停放需求, 将会容纳⼤约
266 空位, 结合与室内/⻓期和室外/短期的⾃⾏⻋停放。

⼏项研究将分析 PDA 项⽬对环境的影响, 例如: ⻛、阴影、⽇光研究、岩⼟⼯程和声⾳/噪⾳、洪⽔泛滥区和废物分
析，以及已经完成的能源建模研究。
提议者致力于推行, 城市的可持续发展目标。了解气候变化的重要性, 及项目将如何适应, 在未来条件及情况, 对气候变
化的影响, 降至为最低, 是本项目设计过程中, 不可缺少的重要组成部分。对这些问题的理解, 增强对于这之前, 未被充

和住宅区, 及现有场地的条件。对这些问题的理解, 提升对于这之前, 未被充分利用的项目场地, 进行开发的发展的好
处，考虑到它使用公共交通、步行和骑自行车的基础设施、靠近主要为就业, 和住宅区, 及现有场地的条件。设计团队
还利用他们在建筑, 和机械系统方面的丰富经验和知识，建立一个设计，以最高限度, 减少能源使用，为可再生能源提
供机会，节约用水，认识物质资源使用。开发项目预计, 将使用混合动力电气化战略计划，这将使现场化石燃料消耗
减少 90% 以上。最后，拟议的开放空间, 将允许雨水渗入, 将有助缓解热岛效应的情况, 为对开放空间的网络, 带来益
处的其中部份。

DEVELOPMENT PLAN 
FOR 
PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA NO. [__] 
103 NORTH BEACON STREET 
BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS 
Dated: November , 2023 
1. 
Development Plan: Pursuant to Section 3-1A.a and Article 80C of the Boston 
Zoning Code (the “Code”), this plan constitutes the Planned Development Area Development Plan 
(the “Development Plan”) for a Planned Development Area Overlay District (the “PDA Overlay 
District”) containing approximately 67,586 square feet (1.55 acres) commonly referred to as 103 
North Beacon Street in the Brighton neighborhood (the “Site”). The Site is more particularly 
described in Section 3, below, and in Exhibit A and Exhibit B attached hereto. The Proponent (as 
defined below) proposes to redevelop the Site by demolishing the existing improvements and 
constructing an approximately 265,000 square-foot (“sf”) mixed-use building with a below-grade 
parking garage (the “Project”). Collectively, the Site and the Project make up the “Planned 
Development Area” or “PDA” for which this Development Plan will constitute and provide the 
permanent zoning. 
This Development Plan sets forth the proposed location and appearance of structures, open 
spaces, uses, densities and dimensions of structures, traffic circulation, parking and loading 
facilities, and other requirements applicable to the PDA. Capitalized terms used but not defined 
herein shall have the meanings assigned to such terms in the Code as in effect as of the date hereof, 
without giving effect to any subsequent amendments to the Code. 
This Development Plan consists of [___] pages of text plus attachments designated 
Exhibits A through G. All references to this Development Plan contained herein shall pertain 
only to such pages and exhibits. This Development Plan shall constitute permanent zoning for the 
Site in accordance with Section 3-1A and Article 80C of the Code and is intended to address all 
requirements of the Code applicable to the Site and the Project. 
2. 
The Proponent: The Proponent of the Project is IQHQ-103 Beacon, LLC, an 
affiliate of IQHQ, Inc. (together with its successors and assigns, “Proponent”). 
The business address and telephone number for the Proponent is: 
IQHQ-103 Beacon, LLC 
c/o IQHQ, Inc. 
201 Washington Street, Suite 3920 
Boston, MA 02108 
(858) 779-1111 

2 
4859-9328-8029, v. 4
3. 
PDA Overlay District: The PDA Overlay District totals approximately 67,586 sf 
(1.55 acres) and is located within the block bounded by North Beacon Street, Arthur Street, Herrick 
Street, and Hichborn Street. The Site is currently improved by a one-story commercial building at 
103 North Beacon Street, surface parking and loading service on Arthur Street. 
As depicted on the draft PDA Overlay Plan, a copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit 
C and is incorporated herein by reference, the PDA Overlay District is located in the 
Allston/Brighton Neighborhood District and the Guest Street Local Industrial-2 zoning subdistrict. 
4. 
The Building: The Proponent proposes the development of a mixed-use/life 
science development with ground level retail amenity space which is designed to bring new 
vibrancy and activity to an existing underutilized site. The contemplated building program consists 
of approximately 258,000 sf of gross floor area (“GFA”) of Core Shell lab-ready space with 
approximately 4,000 GFA of retail space within the ground floor, 3,000 GFA of secure bicycle 
room, two (2) levels of underground parking for approximately 212 vehicles, and so-called “back 
of house” space to support these uses (the “Building”). 
5. 
Proposed Location and Appearance of the Building: Selected elevations 
attached hereto as Exhibit D illustrate the Building’s general appearance. The Site design focuses 
on creating a more generous and enlivened streetscape along North Beacon Street and Arthur Street 
through a wider sidewalk, landscaping, and seating for the public. Envisioned as a conduit for 
activity, the Project has been oriented on the Site to allow for extra wide pedestrian sidewalks 
along both North Beacon and Arthur Street which afford room for sidewalk activation as well as 
facilitate Arthur Street becoming a connector between the nearby Boston Landing project and the 
North Beacon Street Corridor. 
The Building complements the height and massing in the area, while minimizing wind, 
shadow, and solar glare impacts on the surrounding neighborhood. 
6. 
Proposed Density and Dimensions of Structures: The specific height (as defined 
in the Zoning Code) for any building within the Site will be calculated from the average mean 
grade as defined in the Zoning Code, but, notwithstanding the definition of Building Height in 
Article 2 of the Code, no rooftop mechanicals or penthouses or other structures set atop or 
projecting from a rooftop shall be counted towards the overall zoning height of that building 
(“Zoning Height”). The maximum Zoning Height of any building within the Site shall be 112 feet. 
The maximum height of mechanical screening or penthouses on top of the buildings shall not be 
considered in determining the maximum building Zoning Height. Notwithstanding the foregoing, 
the mechanical penthouse or mechanical screen shall not exceed 155 feet in height, and up to 165 
feet inclusive of rooftop exhaust related mechanical elements, such as, flues and exhaust vents that 
may extend above the mechanical screen to an extent not to exceed ten (10) feet; the heights of the 
mechanical screen, penthouse or elements shall be measured from the top of the flat roof of the 
building at its Zoning Height to the highest point of the mechanical screen, penthouse, or element. 

3 
4859-9328-8029, v. 4
The Building is designed to include up to a total of approximately 265,000 square feet of 
GFA1, which results in an FAR of up to 4.36 across the full PDA Overlay District. See Exhibit E 
for massing diagram. The maximum Building Height, FAR and GFA set out above will be the 
only dimensional requirements applicable to the PDA Overlay District. All other dimensional or 
design requirements of the Code shall not be applicable to the PDA Overlay District and are 
superseded by this Development Plan. The Project shall be subject to design, environmental and 
other development review by the BPDA, and aspects of the Project approved as part of such review 
shall be and hereby are deemed to be the dimensional and design requirements applicable to the 
Building and are hereby incorporated in this Development Plan. 
7. 
Proposed Open Space and Landscaping: The Project will revitalize the Site, 
which is currently almost completely covered by the existing building or asphalt. The Project will 
create not less than 11,500 square feet of new publicly accessible open space on the Site. This 
publicly accessible open spaces, coupled with approximately 4,000 GFA of retail space within the 
ground floor of the Building, will help to activate the Site and surrounding area. In addition, the 
public realm area along North Beacon Street and Arthur Street will be improved with extra wide 
pedestrian sidewalks which afford room for sidewalk activation as well as facilitate Arthur Street 
becoming a connector between the nearby Boston Landing project and the North Beacon Street 
Corridor. See Exhibit F for areas of open space as shown and defined. 
The Project’s design strategy focuses on creating a more generous and enlivened 
streetscape along North Beacon Street and Arthur Street through a wider sidewalk, landscaping, 
and seating for the public. 
8. 
Proposed Uses: The Building will be used primarily for office, laboratory, 
research and development, retail and parking facilities (as accessory, ancillary, and principal uses). 
In addition to the uses listed above, all of the uses listed in Exhibit G shall be permitted as of right 
on the PDA Overlay District. 
9. 
Proposed Traffic Circulation: The Site is currently accessed from two wide curb 
cuts located, respectively, on Arthur Street and Hichborn Street. The Project will consolidate the 
curb-cuts and include one curb-cut on Herrick Street for access to both the parking garage and the 
loading service/area. The reduction in curb-cuts is designed to streamline vehicle movements. 
10. 
Proposed Parking and Loading Facilities: The Project will include two levels of 
below-grade parking for approximately 212 vehicles. All loading and service activity will be 
actively managed by the building transportation coordinator, and the Project will provide 161 
secure bicycle parking spaces and 20 publicly accessible bicycle parking spaces. 
11. 
Access to Public Transportation: The Site located near the Massachusetts Bay 
Transportation Authority (“MBTA”) Boston Landing Station which provides access to the 
Framingham/Worcester commuter rail, and is also located along MBTA bus routes 57, 64, 66, and 
86. 
1 All square footages are approximate. GFA is defined in Article 2 of the Code and specifically excludes from 
calculation floor area devoted to garage space, accessory below grade, mechanical equipment and public transit 
improvements. 

4 
4859-9328-8029, v. 4
12. 
Signage: The signage program for the Project shall be subject to design, 
environmental and other development review by the BPDA, and any sign approved as part of such 
review shall be deemed to be in compliance with the Development Plan. 
13. 
Development Review Procedures: All aspects of the Building’s design will be 
subject to ongoing development and design review and approval by the BPDA. 
14. 
Green Building and Resiliency Measures: The Building is subject to Article 37 
(Green Buildings) of the Code, pursuant to Section 80B Large Project Review. It will meet the 
requirements necessary to achieve at least a Gold-level certifiability using LEEDv4 rating system, 
which will exceed the City’s requirements under Article 37. It will be designed with energy-
efficient HVAC and lighting equipment and systems and will incorporate other potential energy 
conservation measures, as reasonable and feasible. 
15. 
Public Benefits: The PDA will provide many public benefits to the Brighton 
neighborhood and to the City of Boston, including the creation of job opportunities and training, 
significant landscaping improvements around the Site, and the generation of additional tax 
revenues: 
a.
Improvements to the Aesthetic Character of the Site: The Project will replace the 
existing one-story brick block commercial building primarily used for retail 
purposes and a significant at-grade parking lot, unenclosed loading bays and 
loading areas situated along Arthur Street that did not allow for open space or 
landscaped areas, with a new building that allows for the provision of publicly 
accessible open space and a more generous streetscape that will visually activate 
and enliven the Site. 
b. Sustainability and Resiliency: The Project will incorporate design elements to 
improve on-site stormwater management and reduce the risk of precipitation-based 
flooding, such as reducing impervious surfaces, increasing the amount of greenery 
and incorporating green infrastructure. The Project is also designed to reduce heat 
island impacts to the extent feasible and it will exceed the requirements of Article 
37 (Green Buildings) aiming to achieve certifiability at least at a Gold level using 
the LEEDv4 rating system. The Proponent is committed to utilizing energy-
efficient HVAC and lighting equipment and systems. 
c.
Social and Economic: The Project is expected to generate approximately 
$3,308,850 million in housing and jobs linkage payments and will result in the 
creation of approximately 300 permanent on-site jobs and approximately 200 
temporary construction jobs. The Project is also expected to generate 
approximately $5 million annually in new real estate tax revenues for the City, and 
significant business tax revenues for the Commonwealth. 

5 
4859-9328-8029, v. 4
d. Transit Oriented Development: The PDA is in close proximity to several MBTA 
bus, and Commuter Rail lines, all of which provide easy access to the Site from 
the surrounding neighborhood and other areas of the City and beyond. The 
Proponent will enter into a Transportation Access Plan Agreement with the Boston 
Transportation Department in which it will commit to Transportation Demand 
Measures (TDMs) consistent with the City’s guidelines. 
e.
Smart Utilities: The New Building will comply with the BPDA’s Smart Utilities 
Policy for Article 80 Development Review, as applicable. 
16. 
Boston Civic Design Commission: The Buildings will require Schematic Design 
Approval by the Boston Civic Design Commission (“BCDC”) pursuant to Article 28 of the Code.
17. 
Applicability: In accordance with Section 80C-9 of the Code, consistency the 
Building with this Development Plan shall constitute compliance with the dimensional, use, and 
all other requirements of the Code, to the extent such requirements have been addressed in the 
Development Plan. Issuance of a Certification of Consistency for the Building will constitute 
compliance with all applicable provisions of the Code with respect to Planned Development Areas. 
18. 
Minor Modification to Plans: This Development Plan sets forth the dimensional, 
use, and other zoning requirements for the PDA Overlay District, to the extent such requirements 
have been addressed in this Development Plan. Upon approval of this Development Plan, final 
plans and specifications for the Building will be submitted to the BPDA pursuant to Section 3-1A, 
Article 80B, and Article 80C of the Code for final design review approval and certification as to 
consistency with this Development Plan, and to other governmental agencies for final approval. 
Subject to consistency with the dimensional regulations set forth in this Development Plan, minor 
changes may occur to the Building’s design described in this Development Plan without requiring 
an amendment to this Development Plan, as determined by the Director of the BPDA in accordance 
with Section 80A-6 of the Code, and subject to the use and dimensional requirements set forth in 
this Development Plan. No changes to the public benefits arising from the community-driven 80B 
process shall require an amendment to this Development Plan, provided that the mitigation and/or 
community benefits as required under this Development Plan are not modified unless approved by 
the BPDA during Article 80B Review. 
19. 
Development Schedule: The Proponent estimates that construction of the Project 
will take approximately 32 months. 
20. 
Proponent’s Obligation to Proceed with the Project: Notwithstanding anything 
set forth herein to the contrary, under no circumstances shall the Proponent be obligated to proceed 
with any Building, or all or any portion of the Project.

1. 
Development Plan: In accordance with Section 3-1A, Sections 51-44 through 51-
49, and Article 80C of the Boston Zoning Code (the “Zoning Code”) of the City of Boston (the 
“City”), this development plan constitutes the Development Plan for Planned Development Area 
(“PDA”) No. 139 (the “Development Plan”), for the proposed redevelopment of a parcel in the 
Allston neighborhood of Boston, commonly known as 1170-1190 Soldiers Field Road (the “Project 
Site”). The Project Site is referred to as the “PDA Area” and includes approximately 6.28 acres 
(273,446 square feet)). The PDA Area is described in more detail in Section 3 below and in the 
legal description attached as Exhibit A, and is shown on the existing site plan attached as 
Exhibit B. 
This Development Plan contemplates the construction of a new, 795,000 square foot, four 
(4) building development, consisting of three (3) buildings for office, life-sciences, research and 
development, and other supporting uses; two (2) levels of associated below-grade parking and 
additional on-grade parking; one (1) 85-unit building for residential use; associated parking within 
the building footprint; and new privately owned public space along with new infrastructure, all as 
more fully described in Section 4 below (the “Project”). 
This Development Plan sets forth the proposed location, appearance and dimension of 
structures, open spaces, and landscaping, proposed uses of the PDA Area, densities, proposed traffic 
circulation, parking and loading facilities, access to public transportation, and such other appropriate 
matters or zoning requirements applicable to the PDA Area. Upon approval, this Development 
Plan shall constitute permanent zoning for the PDA Area. 
This Development Plan consists of eleven (11) pages of text, plus attachments designated 
Exhibit A through Exhibit G. All references herein to this Development Plan refer to such pages 
and exhibits. Unless otherwise set forth herein, all references to terms defined by the Zoning Code 
shall have the meanings set forth in the Zoning Code as of the date of this Development Plan, and 
not as the same may be amended hereafter. The conceptual plans and landscape/open space plan 
(collectively the “Project Materials”) attached hereto as Exhibit D, are subject to design,

environmental and other development review by the BPDA and other government agencies and 
authorities, and the final design of the Project may be revised from the design described herein.

3. 
Planned Development Area Overlay District: The PDA Area is located within the 
Allston/Brighton Neighborhood District, has been designated a CC-1 (“Community 
Commercial”) subdistrict, and has three overlay zoning districts: the Western Avenue/Soldiers 
Field Road Community Commercial Subdistrict, the Soldiers Field Road/Soldiers Field Road 
Extension Greenbelt Protection Overlay District (“GPOD”), and the Coastal Flood Resilience 
Overlay District (“CFROD”). Planned Development Areas are permitted within the PDA Area 
pursuant to Section 51-44 of the Zoning Code. The GPOD subjects the PDA Area to the 
provisions of Article 29 of the Zoning Code. The CFROD subjects the PDA Area to the provisions 
of Article 25A of the Zoning Code. 
 
The PDA Area is approximately 273,446 sf (6.28 acres). It is bounded by Soldiers Field 
Road to the northwest, by land of SGT Holding Corp. to the north, by Smith Playground (a City of 
Boston public park) to the east, by land of Harvard University to the south, and by land of 
VIACOMCBS, Inc. to the southwest. Please refer to the legal description of the PDA, attached as 
Exhibit A, as well as the Site plan attached as Exhibit B for the boundaries of the PDA Area. 
Federal Emergency Management Agency (“FEMA”) Flood Insurance Rate Maps (“FIRM”) 
(Panel Number 25025C0057G) indicate that the PDA Area is not within the FEMA Special Flood 
Hazard Area (“SFHA”) (i.e., subject to inundation by the 1% annual chance flood with average 
depth less than 1 foot or with drainage areas of less than 1 square mile). In addition, the Sea Level 
Rise Flood Hazard Area Map published by the Boston Redevelopment Agency d/b/a the Boston 
Planning & Development Agency (“BPDA”) indicates that the PDA Area includes areas with Sea 
Level Rise (“SLR”) Base Flood Elevation (“BFE”) of 15.5’ Boston City Base (“BCB”) Datum with 
a SLR Design Flood Elevation (“SLR-DFE”) of 16.5’ BCB, which SLR-DFE has been determined 
by adding 12” of freeboard to the SLR-BFE for buildings and uses that are not critical facilities or 
ground floor residential uses. The Project will comply with Article 25A Coastal Flood Resilience 
Overlay District, which requires a SLR-DFE of 16.5’ BCB for non-residential uses and 17.5’ BCB 

 
3 
for residential uses. The ground floors and critical building infrastructure of the East Building, 
North Building, and South Building will be located at or above elevation 18’ BCB to mitigate 
potential impacts from flooding. The minimum first floor elevation for the Residential Building will 
be located at or above 17.5’ BCB to mitigate potential impacts from flooding. 
4. 
Project: The Project consists of four new buildings with new privately owned public 
space, new infrastructure, and associated parking, to be constructed in separate phases or subphases, 
concurrently or independently in any sequence with respect to each other, each being subject to 
BPDA design review approval and eligible for its own Certification of Compliance and Consistency 
or partial certification pursuant to Sections 80B-6 and 80C-8 of the Code. Upon issuance of such 
certification, the proposed buildings and other improvements subject to the same shall be deemed to 
be in compliance with the dimensional, design and environmental requirements applicable to such 
phase as set forth in this Development Plan, and such certification constitutes compliance with the 
requirements of the Code to the extent such requirements have been addressed in this Development 
Plan in accordance with Section 80C-9 of the Code. Any noncompliance of a phase or subphase 
shall not affect compliance of any other phases or subphase for which a Certification of Compliance 
and Consistency or partial certification has been issued, or the right to construct improvements 
thereon as contemplated by this Development Plan. The Project’s floor area ratio (“FAR”), lot 
coverage ratio, and maximum height are all within the new zoning parameters for the Western 
Avenue Corridor Study and Rezoning Plan, which the BPDA authorized on October 13, 2022, and 
has petitioned the Zoning Commission to adopt. 
Three of the buildings will be comprised of office, life science, and complementary uses 
totaling approximately 700,000 square feet (“sf”) of gross floor area (“GFA”), with a maximum 
height of 8 stories (approximately 135’ to the top of the highest occupied floor, and up to 180’ 
inclusive of rooftop mechanical elements and screening with approximately 700 below grade parking 
spaces and 15 on-street parking spaces. The three buildings are comprised of the East Building, 
North Building, and South Building. The East Building will be up to 8 stories high (approx. 135’ to 
the top of the highest occupied floor and up to 180’ inclusive of rooftop and mechanical elements 
and screening) and consist of approximately 240,000 GFA. The North Building will be up to 8 
stories high (approx. 135’ to the top of the highest occupied floor and up to 180’ inclusive of 
rooftop and mechanical elements and screening) and consist of approximately 246,000 GFA. The 
South Building will be up to 7 stories high (approx. 125’ to the top of the highest occupied floor and 
up to 180’ inclusive of rooftop and mechanical elements and screening) and consist of 
approximately 214,000 GFA. The ground floor areas of these three buildings will be tenanted based 
on market, phasing and other considerations and may be used for office, research and development, 
restaurant, entertainment, service, fitness, community, and/or civic uses in addition to the uses 
noted above. 
The fourth building, referred to as the Residential Building, will be designed for residential 
uses consisting of an approximately 95,000 sf, 85-unit apartment building, primarily 6-stories high 
(approx. max. 75’ to the top of the highest occupied floor and up to 90’ inclusive of rooftop and 
mechanical elements and screening), which will include approximately 42 parking spaces within the 
building footprint. 
The Project will include at least two driveways (Driveway A and Driveway B) which will 
provide traffic circulation around the life science buildings and along the northern side of the 

 
4 
Residential Building. The driveways will connect in two locations with Soldiers Field Road to the 
west of the PDA Area and with the McDonald Avenue and Speedway Avenue intersection to its 
southeast. Perimeter streetscapes will include permeable paving within planting zones to improve 
tree irrigation and groundwater recharge. There will be accommodations for 280 bicycles for use by 
employees, accommodations for approximately 52 bicycles will be available to visitors 
(approximately 35 of which will be for visitors to the office and R&D buildings, and approximately 
17 of which will be for resident visitors), and accommodations for approximately 85 bicycles will be 
available for use by the residents. 
The Project will include publicly accessible open space for public enjoyment, with space for 
events, public art, and passive recreation that complement the City’s adjacent William F. Smith Field. 
It will create appropriate pedestrian connections between Herter Park and Smith Field and include 
bicycle accommodations. 
Multiple phases will be used to construct the Project’s buildings and associated parking. It is 
anticipated that Phase 1 will include construction of the East Building, associated below-grade 
parking, open space, and infrastructure improvements. Subsequent phases will include construction 
of the North Building, the South Building, and the Residential Building. However, as set forth 
above, the Project’s phases or subphases may be advanced concurrently or independently in any 
sequence with respect to each other. 
The Project will comply with the requirements of Article 37, Green Buildings, of the Zoning 
Code. The Project will use US Green Building Council’s (“USGBC”) Leadership in Energy and 
Environmental Design (“LEED”) green building rating system to evaluate sustainable design 
measures in accordance with Article 37. The East Building, North Building, and South Building will 
be designed and constructed to be LEED for Core and Shell version 4 Gold certifiable. The 
Residential Building will be designed and constructed to be LEED Gold certifiable in accordance 
with the requirements of Article 37. Significant sustainability and energy efficient strategies will be 
employed for the Residential Building. The Project’s buildings will employ at least one of the five 
system options resulting from a Carbon Neutral Building Assessment. 
The Residential Building aspect of the Project is subject to the Mayor’s Executive Order 
regarding inclusionary affordable housing, dated February 29, 2000, as amended, as well as the 
Inclusionary Development Policy (“IDP”) of the Boston Planning & Development Agency 
(“BPDA”). Twenty percent (20%) of the up to 85 dwelling units in Residential Building, or up to 17 
units, will be IDP units, provided on site, that will have a range of unit sizes and be rented to 
households with a range of 40% to100% of Area Median Income.

Large Project Review: The Project has undergone Large Project Review pursuant 
to Section 80B of the Zoning Code. On July 12, 2021, the Proponents filed a Letter of Intent to the 
BPDA in accordance with Mayor’s Executive Order of October 10, 2000, as amended, governing 
mitigation for development projects. On August 11, 2021, a Project Notification Form (“PNF”) 
was filed for the Project. On March 7, 2022, a Supplemental Information Document (“SID”) was 
filed to describe revisions since the filing of the PNF and to respond to comments. Large Project 
Review has included meetings with nearby property and business owners, as well as other members 
of the public. 
Under Section 80B-7 of the Zoning Code, a Development Impact Project (“DIP”) is 
required to make mitigation payments, or provide equivalent in-kind contributions, to create 
affordable housing and job-training programs. The Project does constitute a DIP for purposes of 
Section 80B-7, and so is required to pay DIP exactions or provide in-kind contributions as follows: 
700,000 sf (100,000 sf threshold) = 600,000 sf. 
Housing Exaction: $13.00 x 600,000 sf = $7,800,000.00 
Jobs Contribution Exaction: $2.39 x 600,000 sf = $1,434,000.00

8. 
Proposed Uses: The Project is a mixed-use project. Upon completion of the 
Project, the PDA Area may have research laboratory, life-sciences, and office uses, retail, restaurant, 
service, community/civic uses (which may include art space uses) fitness center uses, up to 85 
residential units, open space uses, accessory and ancillary services and amenities. Allowed uses for 
the Project are set forth and described in more detail in Exhibit F attached hereto. 
 
This Development Plan expressly modifies the use regulations set forth in Section 51-8 of 
the Zoning Code in accordance with Exhibit E. Exhibit F lists the uses allowed by right in the 
PDA Area, which uses are allowed as either main, accessory, ancillary or interim uses; and lists the 
uses allowed by conditional use permit by the Board of Appeal in the PDA Area, including 
conditional uses allowed as either main, accessory, ancillary or interim uses. 
 
In addition, the placement and maintenance of rooftop wireless communications and other 
telecommunications equipment, such as antennae, dishes, equipment mounting, and equipment 
mounting structures and rooftop energy equipment such as solar panels and equipment shall be 
allowed as of right, subject only to design review by the BPDA. Rooftop equipment such as 
ventilation exhaust as required by code, solar panels, and equipment shall be excluded from the 
calculation of building height. 
 
9. 
Proposed Densities: The Project consists of the buildings depicted on Exhibit D. 
The proposed dimensions for each Building and maximum Building Heights, maximum FAR, and 
maximum GFA for each building and the Project are listed on Exhibit G. Separate parcels may be 
created for financing or conveyancing purposes; however, the density will be measured based on the

7 
In acknowledgement of the likelihood that parking demand may decrease over the life of the 
Project, in the event that the Proponent converts space within any building footprint or parking 
garage to uses described in Exhibit E and Exhibit F constituting Gross Floor Area (GFA), or uses

as may be determined by the BPDA. This Development Plan shall supersede the otherwise 
applicable dimensional, design and other requirements of the Zoning Code, which shall not be 
applicable to the PDA Area. 
 
10. 
Proposed Traffic and Site Circulation: The Proponent will enter into one or more 
Transportation Access Plan Agreements with the Boston Transportation Department to ensure 
proper pedestrian and vehicular circulation for each phase of the Project, or may enter into one 
master Transportation Access Plan Agreement for the Project, which master Agreement may 
allocate mitigation and commitments between each phase of the Project. The Project will provide 
adequate access and traffic circulation as generally shown on the site plan included in Exhibit D, 
attached. 
 
11. 
Parking and Loading Facilities: For the Project, in accordance with Section 51-56 
of the Code, off-street parking and loading facilities will be determined during the BPDA’s Large 
Project Review under Section 80B of the Zoning Code. As noted above, there will be 700 below 
grade parking spaces and 15 on-street parking spaces. The parking ratio of one (1) space per 1,000 
sf of Gross Floor Area of Office and Research & Development/Lab, Retail/Entertainment/Service, 
Civic/Community and Cultural Uses will be delivered. The Residential Building will contain 42 
parking spaces for 85 units, with a parking ratio of 0.49 spaces per dwelling unit. Bicycle parking is 
provided in each phase. Pedestrian connectivity between the Project and Smith Field will be 
accomplished by a raised signalized crosswalk. 
All loading activities will occur in designated areas on the Project site, as generally shown in 
the Project Materials. The Project’s parking and loading facilities, including bicycle facilities, the 
number of parking spaces, and traffic circulation, including access and multi-modal transportation 
improvements on and over the Property, shall be deemed to be in compliance with this 
Development Plan upon issuance of a Certification of Compliance and Consistency pursuant to 
Section 80B-6 and 80C-8 of the Code. All other traffic, parking, loading and circulation 
requirements of the Code shall not be applicable to the Project and the Project site and are 
superseded by this Development Plan. 
12. 
Access to Public Transportation: The Project will supply an interim private 
Shuttle Bus Service to provide access between the site and major transit hubs, such as the Red Line 
in Harvard Square and the Commuter Rail at Boston Landing. The Proponent will work 
cooperatively with the Allston Brighton TMA to implement a shared Shuttle Bus Service to the 

 
8 
referenced major transit hubs for all member companies. When the shared Shuttle Bus Service has 
been implemented, the private Shuttle Bus Service may be phased out. Since the Project is located 
within one-quarter mile of a number of MBTA bus stops on Western Avenue and North Harvard 
Street, a Real Time Display showing bus routes and real time arrivals and departures will be 
provided. 
 
13. 
Green Building and Resiliency Measures: The Project will comply with the 
requirements of Article 37 (Green Buildings) of the Zoning Code. The design team will use the 
appropriate U.S. Green Building Council’s (“USGBC”) Leadership in Energy and Environmental 
Design (“LEED”) green building rating system to evaluate sustainable design. Currently, the 
Proponents have targeted certification for the life science buildings of Project under the LEED 
BD+C Core and Shell (v4) system. The residential building will be targeted to meet LEED BD_C 
New Construction Gold. Compliance with Article 37 will be confirmed by issuance of one or more 
Certifications of Compliance under Section 80B-6 of the Zoning Code. 
 
14. 
Open Spaces, Landscaping, and Pedestrian Environment: Pursuant to the 
Zoning Code Section 51-20, the Project enhances the pedestrian environment by providing an 
approximately 3.5 acres of publicly accessible space, including privately-owned landscaped area open 
to public use as an amenity for the Project and neighboring community and will strengthen the 
Project’s connectivity with the neighborhood. The Developer will provide appropriate management 
and maintenance of publicly accessible space within the Project. Please refer to the landscape plan 
and circulation plan included in Exhibit D, attached. 
 
15.

Other Government Approvals: The Project will require other government 
approvals in addition to this Development Plan. As noted above, the Project is undergoing Large 
Project Review pursuant to Section 80B of the Zoning Code. The Proponents filed the Project 
Notification Form for the Project on August 11, 2021.

authority to review the Development Plan based upon applicable design guidelines. On October 11, 
2022, the Proponent obtained BCDC approval of the design of the buildings and the Project.

Recreation Commission. Accordingly, the Development Plan includes the approval of the Parks and 
Recreation Commission for all buildings or structures to be constructed within 100’ of a park or 
parkway pursuant to Boston Municipal Code Section 7-4.11.

Environmental Impact Report under 301 CMR 11.03(6)(a)5. A Final Environmental Impact Report 
(FEIR) was filed on November 15, 2022.

Certification of Compliance under Section 80B-6 of the Zoning Code, or partial certificates, 
constitutes compliance with the dimensional, use, design, environmental, and other requirements of 
the Zoning Code, in accordance with Section 80C-9 of the Zoning Code, to the extent that such 
requirements are addressed in this Development Plan. Notwithstanding the phasing of the Project, 
the division of ownership of the PDA Area into separate lots or separate legal ownership, the 
separation of buildings or areas of the PDA by public ways or private streets, each separate building 
in the PDA Area shall be eligible for and may receive a Certification of Consistency and a 
Certification of Compliance. Noncompliance of any building in the PDA Area with the 
Development Plan, the Zoning Code or other law shall not affect compliance of any other building 
for which a Certification of Consistency or Certification of Compliance may be or has been issued, 
or the right to construct any other building contemplated by the Development Plan. To the extent 
that any aspect of the existing uses and structures on the Site, or any Existing Interim Uses or 
Interim Uses, are in conflict with any requirement of the Zoning Code not specifically addressed in 
this Development Plan, such requirements shall be deemed inapplicable to the Project and shall be 
deemed waived upon approval of this Development Plan. 
 
20. 
No Duty to Develop the Project: Notwithstanding anything set forth in this 
Development Plan to the contrary, under no circumstances shall the Proponents be obligated to 
proceed with the Project or any Project Component. Construction may proceed in phases, 
subphases, or as one phase, and the delay or non-completion of any Project Component shall not 
affect the compliance or consistency of any other Project Component with this Development Plan. 
 
21. 
Minor Modifications to Plans: This Development Plan constitutes the zoning for 
the PDA Area and the Project. Final plans and specifications for the Project or individual Project 
Components (defined below) will be submitted to the BPDA pursuant to Section 3-1A and 80C of 
the Zoning Code for final design review approval and certification as to consistency with this 
Development Plan, and to other governmental agencies and authorities for final approval. 

 
11 
Accordingly, subject to consistency with the use and dimensional regulations of this Development 
Plan, minor changes may occur to the Project’s design described in this Development Plan. 
 
22. 
Project Components and Phasing: The PDA Area may be reconfigured into 
multiple parcels, which may be under common or separate ownership, and may include subdivision 
or condominium ownership, developed sequentially or simultaneously, and separately developed 
and/or financed. Each such parcel is referred to as a “Project Component.” One or more of the 
Project Components may be further subdivided into one or more separate parcels which may be 
under separate ownership, or one or more of the Project Components may be combined to create 
one single parcel, or a condominium ownership structure may be created for all or part of the 
Project. In the event that current parcels within the PDA Area are divided into Project Components, 
a Certification of Consistency or Partial Certification of Consistency may be issued for any such 
Project Component if, and only if, the Director of the BPDA makes the findings set forth in Article 
80C-8 of the Code. 
 
23. 
Amendment of this Development Plan: The Proponent and owner of the PDA 
Area, or their successors or assigns, or any subsequent owner or Proponent of an individual Project 
Component, or their successors or assigns, may seek amendment of this Development Plan in 
accordance with the procedures prescribed by the Zoning Code, without the consent of any 
Proponent or owner of any other Project Component. In the event that any amendment of this 
Development Plan affects the overall compliance of the Project with this Development Plan, this 
Development Plan will be deemed amended with respect to the Project as a whole, to the extent 
necessary for the overall Project to comply with this Development Plan, without requiring any 
modification of the requirements of this Development Plan as to any other Project Components.

(each a “Building” and collectively, the “Buildings”) containing in the aggregate, approximately 
582,000 square feet of Gross Floor Area1 on two parcels of land in the Allston neighborhood of 
Boston. The two parcels together comprise approximately 136,927 square feet (“s.f.”) or 
approximately 3.14+ acres of land with the existing improvements thereon (the “PDA Overlay 
Area” or the “Project Site”). The PDA Overlay Area is shown on the plan attached hereto as 
Exhibit A and is legally described in Exhibit B attached hereto. 
 
Consistent with the requirements of Article 80C and Section 3-1A.a. of the Code, this 
Development Plan sets forth the proposed location and appearance of the Buildings, the proposed 
open space, landscape and public realm improvements to be undertaken or enabled in connection 
with the Project, the proposed uses at the Buildings, the proposed dimensions and densities of the 
Buildings, the proposed traffic circulation around and within the Project Site, the proposed 
parking accommodations at the Project, the proposed location and access to and from the 
Project’s parking and loading facilities, a description of access to public transportation services, 
and schematic building plans and elevations.

for the Project, are subject to further design refinement and development as well as design 
review by governmental agencies and bodies, including the Boston Redevelopment Authority, 
doing business as the Boston Planning & Development Agency (“BPDA”), and the design of the 
Buildings and such public realm improvements, as well as the Project’s site plan as described 
herein, may evolve in the course of such review.

The Project Site; Proposed Subdivision 
 
The Project Site consists of two contiguous parcels of land with the improvements 
thereon bounded by Western Avenue to the south, Telford Street to the west, Soldiers Field Road 
to the north, and land parcels owned by Harvard University and the City of Boston, respectively, 
to the east. The 1234 Soldiers Field Road parcel (the “1234 Site”) is approximately 51,168 s.f. 
in size (1.17+ acres), and the 1240 Solders Field Road parcel (the “1240 Site”) is approximately 
85,759 s.f. in size (1.97+ acres). 
 
The 1240 Site will be subdivided in order to create a new Lot for the construction of the 
Telford Residential Building (as defined and described below). This new Lot will be located in 
the southwestern portion of the Project Site, at the corner of Telford Street and Western Avenue, 
and comprise approximately 19,330 s.f. (0.44+ acre) of land. A plan showing this subdivision 
and the three zoning Lots to comprise the PDA Overlay Area is attached hereto as Exhibit C. 
The Telford Residential Building will be independently constructed, owned and operated by an 
entity to be established by two local non-profit organizations, Allston Brighton Community 
Development Corporation and The Community Builders, Inc. (“ABCDC/TCB”). 
 
Allston-Brighton Community Development Corporation is a non-profit organization 
established in 1980 to create and preserve affordable housing in the Allston Brighton 
neighborhood, foster community leadership, and assist first-time homeowners in achieving their 
goals. It has developed over 500 units of affordable housing in the Allston-Brighton 
neighborhood. The Community Builders, Inc. is a national non-profit organization based in 
Boston that since its initial inception as South End Community Development in 1964, has 
developed or rehabilitated affordable and mixed-income housing in localities in the Northeast, 
Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions of the United States, including the Charlesview Residences 
development located just across Western Avenue from the Project Site. 

3 
 
The new Lot for the Telford Residential Building will be conveyed in fee simple by the 
1240 Owner to a new entity to be created by the ABCDC/TCB joint venture to develop, own and 
operate the building. 
 
3. 
Existing Zoning 
 
Article 51 of the Code (Allston Brighton Neighborhood District) was recently amended, 
as was the Boston Zoning Map, as a result of the Western Avenue Corridor Study and Rezoning 
(WACRZ) Report, which was adopted by the BPDA in October 2022. As a result, the PDA 
Overlay Area is located within the newly configured Barry’s Corner Community Commercial 
Subdistrict2, as shown on Map 7A/7B/7C/7D of the Boston Zoning Map. The northerly portion 
of the PDA Overlay Area is located within a Greenbelt Protection Overlay District established by 
Section 51-42 of the Code. The PDA Overlay Area is located within Zone “X” (unshaded) as 
shown on the most recent Federal Emergency Management Agency Flood Insurance Rate Map 
for this part of Boston and therefore, is not within any flood hazard district subject to regulation 
under Article 25 of the Code. Nor is the PDA Overlay Area located within the new Coastal 
Flood Resilience Overlay District established by Article 25A of the Code and the Boston Zoning 
Map amendment related thereto. 
 
The provisions of Section 51-44 of the Code allow the creation of Planned Development 
Areas within the Barry’s Corner Community Commercial Subdistrict. Section 51-44 states that 
the purposes of allowing Planned Development Areas within subdistricts such as this one 
include providing a more flexible zoning law; providing public benefits to the Allston- 
Brighton community, including the creation of new job opportunities and affordable housing; 
ensuring public benefits and quality urban design by providing planning and design controls; 
and allowing for the creation of affordable housing. 
 
The recent amendments to Article 51 of the Code included multiple changes applicable to 
the Project, such as allowing multi-family uses above the first floor as permitted uses; providing 
for a maximum Floor Area Ratio for 4.25 for the residential affordability incentive; and the goal 
that Planned Development Areas create new street connections, pedestrians and bicyclist 
facilities as well as opportunities for new transit facilities. Section 51-51 also provides that the 
WACRZ Report provides design guidelines for Proposed Projects in inter alia, the Barry’s 
Corner Community Commercial Subdistrict. The Project as set forth in this Development Plan is 
consistent with all of the foregoing requirements, including without limitation, the use and 
dimensional requirements set forth in “Table 1: Use and Dimensional Standards” of the WACRZ 
Report. 
 
This Development Plan is consistent with the standards set forth in Section 3-1A(a) and 
Section 80C-4 of the Code, as well as the Planned Development Area goals set forth in Section 
51-44 of the Code. As described in this Development Plan and in the Project Notification Form 
(“PNF”) and Draft Project Impact Report (“DPIR”) filed by the Proponent with the BPDA 
pursuant to the provisions of Article 80B of the Code (together, the “Article 80 Submissions”), 
the Project will constitute a well-planned and well-designed development with significant open

ABCDC/TCB, a joint venture of two locally-based non-profit organizations. All of these 
affordable housing units will be permanently income-restricted. 
 
4. 
Project Description; Location and Appearance of the Buildings 
Project Description 
The Project will comprise the construction of four new buildings and related open space 
and public realm improvements, as described below. A conceptual site plan for the Project that 
shows the location of each of the Buildings, their related public realm improvements, the 
proposed open spaces at the Project, and the Site Drive (as defined and discussed below), is 
included in this Development Plan as Exhibit C. 
 
Around half of the Project Site will be used to provide approximately 69,000 s.f. of open 
space and public realm improvements, as further discussed in Section 7 below. The space will 
be comprised of planted and pedestrian areas, as well as the Site Drive, and include a south- 
facing courtyard that will provide options for recreational uses, complementing Allston’s 
existing open spaces such as Smith Field and the parks within the Charles River Reservation. 
The open space will also include dog runs on each of the 1234 Site and the 1240 Site. 
 
A key component of the Project will be the construction of a private site drive bisecting 
the Project Site from Western Avenue to Soldiers Field Road (the “Site Drive”), which will 
enable delivery/loading operations as well as pick-up/drop-off activity for three of the Buildings 
and the south-facing courtyard to be located off the Site Drive, thereby avoiding interference 
with traffic flow on the adjacent public streets. Delivery/loading operations for the Telford 
Residential Building will occur within an internal loading area located off of Telford Street, and 
pick-up/drop-off operations for this building will occur near the building lobby on Telford Street. 
While non-commercial vehicles will be able to access Soldiers Field Road from the Site Drive 
and Telford Street, all truck traffic will be required to access and exit the Project Site from 
Western Avenue, thereby respecting the truck traffic restrictions on Soldiers Field Road. 
 
In consultation with the BPDA and other City agencies, the Proponent has committed to 
grant permanent easement rights to the City of Boston, acting by and through its Public 
Improvement Commission (“PIC”), for the expansion of the rights of way of Telford Street and 
Western Avenue adjacent to the Project Site. These easement rights will allow for the 
Proponent’s installation of wider sidewalks with furnishing zones containing landscaping, new 
street trees and street furniture on both streets, and the City’s installation of protected bicycle 
lanes on both streets and a potential “floating” bus stop on Western Avenue. These future 
easement areas will comprise approximately 11,480 s.f. of the Project Site, subject to finalization 
of the easement areas with the BPDA, the Boston Transportation Department and the PIC, 
followed by applicable PIC approvals. 
 
In addition, the Proponent has committed to granting permanent easement rights to the 
Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation (“DCR”) to enable DCR to construct 

5 
 
a universally accessible southern ramp to a new Telford Street Pedestrian Bridge that may be 
constructed by DCR in the future. This easement area along Telford Street will be 
approximately 3,800 s.f. in size, pending DCR’s design of the future bridge. The construction of 
this new pedestrian bridge will provide a universally accessible means for pedestrians and 
bicyclists to access the Charles Reservation and its recreational resources over Soldiers Field 
Road, and the new ramp’s location will allow the creation of universally accessible access at the 
Telford Street/Soldiers Field Road intersection. 
 
Collectively, the amount of the Project Site proposed to be permanently encumbered with 
easement rights benefitting public agencies for public use (i.e., the PIC and DCR) will be 
approximately 15,280 s.f. (.44+ acre). 
 
Location and Appearance of Buildings 
 
The Project Buildings are described as follows: 
 
• Telford Residential Building – The building to be constructed, owned and 
operated by ABCDC/TBC on the newly-created Lot at the corner of Telford 
Street and Western Avenue (the “Telford Residential Building”) will be 8 stories 
high and contain approximately 72 residential units, comprising a mix of for-sale 
condominium units and rental apartments, as well as approximately 4,000 s.f. of 
ground floor retail space. All of the dwelling units in the building will be income- 
restricted consistent with the City’s Inclusionary Development Policy. The 
Building will share an underground parking garage with the SFR Residential 
Rental Building described below, which garage will accommodate a total of 
approximately 211 vehicles; approximately 39 parking spaces will be reserved to 
residents of the Telford Residential Building. The Building will have an 8th floor 
amenity terrace and building residents will also share an amenity terrace at the 
second floor of the SFR Residential Rental Building described below. The 
Building will also contain a bicycle storage room, other residential amenity 
spaces, a property management office, and approximately 4,000 s.f. of ground 
floor commercial space fronting on Western Avenue. 
 
• Soldiers Field Road Residential Rental Building – This Building near Soldiers 
Field Road on the 1240 Site (“SFR Residential Rental Building”), will be 18 
stories high and contain approximately 380 residential units, residential amenity 
spaces, one or more bicycle storage rooms, and approximately 4,500 s.f. of non- 
residential space that may house an approximately 200-seat music hall venue with 
accessory office and rehearsal space, or in the alternative, retail, restaurant and/or 
other commercial uses that are appropriate for this location. Approximately 152 
parking spaces in the at-grade and underground parking garage to be shared with 
the Telford Residential Building will be reserved for residents of this building. 
An additional 20 spaces will be available for use for the commercial space in both 
this building and the Telford Residential Building. In addition to the resident 
amenity terrace at the second floor to be shared with residents of the Telford 
Residential Building, the SFR Residential Rental Building will also have a second 
amenity terrace on the 18th floor. 

6 
 
• Western Avenue Hotel – The Western Avenue hotel building on the 1234 Site 
(“Western Avenue Hotel”) will be 11 stories high and contain approximately 195 
hotel rooms, approximately 3,500 s.f. of ground floor commercial space fronting 
on Western Avenue, as well as related hotel amenity spaces, including a bicycle 
storage room and an amenity terrace for hotel guests. The Western Avenue Hotel 
and the SFR Condominium Building described below will share an underground 
parking garage to serve approximately 174 vehicles, with approximately 98 
spaces reserved to the hotel. The hotel lobby will face onto the Site Drive, which 
will contain a pick-up/drop-off area for hotel guests. 
 
• SFR Residential Condominium Building – The SFR Residential Condominium 
Building will be 10 stories high and contain approximately 76 for-sale residential 
condominiums, as well as related amenity spaces, including a bicycle storage 
room and a tenth floor outdoor terrace for residents. This building will share an 
underground parking garage podium with the Western Avenue Hotel, with 
approximately 76 spaces reserved to residents of this building. The building 
lobby will front onto the Site Drive, which will contain a pick-up/drop-off area for 
building residents and visitors.

Exhibit E. The ground floor layouts of the Buildings have been designed to focus the 
commercial space at the Project on Western Avenue in order to help activate the pedestrian 
environment there, provide services and amenities to the community, and complement the new 
open space to be created as part of the Project. 
 
The Buildings’ design and layout may evolve during the course of ongoing design review 
of the Project by the BPDA. Consistent with the provisions of this Development Plan and 
Article 80B of the Code, the final plans and specifications for each of the Buildings will be 
subject to approval by the BPDA in accordance with its Development Review Procedures and for 
a determination of the BPDA as to the consistency of each Building with the provisions of this 
Development Plan.

7. 
Open Space, Landscaping and Public Realm Improvements 
 
As noted in Section 4, the Project will include approximately 40,000 s.f. of publicly 
accessible open space, as well as approximately 29,000 s.f. of public realm improvements, 

8 
 
including the Site Drive. A notable feature of the Project will be a large courtyard area fronting 
on Western Avenue that will be designed to allow programming for a variety of events and uses 
and will contain supporting electrical infrastructure for such programs and events. This major 
new open space will be adjacent to ground floor retail spaces that will be marketed to operators 
who can provide complementary goods and services. There will also be dog runs at the 1234 
Site and the 1240 Site to provide alternatives to resident dog use of public parks and public ways 
nearby. 
 
In addition, as shown on the Site Plan, the Proponent has sited each of the Buildings at 
least 25 feet from the property lines on Telford Street and Western Avenue to provide visual 
buffer areas and green spaces adjacent to those streets. 
 
The public realm improvements proposed to be undertaken as part of Project are intended 
to substantially improve area conditions for pedestrians in particular, and to facilitate easier 
circulation through this part of the Allston neighborhood for bicyclists as well. The public 
realm improvements planned along Telford Street and Western Avenue are conceptually shown 
on the plans attached to this Development Plan as Exhibit G. Although existing street trees 
along Western Avenue and Telford Street will need to be removed in order to enable the 
construction of the planned public realm improvements on those streets, those trees will be more 
than replaced by the new street trees to be installed by the Proponent within the newly widened 
rights of way of Telford Street and Western Avenue. All street tree removals and replacements 
will be subject to approval of the City’s Parks Department. 
 
The final design of the public realm improvements described herein will be subject to 
BPDA design review as well as final approvals and/or the issuance of permits from other 
applicable public agencies, including the PIC, the Parks Department, and the City of Boston 
Transportation Department (“BTD”). 
 
8. 
Public Transportation; Pedestrian and Bicycle Circulation 
 
The MBTA operates three bus routes near the Project Site, including the Route 70 and 
Route 86, that run along Western Avenue adjacent to the Project Site. The Project Site is about ½ 
half mile from the MBTA’s Framingham/Worcester commuter line at the Boston Landing 
Station, about one mile from the MBTA’s Red Line Harvard Square Station, and about 1.5 miles 
from the Red Line Central Square Station. 
 
The Project will include secure bicycle spaces for residents and hotel employees, as well 
as outdoor bicycle storage for visitors and the public. The Proponent is also discussing with 
BTD the placement of a Bluebikes bicycle sharing station at the Project Site. 
 
As discussed in Section 7, the public realm improvements planned as part of the Project 
are aimed at enhancing the safety of pedestrians and bicyclists and minimizing 
pedestrian/vehicular conflicts. These improvements will be subject to the receipt of applicable 
approvals from the PIC and BTD, and will be coordinated with other transportation system and 
public realm improvements being undertaken by the City and by proponents of other 
development projects in the Allston neighborhood contemporaneously with the development of 
the Project. 

9 
 
9. 
Green Buildings 
 
All of the Buildings will comply, and in some cases will exceed, the requirements of 
Article 37 (Green Buildings) of the Code relating to “green” buildings. The Proponent has 
committed to achieve U.S. Green Building Council Leadership in Energy and Environmental 
Design (“LEED”) green building certifiability at the Gold level for all four buildings, using the 
LEEDv4 rating system. In addition, the Proponent is pursuing compliance with Passive House 
standards for the Telford Residential Building and the SFR Residential Rental Building. 
 
10. 
Proposed Traffic Circulation, Parking and Loading 
 
The construction of the Buildings will be accompanied by substantial public realm 
improvements on adjacent public streets, as discussed in Section 7 above. These will improve 
pedestrian, bicycle and vehicular circulation in the area. The Proponents’ provision of easements 
to the City of Boston along Western Avenue and Telford Street will materially increase the rights 
of way for these streets and allow for wider sidewalks with planting zones that can include street 
furniture and new street trees; the City’s introduction of protected bicycle lanes; and the City’s 
potential creation of a “floating” bus lane on Western Avenue in front of the Project. As 
demonstrated in the traffic analyses contained in the Article 80 Submissions, the Project will not 
materially affect traffic flow in the area of the Project Site. 
 
The Project will contain parking accommodations for approximately 385 vehicles in two 
garages located on each of the 1234 Site and 1240 Sites. All drop-off/pick-up activities for the 
SFR Rental Residential, SFR Residential Condominium and Western Avenue Hotel Buildings 
will occur off the Site Drive, as will all loading/delivery activities. Because the front lobby of 
the Telford Residential Building will be on Telford Street, drop-off/pick-up activities for that 
building will occur on Telford Street, and loading/delivery operations in the garage will occur off 
a driveway on Telford Street. The general location of the proposed vehicular and loading 
entry/exit points for each of the Buildings in the Project, as well as general locations of the main 
pedestrian entrances, are depicted on the Traffic and Circulation Plans attached to this 
Development Plan as Exhibit H. 
 
11. 
Signage and Design Requirements 
 
Each Building will contain building identification signage as well as signage for any 
retail or other non-residential uses, subject to design review and approval by the BPDA as part of 
the Article 80B design review process. Any such signage approved by the BPDA shall be 
deemed to be consistent with the provisions of this Development Plan. 
 
The issuance of a Partial Certification of Consistency for any Building shall constitute 
compliance with all requirements of Sections 51-42 (Greenbelt Protection Overlay Districts), 51- 
42 through 49 (Planned Development Areas), and Sections 51-51 through 53 (Design) of the 
Code, as well as with all other provisions of Article 51 and the Code addressed herein. 
 
12. 
Additional Public Benefits 
 
Section 51-49 of the Code provides that Development Plans for Planned Development 
Areas within the Allston Neighborhood District should provide for public benefits, such as the 

10 
 
provision of affordable housing available to Allston-Brighton and Boston residents, or 
“improvements to the aesthetic character of the development site and its surroundings, which 
may include the provision of open space connections, of the Charles River waterfront, the 
provision of street trees and other improvements that enhance open space, the improvement of 
the urban design characteristics of the site and its surroundings, or the enhancement of existing 
open space or the creation of new open spaces.” 
 
The Project will include the creation of approximately 72 units of affordable housing that 
will be permanently income-restricted, owned and operated by an affiliate of local non-profit 
organizations, and made available to Allston-Brighton and Boston residents through the City’s 
Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Plan process. 
 
The Project will also greatly improve the aesthetic character of the Project Site, which 
currently contains a combination of obsolete and vacant buildings with accessory parking, and 
surfaces that are nearly 100% impervious. Through the creation of a substantial public realm 
improvements along Telford Street, as well as the proposed grant of easements rights to DCR 
that would make the creation of a universally accessible ramp to a future new Telford Street 
pedestrian bridge possible, and the Project will materially improve pedestrian and bicyclists’ 
access to the rich recreational resources of the Charles River Reservation and its riverfront. As 
noted above, the Project will result in the replacement of 6 existing street trees on Western 
Avenue and Telford Street with approximately 14 street trees (subject to applicable City 
approvals), complementing the planting of approximately 100 trees on the Project Site, greatly 
reducing the urban heat island effect. 
 
In addition to the public benefits outlined above, the Project will also create the following 
public benefits for the residents of the Allston neighborhood and the city of Boston: 
 
• the creation of approximately 170 permanent jobs and approximately 500 
construction jobs; 
 
• new retail/restaurant and other ground floor uses that will activate and energize 
the public realm and provide services and products to serve the community; 
 
• a substantial increase in the City’s property tax revenues from the Project Site; 
and 
 
• the replacement of obsolete commercial buildings with new buildings that will 
contain state-of-the art energy conservation systems, with two of the residential 
buildings designed to meet Passive House standards and all four buildings to be 
LEED certifiable at the Gold level. 
 
The BPDA’s issuance of a Partial Certificate of Consistency pursuant to Section 80C-8 of 
the Code shall conclusively establish consistency with the provisions of Section 51-49 of the 
Code (Public Benefits in PDA’s). 

11 
 
13. 
Current Permitting Status 
 
The Proponent filed the PNF for the Project with the BPDA on September 2, 2020 
pursuant to Article 80B of the Code, and an Environmental Notification Form (“ENF”) under the 
Massachusetts Environmental Policy Act (“MEPA”) with the MEPA Office, notice of which was 
published in the Environmental Monitor on September 23, 2020. The Secretary of Energy and 
Environmental Affairs issued a Certificate on the ENF on October 23, 2020, outlining issues to 
be addressed in a Draft Environmental Impact Report (“DEIR”). On November 2, 2021, the 
BPDA issued a Scoping Determination on the PNF, and the Proponent has filed a Draft Project 
Impact Report (“DEIR/DPIR”) with the BPDA in response to the Scoping Determination. This 
document has also been filed with the MEPA Office in response to the Certificate on the PNF. 
The Proponent will prosecute completion of the Article 80B and MEPA processes for the 
Project. 
 
Because the existing buildings at the Project Site are each over 50 years old, they were 
subject to the demolition delay provisions of Article 85 of the Code. On November 6, 2020, the 
Boston Landmarks Commission found the existing building at the 1234 Site (i.e., the hotel 
building) and the garage facility at the 1240 Site not to be significant. At its February 9, 2022 
public hearing, the Boston Landmarks Commission declined to invoke an Article 85 demolition 
delay for the former Skating Club of Boston facility at the 1240 Site. Hence, the Proponent is 
free to demolish all of the existing buildings at the Project Site in preparation for the 
development of the Project. 
 
Following BPDA approval of the Project and the DEIR/DPIR pursuant to Article 80B of 
the Code, as well as the approval of this Development Plan and an accompanying map 
amendment depicting the boundaries of the PDA Overlay Area as set forth in this Development 
Plan by the BPDA and the Boston Zoning Commission pursuant to Article 80C of the Code, the 
Proponent will seek such further permits and approvals from other governmental agencies as are 
necessary to undertake construction of the Project. These will include, without limitation, 
completion of the MEPA review process, site plan approvals from the Boston Water and Sewer 
Commission, approval of the proposed public realm improvements and easement grants to the 
City from the PIC, street tree removal approvals from the City’s Parks Department, project 
review approval from the City’s Parks and Recreation Commission, demolition and building 
permits from the City of Boston Inspectional Services Department, a fuel storage license and 
garage permit from the City’s Public Safety Commission, Committee on Licenses, and a 
Construction Access and Work Permit from DCR sidewalk replacement along Soldiers Field 
Road and the new site drive curb cut. 
 
14. 
Development Timeline and Other Matters 
 
The Project will be constructed after all applicable governmental reviews have been 
completed and all necessary permits and approvals have been obtained, subject to marketing and 
financing feasibility. The construction of the Project is expected to occur over a period of 
approximately 5-8 years, with construction of the residential buildings and open space on the 
1240 Site commencing first, followed by the development of the two new buildings and related 
open space on the 1234 Site. It is expected that the proposed public realm improvements on 

12 
 
Telford Street and Western Avenue, as well as the initial build-out of the Site Drive, will be 
undertaken in concert with the development of the buildings on the 1240 Site. 
 
It is also contemplated that portions of the Project Site and/or the Buildings and other 
improvements located thereon from time to time may be reconfigured, including without 
limitation, through one or more subdivisions, ground leases, subleases, condominium regimes or 
otherwise, which parcels or sub-areas may be under common or separate ownership, developed 
sequentially or simultaneously, and/or separately developed and/or financed (each such parcel or 
sub-area is referred to herein as a “Project Component”). Therefore, as used herein, the term 
“Proponent” shall mean the Proponent named above or, with respect to any Project Component 
subsequently owned by another entity, such successor in interest (including without limitation, 
ABCDC/TCB). The approval of this Development Plan constitutes approval for any such 
subdivision, re-subdivision or condominium creation at the Project Site. 
 
Notwithstanding anything set forth herein or in the Code to the contrary, this 
Development Plan approves any zoning nonconformity created or increased by the separation of 
ownership of individual Project Components, or by the subdivision, re-subdivision, combination 
or submission to condominium ownership or other forms of ownership of Project Components, 
provided that the requirements set forth in this Development Plan are met with respect to the 
Project Site as if the Project Site were one Lot and such Project Component complies with any 
requirements of this Development Plan applicable to such Project Component. The compliance 
of any Project Component with the requirements of this Development Plan shall be determined 
based upon such Project Component’s compliance with any requirements of this Development 
Plan that apply to such Project Component. The compliance or non-compliance of any one 
Project Component with the provisions of this Development Plan shall not affect the compliance 
of any other Project Component, and each Project Component shall be eligible to receive its own 
Partial Certification of Consistency from the BPDA pursuant to the provisions of Article 80C of 
the Code. 
 
15. 
Applicability 
 
In accordance with Section 80-C of the Code, the consistency of the Project as a whole or 
the consistency of any individual Project Component with the provisions of this Development 
Plan shall constitute compliance with the dimensional, density, use, parking/loading, signage, 
green buildings, Greenbelt Protection Overlay District, design guidelines, telecommunications 
and other requirements of the Code, including without limitation, the provisions of Article 51 
thereof, to the extent such requirements have been addressed in this Development Plan. Thus, no 
Board of Appeal zoning relief shall be required under the Greenbelt Protection Overlay District 
provisions of the Code. To the extent that any aspect of the proposed uses and proposed 
improvements addressed in this Development Plan are in conflict with any requirement of the 
Code, the provisions of this Development Plan shall govern and control. 
 
Schematic plans and elevations for the proposed Buildings are attached to this 
Development Plan as Exhibit E. Upon approval of this Development Plan, final plans and 
specifications for each Building within the Project may be submitted to the BPDA for final 
design review approval pursuant to Article 80B of the Code and for certification as to 
consistency with this Development Plan pursuant to Article 80C of the Code. Accordingly, 

13 
 
subject to the consistency of Buildings with the dimensional and density provisions of this 
Development Plan, modifications to the proposed Project, including without limitation, to the 
exterior design of the Buildings, the publicly accessible open spaces, the Site Drive, and/or the 
parking and loading facilities, will be subject only to BPDA Article 80B design review/approval, 
without the need for amendment of this Development Plan or further BPDA action. The 
BPDA’s approval of final plans and specifications for each Building shall confirm their 
consistency with this Development Plan and with any provisions of the Code discussed in this 
Development Plan. 
 
16. 
Amendment of Development Plan 
 
Any owner of an individual Project Component may seek amendment of this 
Development Plan only as to such Project Component in accordance with the procedures 
required by the Code, without the consent of any other owner of a Project Component; provided, 
however, that no such amendment shall affect the obligations of any other Proponent under any 
agreements between such Proponent(s) and the BPDA. In the event that any amendment to this 
Development Plan proposed by the owner of a Project Component is approved, and such 
amendment affects the overall compliance of the Project with this Development Plan, this 
Development Plan shall be deemed amended with respect to the Project as a whole to the extent 
necessary for the Project to comply with this Development Plan. 
 
17. 
No Obligation to Proceed with Project. 
 
Notwithstanding anything set forth herein to the contrary, under no circumstances shall 
the Proponent or any other party be obligated to proceed with the development of all or any 
portion of the Project.
