Overlay District, and the vast majority of the Site is located within the Community Commercial 
subdistrict as governed by Article 65 of the Code, with only a small portion of the Site located in 
(i) the 2F-5000 subdistrict as governed by Article 65 of the Code, and (ii) the Greenbelt 
Protection Overlay District established by Article 29 of the Code the, all as shown on Map 
5A/5B of the City of Boston Zoning Maps. Pursuant to Section 3-1A.a, Article 65, and Article 
29, Planned Development Areas are permitted within the area that includes the Site. 
 
 
4. 
New Building Project: The Proponent proposes the development of a new six-
story commercial building containing up to 305,000 square feet of gross floor area (“GFA”), 
including laboratory, research and development, office, ground-floor retail/restaurant, and a 
three-level structured below-grade parking facility accommodating off-street parking for 
approximately 417 vehicles (the “New Building”). The New Building will be designed to 
minimize visual impacts to the nearby Savin Hill neighborhood, and will improve upon the 
existing surface parking area that it is replacing. The existing GFA of the Existing Building will 
be considered for the purposes of calculating total GFA and floor area ratio (“FAR”) of the PDA 
area in accordance with Article 80C of the Code. 
 
 
5. 
Proposed Locations and Appearance of New Building Structure: Selected 
elevations attached hereto as Exhibit C illustrate the New Building’s general appearance. The 
New Building is composed of a new six-story structure that reacts to the existing neighboring 
Savin Hill residential community by being set close to the Existing Building, and shields 
portions Patten’s Cove from traffic impacts from Interstate 93. The New Building also provides 
outdoor balconies on portions of the above-grade stories to break up the building massing and 
provide valuable outdoor amenity space for building users. While the New Building will have a 
unique expression tailored to its placement on the Site, there will be both a proximate and 
physical connection between the New Building and the Existing Building, thus ensuring that 
while the New Building is in close proximity to the Existing Building, it also retains its own 
character and expression. 
 
 
 
6. 
Proposed Density and Dimensions of Structures: The specific height (as 
defined in the Zoning Code) for any building within the Site will be calculated from the average 
mean grade as defined in the Zoning Code, but, notwithstanding the definition of Building 
Height in Article 2A of the Code, no rooftop mechanicals or penthouses or other structures set 

 
 
 
atop or projecting from a rooftop shall be counted towards the overall zoning height of that 
building (“Zoning Height”). The maximum Zoning Height of any building within the Site shall 
be 100 feet. The maximum height of mechanical screening or penthouses on top of the buildings 
shall not be considered in determining the maximum building Zoning Height. Notwithstanding 
the foregoing, for commercial buildings, the mechanical penthouse or mechanical screen shall 
not exceed 45 feet in height, and up to 55 feet inclusive of rooftop exhaust related mechanical 
elements, such as, flues and exhaust vents that may extend above the mechanical screen to an 
extent not to exceed 10 feet; the heights of the mechanical screen, penthouse or elements shall be 
measured from the top of the flat roof of the building at its Zoning Height to the highest point of 
the mechanical screen, penthouse, or element. 
 
The New Building will contain up to 305,000 square feet of GFA1. See Exhibit D for massing 
diagram. The Existing Building contains approximately 695,000 square feet of GFA. 
Accordingly, the combined GFA for the New Building and the Existing Building will be up to 
approximately 1,000,000 square feet, which results in an FAR of up to 1.5 across the full PDA 
Site. The maximum Building Height, FAR and GFA set out above will be the only dimensional 
requirements applicable to the PDA Site. All other dimensional or design requirements of the 
Code shall not be applicable to the PDA Site and are superseded by this Development Plan. The 
New Building Project shall be subject to design, environmental and other development review by 
the BPDA, and aspects of the New Building Project approved as part of such review shall be and 
hereby are deemed to be the dimensional and design requirements applicable to the New 
Building and are hereby incorporated in this Development Plan. 
 
 
7. 
Proposed Open Space and Landscaping: The New Building Project will 
revitalize an area that is currently an open asphalt surface parking lot. The New Building Project 
will provide additional landscape improvements that will be constructed contemporaneously with 
the building, including the expansion of the site’s pedestrian path network, providing improved 
pedestrian and bike access between the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority Savin Hill 
transit station and JFK/UMass Red Line/South Shore Commuter Rail Station. 
 
 
8. 
Proposed Uses: The New Building will be used primarily for office, laboratory, 
research and development, and parking facilities (as accessory, ancillary, and principal uses). In 
addition to the uses listed above, all of the uses listed in Exhibit E shall be permitted as of right 
on the full PDA Site. 
 
 
9. 
Proposed Traffic Circulation: The New Building will continue to be served by 
the existing curb-cuts along the Morrissey Boulevard southbound Access Road. Access to the 
existing surface parking spaces will be maintained via a two-way circulatory drive aisle 
surrounding the Project. A pick-up/drop-off area will be provided adjacent to the northeast wall 
of the New Building, along the drive aisle where it separates the Existing Building from the New 
Building. 
 
 
1 All square footages are approximate. GFA is defined in Article 2A of the Code and specifically excludes 
from calculation floor area devoted to mechanical equipment, storage, below-grade parking areas and service and 
loading areas. 

 
 
 
 
10. 
Proposed Parking and Loading Facilities: The New Building will include three 
levels of below-grade parking for approximately 417 vehicles. All loading and service activity 
will be actively managed by the building transportation coordinator, and the New Building will 
provide both secure bicycle parking spaces and publicly accessible bicycle parking spaces. 
 
 
11. 
Access to Public Transportation: The Site is well served by the Massachusetts 
Bay Transportation Authority (“MBTA”); it is approximately 2,000 feet from the JFK/UMass 
Station. This Station is a commuter hub providing connection between three commuter rail lines 
(Greenbush, Kingston/Plymouth, and Middleborough/Lakeville), the MBTA Red Line, and three 
MBTA bus routes (Number 8, 16, and 41). 
 
 
12. 
Signage: The signage program for the New Building shall be subject to design, 
environmental and other development review by the BPDA, and any sign approved as part of 
such review shall be deemed to be in compliance with the Development Plan. 
 
 
13. 
Development Review Procedures: All aspects of the New Building Project 
design will be subject to ongoing development and design review and approval by the BPDA. 
 
 
14. 
Green Building and Resiliency Measures: The New Building is subject to 
Article 37 (Green Buildings) of the Code, pursuant to Section 80B Large Project Review. It will 
meet the requirements necessary to achieve at least a Gold-level certifiability using LEEDv4 
rating system, which will exceed the City’s requirements under Article 37. It will be designed 
with energy-efficient HVAC and lighting equipment and systems and will incorporate other 
potential energy conservation measures, as reasonable and feasible. 
 
Portions of the PDA Site are located within the FEMA-designated Special Flood Hazard 
Area, Zone AE on the FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM [Community Panel No. 
25025C0083J, effective March 16, 2016]). Stormwater infrastructure will be designed to reduce 
the existing peak rates and volumes of stormwater runoff from the PDA Site and will also 
promote stormwater recharge. The stormwater management system for the New Building will 
implement a combination of techniques, some of which being evaluated include: green 
infrastructure, low impact development techniques, and grey infrastructure to mitigate and retain 
stormwater volumes where applicable. The New Building will also implement strategies at the 
ground level to reduce the urban heat island effect, including pervious cover and high albedo 
paving materials, green infrastructure, and other design features to minimize heat island effect. 
The New Building will undergo resiliency review due to its location with the CFROD. 
 
 
15. 
Public Benefits: The PDA will provide many public benefits to the Dorchester 
neighborhood and to the City of Boston, including the creation of job opportunities and training, 
significant landscaping improvements around the Site, the generation of additional tax revenues 
and the incorporation of resiliency measures in the New Building’s design: 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
a. Improvements to the Aesthetic Character of the Site: The New Building will 
replace portions of a large surface parking lot with a high-quality architecture 
that will visually activate and enliven this portion of the PDA Site. 
 
b. Sustainability and Resiliency: The New Building will incorporate design 
elements to improve on-site stormwater management and reduce the risk of 
precipitation-based flooding, such as reducing impervious surfaces, increasing 
the amount of greenery and incorporating green infrastructure. The New Building 
is also designed to reduce heat island impacts to the extent feasible and it will 
exceed the requirements of Article 37 (Green Buildings) aiming to achieve 
certifiability at least at a Gold level using the LEEDv4 rating system. The 
Proponent is committed to utilizing energy-efficient HVAC and lighting 
equipment and systems. 
 
c. Social and Economic: The New Building is expected to generate approximately 
$4.92 million in housing and jobs linkage payments, and approximately 800 
permanent on-site jobs and approximately 400 temporary construction jobs. The 
New Building is also expected to generate more than $6.4 million annually in 
new real estate tax revenues for the City, along with significant State sales and 
business tax revenues for the Commonwealth. 
 
d. Transit Oriented Development: The PDA is in close proximity to several MBTA 
bus, subway and Commuter Rail lines, all of which provide easy access to the 
Site from the surrounding neighborhood and other areas of the City and beyond. 
The Proponent will enter into a Transportation Access Plan Agreement with the 
Boston Transportation Department in which it will commit to Transportation 
Demand Measures (TDMs) consistent with the City’s guidelines. 
 
e. Workforce Development and Training: Recognizing the extraordinary need for 
not only a technician-level workforce in life science, but also the existing dearth 
of efficient and appropriate training and degree programs, the Proponent is 
actively working with local elected officials and the Massachusetts 
Biotechnology Council (“MassBio”, the non-profit company in Massachusetts 
representing the interests of the life science industry who are its members) to 
design a life science jobs training center at the PDA Site. This jobs training 
center aims to offer industry-approved certificate programs designed deliberately 
and intentionally to attract Boston residents into the Existing Building – where 
the jobs center will be located – with the goal that when these residents leave the 
center several months later, they have in-hand a lab certificate and a high five-
figure full-time salary plus benefits job with a life science company. As part of its 
approvals for the interior gut renovation and repurposing of the Existing 
Building, the predecessor-in-interest to the Proponent was required to build-out 
the core and shell of approximately 2,500 square feet of space within the Existing 
Building and provide that space, rent-free, to a local non-profit. The Proponent is 
going well above and beyond that obligation, and is working with MassBio to not 
only provide a 3,000 square foot space for its life science jobs training center, but 

 
 
 
is also working to partner with local educational institutions and MassBio’s 
industry-members to craft multiple technician-level certificate programs designed 
to be completed in a matter of months. These specifically tailored certificate 
programs are being created with current life science companies’ needs in mind so 
that graduates will immediately be in-demand hires for the hundreds of life 
science companies rapidly launching and expanding in Massachusetts and the 
Boston area at a speed that exceeds the established methods of creating a locally 
trained workforce. 
 
f. Smart Utilities: The New Building will comply with the BPDA’s Smart Utilities 
Policy for Article 80 Development Review, as applicable. 
 
16. 
Greenbelt Protection Overlay District: The PDA Site is located in part within 
the Greenbelt Protection Overlay District, as established by Article 29 of the Code. Any portion 
of the Site developed within the Greenbelt Protection Overlay District will comply with the 
standards and requirements set forth in Article 29 of the Code. 
 
 
17. 
Restricted Parking Overlay District: The Site is located within the Restricted 
Parking Overlay District (“RPOD”). Approval of this Development Plan shall constitute 
compliance with all applicable RPOD requirements, and as such, no conditional use permit from 
the Board of Appeals shall be required. 
 
 
18. 
Boston Civic Design Commission: The New Building will require Schematic 
Design Approval by the Boston Civic Design Commission (“BCDC”) pursuant to Article 28 of 
the Code. 
 
19. 
Applicability: In accordance with Section 80C-9 of the Code, consistency of the 
New Building with this Development Plan shall constitute compliance with the dimensional, use 
and all other requirements of the Code, to the extent such requirements have been addressed in 
the Development Plan. Issuance of a Certification of Consistency will constitute compliance by 
the New Building and PDA Site with all applicable provisions of the Code with respect to 
Planned Development Areas. 
 
 
20. 
Minor Modification to Plans: This Development Plan sets forth the 
dimensional, use and other zoning requirements for the PDA Site, including the Existing 
Building, to the extent such requirements have been addressed in this Development Plan. Upon 
approval of this Development Plan, final plans and specifications for the New Building will be 
submitted to the BPDA pursuant to Section 3-1A, Article 80B and Article 80C of the Code for 
final design review approval and certification as to consistency with this Development Plan, and 
to other governmental agencies for final approval. Subject to consistency with the dimensional 
regulations set forth in this Development Plan, minor changes may occur to the New Building’s 
design described in this Development Plan without requiring an amendment to this Development 
Plan, as determined by the Director of the BPDA in accordance with Section 80A-6 of the Code, 
and subject to the use and dimensional requirements set forth in this Development Plan. No 
changes to the public benefits arising from the community-driven 80B process shall require an 
amendment to this Development plan, provided that the mitigation and/or community benefits as 

 
 
 
required under this Development Plan are not modified unless approved by the BPDA during 
Article 80B review. 
 
 
21. 
Development Schedule: The Proponent estimates that construction of the New 
Building will take approximately 32 months. 
 
 
22. 
Proponent’s Obligation to Proceed with the New Building Project: 
Notwithstanding anything set forth herein to the contrary, under no circumstances shall the 
Proponent be obligated to proceed with all or any portion of the New Building Project.

Development Plan. Pursuant to Section 3-1A(a), Sections 66-28 through 66-30, 
and Article 80C of the Boston Zoning Code (the “Code”), this plan (this “Development Plan”) 
constitutes the Planned Development Area Development Plan for an approximately 2.4-acre area 
of land in the Fenway neighborhood (as described in more detail below, the “Project Site”). The 
Proponent (as defined below) proposes to remove the existing structures and improvements on the 
Project Site and construct a mixed-use building including ground-floor retail and restaurants with 
a mix of uses on the upper floors, as well as a cultural/civic use building, an open space area, and 
pedestrian realm improvements, as more fully described below (the “Project”). 
This Development Plan consists of nine (9) pages of text plus attachments designated 
Exhibits A through G, which together establish the proposed: (i) location and appearance of the 
Project; (ii) uses of the Project; (iii) densities and dimensions of the Project; (iv) open spaces and 
landscaping; (v) traffic circulation; (vi) parking and loading facilities; (vii) access to public 
transportation; and (viii) public benefits with regard to the Project. All references to this 
Development Plan contained herein shall pertain only to such pages and exhibits. 
This Development Plan constitutes permanent zoning for the Project Site in accordance 
with Section 3-lA and Article 80C of the Code, and it shall not expire or lapse for any reason. To 
the extent that any aspect of the Project or this Development Plan is in conflict with any 
requirement of the Code not specifically addressed in this Development Plan, such requirement(s) 
shall be deemed to be waived upon approval of this Development Plan. 
Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings assigned to such 
terms in Article 2 of the Code as in effect as of the date this Development Plan becomes effective, 
without giving effect to any subsequent amendments to the Code, and this Development Plan shall 
not be subject to changes to the Code that take effect after such date.

a business address 136 Brookline Avenue, Boston, MA 02115. The Proponent, through an affiliate, 
has entered into an agreement to purchase the Project Site from Star Markets Company, Inc.

foot) area of land known and numbered as 1400 Boylston Street, Boston (Fenway), Massachusetts,

Exhibit A-2. The Project Site is bounded generally by Boylston Street to the north, Kilmarnock

enhancement of existing open space or the creation of new open space; (d) improvements to 
transportation systems; and/or (e) mitigation with respect to transportation, parks, workforce 
development, and the inclusion within the Project of certain public facilities and public 
accommodation.

decommissioned gas station with new diverse and active ground-floor uses, enhancing the 
pedestrian experience and repairing the scar of the former gas station fronting on the Emerald 
Necklace. The Project will incorporate step-backs along the western edge of the proposed building 
to create a softer transition, maintaining sight lines from the adjacent neighborhood and from 
nearby Ramler Park. Finally, the Project’s ground-floor retail/restaurant space and lobbies will be 
set back 15 feet from Boylston Street to foster a vibrant, active streetscape. 
e. 
Transit-Oriented Development. The Project exemplifies smart-growth and 
transit-oriented development by concentrating new commercial uses in close proximity to major 
regional Commuter Rail, train and bus lines that provide easy access to the Project Site from all of 
the City’s neighborhoods and suburbs. 
f. 
Sustainable Design. The Project will comply with the requirements of 
Article 37 of the Code. The Project team will use the U.S. Green Building Council’s Leadership 
in Energy and Environmental Design (“LEED”) green building rating system to evaluate 
sustainable design measures, in accordance with Article 37 of the Code. The Project, as designed, 
will target LEED Gold level certification, and the Project team will continue to research additional 
sustainable and energy-efficient measures as the Project design develops. 
g. 
Additional Mitigation Commitments. The Project has provided additional 
mitigation commitments as set forth in the DPIR (defined below) to satisfy the requirement to 
provide additional mitigation as set forth in Section 66-30 of the Code. 
16. 
Groundwater Conservation Overlay District. Each Building within the Project 
will comply with the standards and requirements applicable to projects within the GCOD set forth 
in Article 32 which may be satisfied by shared stormwater capture and infiltration systems. The 
proponent of each Building shall demonstrate that such Building meets the requirements of Section 
32-6 of the Code by obtaining a stamped certification from a Massachusetts registered engineer 
showing that the requirements of Section 32-6 of the Code are met or, if site constraints prevent 
compliance on-site, such proponent and their engineer have worked with the Boston Water and

Sewer Commission to develop a plan that would achieve the maximum compliance and any 
alternatives that would satisfy compliance. Each proponent shall provide a copy of the stamped 
certification from a Massachusetts registered engineer to the Boston Water and Sewer 
Commission, the BPDA and the Boston Groundwater Trust prior to the issuance of a Certification 
of Consistency for each such Building. As such, upon the issuance of a Certification of 
Consistency for the Building, the Building shall be deemed to be in compliance with Article 32 of 
the Code and shall not need a conditional use permit from the Board of Appeal for Article 32 
purposes. 
17. 
Greenbelt Protection Overlay District. A portion of the Project Site is located 
within the Greenbelt Protection Overlay District established by Article 29 of the Code. In 
connection with the Project, the Proponent will seek approval of the Boston Parks and Recreation 
Commission under applicable City Ordinances. Approval of this Development Plan and issuance 
of a Certification of Consistency for the portion of the Project within the Greenbelt Projection 
Overlay District shall constitute compliance with all applicable requirements of Article 29 of the 
Code and no portion of the Project shall require a conditional use permit from the Board of Appeal 
for Article 29 purposes. 
18. 
Neighborhood Design Overlay District. A portion of the Project Site, including 
the location for the Civic Building, is located within the West Fenway Neighborhood Design 
Overlay District. Prior to issuance of a Certification of Consistency for a portion or all of a 
Building in the portion of the Project Site located in the West Fenway Neighborhood Design 
Overlay District, the BPDA shall provide the Boston Landmarks Commission with a copy of the 
design plans for such Building and the Landmarks Commission may, within thirty (30) days after 
its receipt of such materials provide the BPDA with a report with recommendations to aid the 
BPDA in determining the Building’s consistency with this Development Plan and Section 66-37.2 
of the Code; provided, however, that if the Landmarks Commission has not provided comments 
within thirty (30) days of submission, a Certification of Consistency may issue. 
19. 
Restricted Parking Overlay District. Parking for the Project shall be as provided 
in this Development Plan and shall not require any zoning relief from the Board of Appeal. 
20. 
Development Review Procedures. All aspects of the proposed Project design will 
be subject to ongoing development review and approval by the BPDA under Article 80B of the 
Code. In accordance with these development review procedures, the Proponent filed a Project 
Notification Form (“PNF”) for the Project on June 6, 2022, initiating the Large Project Review 
process with the BPDA. On November 28, 2022, the BPDA issued a Scoping Determination on 
the PNF, and the Proponent filed a Draft Project Impact Report in response to the Scoping 
Determination on September 18, 2023 (the “DPIR”). Because the construction of the Primary 
Building and Civic Building may be phased, it is anticipated that development review may proceed 
separately for each such buildings. 
In addition to BPDA approval of the Project and the DPIR pursuant to Article 80B of the 
Code, and the approval of this Development Plan, the Proponent will seek such further permits 
and approvals from other governmental agencies as are necessary to undertake construction of the 
Project. The final Project plans and specifications, as approved by the BPDA pursuant to the final 
design review procedures described in Section 22 below, will be deemed to be consistent with this

of the Code.

Applicability; Certification of Consistency. In accordance with Section 80-C of 
the Code, consistency of each Building within the Project with this Plan constitutes compliance 
with the dimensional, density, use and all other requirements of the Code to the extent such 
requirements have been addressed in this Development Plan. The issuance of a Certification of 
Consistency for any Building shall evidence compliance with all aspects of Sections 66-39 
(Specific Design Requirement) and 66-40 (Screening and Buffering) of the Code. 
In accordance with Section 80C-9 of the Code, consistency of any Building within the 
Project with this Development Plan and the provisions of existing, applicable zoning in effect as 
of the date this Development Plan is effective shall be evidenced by a Certification of Consistency 
or partial Certification of Consistency, as appropriate, issued by the BPDA with respect to such 
building pursuant to Section 80C-8 of the Code (a “Certification of Consistency”). The issuance 
of a Certification of Consistency for any building within the Project shall evidence compliance of 
such Building with the requirements of this Development Plan (to the extent applicable) and the 
existing, applicable zoning in effect as of the date this Development Plan is approved and shall 
permit the issuance of building permits by the City of Boston Inspectional Services Department 
for the Project. 
It is contemplated that portions of the Project Site and the buildings and other 
improvements located thereon from time to time may be reconfigured into smaller parcels or sub-

ownership, developed sequentially or simultaneously, and/or separately developed and/or financed 
(each such parcel or sub-area is referred to herein as a “Project Component”). 
Notwithstanding anything set forth herein or in the Code to the contrary, for purposes of 
this Development Plan, compliance of the individual Project Components with the requirements 
of this Development Plan will be determined as if the entire Project Site were one Lot, even if it is

Final Approval; Minor Modifications to Plans. This Development Plan sets forth 
the density, dimensional, use and other zoning requirements for the Project and the Project Site.

submitted to the BPDA pursuant to Section 3-1A and Article 80C of the Code for final design 
review approval and certification as to consistency with this Development Plan, and to other 
governmental agencies and authorities for final approval. In light of the comprehensive public 
reviews needed to secure all required permits and approvals for the Project, modifications and

significantly increase the impacts of the Project or Development Plan, the BPDA shall require 
the filing of a Notice of Project Change and/or amendment to this Development Plan.

leasing, market forces, force majeure events, and similar circumstances. Construction of the Civic

to complete the Project or any portion thereof should it decide to proceed with all or any portion 
of the Project.

The Project will include a total of approximately 553,000 sf of development. The building fronting on Boylston 
Street will include 498,000 sf of office and R&D space, approximately 17,000 sf of engaging ground floor retail 
and/or restaurant space, and approximately 33,000 sf of loading/BOH space. An approximately 5,000 sf civic 
building is proposed, which will be programmed in response to community needs and could serve as a Boston 
Public Library neighborhood branch. The project will also include below grade parking to support approximately 
174 net new spaces. Additionally, approximately 1/2 acre of new open space along Park Drive will be created. The 
site is located in the Fenway neighborhood, which includes a mix of retail, office, research and development, and 
residential space. 
The Project proposed numerous public benefits, including: a new publicly accessible open space; spending up to 
$12 million on the the design and construction of a new civic building; protected bike lanes and pedestrian 
pathways; new street trees along Boylston Street and Park Drive; as well as other improvements on Park Drive, 
Boylston Street and Brookline Avenue; leveraging the Project to construct additional new housing opportunities in 
the Fenway neighborhood, including over $18 million to an off-site residential project in the neighborhood and 
$1.3 million to the Fenway Community Development Corporation; dedicating to diversity, equity, and inclusion; 
committing to a life science workforce development initiative in coordination with the BPDA; designing an energy 
efficient building that minimizes carbon emissions; contributing to linkage funds; and creating new jobs.
At the study area intersections, the vehicle operation will be similar from the No-Build to the Build condition, 
indicating that the Project will have a minimal impact on traffic operations in the area. Including the future Green 
Line capacity improvements, the additional trips are not expected to impact transit operations in the area. Secure 
bicycle storage for tenants and visitors will be provided within the Project. The Proponent will improve the 
pedestrian environment by reconstructing the existing public sidewalks adjacent to the Project Site and providing 
a new open space on Park Drive. Loading will be included within the building and access from Kilmarnock St. The 
Proponent is committed to implementing Transportation Demand Management measures to minimize 
automobile usage and Project related traffic impacts.

The Project is designed to minimize impacts in the surrounding neighborhood. The building massing will include 
numerous stepbacks that seek to protect daylight and minimize shadows on the surrounding area. The daylight 
analysis shows that the development will result in daylight impacts similar to the surrounding area. The Project will 
comply with the appropriate City noise regulations. There are no anticipated adverse air quality impacts resulting 
from increased traffic from the Project. The results of the wind study show that the pedestrian level wind 
conditions are expected to be similar to the existing conditions and appropriate for the uses on and around the 
Project Site.
The Project proposes a net zero carbon design that minimizes fossil fuel use on-site, plans for full electrification in 
the future, and promotes the City’s carbon neutral goals. The Project is anticipated to be Gold Certifiable under 
the Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design rating system, highlighting the Project team's efforts to 
reduce the Project's impact on the environment. The Project is proposed to include a new publicly accessible 
open space along with landscaping and trees to minimize the heat island effect and, along with stormwater 
management techniques, encourage stormwater capture and infiltration. The design will include water 
conservation fixtures to minimize water use.

The design of the Project embodies several key urban design principles specific to the Fenway neighborhood and 
the Site, including: 
• Redeveloping an underutilized site to define and strengthen the western gateway into the Fenway; 
• Creating meaningful publicly accessible open space of approximately one-half acre and new Civic Building; 
• Respecting the rhythms of the established neighborhood and the Olmsted Park System; 
• Activating of Boylston Street with engaging ground floor uses; 
• Scaling the Project’s massing down from Boylston Street to the Olmsted Park System; 
• Shaping the buildings to avoid shadow impacts on Ramler Park and the Muddy River; and 
• Enclosing building services and loading operations within the building and eliminating the existing service access.
Although there are no historic or archaeological resources on the Site, the Project has been designed to 
recognize the importance of adjacent historic areas, in particular the Olmsted Park System, Back Bay Fens, and the 
Emerald Necklace. Further, the Project will include protected bicycle lanes to further connect the neighborhood to 
these parks and will also add a new publicly accessible open space that further expands upon the greenery of the 
Olmsted Park System. 
The Project will result in the replacement of a surface parking and older buildings with new landscaped 
streetscapes and new buildings with a modern stormwater management system and water conservation fixtures. 
The Project will take advantage of the existing utility infrastructure in the surrounding area, while minimizing water 
use and wastewater generation. The stormwater management system will capture and infiltrate stormwater, as 
well as substantially improve the stormwater quality of the runoff leaving the Site.

PUBLIC NOTICE 
The Boston Redevelopment Authority (“BRA”), d/b/a the Boston Planning & Development Agency 
("BPDA"), hereby gives notice pursuant to Section 3-1A and Article 80 of the Boston Zoning Code 
(“Code”), that on December 14, 2023, the BPDA received a Proposed Planned Development Area 
(“PDA”) development Plan approval (the “PDA Development Plan”) from Samuels & Associates 
Development LLC (the “Proponent”) for a site located at 1400 Boylston Street (the “Project Site”) 
in the Fenway neighborhood of Boston. 
The Project as described in the PDA Development Plan will include a new approximately 553,000 
square foot mixed-use building, including approximately 498,000 square feet of office and 
research and development uses, together with retail, restaurant, below-grade parking, service and 
accessory uses. The Proposed Project will also include a Civic Building which will be programmed in 
response to community needs and could serve as a Boston Public Library neighborhood branch, as 
well as new publicly accessible open space. 
The Proponent is requesting the BPDA’s approval of the PDA Development Plan pursuant to 
Article 80 and Section 3-1A of the Code. The BPDA’s approval would authorize the Director of 
the BPDA to petition the Boston Zoning Commission to approve the PDA Development Plan and 
an associated amendment to Map 1Q, Fenway Neighborhood District. 
The PDA Development Plan may be obtained from the BPDA website at the following link: 
http://www.bostonplans.org/projects/development-projects/1400-boylston-street 
Public comments on the PDA Development Plan, including the comments of public agencies, 
should be submitted in writing to Quinn Valcich, BPDA by email to quinn.w.valcich@Boston.gov 
within forty-five days of the publication of this notice. 
In accordance with the BPDA's Language Access Policy, all vital project documents will be 
translated into Mandarin and Cantonese and will be available for review on the project 
webpage on the BPDA's website. Both Mandarin and Cantonese interpretation will be offered 
for all Article 80 Public Meetings. Should you require translation of vital project documents or 
interpretation of project Public Meetings in a language other than Mandarin or Cantonese, 
please submit your request to Quinn Valcich at quinn.w.valcich@boston.gov with a minimum of 
14 days notice.

1. 
Development Plan: Pursuant to Section 3-1A.a and Article 80C of the Boston 
Zoning Code (the “Code”), this plan constitutes the Planned Development Area Development 
Plan (the “Development Plan”) for a Planned Development Area Overlay District (the “PDA 
Overlay District”) containing approximately 135,716 square feet (3.11 acres) commonly referred 
to as 155 North Beacon Street in the Brighton neighborhood (the “Site”). The Site is more 
particularly described in Section 3, below, and in Exhibits A & B attached hereto. The 
Proponent (as defined below) proposes to construct a campus consisting of three new connected 
commercial buildings at the Site containing office, research and development, and related uses at 
the Site (the “Project”). Collectively, the Site and the Project make up the “Planned Development 
Area” or “PDA” for which this Development Plan will constitute and provide the permanent 
zoning. 
 
This Development Plan sets forth the proposed location and appearance of structures, 
open spaces, uses, densities and dimensions of structures, traffic circulation, parking and loading 
facilities, and other requirements applicable to the PDA. Capitalized terms used but not defined 
herein shall have the meanings assigned to such terms in the Code as in effect as of the date 
hereof, without giving effect to any subsequent amendments to the Code. 
 
This Development Plan consists of [___] pages of text plus attachments designated 
Exhibits A through F. All references to this Development Plan contained herein shall pertain 
only to such pages and exhibits. This Development Plan shall constitute permanent zoning for 
the Site in accordance with Section 3-1A and Article 80C of the Code and is intended to address 
all requirements of the Code applicable to the Site and the Project. 
 
2. 
The Proponent: The Proponent of the Project is IQHQ-155 Beacon, LLC, an 
IQHQ entity (together with its successors and assigns, “Proponent”). 
 
The business address and telephone number for the Proponent is:

3. 
PDA Site: The PDA Site totals approximately 135,716 square feet (3.11 acres), 
and is bounded to the north by the 6-level Guest Street Parking Garage, to the east by Life Street 
and iStorage Self Storage facility, to the south by North Beacon Street and 3-story residential 
apartments, and to the west by the WGBH Headquarters. The Site is currently improved by a two 
story, approximately 199,316 square-foot industrial-type brick building used for commercial 
uses, which will be demolished. 
 
 
The PDA Site is located in the Allston/Brighton Neighborhood District and the Guest 
Street Local Industrial-2 zoning subdistrict. 
 
 
4. 
The Buildings: The Proponent proposes the development of a new life science 
campus to include three connected and sustainably designed (R&D)/office buildings, totaling 
approximately 412,649 square feet of gross floor area (“GFA”), including (i) a 4-6 story 
approximately 186,533 sf GFA building (“Building 1”), (ii) a 6 story approximately 169,142 sf 
GFA building (“Building 2”), and (iii) a 3 story approximately 56,974 sf GFA building 
(“Building 3”, and together with Building 1 and Building 2, the “Buildings”), as well as a two-
level structured below-grade parking facility accommodating off-street parking for 
approximately 324 vehicles. 
 
 
5. 
Proposed Locations and Appearance of Buildings 1-3: Selected elevations 
attached hereto as Exhibit C illustrate each new Buildings’ general appearance. The new 
connected Buildings are sited along North Beacon Street, the Service Alley, and Life Street so 
that they create two new public plazas, one at the center of the Site, and one along Life Street. In 
addition, Buildings 1 and 3, which are along North Beacon Street and across the street from 
residential buildings, start with lower massing along North Beacon Street so that the main height 
and massing are set away from these lower residential buildings, and their main massing is set to 
north to be consistent with the larger commercial buildings near that portion of the Site. 
 
 
 
6. 
Proposed Density and Dimensions of Structures: The specific height (as 
defined in the Zoning Code) for any building within the Site will be calculated from the average 
mean grade as defined in the Zoning Code, but, notwithstanding the definition of Building 
Height in Article 2A of the Code, no rooftop mechanicals or penthouses or other structures set 
atop or projecting from a rooftop shall be counted towards the overall zoning height of that 
building (“Zoning Height”). The maximum Zoning Height of any building within the Site shall 
be 92 feet. The maximum height of mechanical screening or penthouses on top of the buildings 
shall not be considered in determining the maximum building Zoning Height. Notwithstanding 
the foregoing, for commercial buildings, the mechanical penthouse or mechanical screen shall 
not exceed 45 feet in height, and up to 55 feet inclusive of rooftop exhaust related mechanical 
elements, such as, flues and exhaust vents that may extend above the mechanical screen to an 
extent not to exceed 10 feet; the heights of the mechanical screen, penthouse or elements shall be 
measured from the top of the flat roof of the building at its Zoning Height to the highest point of 
the mechanical screen, penthouse, or element. 
 

 
 
The new Buildings will contain up to a total of approximately 412,649 square feet of GFA1, 
which results in an FAR of up to 3.1 across the full PDA Site. See Exhibit D for massing 
diagram. The maximum Building Height, FAR and GFA set out above will be the only 
dimensional requirements applicable to the PDA Site. All other dimensional or design 
requirements of the Code shall not be applicable to the PDA Site and are superseded by this 
Development Plan. The Project shall be subject to design, environmental and other development 
review by the BPDA, and aspects of the Project approved as part of such review shall be and 
hereby are deemed to be the dimensional and design requirements applicable to the new 
Buildings and are hereby incorporated in this Development Plan. 
 
 
7. 
Proposed Open Space and Landscaping: The Project will revitalize the Site, 
which is currently almost completely covered by the existing building or asphalt. The Project 
will create approximately 30,500 square feet of new publicly accessible open space, spread 
between a central courtyard located between Buildings 1, 2, and 3, and with an additional open 
plaza area along Life Street. These publicly accessible open spaces, coupled with public access 
through the public ground floor amenity space between Building’s 2 & 3, will help to activate 
the courtyard and eastern portions of the Site. In addition, the public realm area along North 
Beacon Street will be improved with increased sidewalk width for pedestrians, and added street 
trees (in addition to those present which are planned to be retained) for greenery and shade. See 
Exhibit E for areas of open space as shown and defined. 
 
 
8. 
Proposed Uses: The New Building will be used primarily for office, laboratory, 
research and development, and parking facilities (as accessory, ancillary, and principal uses). In 
addition to the uses listed above, all of the uses listed in Exhibit F shall be permitted as of right 
on the PDA Site. 
 
 
9. 
Proposed Traffic Circulation: The Site is currently accessed from wide curb 
cuts on North Beacon Street and Life Street, and the Site will continue to be accessed from the 
southwestern corner of the Site along North Beacon Street and the northeastern corner of the Site 
along Life Street through portions of these existing curb cuts. 
 
 
10. 
Proposed Parking and Loading Facilities: The Project will include two levels 
of below-grade parking for approximately 324 vehicles. All loading and service activity will be 
actively managed by the building transportation coordinator, and the Project will provide both 
secure bicycle parking spaces and publicly accessible bicycle parking spaces. 
 
 
11. 
Access to Public Transportation: The Site located near the Massachusetts Bay 
Transportation Authority (MBTA) Boston Landing Station which provides access to the 
Framingham/Worcester commuter rail, and is also located along the Route 57, Route 64, Route 
66, and Route 86 MBTA bus routes.

12. 
Signage: The signage program for the Buildings shall be subject to design, 
environmental and other development review by the BPDA, and any sign approved as part of 
such review shall be deemed to be in compliance with the Development Plan. 
 
 
13. 
Development Review Procedures: All aspects of the Buildings’ design will be 
subject to ongoing development and design review and approval by the BPDA. 
 
 
14.

energy-efficient HVAC and lighting equipment and systems and will incorporate other potential 
energy conservation measures, as reasonable and feasible. 
 
 
15.

neighborhood and to the City of Boston, including the creation of job opportunities and training, 
significant landscaping improvements around the Site, and the generation of additional tax 
revenues:

existing building, which has a monolithic floorplate that does not allow for open 
or landscaped areas, with a dynamic set of three buildings that allows for publicly 
accessible open spaces and a more generous streetscape that will visually activate 
and enliven the Site. The Project will also expand and enhance the public realm 
on Life Street with the realignment of Life Street pursuant to the 2012 Brighton 
Guest Street Area Planning Study, as coordinated with BTD.

Development Plan. Pursuant to Section 3-1A(a), Sections 51-44 through 51-49, 
and Article 80C of the Boston Zoning Code (the “Code”), this plan constitutes the Planned 
Development Area Development Plan (the “Development Plan”) for the redevelopment of an 
approximately 1.2-acre (+/-50,277-square-foot) site known and numbered as 176-182 Western 
Avenue, Allston, Boston, Massachusetts (the “Project Site”), as described in Exhibit A-1 hereto 
and shown on the boundary plan attached hereto as Exhibit A-2. The Proponent (as defined below) 
proposes to demolish the existing buildings and improvements on the Project Site and construct a 
mixed-use project comprising a building containing, in aggregate, approximately 200,100 square 
feet of Gross Floor Area (as defined in Article 2A of the Code as of the date of this Development 
Plan, “GFA”), including residential uses (up to 280 rental units), ground-floor retail, restaurant, 
service, shared amenity and accessory uses, parking uses, as well as outdoor amenity space and 
pedestrian realm improvements, as more fully described below (the “Project”). 
This Development Plan consists of seven (7) pages of text plus attachments designated 
Exhibits A-1 through G, which together establish the proposed: (i) location and appearance of the 
Project; (ii) uses; (iii) densities and dimensions of the Project; (iv) open spaces and landscaping; 
(v) traffic circulation; (vi) parking and loading facilities; (vii) access to public transportation; and 
(viii) public benefits with regard to the Project. All references to this Development Plan contained 
herein shall pertain only to such pages and exhibits. 
This Development Plan constitutes permanent zoning for the Project Site in accordance 
with Section 3-lA and Article 80C of the Code, and it shall not expire or lapse for any reason. In 
accordance with Section 80C-9 of the Code, consistency of the Project with this Development 
Plan, which shall be evidenced by a Certification of Consistency issued by the Boston 
Redevelopment Authority, d/b/a Boston Planning & Development Agency (the “BPDA”) pursuant 
to Section 80C-8 of the Code (a “Certification of Consistency”), constitutes compliance with the 
requirements of the underlying zoning in effect as of the date this Development Plan is approved 
to the extent that such requirements are addressed in this Development Plan. To the extent that any 
aspect of the Project or this Development Plan is in conflict with any requirement of the Code not 
specifically addressed in this Development Plan, such requirement(s) shall be deemed to be waived 
upon approval of this Development Plan. 
Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings assigned to such 
terms in Article 2A of the Code as in effect as of the date this Development Plan is approved, 
without giving effect to any subsequent amendments to the Code.

3. 
Project Site. The Project Site consists of approximately 1.2 acres (+/- 50,277 
square feet) of land bounded generally by Western Avenue to the north, Bertram Street to the south, 
North Harvard Street to the west, and Travis Street to the east. The Site comprises four parcels, 
two located at 176-182 Western Avenue, currently containing multiple surface parking lots, a 
vacant one-story commercial building, and a vacant three-story residential building. A third parcel 
located at 9 Travis Street contains a vacant single-story commercial building and surface parking, 
and the fourth parcel, located at 204-206 North Harvard, contains a vacant one-story commercial 
structure and surface parking. 
The Project Site is located within the Barry’s Corner Community Commercial Subdistrict 
of the Allston/Brighton Neighborhood District (the “BCCC Subdistrict”), carrying a designation 
of “Barry’s Corner CC-1” on Zoning Map 7B/7D, Allston/Brighton Neighborhood District, 
effective as of October 26, 2021. Pursuant to Section 51-44 of the Code, Planned Development 
Areas are permitted within the BCCC Subdistrict. This Plan establishes a Planned Development 
Area Overlay District consistent with the boundaries of the Project Site. 
4. 
Project. The Proponent proposes to demolish the existing buildings on the Project 
Site, and to construct a pedestrian-oriented, mixed-use building including residential uses, ground-
floor retail, restaurant, and service uses, parking and loading uses and other uses described herein. 
As shown on the site plan attached hereto as Exhibit B (the “Site Plan”), the Project comprises an 
approximately seven-story building, containing approximately 200,00 square feet of GFA, 
including residential space (up to 280 units), ground-floor retail, restaurant, services and accessory 
spaces, shared amenity space, and approximately 10,000 square feet of outdoor amenity spaces 
located on various roof terraces, served by a structured parking garage as described in more detail 
below. The retail component of the Project will be located along Western Avenue and North 
Harvard Street, wrapping around the structured parking. The Project will also include enclosed 
secure bike storage areas for residents and employees of the Project, as well as publicly accessible 
short-term bicycle parking spaces and new on-street parking spaces, all of which is described in 
more detail in Section 10 below. The Project will create approximately 11,000 square feet of new 
sidewalk area and active café zone along the Project Site frontage, along with new landscaping 
and hardscaped public spaces and additional amenities.

required pursuant to Section 51-44 of the Code, the Project is consistent with the urban planning 
and design initiatives set forth in the Western Avenue Corridor Study and Rezoning (“WACRZ 
Study”), which study commenced at approximately the same time that the Project was preparing 
to initiate review under Article 80 of the Code. The WACRZ Study, along with corresponding text 
and map amendments to the Code, was approved by the BPDA’s Board of Directors (the “BPDA 
Board”) on October 13, 2022, and corresponding zoning amendments were approved by the 
Boston Zoning Commission on November 9, 2022. Further, as required by Section 51-45 of the 
Code, the Project is consistent with “Table 1: Use and Dimensional Standards” of the WACRZ 
Study.

Proposed Densities and Dimensions; Other Bulk and Dimensional Controls. 
The Project, as described above and shown on the Site Plan, consists of a mixed-used 
residential building, subject to the following bulk and dimensional controls: (i) a maximum Floor 
Area Ratio of 4.0; (ii) a maximum Lot Coverage of 80%; (iii) a maximum Building Height of 90 
feet; and (iv) a minimum 10-foot setback along Western Avenue. These are the only bulk and 
dimensional controls applicable to the Project. 
As used herein: (1) “Building Height” shall mean “the vertical distance from grade to the 
top of the highest point of the roof beams of a flat roof, or the mean level of the highest gable or 
of the slope of a hip roof, excluding belfries, cupolas, domes, monuments, church spires, water, 
observation, radio and transmission towers, windmills, chimneys, smokestacks, silos, derricks, 
conveyors, masts, flagpoles, aerials, elevator penthouses, water tanks, monitors, signs, solar PV 
improvements or other roof structures and penthouses normally built above the roof and not used 
or designed to be used for human occupancy”. For the purposes of this Development Plan, grade, 
as calculated in accordance with the Code, is calculated as approximately 18 feet (Boston City 
Base). (2) “Floor Area Ratio” shall have the meaning set forth in Article 2A of the Code as of the 
date of this Development Plan, provided that floor area dedicated to parking and loading uses do 
not count towards the calculation of Floor Area Ratio. (3) “Lot Coverage” shall mean the total 
building footprint divided by the total area of the lot. For the purposes of calculating Floor Area 
Ratio and Lot Coverage, the term “total area of the lot” shall mean 50,277 square feet, which 
measurement is inclusive of areas that will be devoted to public realm improvements on the Project 
Site.

for use by tenants and their employees, residents, guests and other visitors to the Project, as 
generally set forth on Exhibit E to this Development Plan. The Project incorporates roof terrace 
amenity green spaces on various levels that total approximately 10,000 square feet for use by 
Project residents, including a planted area to assist with drainage/stormwater management and 
mitigate urban heat island effect. Further, the Project is set back from the property line in order to

Proposed Traffic Circulation; Parking and Loading Facilities. The Project will 
provide adequate access and traffic circulation in accordance with city standards, as generally 
shown on Exhibit F to this Development Plan. As described above, the Project features off-street 
parking spaces interior to the Project Site at a maximum parking ratio at or below that established 
pursuant to the City of Boston Transportation Department’s (“BTD”) Bike Parking Guidelines, 
Version 2.0 (January 2020) (the “BTD Guidelines”). The project is currently anticipated to provide 
parking at a ratio of .23 spaces per residential unit, however this ratio is subject to further 
adjustment in consultation with BTD and the final parking ratio required for the project shall be 
established in the Transportation Access Plan Agreement (“TAPA”) executed by the Proponent 
and BTD with respect to the Project. The interior parking will provide direct, secure access to the 
Project and will streamline vehicular circulation, with all passenger vehicles entering and exiting 
the parking structure through an entry/exit on Travis Street. The Project will also provide 
approximately one long-term bicycle space per residential unit, plus an additional approximately 
one long-term bicycle space per 3,000 square feet of retail GFA, within the Project, which spaces 
will be indoor, secure and reserved for employees and residents of the Project. In addition to the 
dedicated off-street parking and bike storage, the Project will provide (i) approximately nine on-

interior and exterior public spaces through art. A minimum of 25%

I. 
The PDA Master Plan 
On August 10, 2006 the Boston Redevelopment Authority d/b/a the Boston Planning & 
Development Agency (the “Authority” or the “BPDA”) originally approved and on January 10, 
2007 the Boston Zoning Commission (the “Zoning Commission”) adopted a Planned 
Development Area Master Plan for The 100 Acres, defined and described in further detail in a 
document entitled “Master Plan for Planned Development Area No. 69, South Boston/The 100 
Acres, Boston,” which plan has been amended five times since it was first adopted, by that 
certain First Amendment dated as of June 12, 2012, that certain Second Amendment dated as of 
December 24, 2012, that certain Third Amendment dated as of November 1, 2016, that certain 
Fourth Amendment dated as of February 8, 2018, and that certain Fifth Amendment dated as of 
October 21, 2020, and which is proposed to be further amended with a Sixth Amendment to 
Master Plan for Planned Development Area No. 69 (the “Sixth Amendment”) filed 
simultaneously herewith as was the case in prior amendments to the PDA Master Plan (as 

 
2 
amended through and including the Sixth Amendment, the “PDA Master Plan” or “PDA No. 69” 
for the purposes of this Development Plan). 
The “100 Acres” planning area to which the PDA Master Plan is applicable is a 47-acre 
parcel bounded generally by the Fort Point Channel and A Street to the west, Summer Street to 
the north, the South Boston Bypass Road/Haul Road to the east, and West First Street and Mount 
Washington Avenue to the south. By its own terms, PDA No. 69 “sets forth a statement of the 
development concept” for proposed new development within the so-called “100 Acres” planning 
area, “including, inter alia, the planning objectives and character of the development, the 
proposed uses of the area, the range of dimensional requirements contemplated for each of the 
proposed uses, and the proposed phasing of construction of the development”, and … “provides 
for one or more PDA Development Plans … to be submitted providing more specific information 
about various Proposed Project and components thereof.” The PDA Master Plan further 
envisions the 100 Acres planning area as “a dense, varied, and lively urban district”. This 
Development Plan and corresponding Sixth Amendment, filed as before to effect conforming 
amendments to the PDA Master Plan consistent therewith, once approved by the Zoning 
Commission, will effectuate the zoning and land use controls to enable the conversion of a 
surface parking lot to a lively urban district as described conceptually in the PDA Master Plan, 
and deliver significant other benefits beyond those previously contemplated. 
II.

This Development Plan: (a) is applicable to the Project Site, consisting of Parcels G4, G5, 
G6, FT1, HW3 and portions of Parcels HW4 and FT2; and (b) sets forth the proposed location 
and appearance of structures, civic spaces, open spaces, public parks and landscaping, uses, 
densities and dimensions of structures, traffic circulation, bicycle access, parking and loading 
facilities, and other zoning requirements applicable to the approximately 1,098,292 gross square 
feet (as that term is defined in the Code) of development in three new buildings with below-
grade parking, as well as new streets, improvements to the Harborwalk, and extensive new 
public open space, including two new proposed public parks (the “Project”), all as more fully 
described below. Uses in the Project will consist of “residential/commercial mixed use” and 
“industrial/commercial mixed-use” (as such terms are described in the PDA Master Plan), 
including, without limitation, residential, office, research & development (including life sciences 
and laboratory), and other mixed-use space, including but not limited to retail, gallery, restaurant

sets forth information on the Project including the proposed location and appearance of 
structures, open spaces and landscaping, densities, proposed traffic circulation, parking and 
loading facilities, access to public transportation, as well as the dimensional, use and other 
zoning applicable to the Project. Furthermore, in accordance with the applicable provisions of 
the Code, including Section 80C, the Development Plan herein addresses the applicable 
underlying zoning requirements, including without limitation, the PDA Master Plan. The Project 
has undergone Article 80B Large Project Review consistent with the review and approval of this 
Development Plan.

V. 
Project Site Description/Project Area 
The Project will be developed on the Project Site as described above, an approximately 
6.46-acre site located at 244-284 A Street, along the Fort Point Channel in the Fort Point 
Channel neighborhood of South Boston as depicted on Exhibit A and described in Exhibit B 
hereto. The Project Site is also located within so-called Commonwealth Tidelands, the 
development and use of which are subject to licensing and use requirements set forth in M.G.L. 
c. 91 and the regulations promulgated thereunder set forth at 310 CMR 9.00 et seq. (“Chapter 
91”). The Project Site is within the “2009 South Boston Municipal Harbor Plan Amendment” 
(“MHPA”) to the South Boston Waterfront District Municipal Harbor Plan submitted by the City 
and the BPDA and approved by the Secretary of Energy and Environmental Affairs (“EOEEA”.) 
The Project Site will also host a portion of the City of Boston’s planned resiliency Berm along 
the Fort Point Channel waterfront, which Berm will provide a benefit to immediate abutters and 
the larger South Boston neighborhood. 
Significant public infrastructure is also located within the Project Site. The subsurface of 
the Project Site contains a portion of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts Department of 
Transportation (“MassDOT”) Central Artery I-90 Tunnel (the “I-90 Tunnel”). MassDOT has 
recently undertaken repairs to the infrastructure located beneath the surface of the Project Site, 
including much needed repairs to the so-called “Super Plug” to ensure the safety and stability of 
the I-90 Tunnel, and requires the ability to access the so-called “Super Plug” in the future. Water, 

 
5 
sewer and stormwater infrastructure owned by the Boston Water & Sewer Commission 
(“BWSC”) is also located within the Project Site. This infrastructure includes stormwater outfall 
and flood protection facilities, including a BWSC owned and maintained outfall (the “Outfall”) 
which connects to the Fort Point Channel and allows for the decanting of stormwater runoff from 
the surrounding neighborhood so as to diminish the risk of flooding. BWSC has the right to 
maintain its Outfall into the Fort Point Channel immediately adjacent to Parcel HW3 and may 
require access to the surface and subsurface of the Project Site as required to maintain its 
infrastructure. The public infrastructure beneath the Project Site is more particularly shown on 
Exhibit D. 
According to Zoning Map 4, the Project Site is located within the: (i) Groundwater 
Conservation Protection Overlay District (“GCOD”) subject to the requirements set forth in 
Article 28 of the Code; (ii) the Restricted Parking Overlay District (“RPOD”) subject to the 
requirements set forth in Section 3-1A.c of the Code; (iii) the Flood Hazard District subject to 
the requirements set forth in Article 25 of the Code; and (iv) the Coastal Flood Resilience 
Overlay District (“CFROD”) subject to the requirements set forth in Article 25A of the Code. 
The Project Site is located adjacent to but outside of the Fort Point Channel Landmark District. 
The “underlying zoning” for the Project Site, to the extent that the PDA No. 69 was not in effect, 
would place the Project Site within the M-2 Restricted Manufacturing District and the overlay 
districts identified in this paragraph (GCOD, RPOD, Flood Hazard District, and CFROD). 
The Project Site is entirely located within Zone AE, an area within the one percent (1%) 
annual chance flood, as shown on the Federal Emergency Management Agency Flood Insurance 
Rate Map for the City of Boston, Suffolk County, Massachusetts, Map Number 25025C0081J 
having an effective date of March 16, 2016 and the CFROD as described above. Given the 
location of the Project Site within the Flood Zone and the CFROD, the development of the 
Project has been designed to comply with the existing requirements of the Code pertaining to 
such areas, including those set forth in Article 25A of the Code which describes those 
requirements applicable within the CFROD. The Project will not impact any historic resources in 
the areas. The Project Site does not include any structure, site, or building listed or potentially 
eligible for listing on the National Register of Historic Places or Commonwealth of 
Massachusetts Register of Historic Places. The Fort Point Channel Sea Wall is immediately 
adjacent to the Project Site and the Project Site is located in close proximity to the Fort Point 
Channel Landmark District as established by the City of Boston Landmarks Commission in 2008 
and the Fort Point Channel National Register Historic District. As there are no existing structures 
on the Project Site, review of any anticipated demolition in accordance with the provisions of 
Article 85 of the Code will not be required.

Harborwalk: The Project will include improvements to the existing Harborwalk along 
the Fort Point Channel, including new pathways, accessible ramps, and landscaping. The 
width of the Harborwalk will be maintained, and the grade of the Harborwalk will be 
raised to an elevation which places the Harborwalk above the projected future tidal cycles 
while still providing a proximity to the Fort Point Channel and connection to the Fort 
Point Channel Watersheet. 
Berm: The Project will also include the creation of the Berm, which will be a part of a 
larger resiliency measure that is anticipated to prevent flooding related to sea level rise 
and storm surge and contribute to flood protection in the immediate neighborhood and 
larger South Boston. The Berm will be an integral part of the Fort Point Channel Park 
and provide increased access to open space and a design which minimizes any visual or 
physical obstruction, providing a seamless connection from the Fort Point Channel to the 
new public parks and public realm improvements to be constructed on the Project Site 
and beyond into the larger community. 
Binford Street Open Space: On the southwest corner of and just outside of the Project 
Site, a new connection is proposed from the Harborwalk and Binford Street Park to 
Necco Street (“Binford Open Space”). This pathway, along with a dedicated cycle track 
on Necco Street to the northern edge of Necco Street Park, will be a part of the South Bay 
Harbor Trail. 
Wormwood Extension: The Project will also include a pedestrian connection from Necco 
Street to A Street along the southern edge of the Necco Street Park. The promenade will 
be designed and maintained as a clear and primary public pedestrian link between A 
Street and the Fort Point Channel/Harborwalk, and may include programing elements to 
foster activation, including food trucks or temporary markets. 

 
9 
Streetscape, Pedestrian and Bicycle Improvements: The Project will include 
improvements along streets adjacent to and through the Project Site in compliance with 
Boston Complete Streets guidelines in a manner which prioritize the pedestrian 
experience. As part of the Project, Parcel 3 and Parcel 4 shown on the plan at Exhibit F-1, 
more particularly described in Exhibit F-6, and containing approximately 11,205 SF and 
1,297 SF respectively, will be dedicated through an easement or fee transfer to the City of 
Boston, acting by and through its Public Works Department, for right of way 
improvements and the Proponent will construct Necco Street Extension, shown as Parcel 
5 on the plan at Exhibit F-1 and more particularly described in Exhibit F-7. The design of 
the Streetscape improvements will be multimodal for pedestrian, bicyclists, transit users 
and motor vehicle drivers, and will include new sidewalks, street trees, bicycle lanes, and 
other landscaping. The Project will also include pedestrian and bicycle pathways, plazas, 
and landscaped open space. The Project includes a new connection from the Harborwalk 
to Necco Street in the northwest corner of the Project Site at Fort Point Channel Park, 
providing a connection for pedestrians and bicyclist to Necco Street Park. These 
pedestrian and bicycle connections will foster greater connectivity between the 
community and waterfront, and also provide more opportunities to activate the 
Harborwalk with pedestrian foot traffic and seasonal activities. The amount of new public 
open space will exceed the requirements of PDA No. 69 and Chapter 91. 
Civic/Cultural Space and Public Art: The inclusion of public art and approximately 
15,000 SF of base rent-free Civic/Cultural space throughout the ground floors of the 
Project represent an effort to create a strong connection between the Project and the 
existing fabric of the neighborhood. Various elements of public art dispersed throughout 
the Project Site, including within the publicly-accessible interior spaces, will establish a 
welcoming atmosphere to all community members, while offering opportunities for local 
artists and organizations to display their work. The Proponent’s goal for this public art is 
that at least twenty-five (25) percent of the artists be minority or women artists. This 
comprehensive public art program will be funded by the Proponent and include 
permanent sculptures, rotating art, curated/temporary art, urban infrastructure art, street 
furniture and performing art in collaboration with the Mayor’s Office of Arts and Culture. 
All of these measures will be subject to further review and refinement during the course 
of Chapter 91 Licensing and continued BPDA and Mayor’s Office of Arts and Culture 
review. 
These Public Realm Enhancements, along with retail, restaurant, publicly accessible 
commercial, cultural and civic spaces in the ground floors of the Project Components will afford 
facilities of public accommodation with a mix of uses, will bring vitality to the Project Site and 
enhance the vibrant Fort Point neighborhood. 
The final square footages devoted to each of the uses within the Project Components on 
the Project Site will vary depending on market conditions from time to time, but will include 
only uses permitted under the Development Plan and PDA Master Plan. Consistent with the 
requirements of the PDA Master Plan, the sole dimensional regulations applicable to the Project 
are those of building height and floor area ratio (“FAR”), and the building height and FAR of the 
Project shall not exceed those that are permitted under the Development Plan and PDA Master 
Plan. Consistent with Section XX of this Development Plan, the Project and each Project

Component shall be subject to approval by the BPDA in accordance with its Development

refined so as to: minimize shadows on open space; reflect new engineering data which enables

community. The proposed elevation of approximately 21.5 feet BCB meets the required Sea 
Level Rise Design Flood Elevation (SLR-DFE) under Article 25A for the Residential Building

Design Flood Elevation (SLR-DFE) under Article 25A for each of the Commercial Mixed-Use

City’s IDP and the Proponent will enter into an Affordable Rental Housing Agreement and

13 
approximately 340 residential units and will deliver 20% of the residential units as on-site

seeking to strike a clear relationship with its immediate surroundings while enhancing the public

commitments to public art and for creating an environment to foster the arts, and the addition of

Master Plan.

been designed to enhance use by the public by allowing for greater activation of the building’s 
ground floor public programs and framing views of the Fort Point Channel. The articulation of 
the northwest corner of the Residential Building, which has multiple corners stepping back to the 
south, opens up views to the Fort Point Channel. The modest increase in building height with 
corresponding decrease in lot coverage have resulted in an enhanced public experience, a more

permeable and open site plan, and reduced full-height frontage along the Harborwalk, while 
ultimately reducing net new shadows when compared to the massing previously described in the 
PDA Master Plan.

Authority in connection with the review and approval of the Project under Article 80B of the 
Code. The wind studies indicated that pedestrian-level winds attributable to the proposed heights

its adjacent watersheet. The Project team has designed and will implement wind-mitigating 
canopies and landscape screening solutions at areas to address original conditions categorized as 
‘Uncomfortable.’ The Project team will continue to evaluate pedestrian-level wind conditions as 
the design advances. The Project Site will remain comfortable at the pedestrian level, with some 
areas experiencing improved wind conditions due to the Project. Shadow impacts have been 
minimized to the extent practicable to avoid noticeable pedestrian impacts and are in compliance 
with the specific requirements of the BPDA’s requirements under Article 80B Review and the

constitute compliance with all applicable wind and shadow requirements, including, without 
limitation, those set forth in the Code and those pursuant to which the Authority is the permit

The Project has been designed to maximize the connection between the interior ground 
floor spaces of public accommodation and the exterior outdoor public realm, taking great care to 
activate the frontages with publicly accessible space. The Proponent has committed to providing 
approximately 15,000 SF of base-rent free Civic/Cultural space on the ground floor level of the 
Project, the use and programming of which will be subject to further clarification during the 
course of the Chapter 91 Licensing in collaboration with the BPDA Design Review processes

schedule/process aimed at meeting the evolving needs of the local creative economy, and further

In terms of programming, the Project team has taken great care to activate the frontages 
of each building with publicly accessible space and to support watersheet and parks activation. 
The Proponent envisions a variety of watersheet activation opportunities at and adjacent to the 
Project Site to provide the public an opportunity to access the water and support a wide variety 
of recreational small boat activities as well as other cultural and artistic programming. To

access for people who have been excluded in the past, the Proponent recognizes the need for

overlook and dock on the watersheet to provide a secondary stage for the amphitheater to be

with stakeholders including the BPDA, adjacent landowners, and BWSC.
