XV. 
Proposed Traffic Circulation with Improvements to Pedestrian Access 
As shown on Exhibit H attached hereto, the Project will extend Necco Street from its 
current terminus at Garage Access Way (a private driveway) through the Project Site to Binford 
Street, which connects to A Street. Wormwood Extension, a new connection described above 
between Necco Street Extension and A Street, will be dedicated to pedestrians, with the ability to 
support access of emergency vehicles. These extensions of Necco Street and Wormwood Street 
will improve vehicular, pedestrian and bicycle circulation, and will create sidewalks where there 
are none. The Project has also modified certain of the vehicular ways previously shown on the 
PDA Master Plan, removing Channel Street, which would otherwise extend from Binford Street 
toward the Fort Point Channel watersheet in order to strengthen the connection to the Fort Point 
Channel for pedestrians and bicyclists without motorized vehicular traffic. The Proponent also 
proposes to strengthen the connection to the watersheet and create usable, green open space by 
removing portions of Binford Street adjacent to the waterfront and replacing the existing 
roadway with additional greenspace, subject to obtaining all required City approvals for the 
discontinuance of the roadway. The promenade will be designed and maintained as a clear and 
primary public pedestrian link between A Street and the Fort Point Channel/Harborwalk. The 
public’s access to the waterfront and experience along the Harborwalk will be significantly 
enhanced by not having an adjacent vehicular roadway in potential conflict with optimal public 
access. The Sixth Amendment approved simultaneously with the approval of this Development 
Plan will include modifications to Exhibit H, the “Rights-of-Way” Plan to effectuate the 
improvements shown on Exhibit H attached hereto and as described in this section. 
Emergency vehicle access to the Harborwalk and to Gillette’s Pumphouse (accessed 
through a tide gate) will be maintained from the intersection of Binford and Necco streets along a 
slightly widened proposed bike and pedestrian link to the Harborwalk. Access to the MassDOT 
emergency access location for the I-90 tunnel will also be from the Binford and Necco streets 
intersection. 
The Project includes the reconstruction of A Street between Binford Street and Garage 
Access Way to Boston Complete Street standards which will include pedestrian safety 
enhancements through bump outs and daylighting of intersections, protected bicycle lanes, on-
street parking and properly-sized travel lanes. 
XVI. Parking and Loading Facilities 
As allowed under the South Boston Parking Freeze Permit #APCC367669 issued by the 
Boston Air Pollution Control Commission (APPC), the Project Site is currently authorized for 
public “P” parking spaces allowing for parking by the general public for a fee in 814 parking 
spaces. After redevelopment of the Project Site, the existing parking lot will be transformed to 
enable the Project which will provide no more than 415 parking spaces to serve the Project as a 
whole in the Garage. 

 
20 
Loading for the Commercial Mixed-Use and Residential Component will be provided off 
of a dedicated Alleyway from the Necco Street Extension located between Parcel G4 and Parcel 
G5, which Alleyway will provide access for loading operations serving the Residential Building 
and the Commercial Mixed-Use Building. Loading operations serving the Lab/R&D Building 
will be provided off of Binford Street. 
Building upon the strongly transit-oriented nature of the Project’s location, the significant 
commitments to vehicular, pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure improvements that the 
Proponent has designed and in response to local transportation goals, the Project will seek to 
minimize dependence on auto travel and will implement a comprehensive package of 
transportation demand management (“TDM”) strategies to reduce auto trips and parking demand. 
As part of TDM, and management of the Garage in general, the proposed parking supply will 
reflect the limited parking ratios and incorporation of shared parking between residential, 
lab/R&D and commercial uses that is currently being employed at similar urban, mixed-use, 
transit-oriented developments throughout the City of Boston. 
In addition, the Project will include three new on-site bike sharing stations dedicating 
areas within the Project Site and providing funding for such implementation. The Proponent will 
also provide both short-term and long-term bicycle racks within the Project. 
Loading, service and trash removal for each Project Component will take place from 
loading bays in the areas shown on the Project Plans at Exhibit E, as they may be further refined, 
revised, amended and approved pursuant to BPDA or BTD Design Review and other applicable 
agencies and authorities. 
XVII. Signage 
Signage for the Project shall consist of those signs permitted by Article 11 of the Code, 
and any additional signage approved pursuant to BPDA Design Review under its Development 
Review Guidelines as part of a comprehensive sign design for each of the Commercial Mixed-
Use, Residential, Lab/R&D Components. Signage will also be consistent with the requirements 
of the Chapter 91 License(s) for the Project. Signage, both informational and interpretive, will be 
strategically integrated into the Project’s open spaces to assist with wayfinding and to augment 
the overall character/narrative of the Project Site, including signage as required as part of the 
Chapter 91 licensing process and due to the incorporation of elements of the South Bay Harbor 
Trail within the Project Site. 
XVIII. Access to Public Transportation 
The Project Site is well served by existing public transportation, including being in close 
proximity to South Station with immediate access to multiple transportation services, including 
commuter rail, rapid transit, bus service and rail. The Project’s location and design, which 
includes multimodal design for improved access by pedestrian, bicyclists, and transit users, 
including new sidewalks and bicycle lanes, will allow for customers, residents and employees 
living in and around Boston to walk and ride their bikes to the Project.

In addition to the above, the Proponent will implement robust TDM strategies to take full

XIX. Public Benefits from the Project 
The Project will substantially revitalize the Project Site and serve to integrate and connect 
the surrounding Fort Point, South Boston, Dorchester and South End neighborhoods through the 
creation of a vibrant, sustainable, mixed-use and accessible development. The Project will 
deliver numerous public benefits, including considerable urban design, watersheet activation,

affordable housing, resiliency, accessibility and public realm improvements, a mix of new job 
and housing opportunities, and new tax revenues. 
The Project will generate many significant public benefits for the surrounding 
neighborhood and the City as a whole, both during construction and on an ongoing basis upon its 
completion. 
Affordable Housing & Artist Housing: The Proponent is committed to strengthening the 
availability of affordable housing in Boston and will deliver 20% of the residential units 
as on-site affordable housing, well in excess of the 13.0% IDP requirement. In addition, 
the Fort Point neighborhood has long been a hub for artists, some of which have been 
displaced from the community due to lack of affordable housing options. The Proponent 
has incorporated strategies for meeting AFFH goals to address this issue. The Project 
team will work with MOAC, DND and the BPDA to facilitate this commitment. 
New Public Open Space and Parks: The Proponent will plan and construct public open 
spaces on and adjacent to the Project Site which are reflective of the goals and guiding 
principles articulated in the PDA Master Plan as updated by the more recent Fort Point 
100 Acres Open Space Concept Plan to deliver public, vibrant, equitable, accessible, 
resilient and connected open spaces in what is now predominately surface parking, 
including the Necco Street Park, the Fort Point Channel Park and the possible Binford 
Open Space. These “destination parks” will support a mix of uses including a flexible 
space for events, play and gathering, a children’s nature-play area, grills with picnic 
tables, a linear pedestrian walkway/plaza designed to host food trucks or temporary 
markets, a waterfront amphitheater for performing arts, an interactive water feature, 
shade from trees and seating. 
Active, Mixed-Uses and Dedicated Civic and Community Space on the Ground Floor:

restaurants, civic spaces, cultural and educational spaces, retail uses, and lobbies 
consistent with the applicable provisions of Chapter 91. The Project Site will achieve the 
goal of ensuring connectivity between ground-level uses and open space; encouraging 
restaurants from a variety of price points, including affordable; providing other uses that 
attract people to the waterfront; providing year-round public spaces with options that do 
not require payment for participation; providing community uses indoors that extend the 
public realm and remove a sense of privatization; and providing a mix of uses to promote 
a vibrant, equitable and accessible environment. This will all be complemented by the 
new-and-programmed open spaces that will be delivered by the Proponent, including an 
amphitheater for performances and music.

diverse program mix to meet local needs while developing a model for integrated 
resiliency and sustainability. 
The Project will include a section of the Berm, a critical flood defense system, proposed 
by the City for the Fort Point Channel area as part of the City’s Climate Ready Boston

coastal flood risk reduction for the Fort Point Channel and a large portion of the South 
Boston community. The Berm will be integral to the site design to meet the intent of the 
City’s ongoing resiliency efforts and protect existing neighborhoods around the Project 
Site from stormwater surge and projected sea level rise. The design of the Project will 
enhance waterfront access and to provide integration with the Berm. 

 
25 
The Project will significantly improve the existing stormwater management conditions at 
the Project Site from the now-existing surface parking lot by reducing runoff volume 
from the Project Site to the Harbor. The implementation of various measures including (i) 
adding pervious area which will allow for the natural recharge of water to the subgrade, 
reducing runoff volumes to the Harbor outfall, (ii) treating all impervious surface runoff 
with a water quality structure prior to discharging to the Harbor, improving water quality 
of the runoff from the Project Site significantly, (iii) including larger and longer 
stormwater pipe runs, (iv) infiltrating a minimum volume of 1.25-inches of runoff over 
the total Project Site roof area and hardscape areas with subsurface infiltration systems, 
and (v) installing two new backflow preventer structures located within double chamber 
tanks upstream of the existing outfall and tide gate structure, which will provide backup 
protection to the existing structure and prevent seawater from the Harbor from entering 
the closed drainage system in conditions where the tide level is higher than the pipe 
system will achieve this result. 
Sustainable Design/Green Building: The Proponent is committed to building a LEED 
certifiable project, with a target of the Gold level, by incorporating sustainable design 
features into the Project to preserve and protect the environment. The Project will 
incorporate a holistic approach to sustainability, while mitigating the environmental 
impacts of energy, water and material use. The Project will be designed to reduce 
greenhouse gas emissions by incorporating energy-efficient thermal envelopes, 
incorporating mechanical systems that conserve energy, including through efficient 
electrification, energy recovery systems and on-site solar photovoltaics. 
The Project’s design is resilient and will increase the amount of permeable, green spaces 
onsite as compared to the existing surface parking lot condition, and is intended to 
minimize extreme heat. By: (i) introducing the significant amount of open space 
characterized by large portions of landscaped area; (ii) adding stormwater harvesting and 
infiltration systems, and permeable pavers; (iii) expanding planting soil volumes along 
sidewalks and portions of the park plazas to encourage infiltration; (iv) adding rain 
gardens along park edges to increase storage during major storm events; and (v) planting 
locations ‘downstream’ of plazas and sidewalks to reduce and filter runoff, the Project 
will improve upon the current stormwater management condition and reduce stormwater 
rates and volumes that flow into the BWSC storm drainage system.

Channel will be provided as part of the Project, including new pathways, ADA-compliant 
accessible inclines, and landscaping.

may occur to the Project’s design described in this Development Plan without requiring a further 
amendment to either of PDA No. 69 and/or this Development Plan as the case may be. This 
provision is in addition to and not in substitution of the provisions related to reconstruction or 
replacement set forth in Section XXI herein. 
XXIV. Amendment of Development Plan 
Any owner of the Residential Component, the Commercial Mixed-Use Component, the 
Lab/R&D Component or the Garage Component, or any sub-parcel or building within a parcel or 
sub-parcel covered by this Development Plan may seek a further amendment of this 
Development Plan as to such parcel, sub-parcel or building, in accordance with the procedures 
prescribed by the Code without the consent of all other owners of parcels, sub-parcel or building. 
In the event any amendment to this Development Plan proposed by the owner of a parcel, sub-
parcel or building is approved, and such amendment affects the overall compliance of the Project 
with this Development Plan, this Development Plan shall be deemed amended with respect to the 
Project as a whole to the extent necessary for the overall Project to comply with this 
Development Plan. 
XII. 
Schedule 
The Proponent expects to commence development of each of the Project Components in 
2022 with anticipated completion in 2025. The construction of the Project Components is not 
planned to be phased at this time. The fit-out of tenant spaces will proceed as leases are signed. 
This schedule is subject to adjustment as necessary pending completion of BPDA Design 
Review, Chapter 91 Licensing, and the receipt of all applicable permits and approvals required 
for the Project. 
XXV. Proponent’s Obligations to Proceed with Project 
Notwithstanding anything set forth herein to the contrary, under no circumstances shall 
the Proponent be obligated to proceed with all or any portion of the Project or a Project 
Component.

SIXTH AMENDMENT TO MASTER PLAN 
FOR 
PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA NO. 69 
SOUTH BOSTON/THE 100 ACRES 
July 14, 2022 
Pursuant to Section 3-1A and Section 80C-7 of the Zoning Code of the City of Boston, as 
amended (the “Zoning Code”), this amendment constitutes the Sixth Amendment to the Master 
Plan for Planned Development Area No. 69, South Boston/The 100 Acres dated January 10, 
2007, as amended (“Sixth Amendment”). Capitalized terms not defined in this Sixth Amendment 
are as defined in the Zoning Code as of the date hereof. 
1. 
The PDA Master Plan. On August 10, 2006, the Boston Redevelopment 
Authority now d/b/a the Boston Planning & Development Agency (the “Authority” or the 
“BPDA””) approved an amendment to the Boston Zoning Maps to create Planned Development 
Area No. 69, and also approved a Master Plan for Planned Development Area No. 69, South 
Boston/The 100 Acres. Such map amendment and plan were approved by the Boston Zoning 
Commission (the “Zoning Commission”) on January 10, 2007, and became effective on January 
10, 2007; the plan was subsequently amended by (1) a First Amendment thereto approved by the 
Authority on June 12, 2012, by the Zoning Commission on July 11, 2012, and effective as of 
July 12, 2012, (2) a Second Amendment thereto approved by the Authority on June 13, 2013, by 
the Zoning Commission on July 10, 2013 and effective as of July 10, 2013, (3) a Third 
Amendment thereto approved by the Authority on November 1, 2016, by the Zoning 
Commission on November 16, 2016, and effective as of November 18, 2016; (4) a Fourth 
Amendment thereto approved by the Authority on February 18, 2018, by the Zoning 
Commission on March 7, 2018, and effective as of March 12, 2018; and (v) a Fifth Amendment 
thereto approved by the Authority on September 10, 2020, by the Zoning Commission on 
October 21, 2020, and effective as of October 28, 2020 (as so amended, the “PDA Master Plan” 
or PDA No. 69””). The PDA Master Plan provides for the redevelopment of an approximately 47 
acre area of land in South Boston, Massachusetts bounded generally by the Fort Point Channel 
and A Street to the west, Summer Street to the north, the South Boston Bypass Road to the east, 
and West First Street and Mt. Washington Avenue to the south, but excludes those properties 
identified as 249 A Street, 326 A Street, 21 Wormwood Street, 33 Wormwood Street and 285 
Summer Street (the “Site”). In addition, the PDA Master Plan provides that the properties within 
Planned Development Area No. 53 (“PDA No. 53”) are to continue to be governed by the 
Development Plan for PDA No. 53, as the same may be amended from time to time. The Site is 
more particularly described and depicted on Exhibits B and C to the PDA Master Plan and 
comprises a portion of the BPDA planning area known as the “100 Acres.” 
The PDA Master Plan was adopted in order to support the redevelopment of the 100 
Acres area into a dense, varied and lively urban district that contains a broad range of uses such 
as residential, industrial, retail, service, research and development, office, open space and 

 
2 
 
cultural uses. The purpose of this Sixth Amendment to PDA No. 69 is to ensure that the vibrant 
community envisioned in PDA No. 69 is implemented. 
2. 
Development of Parcels G4, G5, G6, FT1, HW3, and portions of Parcels 
HW4 and FT2. The proponent of this Sixth Amendment is Channelside Acquisitions, LLC a 
Delaware limited liability company (the “Proponent”) which owns the property also known as 
244-284 A Street. The Proponent wishes to develop this approximately 6.46-acre site along the 
Fort Point Channel in the Fort Point neighborhood of South Boston, which currently includes a 
surface parking lot, is roughly bound by a private driveway (referred to herein as the “Garage 
Access Way”) and privately owned land currently under development known as 15 Necco Street 
to the northeast, A Street to the southeast, Binford Street to the southwest, and the Fort Point 
Channel to the northwest shown on Exhibit A hereto, legally described on Exhibit B attached 
hereto, and includes Parcels G4, G5, G6, FT1, HW3 and portions of Parcels HW4 and FT2 as 
shown on the existing PDA Master Plan (the “Project Site”). The Proponent proposes 
coordinated development on these parcels, as follows: 
(i) 
Construction on Parcel G4 of a new residential building containing approximately 
357,807 sf of Gross Floor Area, to house residential, commercial, retail, restaurant, 
and other Facilities of Public Accommodation uses (as defined in the M.G.L. 
Chapter 91 regulations) on the ground floor and other uses, together with uses 
accessory and ancillary thereto. The new building on Parcel G4 will have a 
maximum Building Height of 180 feet. 
(ii) 
Construction on Parcel G5 of a new commercial mixed-use building containing 
approximately 322,102 sf of Gross Floor Area, including, commercial, retail, 
restaurant and other Facilities of Public Accommodation uses on the ground floor 
and other uses, together with uses accessory and ancillary thereto. The new 
building on Parcel G5 will have a maximum Building Height of 180 feet. 
(iii) 
Construction on Parcel G6 of a new laboratory/research and development building 
containing approximately 418,383 sf of laboratory, research and development, life 
sciences and mixed-use space including commercial, retail, restaurant, and other 
Facilities of Public Accommodation uses on the ground floor and other uses, 
together with uses accessory and ancillary thereto. The Proponent has committed 
that the uses of this building on Parcel G6 will not exceed Biosafety Level (BSL) 2 
in accordance with the policies established by the Centers for Disease Control and 
Prevention. The new building on Parcel G6 will have a maximum Building Height 
of 123 feet. 
(iv) 
Construction of a below-grade parking garage with a capacity for up to four 
hundred fifteen (415) parking spaces to be constructed below-grade 
(v) 
Construction of new public open space on Parcels HW3, HW4, FT1 and FT2 as 
shown on Exhibit G (Open Space Plan) to the PDA Master Plan, including two 
public parks; and 

 
3 
 
(vi) 
Permanent widening and reconstruction of the City of Boston’s Harborwalk along 
the Fort Point Channel located on Parcels HW3 and HW4, including the 
implementation of a berm, a critical climate resilience measure (the “Berm”). 
Collectively, the foregoing improvements outlined in (i) — (vi) above constitute the 
“Project.” 
The Proponent will be providing residential housing, including artist housing and accompanying 
artist workspace, which is not otherwise being provided within the G Parcels, on Parcel G4. Of 
this housing, approximately 20% will be affordable, well in excess of the City’s IDP 
requirements. While the G Parcels as a whole do not meet the PDA Master Plan goal that 
envisioned “at least one-third residential or artist life/work in character”, by providing 
approximately one-third of the Project as residential housing, with a significant affordable and 
artist housing/artist workspace component, the Project will deliver impactful housing which will 
foster a vibrant, accessible, artist-supportive, inclusive, 24-hour environment and deliver on the 
vision set forth in the PDA Master Plan. 
Table 1 of the Master Plan provided for a cumulative FAR at “Full build-out” of 3.7 for Parcel 
Grouping G1-G8.1 Pursuant to the terms of the Master Plan, “Full build-out” may occur upon 
certain determinations having been made by the BPDA and the Boston Transportation 
Department (“BTD”). Through the Article 80 Review process for this Project, the BPDA has 
informed the Proponent that the Project Site can obtain “Full build-out” as each of BPDA and 
BTD have determined that significant transportation improvements capable of supporting 
additional development have been made within both the 100 Acres and the 1000 Acres. 
Therefore, the Project has been designed to effectuate the “Full build-out” for the Project Site. 
The Project Site will include a significant amount of publicly accessible open space totaling 
approximately 156,000 square feet, or 56% of the Project Site, including two public parks, along 
with a network of additional open spaces that increase the amount of open space provided on the 
Project Site by approximately 18,000 sf over the amount required by PDA No. 69 by virtue of a 
reduction in building footprint. Furthermore, the Project Site will provide approximately 31,000 
square feet more landscaped accessible pedestrian open space than what is described in PDA No. 
69 due to both the reduction in building footprint and elimination of unnecessary roadways, and 
Necco Street Park has been increased by approximately 50%. Moreover, the quality of the public 
open space has been substantially improved from that envisioned in the PDA Master Plan, 
including, but not limited to, by virtue of the conveyance of the parks to the City of Boston. 
 
1 Table 1 establishes the “Full-build” for the G Parcels, Parcels G1 through G8, of 3.7, with no FAR being 
established for each individual G Parcel. As the G Parcels contain 513,514 SF, PDA No. 69 authorizes up to 
1,900,000 of new gross floor area on the G Parcels. The Proponent’s planned development of the Project Site, when 
taken together with other G Parcels, will not exceed the 3.7 FAR authorized by PDA No. 69 for the G Parcels. The 
details are as follows: (i) the BPDA-approved redevelopment of Parcel G3 authorized 316,100 SF of gross floor 
area, (ii) the Proponent’s development of the Project Site (including development of Parcels G4, G5 and G6) 
contains 1,098,292 SF of new gross floor area; and (iii) the remaining redevelopment potential for Parcels G7 and 
G8 is 485,608 SF of new gross floor area. This allocation of square footage among the G Parcels is further 
delineated in an Assignment and Assumption of Contracts, Development Rights and Other Property Rights recorded 
with the Suffolk County Registry of Deeds in Book 61114, Page 152 as amended, which amendment is recorded 
with the Suffolk County Registry of Deeds in Book 62361, Page 28. 
 

 
4 
 
These new publicly accessible open spaces will foster greater connectivity between the 
community and waterfront, and also provide more opportunities to activate the Harborwalk with 
pedestrian foot traffic and seasonal activities. 
In connection with the development of the Project, the Proponent is seeking Authority and 
Zoning Commission approval concurrently for this Sixth Amendment as well as for that certain 
“Development Plan for 244-284 A Street/South Boston, Fort Point Channel, South Boston within 
Planned Development Area No. 69, South Boston/The 100 Acres.” Once approved by the Zoning 
Commission, each of the Sixth Amendment to PDA No. 69 and the Development Plan will 
effectuate the zoning and land use controls to enable the conversion of a surface parking lot on 
the Project Site to a lively urban district as described conceptually in the PDA Master Plan and 
deliver significant other benefits beyond those previously contemplated. 
3. 
Public Realm Enhancements and Allocated Enhancements. Reference is made 
to the Public Realm Enhancements as described in the PDA Master Plan and that certain 
Amended and Restated Memorandum of Agreement dated as of January 10, 2007 between the 
Authority and certain “Owner Parties” (as defined therein) (as amended to date, the “100 Acres 
MOA”). Pursuant to the PDA Master Plan and the 100 Acres MOA, certain Allocated 
Enhancements” (as defined therein) are assigned to the Project Site. This Sixth Amendment 
confirms that the Allocated Enhancements assigned to Parcels G4, G5, and G6 shall remain the 
same and consist of the following: 
(i) 
Extension of Necco Street to Binford Street; 
(ii) 
Construction of open space FT2 and open space (partial) FT1; 
(iii) 
Construction of open space and infrastructure within HW3 and HW4; 
(iv) 
Implementation of the Berm, a critical climate resilience measure; 
(v) 
Construction of Necco Street Park and Fort Point Channel Park, and 
(vi) 
The reconstruction and redesign of A Street between Binford Street to the south 
and Garage Access Way to the north along the frontage to exceed Boston 
Complete Streets standards. 
Furthermore, this Sixth Amendment eliminates unnecessary paved areas, including that section 
of Channel Street which previously surrounded Parcel G5 and connected to Binford Street, 
resulting in enhanced open space and access to the waterfront. Similarly, the Sixth Amendment 
eliminates the construction of Wormwood Street between A Street and Necco Street and 
enhances the design of Fort Point Avenue between A Street and Necco Street so as to provide for 
improved and accessible open space. 
This Development Plan sets forth the New Public Open Space and Infrastructure Improvements 
(collectively the “Public Realm Enhancements”) for the Project Site as contemplated in the PDA 
Master Plan. The dedication of additional publicly-accessible open space, new City of Boston 
owned parks and the Berm within the Project Site are exceptional Public Realm Enhancements, 
beyond that envisioned in the PDA Master Plan.

These new Exhibits solely reflect the modest changes in the site plan for the Project, the 
changes in the footprint of the buildings as a result of insight provided by improved engineering 
data for construction over subsurface tunnels, the modification of rights of way, and extensive 
new public realm improvements over that previously depicted on the PDA Master Plan. The 
Project has been designed in a manner consistent with the PDA Master Plan as refined so as to: 
minimize shadows on open space; reflect new engineering data which enables the design of the 
Project to move off of the I-90 Tunnel; realigning and reducing building footprints so as to allow 
for increased, more impactful open space at ground level with corresponding increases in 
building height in order to meet the anticipated density for the Project Site; allow for a widened 
rights-of-way and increased bicycle and pedestrian access; and allow more direct sunlight to the 
street level. The Project reflects a reconfiguration of certain of the parcels depicted on Exhibit I 
of the PDA Master Plan as is necessary to effect the Project’s design, while describing the 
allowed height, density and use of said parcels as required consistent with the terms of the PDA 
Master Plan. Approximately 156,000 square feet of the Project Site will be developed as open 
space available for public use, including the creation of two new public parks; the Harborwalk 
improvements, will now include the Berm, a critical climate resilience measure. In addition, the 
Project will connect with open space to be created by others to the north of the Project Site.

1.
Development Plan. Pursuant to Section 3-1A(a), Sections 51-44 through 51-49, and 
Article 80C of the Boston Zoning Code (the “Code”), this plan constitutes the Planned 
Development Area Development Plan (the “Development Plan”) for the redevelopment of an 
approximately 1.8-acre (+/-79,114-square-foot) site known and numbered as 250 Everett Street, 
Boston (Allston), Massachusetts (the “Project Site”), as described in Exhibit A-1 hereto and 
shown on the boundary plan attached hereto as Exhibit A-2. The Proponent (as defined below) 
proposes to demolish the existing building and improvements on the Project Site and construct a 
building containing, in aggregate, approximately 256,250 square feet of Gross Floor Area (as 
defined in Article 2 of the Code as of the date of this Development Plan, “GFA”), including 
residential uses (approximately 240 residential units), indoor and outdoor amenity spaces for 
residents, accessory parking, as well as publicly accessible open space and public realm 
improvements, as more fully described below (the “Project”). 
This Development Plan consists of eight (8) pages of text plus attachments designated 
Exhibits A-1 through E, which together establish the proposed: (i) location and appearance of the 
Project; (ii) uses; (iii) densities and dimensions of the Project; (iv) open spaces and landscaping; 
(v) traffic circulation; (vi) parking and loading facilities; and (vii) access to public transportation 
with regard to the Project. All references to this Development Plan contained herein shall pertain 
only to such pages and exhibits. 
This Development Plan constitutes permanent zoning for the Project Site in accordance 
with Section 3-1A and Article 80C of the Code, and it shall not expire or lapse. In accordance 
with Section 80C-9 of the Code, consistency of the Project with this Development Plan, which 
shall be evidenced by a Certification of Consistency issued by the Boston Redevelopment 
Authority d/b/a Boston Planning & Development Agency (the “BPDA”) pursuant to Section 
80C-8 of the Code (a “Certification of Consistency”), constitutes compliance with the 
requirements of the underlying zoning in effect as of the date this Development Plan is approved 
to the extent that such requirements are addressed in this Development Plan. Capitalized terms 
used but not defined herein shall have the meanings assigned to such terms in Article 2 of the 
Code as in effect as of the date this Development Plan becomes effective, without giving effect 
to any subsequent amendments to the Code. 

2 
2.
The Proponent. The Proponent of the Project is Mill Creek Residential (and its affiliates, 
designees, successors and assigns), having a business address of 84 State Street, Suite 920, 
Boston, MA 02109. 
3.
Project Site. The Project Site consists of approximately 1.8 acres (+/-79,114 square feet) 
of land bounded generally by Everett Street to the east, an existing senior housing building to the 
south, an existing surface parking lot to the west, and an existing retail building and an access 
driveway to the north. 
The Project Site straddles (i) the Barry’s Corner Community Commercial Subdistrict (the 
“BC Subdistrict”) and (ii) the Everett/Telford Community Commercial Subdistrict (the “ET 
Subdistrict”), both subdistricts of the Allston/Brighton Neighborhood District, carrying 
designations of “Barry’s Corner CC-1” and “Everett/Telford CC-1,” respectively, on Zoning 
Map 7B/7D, Allston/Brighton Neighborhood District, effective as of August 29, 2024. 
Both the BC Subdistrict and the ET Subdistrict were created as part of the 
implementation of the Western Avenue Corridor Study and Rezoning (the “WACRZ Study”). 
The WACRZ Study, along with corresponding text and map amendments to the Code, was 
approved by the BPDA’s Board of Directors (the “BPDA Board”) on October 13, 2022, and 
corresponding zoning amendments were approved by the Boston Zoning Commission on 
November 9, 2022. The WACRZ Study further divides the WACRZ subdistricts into fifteen 
alphanumeric zones. The Project Site straddles the ‘1b’ and ‘2a-4’ zones (respectively, “Zone 
1b” and “Zone 2a-4”). Zone 1b is located within the ET Subdistrict and Zone 2a-4 is located 
within the BC Subdistrict. 
As the Project Site straddles two different zoning subdistricts (the BC Subdistrict and the 
ET Subdistrict) and also two different WACRZ Study alphanumeric zones (Zone 1b and Zone 
2a-4), under the transition zoning rules of Section 12-1 of the Code, the zoning regulations 
applying to the less restricted portion of the Project Site extend thirty feet into the more 
restrictive zoning district. The Project’s compliance with Code requirements is accordingly 
calculated in conformance with Section 12-1 of the Code. 
Pursuant to Section 51-44 of the Code, Planned Development Areas are permitted within 
both the BC Subdistrict and the ET Subdistrict. This Plan establishes a Planned Development 
Area Overlay District consistent with the boundaries of the Project Site. A companion map 
amendment to the Zoning Map will depict the boundaries of the Planned Development Area 
Overlay District in a manner consistent with this Development Plan. 
4.
Project. The Proponent proposes to demolish the existing building on the Project Site, 
and to construct a building including residential uses and accessory uses, and other uses 
described herein. As shown on the site plan attached hereto as Exhibit B (the “Site Plan”), the 
Project comprises a six-story building, containing approximately 256,250 square feet of GFA, 
including approximately 240 residential units, accessory private indoor and outdoor amenity 
spaces, and accessory parking and loading in a below-grade parking garage with ingress and 
egress from Everett Street, as described in more detail below. The Project will also include 
enclosed secure bike storage areas in compliance with City requirements, as well as publicly 
accessible short-term bicycle parking spaces, all of which are described in more detail in Section 

3 
11 below. The Project will create active open spaces along the Project Site frontage, along with 
new landscaping and hardscaped publicly accessible spaces and a new publicly accessible open 
space at the Project Site’s southern edge, all as generally shown on Exhibit E attached hereto.

Planning Context; Compliance with Planning and Design Principles. As required 
pursuant to Section 51-44 of the Code, the Project is consistent with the urban planning and 
design initiatives set forth in the WACRZ Study. As required by Section 51-45 of the Code, the 
Project is consistent with “Table 1: Use and Dimensional Standards” of the WACRZ Study and 
Table 2 of Section 51-45 of the Code. Specifically, the Project complies with the following 
dimensional standards provided in “Table 1: Use and Dimensional Standards” of the WACRZ 
Study: (i) Floor Area Ratio (Incentive FAR); (ii) Lot Coverage; and (iii) Height, as further 
detailed below in Section 8.

Allowed Uses. As required by Section 51-45 of the Code, the Project is consistent with

8.
Proposed Densities and Dimensions; Other Bulk and Dimensional Controls.
Pursuant to Section 51-45 of the Code, the dimensional requirements for a Proposed 
Project within a Planned Development Area in the BC Subdistrict or the ET Subdistrict shall be 
as set forth in an applicable approved Development Plan and consistent with “Table 1: Use and 
Dimensional Standards” of the WACRZ Study. Accordingly, the Project, as described above and 
shown on the Site Plan, consists of a multifamily residential building, subject to the following 
bulk and dimensional controls: (i) a maximum Floor Area Ratio (“FAR”) of 3.24 calculated in 
accordance with Section 12-1 and the bonus FAR provisions of the WACRZ Study as described 
below; (ii) a maximum Lot Coverage of 60%; and (iii) a maximum Building Height of 65 feet. 
These are the only bulk and dimensional controls applicable to the Project. 
Under Section 51-45(2) of the Code, the maximum allowable FAR is provided by “Table 
1: Use and Dimensional Standards” in the WACRZ Study. “Table 1: Use and Dimensional 
Standards” of the WACRZ Study provides bonus FAR allowances for various levels of 
affordability. Pursuant to “Table 2: Affordability Incentive” of the WACRZ Study, a 17% on-site 
affordability requirement allows for a maximum Incentive FAR of 4.0 in the BC Subdistrict and 
a maximum Incentive FAR of 3.0 in the ET Subdistrict. Because the Project will devote at least 

4 
17% of its residential gross floor area to affordable housing (as defined and described in the 
WACRZ Study), it qualifies for the Incentive FAR dimensional control in “Table 1: Use and 
Dimensional Standards” of the WACRZ Study 
Although the Project Site straddles two zoning subdistricts, the Project Site consists of a 
single lot for purposes of zoning compliance and a single value for FAR is calculated as a 
blended proportional requirement between the two subdistricts. As mentioned, Section 12-1 of 
the Code on transition zoning extends the less restrictive zoning for another thirty feet from the 
boundary line. Here, the BC Subdistrict (Zone 2a-4) provides a less restrictive Incentive FAR 
requirement of 4.0. Accounting for the thirty-foot transition extension of the BC Subdistrict, a 
maximum FAR of 3.24 is allowed for the Project Site given that it will meet the 17% on-site 
affordability requirement described above. This calculation assumes the boundary line between 
the BC Subdistrict and ET Subdistrict aligns with the centerline of Raymond Street, as shown on 
Zoning Map 7B/7D, as adopted on November 9, 2022 as Map Amendment Number 748. 
Regarding maximum Lot Coverage, pursuant to Section 51-45(2) and “Table 1: Use and 
Dimensional Standards” of the WACRZ Study, both Zone 1b and Zone 2a-4 provide for a 
maximum Lot Coverage of 60%. 
Regarding Building Height, pursuant to Section 51-45(2) and “Table 1: Use and 
Dimensional Standards” of the WACRZ Study, Zone 1b provides for a maximum Building 
Height of 65 feet and Zone 2a-4 provides for a maximum Building Height of 125 feet. The 
Project will comply with the more restrictive dimensional control of 65 feet for maximum 
Building Height. 
9.
Proposed Open Space. The Project will provide open spaces for use by residents, guests, 
and other visitors to the Project, as generally set forth on Exhibit E to this Development Plan. 
The Project incorporates a residential scale entry plaza, a second level resident amenity courtyard 
and other exterior open space for use by Project residents. Further, the Project includes publicly 
accessible open space along the eastern frontage and southern edge of the Project Site and is set 
back from the property line in order to prioritize pedestrian use and walkability along Everett 
Street. Enhanced vegetation through these open spaces and along the streetscape will improve 
biodiversity on the Project Site. Along the Project Site’s southern edge, a publicly accessible 
open space will prioritize existing tree preservation, feature various seating options, and provide 
opportunities for placemaking and historical interpretive elements. 
10.
Sustainable Design. The Project will comply with the requirements of Article 37 of the 
Code. The Project team will use the U.S. Green Building Council’s Leadership in Energy and 
Environmental Design (“LEED”) green building rating system to evaluate sustainable design 
measures, in accordance with Article 37 of the Code. The Project, as designed, will target LEED 
Gold level certifiability. 
11.
Proposed Traffic Circulation; Parking, Bicycle and Loading Facilities. The Project 
will provide adequate access and traffic circulation in accordance with City standards, as 
generally shown on Exhibit B to this Development Plan. The Project is currently anticipated to 
provide parking at a ratio of up to 0.50 vehicle spaces per dwelling unit (approximately 120 total 
vehicles) which conforms with both the Boston Transportation Parking (“BTD”) Parking 

5 
Maximums and the Parking Maximums included in the WACRZ Study. This ratio is subject to 
finalization in consultation with BTD; the final parking ratio required for the Project shall be 
established in the Transportation Access Plan Agreement (“TAPA”) executed by the Proponent 
and BTD with respect to the Project. The below-grade parking garage will provide direct, secure 
access to the Project and streamline vehicular circulation, with all passenger vehicles entering 
and exiting the parking garage through an entry/exit on Everett Street. In compliance with the 
City’s Bicycle Parking Guidelines, the Project will also provide one long-term bicycle space per 
residential unit within the Project, which spaces will be indoor and secure. In addition to the 
dedicated off-street parking and bike storage, the Project will provide approximately 48 short-
term bicycle spaces, which will be publicly accessible and convenient for guests and visitors of 
the Project. With respect to loading facilities serving the Project, loading facilities will be 
accessed from Everett Street. The parking and loading facilities are subject to refinement as 
development review of the Project proceeds as set forth below. The foregoing shall be the only 
parking, bike parking and loading requirements applicable to the Project, subject to final design 
review and TAPA review.

Development Plan Approval Standards. Section 51-49 of the Code provides that the 
BPDA may approve a planned development area development plan in the BC Subdistrict and the 
ET Subdistrict of the Allston/Brighton Neighborhood District as meeting the requirement of 
Section 80C-4 if the BPDA finds that such development plan proposes a plan for public benefits, 
including, in relevant part, (i) provision of Affordable Housing available to Allston/Brighton and 
Boston residents; (ii) improvements to the aesthetic character of the development site and its 
surroundings, which may include the provision of open space connections, the provision of street 
trees and other improvements that enhance open space, the improvement of the urban design 
characteristics of the Project Site and its surroundings, or the enhancement of existing open 
space or the creation of new open space; or (iii) creation of new street connections, pedestrian 
and bicyclist facilities, and new transit facilities. As addressed in Section 14 and other Sections 
of this Development Plan, this Development Plan proposes a comprehensive plan of public 
benefits to be derived from the Project, consistent with Section 51-49 of the Code.


Creation of Housing Opportunities. The Project will provide a variety of housing 
options for the residents of Allston/Brighton and the City of Boston, including a 
substantial number of affordable housing units. The Project will devote 17% of its 
residential floor area to affordable housing (as defined and described in the 
WACRZ Study) which is anticipated to be approximately 41 units, including 
family-sized units. An Affordable Rental Housing Agreement and Restriction with 
the BPDA will govern the Project’s affordable housing commitments.

PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA DEVELOPMENT PLAN. On March 
14, 2019, the Boston Redevelopment Authority, doing business as the Boston Planning & 
Development Agency (the “Authority”) approved an Amended and Restated Planned 
Development Area Master Plan for Planned Development Area No. 51 pursuant to Article 3, 
Section 3-1A and Article 80, Section 80C of the Boston Zoning Code (the “Code”) for the Hood 
Park in Charlestown (the “Development”), which Master Plan was amended by First 
Amendment to Amended and Restated Master Plan approved by the Authority on December 12, 
2019 (as amended, the “PDA Master Plan”). Capitalized terms used herein without definition 
which are defined in the PDA Master Plan shall have the meanings ascribed to them therein. 
 
On October 20, 2000 the Boston Zoning Commission (the “Commission”), by the 
adoption of Map Amendment No. 382, approved the PDA Master Plan and amended the series of 
maps entitled “Zoning Districts City of Boston,” dated August 15, 1962, as amended, by adding 
a “D” designation, indicating a Planned Development Area overlay district, to the Site. 
 
The PDA Master Plan contemplates that one or more PDA Development Plans for phases 
of the Development may be submitted either simultaneously with or subsequent to the 
submission of the PDA Master Plan. 
 
In accordance with Article 3, Section 3-1A of the Code and Article 80, Section 80C, this 
development plan sets forth information on the construction of a building to contain up to 91 
residential units, and a hotel of up to 160 rooms (or keys) with related amenities, food service 
and café areas, and a below grade parking garage with up to 224 parking spaces to be shared 
with another retail structure that will be subject to a separate Development Plan within the PDA

Rutherford Avenue, construction of a shared, fifteen (15) foot wide, multi-use, pedestrian and 
bicycle path along the northern property boundary, and the construction of Hood Green, the open 
space area described in the PDA Master Plan (collectively, the “Project”). The Project is located

on a portion of an approximately twenty-acre site which is the former Hood Dairy Plant located 
on the west side of Rutherford Avenue in the Charlestown section of Boston, Suffolk County, 
Massachusetts (the “Site”) within a Special Purpose Overlay District Planned Development Area 
(“PDA”). The Project will be located on a vacant portion of the site that was most recently used 
for surface parking. 
 
This development plan includes the proposed location and appearance of structures, open 
spaces and landscaping, the proposed uses of the Project, the proposed dimensions of the 
structure, the proposed density, the proposed traffic circulation, parking and loading facilities, 
access to public transportation and other major elements of the Project (the “Development 
Plan”).

PROPOSED DIMENSIONS OF STRUCTURE. The Project will have 
eighteen levels, including the mechanical penthouse, plus rooftop mechanical equipment, rooftop 
solar panels, penthouses and screen walls for a total maximum height of 215 feet. The gross

9. 
PROPOSED VEHICULAR AND PEDESTRIAN TRAFFIC 
CIRCULATION. 
 
Traffic Circulation: 
 
Currently, the Site has access from Rutherford Avenue on a driveway from the northern 
portion of the Site to Rutherford Avenue. As described in the PDA Master Plan, Supertest Street 
will be constructed in the northern portion of the Site to connect with Rutherford Avenue and 
Stack Street. There is also access from the Site onto D Street leading to Spice Street, Cambridge 
Street and Sullivan Square. This driveway primarily serves traffic coming from or heading 
toward Spice Street. As described in the PDA Master Plan, Stack Street will lead from Hood 
Park Drive to D Street and will replace the current driveway near this location. 
 
The Site is located on the west side of Rutherford Avenue (Route 99) and just east of 
Interstate Route 93 (I-93), which runs parallel to Route 99. The Route 99 underpass is adjacent 
to the Site, with two travel lanes in each direction. The I-93 overpass adjacent to the Site 
connects Charlestown with I-93 North, with two travel lanes in each direction. Rutherford 
Avenue itself near the Site is divided into a one-way pair by the Route 99 underpass and I-93 
overpass. 
 
The Site can be directly accessed by entering traffic from the I-93 overpass via Spice 
Street and Rutherford Avenue. Traffic from the Route 99 underpass, however, cannot access the 
Site directly. Traffic leaving the Site toward the north can utilize D Street to Spice Street to 
Cambridge Street. Spice Street has one travel lane in each direction with parking on both sides 
of the street. 
 
 
Pedestrian Circulation: 
 
The major pedestrian route to the Site is Hood Park Drive, Stack Street and the to be 
constructed Supertest Street leading off of Rutherford Avenue. Hood Park Drive includes

PUBLIC BENEFITS. The Project, as a part of the Development, will provide 
substantial public benefits to the City of Boston and the surrounding neighborhood. These 
benefits will include: 
 
Constructive Reuse of an Industrial Site. The Project continues the transformation of 

 
6 
 
the former Hood Dairy plant from an obsolete industrial plant to a state-of-the-art 21st 
century mixed-use development. 
 
The significant landscaping program will provide the neighborhood with a new outdoor 
softscape area which will improve the water quality and reduce runoff in and around the 
Site by replacing the current expanses of asphalt on the Site with new pervious areas. 
 
The proposed uses of the Development will result in a reduction in traffic impacts (i.e., 
noise, road infrastructure damages, air quality) by the elimination of uses relying upon 
trucks and other heavy vehicles that currently service the Site. 
 
Construction Employment. Construction of the Project will create approximately 450 
construction jobs and will be subject to a Boston Residents Construction Employment 
Plan. 
 
Permanent Employment. The Project will result in approximately 35 permanent jobs. 
 
Redirected Growth. The Development will enhance the City’s goals of providing mixed-
use developments for residential, commercial and retail close to major transit hubs. 
 
Affordable Housing Creation. The Project will result in the creation of eighteen (18) off-
site two, three and four bedroom family affordable housing units in the West Rutherford 
area of the Charlestown neighborhood. 
 
Enhanced Pedestrian & Bicycle Network. The Development will result in the creation of 
a fifteen (15) foot wide multi-use pedestrian and bicycle path extending along the 
Projects northerly property line from Rutherford Avenue to Stack Street. 
 
Hood Green. The Development will result in the creation of a new approximately one (1) 
acre publicly accessible open space on top of the below-grade parking structure, between 
Supertest Street and the northern property boundary, including soft and hardscape 
finishes, plantings, trees, recreational components, and public access accommodations, 
referred to as “Hood Green”. 
 
PLAN: Charlestown. The Development will foster and enhance the development goals 
of the PLAN: Charlestown planning initiative approved by the Authority in 2023 by 
providing affordable housing, open space areas, and improved connectivity in 
Charlestown.

Areas are permitted within the BCCC Subdistrict. This Plan establishes a Planned Development 
Area Overlay District consistent with the boundaries of the Project Site. 
4.
Project. The Proponent proposes to demolish the existing buildings on the Project 
Site, and to construct a pedestrian-oriented, mixed-use building. As shown on the site plan attached 
hereto as Exhibit B (the “Site Plan”), the Project comprises an approximately three-story building, 
containing approximately 92,300 square feet of GFA, including office, research and development 
space, high bay light manufacturing space, ground floor co-working/meeting space available for 
use by the public, public service space made suitable for use by Boston Emergency Medical 
Services, including ambulance space, accessory spaces including parking and loading, and shared 
amenity space, served by a structured parking garage as described in more detail below. The Project 
will also include enclosed secure bike storage areas for employees of and visitors to the Project, 
as well as publicly accessible short-term bicycle parking spaces, all of which is described in more 
detail in Section 10 below. The Project will create a substantial, publicly accessible courtyard 
directly accessible from both Western Avenue and the ground floor co-working and meeting space, 
including new landscaping and a hardscaped plaza. 
5.
Planning Context; Compliance with Planning and Design Principles. As 
required pursuant to Section 51-44 of the Code, the Project is consistent with the urban planning 
and design initiatives set forth in the Western Avenue Corridor Study and Rezoning (“WACRZ 
Study”). The WACRZ Study, along with corresponding text and map amendments to the Code, 
was approved by the BPDA’s Board of Directors (the “BPDA Board”) on October 13, 2022, and 
corresponding zoning amendments were approved by the Boston Zoning Commission on 

3 
4894-7411-5210, v. 4
November 9, 2022. Further, as required by Section 51-45 of the Code, the Project is consistent 
with “Table 1: Use and Dimensional Standards” of the WACRZ Study. 
6.
Proposed Location and Appearance of the Project. The elevation plans 
appended as Exhibit C to this Development Plan illustrate the Project’s proposed location and 
general appearance. The Project is subject to ongoing design, environmental, and other 
development review by the BPDA, and by other governmental agencies and authorities, and the 
design, location, layout, and appearance of the Project may evolve in the course of such review, to 
the extent consistent with the use and dimensional limitations contained in this Development Plan. 
7.
Allowed Uses. The Project Site may be used for those office; research and 
development; light manufacturing; co-working/meeting space open to the public; public service 
space, including ambulance space; parking; loading; open space; and accessory and ancillary uses, 
and all other uses listed in Exhibit D to this Development Plan, and for any uses allowed as-of-
right within the BCCC Subdistrict (or such other underlying zoning district or subdistrict that may 
include the Project Site) from time to time. Any uses listed on Exhibit D are permitted within the 
Project Site as either primary, accessory, or ancillary uses, and may be substituted for any specific 
uses described in the text of this Development Plan without requiring any amendment to this 
Development Plan. Uses not listed on Exhibit D and not otherwise allowed as-of-right within the 
BCCC Subdistrict from time to time shall require an amendment to this Development Plan. 
8.
Proposed Densities and Dimensions; Other Bulk and Dimensional Controls. 
The Project, as described above and shown on the Site Plan, consists of a mixed-used building, 
subject to the following bulk and dimensional controls: (i) a maximum Floor Area Ratio of 1.65; 
(ii) a maximum Lot Coverage of 70%; (iii) a maximum Building Height of up to 75 feet in the 
portion of the Project Site located in Zone 2b in the BCCC Subdistrict as depicted on the Zoning 
Map1 and up to 80 feet in the portion of the Project Site located in Zone 2-b-2 in the BCCC 
Subdistrict as depicted on the Zoning Map; and (iv) a minimum 15-foot setback along Western 
Avenue. These are the only bulk and dimensional controls applicable to the Project. 
As used herein: (1) “Building Height” shall have the meaning set forth in Article 2 of the 
Code as of the date of this Development Plan, provided that Grade for purposes of calculating 
Building Height is +/- 16’-0” Boston City Base and provided further that exhaust stacks and flues 
may extend 10 feet above the above- referenced Building Heights ; and (2) “Lot Coverage” shall 
mean the total building footprint divided by the total area of the lot. For the purposes of calculating 
Lot Coverage and Floor Area Ratio, the term “total area of the lot” shall mean 55,952 square feet, 
which measurement is inclusive of areas that will be devoted to public realm improvements on the 
Project Site and inclusive of areas owned by the Proponent within an adjacent private way. 
9.
Proposed Open Space and Landscaping. The Project will provide ground level 
open spaces for use by tenants and their employees, guests and other visitors to the Project, as 
generally set forth on Exhibit E to this Development Plan. The Project includes a substantial, 
publicly accessible courtyard directly accessible from both Western Avenue and the ground floor 
co-working and meeting space and includes a hardscape and landscaped plaza adjacent to the

sidewalk that leads to the building entry. Further, the Project is set back from the property line in 
order to prioritize pedestrian use and walkability along Western Avenue. Street tree plantings along 
Western Avenue will significantly increase and diversify the Project Site’s urban tree canopy and 
will provide shade for the new sidewalk and courtyard area along the Project Site frontage. 
10.
Proposed Traffic Circulation; Parking and Loading Facilities. The Project will 
provide adequate access and traffic circulation in accordance with city standards, as generally 
shown on Exhibit F to this Development Plan. As described above, the Project features off-street 
parking spaces interior to the Project Site at a maximum parking ratio at or below that established 
pursuant to the City of Boston Transportation Department’s (“BTD”) Maximum Parking Ratios 
for Large Development Project Review: Bike Parking Guidelines, Version 2.1 (February 2022)
(the “BTD Guidelines”). The Project is currently anticipated to provide approximately thirty-six 
(36) vehicle parking spaces; however this number is subject to further adjustment in consultation 
with BTD and the final vehicular parking figures required for the Project shall be established in 
the Transportation Access Plan Agreement (“TAPA”) executed by the Proponent and BTD with 
respect to the Project. The interior parking will provide direct, secure access to the Project and will 
streamline vehicular circulation, with all passenger vehicles entering and exiting the parking 
structure through an entry/exit on McDonald Avenue. 
The Project will provide bicycle parking pursuant to the BTD’s Bike Parking Guidelines, Version 
2.1 (January 2021) with approximately one long-term bicycle space per 2,500 square feet of 
office/research and development space and one outdoor visitor bicycle space per 20,000 square 
space of office/research and development space. Therefore, the Project will provide approximately 
thirty-six (36) secure bike spaces, which will be indoor, secure and reserved for employees and 
approximately five (5) short-term outdoor bicycle spaces for visitors. 
Off-street Project loading and service facilities will be located along McDonald Avenue with two 
(2) loading bays for building service and two (2) ambulance bays. The parking and loading 
facilities for the Project are generally shown on Exhibit G to this Development Plan and are subject 
to refinement as development review of the Project proceeds as set forth below. The foregoing 
shall be the only parking, bike parking and loading requirements applicable to the Project. 
Potential impacts stemming from the above parking and loading facilities have been 
adequately studied by the BPDA and BTD in the course of Large Project Review for the Project. 
The Proponent will provide for mitigation to address any such traffic impacts in a manner 
consistent with the TAPA. 
11.
Access to Public Transportation. The Project Site is well served by public 
transportation. The Project Site is served by three Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority 
(“MBTA”) bus routes in its immediate proximity. MBTA Route 70 and Route 86 operate along 
Western Avenue adjacent to the Project Site, with stops at Western Avenue/Everett Street and 
Western Avenue/Riverdale Street. MBTA Route 66 has two nearby stops along North Harvard 
Avenue at Western Avenue and at Kingsley Street. 
The Project Site is situated about one mile north of the MBTA’s Boston Landing Station, which 
serves the Framingham/Worcester commuter rail line with service to Back Bay Station and South 
Station. Commuters can transfer to MBTA Orange Line trains at Back Bay Station, and to MBTA 

5 
4894-7411-5210, v. 4
Red Line trains (as well as other Commuter Rail trains and Amtrak regional trains) at South 
Station. The Project Site sits on Western Avenue, which itself is a major thoroughfare that traverses 
through the Allston/Brighton neighborhood with bus stops servicing Harvard Square, Waltham 
Center, Reservoir, Sullivan Square, Central Square, Kendall Square and University Park, among 
others. Together, these public transportation nodes provide convenient access to much of Greater 
Boston. 
12.
Signage. Signs shall be permitted on the Project Site to the extent they comply with 
Article 11 of the Code, or as approved from time to time through Article 80 design review by the 
BPDA. Any sign approved as part of such review will be deemed to comply with this Development 
Plan and the Code. 
13.
Development Plan Approval Standards. Section 51-49 of the Code provides that 
the BPDA may approve a planned development area development plan in the BCCC Subdistrict 
of the Allston/Brighton Neighborhood District as meeting the requirement of Section 80C-4 if the 
BPDA finds that such development plan proposes a plan for public benefits, including one or more 
of the following: (a) diversification and expansion of Boston’s economy and job opportunities 
through economic activity, such as private investment in manufacturing, commercial, or research 
and development uses; or (b) creation of new job opportunities and establishment of educational 
facilities, career counseling, or technical assistance providing instruction or technical assistance in 
fields related to such jobs; or (c) provision of Affordable Housing available to Allston/Brighton 
and Boston residents; or (d) improvements to the aesthetic character of the development site and 
its surroundings, which may include the provision of open space connections, of the Charles River 
waterfront, the provision of street trees and other improvements that enhance open space, the 
improvement of the urban design characteristics of the Project Site and its surroundings, or the 
enhancement of existing open space or the creation of new open space; or (e) creation of new street 
connections, pedestrian and bicyclist facilities, and new transit facilities. As addressed in Section 
14 and other Sections of this Development Plan, this Development Plan proposes a comprehensive 
plan of public benefits to be derived from the Project, consistent with Section 51-49 of the Code. 
As noted above, Section 51-45 of the Code also requires that any planned development area 
development plan approved in the BCCC Subdistrict be consistent with “Table 1: Use and 
Dimensional Standards” of the WACRZ Study. As addressed in Sections 7 and 8 above, the 
Project’s use and dimensional constraints are consistent with the WACRZ Study. 
14.
Public Benefits. The Project’s public benefits include the following: 
a.
Economic Health and Diversity. The Project provides “graduation” space 
for early-stage life science companies that will enhance other uses on the Western Avenue corridor 
and not compete with them. The Project will contribute extensively to the economic health and 
wellbeing of the Allston/Brighton neighborhood, and the City of Boston more generally, by 
generating substantially increased property taxes, new tax revenues, and diverse job opportunities. 
b.
Creation of Job Opportunities. The Proponent will revitalize the existing 
underutilized site, returning jobs and revenue to the Allston/Brighton neighborhood and the city. 
The mix of uses at the Project will create a substantial number of job opportunities, including 
approximately 200 construction jobs and approximately 300 permanent jobs upon stabilization. 

6 
4894-7411-5210, v. 4
c.
Creation of Publicly Accessible Co-Working Space. The Project will 
provide approximately 3,000 square feet of GFA of co-working and meeting space made available 
for use by the public subject to community demand. This space will provide an amenity to area 
residents and workers and facilitate meeting and collaboration. 
d.
Creation of Public Service Space. The Project will provide public service 
space made suitable for use by Boston Emergency Medical Services if and as desired, anticipated 
to include two replacement ambulance bay spaces and other accessory uses. 
e.
Public Realm Improvements. The Proponent has committed to undertake 
improvements that enhance the public realm consistent with the WACRZ Study’s public realm 
guidelines. These enhancements include providing pedestrian-focused walkable streets with wide 
sidewalks along Western Avenue as well as a large, publicly accessible plaza that will be accessible 
from both Western Avenue and the co-working and meeting space. The building is set back from 
Western Avenue to facilitate the continued improvements along Western Avenue, including a 
planting zone and separated bicycle lane along the Western Avenue frontage. 
f.
Urban Design Benefits. The Project’s design will activate an underutilized 
site, provide a publicly accessible plaza, and will significantly increase and diversity the Project 
Site’s urban tree canopy while also reducing the Project Site’s urban heat island gain compared to 
existing conditions. The Project’s lobbies at ground-level will create a continuously active 
streetscape that will support and enhance the area. 
g.
Smart Growth/Transit-Oriented Development. The Project exemplifies 
smart-growth and transit-oriented development by concentrating new commercial uses in close 
proximity to major regional Commuter Rail and bus lines that provide easy access to the Project 
Site from all of the City’s neighborhoods and suburbs. The Project will also provide a number of 
key transportation improvements that will improve the pedestrian and bicycling experience 
throughout the area, including (i) enhancements to pedestrian and bike safety features in adjacent 
public ways, (ii) space for a bikeshare station on or adjacent to the site; and (iii) a proactive 
transportation demand management (TDM) plan to encourage building users to utilize alternative 
forms of transportation in accordance with the BTD Guidelines. 
h.
Sustainable Design. The Project will comply with the requirements of 
Article 37 of the Code. The Project team will use the U.S. Green Building Council’s Leadership 
in Energy and Environmental Design (“LEED”) green building rating system to evaluate 
sustainable design measures, in accordance with Article 37 of the Code. The Project, as designed, 
will target LEED Gold level certifiability, and the Project team will continue to research additional 
sustainable and energy-efficient measures as the Project design develops. 
15.

ongoing development review and approval by the BPDA under Article 80B of the Code. In 
accordance with these development review procedures, the Proponent filed a Project Notification 
Form for the Project on October 12, 2023, initiating the Large Project Review process with the 
BPDA.
