3. 
PDA Site: The PDA Site totals approximately 97,739 square feet (2.24 acres), 
and is bounded by William T. Morrissey Boulevard to the east, the former Boston Globe 
headquarters building now known as “Southline” to the south, Interstate Highway 93 to the west, 
and 55 Morrissey Boulevard to the north. The Site is currently improved with a single-story 
vacant commercial building with large areas of impervious surface parking. 
The PDA Site is located within the Community Commercial zoning subdistrict of the 
Dorchester Neighborhood District as governed by Article 65 of the Code, as well as (i) a 
Restricted Parking Overlay District (“RPOD”) established by Section 3-1A.c of the Code, (ii) the 
Coastal Flood Resilience Overlay District (“CFROD”) established by Article 25A of the Code, 
and (iii) eastern portions of the Site along Morrissey Boulevard are located within the Morrissey 
Boulevard Greenbelt Protection Overlay district (“GPOD”) established by Article 29 of the 
Code. Pursuant to Section 3-1A(a) and Section 65-28, Planned Development Areas are permitted 
within the area that includes the PDA Site, and the Project is subject to the overriding zoning 
regulations set forth in Master Planned Development Area No. 146, entitled Columbia Point 
Crossing Master Pan, dated December 14, 2023, which includes an approximately 8.9 acre area 
including 35-45 Morrissey Boulevard, 55 Morrissey Boulevard, and the Site (the “Master 
PDA”). 
4. 
New Building Project: The Proponent proposes the development of two new 
residential buildings containing approximately 754 residential units, which are (i) “Building A”, 
an 18-story building containing up to 335,000 square feet of gross floor area (“GFA”) and 
including residential use, ground-floor commercial uses, amenity and community/civic spaces, 
and an up to three-level structured below-grade parking facility accommodating off-street 
parking for approximately 179 vehicles, and (ii) “Building B”, an 18-story building containing 
up to 320,000 square feet of GFA and including residential use, ground-floor commercial uses, 
amenity and community/civic spaces, and an up to three-level structured below-grade parking 
facility accommodating off-street parking for approximately 235 vehicles (each a “New 
Building”, and collectively the “New Buildings”). The New Buildings will improve upon the 
existing surface parking and vacant single-story building it is replacing. 
5. 
Proposed Locations and Appearance of New Buildings: Selected elevations 
attached hereto as Exhibit C illustrate each New Building’s general appearance. Building A and 
Building B respond to both the immediate context of the highway and the ocean side, and the 
broader environmental characteristics of the area. Building A acts as a buffer between Interstate 
93 and the Community Park, and draws on the sweeping curve of Interstate 93 to define the main 
massing of the building while creating a stepped down massing and angled form along the 
Community Park to create an inviting public realm. Building B creates a strong orthogonal street 
presence along Morrissey Boulevard, thus allowing the building massing to act as a 
corresponding massing to Building A, while similarly breaking up and stepping down the 
massing towards the Community Park. While both Building A and Building B have unique 

expressions tailored to their placement on the Site, they each have a proximate and physical 
connection to each other, and the surrounding urban context. 
6. 
Proposed Density and Dimensions of Structures: The range of dimensional 
requirements for the Project are as set forth in the Master PDA, and specifically for the New 
Buildings are (i) the maximum site-wide FAR for the entire approximately 8.9 acre Master PDA 
site area is 4.0 which shall include the GFA as set forth in the New Buildings, and (ii) the 
Maximum Height, as such term is defined in the Master PDA, is 206 for Building B and 204 feet 
for Building A. 
The New Buildings will contain up to 655,000 square feet of GFA1. See Exhibit D for massing 
diagram. Accordingly, this results in an FAR of less than the maximum 4.0 allowed across the 
full Master PDA area. Building A will have a Maximum Height of up to 206 feet, and Building 
B will have a Maximum Height of up to 204 feet. The Maximum Building Height and FAR set 
out above are the only dimensional requirements applicable to the PDA Site pursuant to the 
Master PDA. All other dimensional or design requirements of the Code are not be applicable to 
the PDA Site and are superseded by this Development Plan and the Master PDA. The Project 
shall be subject to design, environmental and other development review by the BPDA, and 
aspects of the Project approved as part of such review shall be and hereby are deemed to be the 
dimensional and design requirements applicable to the New Buildings and are hereby 
incorporated in this Development Plan. 
7. 
Proposed Open Space and Landscaping: The Project will revitalize an area that 
is currently an open asphalt surface parking lot by providing an approximately 23,900 square 
foot community park (“Community Park”) that will be open to the public in perpetuity. The 
Project will provide additional landscape improvements that will be constructed 
contemporaneously with each of the New Buildings, including the expansion of the Site’s 
pedestrian and bicycle network to provide improved pedestrian and bike access between 
neighboring properties and JFK/UMass Red Line/South Shore Commuter Rail Station. 
8. 
Proposed Uses: The New Building will be used primarily for residential use and 
parking facilities (as accessory, ancillary, and principal uses). In addition to the uses listed 
above, all of the uses listed in Exhibit E shall be permitted as of right on the full PDA Site. 
9. 
Proposed Traffic Circulation: The Project will continue to be served by the 
existing curb-cuts along the Morrissey Boulevard, and will create a new, off-site, “A Street” 
public roadway connecting to Morrissey Boulevard and running adjacent to the northern edge of 
the Site, and a new “West Street” roadway along and within the western edge of the Site. Access 
to the below-grade parking spaces will be provided for Building A from the West Street, and for 
Building B from A Street. A pick-up/drop-off area will be provided along portions of A Street. 
Rights to A street for the Project are being provided by the owner of 55 Morrissey Boulevard 
through binding legal agreements. 
1 All square footages are approximate. GFA is defined in Article 2 of the Code and specifically excludes 
from calculation floor area devoted to mechanical equipment, storage, below-grade parking areas and service and 
loading areas. 

10. 
Proposed Parking and Loading Facilities: The New Buildings will each include 
three levels of below-grade parking for approximately 414 vehicles. All loading and service 
activity will be actively managed by the building transportation coordinator, and the New 
Buildings will provide both secure bicycle parking spaces and publicly accessible bicycle 
parking spaces. 
11. 
Access to Public Transportation: The Site is well served by the Massachusetts 
Bay Transportation Authority (“MBTA”); it is approximately 1,300 feet from the JFK/UMass 
Station. This Station is a commuter hub providing connection between three commuter rail lines 
(Greenbush, Kingston/Plymouth, and Fall River/New Bedford), the MBTA Red Line, and three 
MBTA bus routes (Number 8, 16, and 41). 
12. 
Signage: The signage program for the New Buildings shall be subject to design, 
environmental and other development review by the BPDA, and any sign approved as part of 
such review shall be deemed to be in compliance with the Development Plan and the Master 
PDA. 
13. 
Development Review Procedures: All aspects of the Project design will be 
subject to ongoing development and design review and approval by the BPDA. 
14. 
Green Building and Resiliency Measures: The New Buildings are subject to 
Article 37 (Green Buildings) of the Code, pursuant to Section 80B Large Project Review. The 
New Buildings will meet the requirements necessary to achieve at least a Gold-level certifiability 
using LEEDv4 rating system and Passive House PHIUS 2024 standards, and will be designed 
with energy-efficient HVAC and lighting equipment and systems and will incorporate other 
potential energy conservation measures, as reasonable and feasible. 
Portions of the PDA Site are located within the FEMA-designated Special Flood Hazard 
Area, Zone AE on the FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM [Community Panel No. 
25025C0083J, effective March 16, 2016]). Portions of the Site are also similarly included in the 
CFROD district, and, as set forth below and reviewed during the related Article 80B process for 
the Project, all regulations set forth in the CFROD shall be deemed satisfied by the endorsement 
of this PDA Development Plan. The Project will be responding to sea level rise primarily by 
elevating the majority of the ground floors of Building A and Building B to a Design Floor 
Elevation (“DFE”) of 21.5-feet Boston City Base datum (“BCB”), and the Community Park will 
mostly be raised to the same DFE of 21.5-feet BCB. Stormwater infrastructure will be designed 
to reduce the existing peak rates and volumes of stormwater runoff from the PDA Site and will 
also promote stormwater recharge. The stormwater management system for the New Buildings 
will implement a combination of techniques, some of which being evaluated include: green 
infrastructure and low impact development techniques to mitigate and retain stormwater volumes 
where applicable. The New Buildings will also implement strategies at the ground level to 
reduce the urban heat island effect, including pervious cover and high albedo paving materials, 
green infrastructure, and other design features to minimize heat island effect. 

15. 
Public Benefits: The PDA will provide numerous public benefits for the 
Columbia Point neighborhood, Dorchester, and the City of Boston as a whole, both during 
construction, and on an ongoing basis once in operation, as follows: 
a.
Improvements to the Aesthetic Character of the Site: The New Buildings and the 
Community Park will replace portions of a large surface parking lot with high-
quality architecture and landscaped public open space that will visually activate 
and enliven the PDA Site. 
b. Affordability & Housing: Consistent with the Master PDA, the Project will 
exceed the City's applicable Inclusionary Development Policy (“IDP”) by 
providing 20 percent affordable units (approximately 150 units). The Proponent 
intends to work with the Boston Planning Department and the community on the 
appropriate mix of unit types for affordable housing units in accordance with the 
requirements of the IDP. 
c.
Transportation Mitigation: The Proponent will be designing and constructing A 
Street, an entirely new off-site roadway of approximately 15,000 sf, including 
locations for new city utilities; construction of the roadway will be paid for by 
the Proponent at an estimated value/cost of approximately $5 million. The 
Project will also activate an underutilized site with enhanced streetscapes that 
include new street lighting, planting areas, and landscaped sidewalks that meet 
MAAB and ADA standards. 
d. Community Benefits: The Project is committed to providing approximately 7,450 
sf of ground floor space to be provided as community/civic space, the exact 
programming of which will be confirmed in collaboration with the City and 
interested stakeholders. The Project will also partner with local organizations 
and institutions like the Mayor's Office of Arts and Culture, as well as other local 
institutions, to sponsor permanent and rotating/short-term art installations on the 
Project Site by a diverse range of artists. The Project also transforms a site 
largely covered by impervious asphalt surface parking and replaces it with an 
approximately 23,900 sf Community Park that will be dedicated to the public, 
allowing community members an entirely new space within the Columbia Point 
neighborhood for active and passive recreational use. 
e.
Sustainability & Resiliency: Energy conservation and other sustainable design 
measures are integral to the Project. The Proponent is designing the Project to be 
certifiable under LEED-Gold and Passive House PHIUS 2024 standards. The 
Proponent will also incorporate sustainable and healthy design features into the 
Project to preserve and protect the environment. The Proposed Project will 
employ energy- and water-efficient features for mechanical, electrical, 
architectural, and structural systems, as well as materials, where feasible. 
Sustainable design elements relating to building energy management systems, 
lighting, recycling, conservation measures, local building materials, and clean 
construction vehicles will also be included, to the greatest extent practicable. 

f.
Urban Comfort: To mitigate against impacts from additional residents and their 
use of existing public parks/open space, the Project will contribute $1 per sf of 
GFA of residential space to the City of Boston Parks Department, to be delivered 
in lump sum within thirty (30) days after issuance of each applicable occupancy 
permit for each residential building, and to be utilized for the ongoing 
maintenance of Moakley Park. The Proponent is also committed to increasing 
the total tree canopy coverage on the Site, upon full maturity of the new tree 
plantings, by replacing large areas of asphalt-covered surface parking with 
thoughtfully designed and landscaped open space and streetscapes. 
g. Transit Oriented Development: The Project is adjacent to the JFK/UMass MBTA 
Station, which provides easy access to the Site from the surrounding 
neighborhood and other areas of the City and beyond through transit service by 
the MBTA Red Line and three MBTA bus routes, namely the 8, 16, and 41 bus 
lines. The Proponent will enter into a Transportation Access Plan Agreement 
with BTD in which it will commit to Transportation Demand Measures 
consistent with applicable City Guidelines. 
h. Smart Utilities: The Project will comply with the Boston Planning Department’s 
Smart Utility Policy for Article 80 Development Review, as applicable. 
Additionally, in accordance with Boston’s Electric Vehicle (“EV”) Readiness 
Policy, 25 percent of the net new parking spaces in the Proposed Project’s below-
grade garage will be equipped with EV supply equipment, and the remaining 75 
percent of the parking spaces will be EV ready for future installation. 
16. 
Greenbelt Protection Overlay District & Restricted Parking Overlay District: 
The Site is located in both (in part) the GPOD, as established by Article 29 of the Code, and, (in 
whole), the RPOD. Approval of this Development Plan shall constitute compliance with all 
applicable GPOD and RPOD requirements, and, as such, no conditional use permit or further 
review shall be required by the BPDA or the Board of Appeals. 
17. 
Coastal Flooding Resilience Overlay District: The Site is located within the 
CFROD, and approval of this Development Plan and the related Article 80B process for this 
Project shall constitute compliance with all applicable CFROD requirements. 
18. 
Boston Civic Design Commission: The New Buildings required Schematic 
Design Approval by the Boston Civic Design Commission (“BCDC”) pursuant to Article 28 of 
the Code, and were approved by the BCDC on July 1, 2025.
19. 
Applicability: In accordance with Section 80C-9 of the Code, consistency of the 
New Buildings with this Development Plan and the Master PDA shall constitute compliance 
with the dimensional, use, and all other requirements of the Code, to the extent such 
requirements have been addressed in the Development Plan and the Master PDA. Issuance of a 
Certification of Consistency will constitute compliance by the New Buildings and PDA Site with 
all applicable provisions of the Code with respect to Planned Development Areas. 

20. 
Minor Modification to Plans: This Development Plan and the Master PDA set 
forth the dimensional, use, and other zoning requirements for the PDA Site, to the extent such 
requirements have been addressed in this Development Plan. Upon approval of this Development 
Plan, final plans and specifications for each New Building will be submitted to the BPDA 
pursuant to Section 3-1A, Article 80B, and Article 80C of the Code for final design review 
approval and certification as to consistency with this Development Plan, and to other 
governmental agencies for final approval. Subject to consistency with the dimensional 
regulations set forth in this Development Plan and the Master PDA, minor changes may occur to 
a New Building’s design described in this Development Plan without requiring an amendment to 
this Development Plan, as determined by the Director of the BPDA in accordance with Section 
80A-6 of the Code, and subject to the use and dimensional requirements set forth in this 
Development Plan and the Master PDA. No changes to the public benefits arising from the 
community-driven 80B process shall require an amendment to this Development Plan or Master 
PDA, provided that the mitigation and/or community benefits as required under this 
Development Plan or Master PDA are not modified unless approved by the BPDA during Article 
80B review. 
21. 
Development Schedule: The Proponent estimates that construction of the New 
Buildings will take approximately 32 months, and are likely to be constructed in phases. 
22. 
Proponent’s Obligation to Proceed with the Project: Notwithstanding anything 
set forth herein to the contrary, under no circumstances shall the Proponent be obligated to 
proceed with all or any portion of the Project.

This Master PDA proposes development of up to 1.56 million gross square feet across seven (7) new buildings, four of which
will house office/life science uses and three of which will consist of multi-family housing, along with below-grade parking. The
ground floors of all buildings will include a mix of restaurant, retail and/or public space. The existing grocery store will be
relocated to one of the new buildings and remain operational throughout the duration of construction, which is anticipated to
occur in three phases. The Project contemplates the creation of a new roadway network within the Master PDA Area including
new bicycle and pedestrian pathways and the development of other publicly available open space, including four (4) street-level
community parks; a total of approximately 4.7 acres of publicly accessible open space. The Project reimagines the Master PDA
Area as a vibrant mixed-use neighborhood, providing a welcoming and inclusive environment for use by shoppers, area
employees, and area residents and creating a key link from the neighboring Dorchester communities to the greater Columbia
Point area.
The public benefits associated with the Project include: (i) new publicly accessible open space/parks with community-specific programming totaling 1.27
acres, (ii) new approximately 7,500 square foot interior community space to accommodate public programs for job and technical training specifically
geared towards the businesses and tenants that will occupy the Project, (iii) new publicly accessible roadways and bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure
on the Site, (iv) in total, approximately 4.7 acres (54%) of the Master PDA Area includes publicly accessible open spaces, public realm, and roadways, (v)
millions of dollars in housing and jobs linkage payments with a commitment to work with local elected officials and community stakeholders to direct the
linkage payments to local neighborhood, housing and jobs needs, (vi) development of a key link from the Columbia/Savin Hill Neighborhood to UMass,
Bay City, and waterfront areas, (vii) phase-specific financial contributions for projects to improve the surrounding area, which may include infrastructure
improvements along Morrissey Blvd., Kosciuszko Circle, and the JFK/UMass MBTA station, (viii) partnership with local community groups to support home
ownership in the immediate neighborhood, (ix) new affordable housing units in each residential building that comply with or exceed the City’s
Inclusionary Development Policy, (x) a project that will promote private investment in research and development in the life sciences sector and offer new
high paying job and career opportunities, (xi) new retail and service space that will attract and support local retailers and businesses, and (xii) new
construction and permanent jobs.
A transportation study has been developed to understand and mitigate the impacts associated with the Project
and to devise a comprehensive transportation mitigation and improvement plan in the vicinity of the Project that
supports future operations of the Project and provides area-wide transportation improvements to the
Columbia-Morrissey Subdistrict of Boston. The Project is committed to help fund future improvements to the
infrastructure along Morrissey Blvd., Kosciuszko Circle and at the JFK/UMass MBTA Station to mitigate the impacts
of the Project. Within the Project boundary, all new streets have been designed to meet Boston Complete Streets
guidance and promote safe pedestrian, bicycle, and vehicular circulation. As the site is located one-tenth of a mile
from the JFK/UMass MBTA Station, an emphasis will be placed on encouraging the use of public transportation for
employees, visitors, and residents.

The Project seeks to create a vibrant mixed-use neighborhood in what is currently an unwelcoming area dominated by a congested
Morrisey Blvd. thoroughfare and uninspired buildings lacking character and any publicly accessible open space. The Project will provide a
welcoming and inclusive environment for use by shoppers, employees, and area residents as a workplace hub for life sciences,
complimented by residential housing and enlivened publicly accessible open spaces. The neighborhood will center around the newly
created Main Street, drawing attention away from Morrissey Blvd. and on to an activated tree lined streetscape with retail, restaurants
with café zones and generous pedestrian friendly sidewalks. A mix of local small business retail will be bolstered by the anchor grocery
store helping draw visitors and residents alike into the Project Site. The publicly accessible park spaces will provide a much needed
amenity for the local community and will include spaces for family and community programing as well as inviting areas to play and relax.
Building heights will scale up as they approach the norther end of the Site adjacent to the JFK/UMass station, locating the greater density
closer to the highly proximate public transportation. A blend of building facades highlighting the variety of uses will create architectural
diversity within the site. When complete, the development will form a key link from the Columbia/Savin Hill Neighborhood to UMass, Bay
City, and waterfront areas.
There are no historic resources on the Project Site listed in the State and National Registers of Historic Places or
included in the Inventory of Historic and Archeological Assets of the Commonwealth.
The Project Site currently contains multiple commercial buildings served by public utilities. The existing
infrastructure surrounding the Project Site, including sanitary sewer, storm drainage, water, gas, electric and
telecommunications, is anticipated to have adequate capacity to service the Project needs.

1. 
Development Plan: Pursuant to Section 3-1A.a and Article 80C of the Boston 
Zoning Code (the “Code”), this plan constitutes the Planned Development Area Development 
Plan (the “Development Plan”) for a Planned Development Area Overlay District (the “PDA 
Overlay District”) containing approximately 97,739 square feet (2.24 acres) commonly referred 
to as 75 Morrissey Avenue in the Dorchester neighborhood (the “Site”). The Site is more 
particularly described in Section 3, below, and in Exhibits A & B attached hereto. The 
Proponent (as defined below) proposes to construct two new residential buildings with a mix of 
ground-floor commercial uses, amenity and community/civic spaces, and subgrade parking, 
along with an approximately 23,900 sf community park and on- and off-site roadway 
improvements (collectively, the “Project”). But for the off-site roadway improvements 
specifically set forth herein, the Project makes up the “Planned Development Area” or “PDA” 
for which this Development Plan will constitute and provide the permanent zoning. 
This Development Plan sets forth the proposed location and appearance of structures, 
open spaces, uses, densities and dimensions of structures, traffic circulation, parking and loading 
facilities, and other requirements applicable to the PDA. Capitalized terms used but not defined 
herein shall have the meanings assigned to such terms in the Code as in effect as of the date 
hereof, without giving effect to any subsequent amendments to the Code. 
This Development Plan consists of seven pages of text plus attachments designated 
Exhibits A through E. All references to this Development Plan contained herein shall pertain 
only to such pages and exhibits. This Development Plan shall constitute permanent zoning for 
the Site in accordance with Section 3-1A and Article 80C of the Code and is intended to address 
all requirements of the Code applicable to the Site and the Project. 
2. 
The Proponent: The Proponent of the Project is Copper Mill Morrissey, LLC 
and POB CC 75 Morrissey LLC, (collectively, with its successors and assigns, “Proponent”). 
The business address, telephone number and designated contact for the Proponent is:

3. 
PDA Site: The PDA Site totals approximately 97,739 square feet (2.24 acres), 
and is bounded by William T. Morrissey Boulevard to the east, the former Boston Globe 
headquarters building now known as “Southline” to the south, Interstate Highway 93 to the west, 
and 55 Morrissey Boulevard to the north. The Site is currently improved with a single-story 
vacant commercial building with large areas of impervious surface parking. 
The PDA Site is located within the Community Commercial zoning subdistrict of the 
Dorchester Neighborhood District as governed by Article 65 of the Code, as well as (i) a 
Restricted Parking Overlay District (“RPOD”) established by Section 3-1A.c of the Code, (ii) the 
Coastal Flood Resilience Overlay District (“CFROD”) established by Article 25A of the Code, 
and (iii) eastern portions of the Site along Morrissey Boulevard are located within the Morrissey 
Boulevard Greenbelt Protection Overlay district (“GPOD”) established by Article 29 of the 
Code. Pursuant to Section 3-1A(a) and Section 65-28, Planned Development Areas are permitted 
within the area that includes the PDA Site, and the Project is subject to the overriding zoning 
regulations set forth in Master Planned Development Area No. 146, entitled Columbia Point 
Crossing Master Pan, dated December 14, 2023, which includes an approximately 8.9 acre area 
including 35-45 Morrissey Boulevard, 55 Morrissey Boulevard, and the Site (the “Master 
PDA”). 
4. 
New Building Project: The Proponent proposes the development of two new 
residential buildings containing approximately 754 residential units, which are (i) “Building A”, 
an 18-story building containing up to 335,000 square feet of gross floor area (“GFA”) and 
including residential use, ground-floor commercial uses, amenity and community/civic spaces, 
and an up to three-level structured below-grade parking facility accommodating off-street 
parking for approximately 179 vehicles, and (ii) “Building B”, an 18-story building containing 
up to 320,000 square feet of GFA and including residential use, ground-floor commercial uses, 
amenity and community/civic spaces, and an up to three-level structured below-grade parking 
facility accommodating off-street parking for approximately 235 vehicles (each a “New 
Building”, and collectively the “New Buildings”). The New Buildings will improve upon the 
existing surface parking and vacant single-story building it is replacing. 
5. 
Proposed Locations and Appearance of New Buildings: Selected elevations 
attached hereto as Exhibit C illustrate each New Building’s general appearance. Building A and 
Building B respond to both the immediate context of the highway and the ocean side, and the 
broader environmental characteristics of the area. Building A acts as a buffer between Interstate 
93 and the Community Park, and draws on the sweeping curve of Interstate 93 to define the main 
massing of the building while creating a stepped down massing and angled form along the 
Community Park to create an inviting public realm. Building B creates a strong orthogonal street 
presence along Morrissey Boulevard, thus allowing the building massing to act as a 
corresponding massing to Building A, while similarly breaking up and stepping down the 
massing towards the Community Park. While both Building A and Building B have unique 

expressions tailored to their placement on the Site, they each have a proximate and physical 
connection to each other, and the surrounding urban context. 
6. 
Proposed Density and Dimensions of Structures: The range of dimensional 
requirements for the Project are as set forth in the Master PDA, and specifically for the New 
Buildings are (i) the maximum site-wide FAR for the entire approximately 8.9 acre Master PDA 
site area is 4.0 which shall include the GFA as set forth in the New Buildings, and (ii) the 
Maximum Height, as such term is defined in the Master PDA, is 206 for Building B and 204 feet 
for Building A. 
The New Buildings will contain up to 655,000 square feet of GFA1. See Exhibit D for massing 
diagram. Accordingly, this results in an FAR of less than the maximum 4.0 allowed across the 
full Master PDA area. Building A will have a Maximum Height of up to 206 feet, and Building 
B will have a Maximum Height of up to 204 feet. The Maximum Building Height and FAR set 
out above are the only dimensional requirements applicable to the PDA Site pursuant to the 
Master PDA. All other dimensional or design requirements of the Code are not be applicable to 
the PDA Site and are superseded by this Development Plan and the Master PDA. The Project 
shall be subject to design, environmental and other development review by the BPDA, and 
aspects of the Project approved as part of such review shall be and hereby are deemed to be the 
dimensional and design requirements applicable to the New Buildings and are hereby 
incorporated in this Development Plan. 
7. 
Proposed Open Space and Landscaping: The Project will revitalize an area that 
is currently an open asphalt surface parking lot by providing an approximately 23,900 square 
foot community park (“Community Park”) that will be open to the public in perpetuity. The 
Project will provide additional landscape improvements that will be constructed 
contemporaneously with each of the New Buildings, including the expansion of the Site’s 
pedestrian and bicycle network to provide improved pedestrian and bike access between 
neighboring properties and JFK/UMass Red Line/South Shore Commuter Rail Station. 
8. 
Proposed Uses: The New Building will be used primarily for residential use and 
parking facilities (as accessory, ancillary, and principal uses). In addition to the uses listed 
above, all of the uses listed in Exhibit E shall be permitted as of right on the full PDA Site. 
9. 
Proposed Traffic Circulation: The Project will continue to be served by the 
existing curb-cuts along the Morrissey Boulevard, and will create a new, off-site, “A Street” 
public roadway connecting to Morrissey Boulevard and running adjacent to the northern edge of 
the Site, and a new “West Street” roadway along and within the western edge of the Site. Access 
to the below-grade parking spaces will be provided for Building A from the West Street, and for 
Building B from A Street. A pick-up/drop-off area will be provided along portions of A Street. 
Rights to A street for the Project are being provided by the owner of 55 Morrissey Boulevard 
through binding legal agreements. 
1 All square footages are approximate. GFA is defined in Article 2 of the Code and specifically excludes 
from calculation floor area devoted to mechanical equipment, storage, below-grade parking areas and service and 
loading areas. 

10. 
Proposed Parking and Loading Facilities: The New Buildings will each include 
three levels of below-grade parking for approximately 414 vehicles. All loading and service 
activity will be actively managed by the building transportation coordinator, and the New 
Buildings will provide both secure bicycle parking spaces and publicly accessible bicycle 
parking spaces. 
11. 
Access to Public Transportation: The Site is well served by the Massachusetts 
Bay Transportation Authority (“MBTA”); it is approximately 1,300 feet from the JFK/UMass 
Station. This Station is a commuter hub providing connection between three commuter rail lines 
(Greenbush, Kingston/Plymouth, and Fall River/New Bedford), the MBTA Red Line, and three 
MBTA bus routes (Number 8, 16, and 41). 
12. 
Signage: The signage program for the New Buildings shall be subject to design, 
environmental and other development review by the BPDA, and any sign approved as part of 
such review shall be deemed to be in compliance with the Development Plan and the Master 
PDA. 
13. 
Development Review Procedures: All aspects of the Project design will be 
subject to ongoing development and design review and approval by the BPDA. 
14. 
Green Building and Resiliency Measures: The New Buildings are subject to 
Article 37 (Green Buildings) of the Code, pursuant to Section 80B Large Project Review. The 
New Buildings will meet the requirements necessary to achieve at least a Gold-level certifiability 
using LEEDv4 rating system and Passive House PHIUS 2024 standards, and will be designed 
with energy-efficient HVAC and lighting equipment and systems and will incorporate other 
potential energy conservation measures, as reasonable and feasible. 
Portions of the PDA Site are located within the FEMA-designated Special Flood Hazard 
Area, Zone AE on the FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM [Community Panel No. 
25025C0083J, effective March 16, 2016]). Portions of the Site are also similarly included in the 
CFROD district, and, as set forth below and reviewed during the related Article 80B process for 
the Project, all regulations set forth in the CFROD shall be deemed satisfied by the endorsement 
of this PDA Development Plan. The Project will be responding to sea level rise primarily by 
elevating the majority of the ground floors of Building A and Building B to a Design Floor 
Elevation (“DFE”) of 21.5-feet Boston City Base datum (“BCB”), and the Community Park will 
mostly be raised to the same DFE of 21.5-feet BCB. Stormwater infrastructure will be designed 
to reduce the existing peak rates and volumes of stormwater runoff from the PDA Site and will 
also promote stormwater recharge. The stormwater management system for the New Buildings 
will implement a combination of techniques, some of which being evaluated include: green 
infrastructure and low impact development techniques to mitigate and retain stormwater volumes 
where applicable. The New Buildings will also implement strategies at the ground level to 
reduce the urban heat island effect, including pervious cover and high albedo paving materials, 
green infrastructure, and other design features to minimize heat island effect. 

15. 
Public Benefits: The PDA will provide numerous public benefits for the 
Columbia Point neighborhood, Dorchester, and the City of Boston as a whole, both during 
construction, and on an ongoing basis once in operation, as follows: 
a.
Improvements to the Aesthetic Character of the Site: The New Buildings and the 
Community Park will replace portions of a large surface parking lot with high-
quality architecture and landscaped public open space that will visually activate 
and enliven the PDA Site. 
b. Affordability & Housing: Consistent with the Master PDA, the Project will 
exceed the City's applicable Inclusionary Development Policy (“IDP”) by 
providing 20 percent affordable units (approximately 150 units). The Proponent 
intends to work with the Boston Planning Department and the community on the 
appropriate mix of unit types for affordable housing units in accordance with the 
requirements of the IDP. 
c.
Transportation Mitigation: The Proponent will be designing and constructing A 
Street, an entirely new off-site roadway of approximately 15,000 sf, including 
locations for new city utilities; construction of the roadway will be paid for by 
the Proponent at an estimated value/cost of approximately $5 million. The 
Project will also activate an underutilized site with enhanced streetscapes that 
include new street lighting, planting areas, and landscaped sidewalks that meet 
MAAB and ADA standards. 
d. Community Benefits: The Project is committed to providing approximately 7,450 
sf of ground floor space to be provided as community/civic space, the exact 
programming of which will be confirmed in collaboration with the City and 
interested stakeholders. The Project will also partner with local organizations 
and institutions like the Mayor's Office of Arts and Culture, as well as other local 
institutions, to sponsor permanent and rotating/short-term art installations on the 
Project Site by a diverse range of artists. The Project also transforms a site 
largely covered by impervious asphalt surface parking and replaces it with an 
approximately 23,900 sf Community Park that will be dedicated to the public, 
allowing community members an entirely new space within the Columbia Point 
neighborhood for active and passive recreational use. 
e.
Sustainability & Resiliency: Energy conservation and other sustainable design 
measures are integral to the Project. The Proponent is designing the Project to be 
certifiable under LEED-Gold and Passive House PHIUS 2024 standards. The 
Proponent will also incorporate sustainable and healthy design features into the 
Project to preserve and protect the environment. The Proposed Project will 
employ energy- and water-efficient features for mechanical, electrical, 
architectural, and structural systems, as well as materials, where feasible. 
Sustainable design elements relating to building energy management systems, 
lighting, recycling, conservation measures, local building materials, and clean 
construction vehicles will also be included, to the greatest extent practicable. 

f.
Urban Comfort: To mitigate against impacts from additional residents and their 
use of existing public parks/open space, the Project will contribute $1 per sf of 
GFA of residential space to the City of Boston Parks Department, to be delivered 
in lump sum within thirty (30) days after issuance of each applicable occupancy 
permit for each residential building, and to be utilized for the ongoing 
maintenance of Moakley Park. The Proponent is also committed to increasing 
the total tree canopy coverage on the Site, upon full maturity of the new tree 
plantings, by replacing large areas of asphalt-covered surface parking with 
thoughtfully designed and landscaped open space and streetscapes. 
g. Transit Oriented Development: The Project is adjacent to the JFK/UMass MBTA 
Station, which provides easy access to the Site from the surrounding 
neighborhood and other areas of the City and beyond through transit service by 
the MBTA Red Line and three MBTA bus routes, namely the 8, 16, and 41 bus 
lines. The Proponent will enter into a Transportation Access Plan Agreement 
with BTD in which it will commit to Transportation Demand Measures 
consistent with applicable City Guidelines. 
h. Smart Utilities: The Project will comply with the Boston Planning Department’s 
Smart Utility Policy for Article 80 Development Review, as applicable. 
Additionally, in accordance with Boston’s Electric Vehicle (“EV”) Readiness 
Policy, 25 percent of the net new parking spaces in the Proposed Project’s below-
grade garage will be equipped with EV supply equipment, and the remaining 75 
percent of the parking spaces will be EV ready for future installation. 
16. 
Greenbelt Protection Overlay District & Restricted Parking Overlay District: 
The Site is located in both (in part) the GPOD, as established by Article 29 of the Code, and, (in 
whole), the RPOD. Approval of this Development Plan shall constitute compliance with all 
applicable GPOD and RPOD requirements, and, as such, no conditional use permit or further 
review shall be required by the BPDA or the Board of Appeals. 
17. 
Coastal Flooding Resilience Overlay District: The Site is located within the 
CFROD, and approval of this Development Plan and the related Article 80B process for this 
Project shall constitute compliance with all applicable CFROD requirements. 
18. 
Boston Civic Design Commission: The New Buildings required Schematic 
Design Approval by the Boston Civic Design Commission (“BCDC”) pursuant to Article 28 of 
the Code, and were approved by the BCDC on July 1, 2025.
19. 
Applicability: In accordance with Section 80C-9 of the Code, consistency of the 
New Buildings with this Development Plan and the Master PDA shall constitute compliance 
with the dimensional, use, and all other requirements of the Code, to the extent such 
requirements have been addressed in the Development Plan and the Master PDA. Issuance of a 
Certification of Consistency will constitute compliance by the New Buildings and PDA Site with 
all applicable provisions of the Code with respect to Planned Development Areas. 

20. 
Minor Modification to Plans: This Development Plan and the Master PDA set 
forth the dimensional, use, and other zoning requirements for the PDA Site, to the extent such 
requirements have been addressed in this Development Plan. Upon approval of this Development 
Plan, final plans and specifications for each New Building will be submitted to the BPDA 
pursuant to Section 3-1A, Article 80B, and Article 80C of the Code for final design review 
approval and certification as to consistency with this Development Plan, and to other 
governmental agencies for final approval. Subject to consistency with the dimensional 
regulations set forth in this Development Plan and the Master PDA, minor changes may occur to 
a New Building’s design described in this Development Plan without requiring an amendment to 
this Development Plan, as determined by the Director of the BPDA in accordance with Section 
80A-6 of the Code, and subject to the use and dimensional requirements set forth in this 
Development Plan and the Master PDA. No changes to the public benefits arising from the 
community-driven 80B process shall require an amendment to this Development Plan or Master 
PDA, provided that the mitigation and/or community benefits as required under this 
Development Plan or Master PDA are not modified unless approved by the BPDA during Article 
80B review. 
21. 
Development Schedule: The Proponent estimates that construction of the New 
Buildings will take approximately 32 months, and are likely to be constructed in phases. 
22. 
Proponent’s Obligation to Proceed with the Project: Notwithstanding anything 
set forth herein to the contrary, under no circumstances shall the Proponent be obligated to 
proceed with all or any portion of the Project.

described in Section 17 of the Second Amendment, the “Proponent may seek to expand 

3 
 
the Project in the future to accommodate additional hotel, retail or other uses on the Site. 
In such event, the Proponent will seek to amend this Development Plan accordingly at 
such time.” 
 
8. Proposed Densities and Dimensions of New Hotel. The dimensional requirements 
applicable to the Project, in lieu of the underlying zoning requirements, are as follows. 
The Second Amendment does not index any specific Floor Area Ratio (“FAR”) 
requirements for individual projects within its Site Area (defined by the PDA as “Project 
Components”). Rather, it merely allows for up to 899,000 Gross Floor Area (“GFA”) of 
new development to be allocated among all Project Components, “as long as the total 
Gross Floor Area does for all structures on the Site does not exceed the total maximum 
Gross Square Floor Area.” Thus, to comply with the PDA, the Third Amendment’s 
proposed new hotel GFA of approximately 150,000, when added to total GFA of Hotels I 
and II of approximately 328,645 GFA, and the potential Parking Garage, must not exceed 
899,000 total GFA. The total GSF of the three hotels in this Third Amendment is 
approximately 478,645 GFA, well below the maximum GFA of 899,000. See Article 9 
and its footnote #1 of the Second Amendment (“Proposed Densities and Dimensions of 
Structures”). 
 
9. Proposed Traffic Circulation. 
 
As shown on the Site Plan and the Design Plans, the Proponent proposes to modify the 
Anchor Street, as previously developed with the prior phase, to more appropriately 
accommodate the new Hotel main entrance location, as well as to facilitate the additional 
drop-off and pick up for guests arriving or leaving the third Hotel, as well as ride-share 
vehicles similarly accommodating guest movement. The modification from perpendicular 
“head-in” parking spaces to more traditional parallel parking / curb-site short term 
parking spaces will ease traffic congestion, reduce potential traffic conflicts, and 
generally align Anchor Street, as a private way controlled by the MCCA, with typical 
City of Boston public street configurations at similar Hotel and hospitality locations 
throughout the city. 
 
10. Proposed Parking and Loading Facilities. 
 
The Proponent proposes to continue the existing use of the “Temporary Parking Area” 
defined in the prior Phase and documented as a component of the Planned Development 
Area No. 50 until such time as a permanent parking structure is developed. The current 
two (2) hotels utilize approximately 120 spaces within the 350 space surface parking area 
immediately southwest of the Element Hotel. The Project’s Hotel III intends to lease an 
additional seventy-five (75) parking spaces within the 350 space “Temporary Parking 
Area” from the MCCA, to accommodate additional parking demand associated with the 
new Hotel III. As outlined in the original Phase approvals, this “Temporary Parking 
Area” will remain available for parking use, under the executed leases, until such time as 
a permanent structured Parking Garage is developed and made operational, at which time 
the total number of leased spaces for the three (3) hotels will be accommodated within 
such new parking structure. 

4 
 
For a period of up to five (5) years, beginning with commencement of construction of the 
Parking Garage, said approximately 195 spaces may be located from time to time on the 
BCEC South Parking Lot, which is located between the BCEC and Cypher Street, and/or 
on other land owned and/or controlled by the Proponent within a 0.50 mile radius of the 
Site (the area in which any of said approximately 195 spaces are located from time to 
time during such period, the "Temporary Parking Area"). Notwithstanding anything to 
the contrary in the Code, during such period, (a) the use of the Temporary Parking Area 
for such use will be ancillary to the Project, (b) the Temporary Parking Area shall be 
deemed a part of Planned Development Area No. 50, and (c) such ancillary parking use 
shall be a permitted use under this Development Plan. The Proponent's use of the 
Temporary Parking Area shall be terminated when the Parking Garage is open for 
operation and thus available for use by workers, visitors and guests of the Hotel 
Development and the BCEC, and, at such time, the Temporary Parking 
Area shall no longer be deemed a part of Planned Development Area No. 50. 
 
11. Signage. Signs shall be permitted on the Site as approved from time to time through BPD 
Article 80 design review. Such signage may include electronic signs. The Proponent shall 
be required to submit a Comprehensive Sign Design Plan, in accordance with Article 11 of 
the Code, to the BPD. 
 
12. Access to Public Transportation. The Site is well-served by public transportation. It is 
located in close proximity to the World Trade Center Silver Line station. This proximity to 
the Silver Line, which serves South Station and downtown Boston, as well as Logan 
Airport, is particularly important for out-of-town guests at the hotels. In addition, the Site 
is accessible to and from South Station, which is located within one (1) mile of the Site, by 
pedestrians and by MBTA bus service (Route 7), which runs to and from South Station and 
stops within one block of the Site. 
 
13. Public Benefits. The public benefits of the Project include those described below: 
 
a. Economic Development: The Project will result in significant financial 
benefits to the city and the region in fulfillment of the MCCA’s public purpose. It 
constitutes an important component of enhancing the City's ability to become one 
of the primary locations for national conventions and meetings as well as a 
significant player in the international conventions marketplace. Such increased use 
of the BCEC will not only create new jobs at these hotels and the associated retail 
and/or restaurant developments, but also increased economic activity throughout 
the South Boston Seaport District and the City. In addition, the Project would 
significantly contribute to the development of the South Boston Seaport District 
and the "Innovation District," in which the Site is located. 
 
b. Public Realm and Urban Design Benefits: The Project will enliven this currently 
vacant Site and provide an appealing, pedestrian-friendly streetscape in an area of 
the city that is the focus of important redevelopment efforts. The Project is expected 
to include publicly accessible ground-level lobby areas and associated outdoor 
seating. The Project will also include significant streetscape improvements to the 

5 
 
pedestrian realm at and surrounding the Site, including a landscape zone, new 
sidewalks and new street trees, and it will improve abutting streets and sidewalks 
to improve roadway quality, traffic flow, handicapped access and pedestrian safety. 
 
c. Job Creation: The mix of uses at the Project will create a significant number of job 
opportunities at the Site. These jobs will be at a variety of wage and skill levels and 
will boost a range of job sectors, including the hotel and retail/restaurant industries. 
The Project is anticipated to directly create approximately 225 full- and parttime 
construction jobs and 95 full- and part-time hospitality jobs. 
 
d. Sustainable Design. Hotel III will be designed and constructed to meet or exceed 
the rating level of "LEED Gold”. The Project shall comply with the requirements 
of Article 37, Green Buildings, of the Code, and address Article 80’s required 
review and reports on Green Building, Smart Utilities and the like. The Site is also 
situated within the boundaries of the City’s Coastal Flood Resiliency Overlay 
District (“CFROD”), which is regulated by Article 25A of the Zoning Code. Due 
to the Project’s size and scale within the CFROD (for a new Use in excess of 50,000 
gross square feet), it is subject to the requirements of Article 25A and will comply 
with the same. 
 
e. Non Discrimination: Boston Residents Jobs Policy: The Proponent will comply 
with the City of Boston's Boston Residents Construction Jobs Policy with respect 
to hiring Boston residents, minorities, and women for construction jobs. 
 
 
14. Minor Modifications to Plans. This Third Amended and Restated Development Plan sets 
forth the dimensional, use and other zoning requirements for the Project and the Site, to 
the extent such requirements have been addressed in this Development Plan. Once this 
Development Plan is approved, final plans and specifications for the Project will be 
submitted to the BRA pursuant to Section 3-lA, Article 80B, and Article 80C of the Code 
for final design review approval and certification as to consistency with this Development 
Plan, and to other governmental agencies and authorities for final approval. Accordingly, 
subject to consistency with the dimensional and other regulations set forth herein, changes 
may occur to the Project's design described in this Development Plan without requiring an 
amendment to this Development Plan. 
 
15. Development Schedule. The Proponent estimates that construction of Hotel III will 
commence in Fall of 2026 and that the hotels will open in Fall of 2029. 
 
16. Future Development. The Proponent may seek to expand the Project in the future to 
accommodate additional hotel, retail or other uses on the Site. In such event, the Proponent 
will seek to amend this Development Plan accordingly at such time, if necessary. 
 
17. No Duty to Develop the Project. Notwithstanding anything set forth in this Development 
Plan to the contrary, under no circumstances shall the Proponent or any designee thereof 
be obligated to proceed with the Project, or any portion thereof, or, once the Proponent or 

6 
 
any designee thereof does proceed with the Project, or any portion thereof, to complete the 
Project or such portion. 
 
18. Applicability. In accordance with Section 80-C of the Code, consistency of the Project with 
this Development Plan constitutes compliance with the dimensional, use and all other 
requirements of the Code to the extent such requirements have been addressed in this 
Development Plan. To the extent that any aspect of proposed uses and proposed structures 
addressed in this Development Plan are in conflict with any requirement of the Code, this 
Development Plan shall govern. 
 
19. Compliance of Project Components. Compliance of Project Components with the 
requirements of this Development Plan shall be determined based on each Project 
Component's compliance with the requirements of this Development Plan applicable to 
such Project Component. Each Project Component shall receive its own Certification of 
Consistency or Partial Certification of Consistency pursuant to Section 80C-8 of the Code. 
Any owner of an individual Project Component may seek amendment of this Development 
Plan only as to such Project Component in accordance with the procedures prescribed by 
Section 80C-7 of the Code without the consent of any other owner of a Project Component; 
provided, however, that no such amendment shall affect the obligations of the Proponent 
or any designee thereof under any agreements between the Proponent and the BPD. In the 
event that any amendment to this Development Plan proposed by the owner of a Project 
Component is approved, and such amendment affects the overall compliance of the Project 
with this Development Plan, this Development Plan shall be deemed amended with respect 
to the Project as a whole to the extent necessary for the overall Project to comply with this 
Development Plan. 
 
20. Miscellaneous. Unless otherwise set forth herein, all references to terms set forth 
in the Code shall have the meaning set forth in the Code as amended to the effective date 
hereof, and not as the same may be amended hereafter. Except as amended by this Third 
Amendment and the required BPD Design Review process, the Second Amendment, and 
all previous PDA Plans, remain unmodified and in full force and effect.

Location and Description of 
Planned Development Area 
The site is a parcel of land known as 371-401 D Street, consisting 
of a total of approximately 243,181 square feet (approximately 
5.6 acres) located on D Street, South Boston (the “Site”). The 
Site is located across D Street from the Boston Convention and 
Exhibition Center (the "BCEC") and currently includes two (2) 
hotels, known as the Element and Aloft, respectively, a surface 
parking lot and certain undeveloped land area along the MCCA’s 
Butler and Anchor Streets, at the rear of the Site. 
 
This Development Plan amends and restates the Second Amended 
and Restated Development Plan at the Site, which was approved 
by the Boston Redevelopment Authority (the "BRA") on May 16, 
2013, approved and adopted by the Zoning Commission of the 
City of Boston on June 12, 2013, in its entirety (the “Second 
Amendment”; and this amendment is the “Third Amendment”). 
Project 
Under a long-term land lease with the MCCA, the Proponent 
seeks to further revitalize and activate the Site as a next phase of 
development under the PDA, with the construction of a new 
fourteen (14) story hotel structure with up to 438 rooms (keys) of 
approximately 150,000 gross square feet (the “Project” or “Hotel 
III”). The Project’s vehicular parking will be accommodated by 
the existing surface parking lot at the Site. The new hotel 
development will enhance and integrate with the existing 
hospitality uses at the Site, with improved pedestrian 
connectivity for its adjacency to the Element and the Aloft. In 

2 
addition, the Proponent seeks to modify the existing layout of the 
Element Hotel by increasing layout efficiency, resulting in up to 
an additional 20 keys within the existing volume and area of the

Development Plan: In accordance with Section 3-1A, Sections 64-28 through 64-31 and 
Section 80C of the Boston Zoning Code (as in effect on the date hereof, the “Code”), this plan 
constitutes a Development Plan for Planned Development Area No. ___ (the “Development 
Plan”) and sets forth information describing the development of a project (the “Proposed 
Project”) at 41 Berkeley Street in the South End Neighborhood of Boston described in greater 
detail below (the “Project Site”). 
This Development Plan sets forth information on the proposed development of the 
Proposed Project, including the proposed location and appearance of structures, open spaces and 
landscaping, proposed uses, densities, proposed traffic circulation, parking and loading facilities, 
access to public transportation and proposed dimensions of structures. This Development Plan 
provides the zoning for the Proposed Project, which is also undergoing review under Section 
80B of the Code. A Project Notification Form (“PNF”) for the Proposed Project was filed with 
the Boston Redevelopment Authority (now doing business as the Boston Planning & 
Development Agency) (the “BRA”) on September 14, 2020, which commenced a period of 
public review, which concluded on December 29, 2020. A Supplemental Information Document 
(“SID”) was filed with the BRA on September __, 2022 in response to a request for 
Supplemental Information issued by the BRA on March 21, 2021. The Proposed Project is also 
undergoing review by the Boston Civic Design Commission (“BCDC”) in accordance with 
Article 28 of the Code. BCDC approved the design of the Proposed Project on June 7, 2022. 
Based upon that process and approval of this Development Plan, final plans and specifications 
for the Proposed Project will be submitted to the BRA pursuant to Sections 80B and 80C of the 
Code for final design review approval and certification as to consistency with this Development 
Plan. 
This Development Plan consists of thirteen (13) pages of text and Exhibits A – E. All 
references to this Development Plan contained herein shall pertain only to such thirteen (13) 
pages of text and Exhibits A – E. Exhibit D is subject to design, environmental and other 

2 
 
development review by the BRA and by other governmental agencies and authorities, and the 
final design of the Proposed Project as described herein may evolve in the course of such review. 
All references herein to terms set forth in the Code shall have the meanings set forth in the Code, 
as amended to the effective date hereof, and not as the same may be amended hereafter. 
Upon approval, this Development Plan will constitute permanent zoning for the Project 
Site in accordance with Section 3-1A, Section 64-29 and Section 80C of the Code. In accordance 
with Section 80C-8 and 80C-9 of the Code, consistency of the Proposed Project or any Project 
Component with this Development Plan as evidenced by the issuance of one or more 
Certifications of Consistency by the BRA constitutes compliance with the requirements of the 
Code to the extent such requirements have been addressed in this Development Plan. To the 
extent that the Director of the BRA certifies consistency with this Development Plan, the 
Proposed Project or any Project Component, will be deemed to be in compliance with the 
requirements of the Code. 
Proponent: Appleton Berkeley Propco, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, (the 
“Proponent”), an affiliate of Related Beal, LLC, a Boston-based, fully integrated real estate firm 
focused on development and investment opportunities in Boston, with extensive experience and 
expertise in commercial, mixed-use and residential development. The Proponent has an 
agreement with the Benjamin Franklin Cummings Institute of Technology (“BFCIT”), the 
current fee owner of the Project Site, to acquire the Project Site, after having obtained the 
approvals required to enable the Proposed Project’s development.
