Proposed Location: The Project Site is an approximately one and twenty-six tenths (1.26) 
acre parcel of land (approximately 53,425 square feet) located at 41 Berkeley Street, also known 
as the BFCIT Campus. The Project Site is directly bound by Appleton Street to the north, 
Berkeley Street to the west and south, and Tremont Street to the east. The Project Site does not 
include the land and improvements thereon known and numbered 6 and 6A Appleton Street, all 
as more specifically described in the legal description and depicted on the Project Site Plan, 
attached hereto as Exhibit A-1 and Exhibit B-1, respectively 
The Proposed Project contemplates three distinct developments on three separate parcels. 
Each of these development parcels may in the future be owned and developed by individual 

3 
 
developers. After the major discretionary permits for the Proposed Project have been obtained, 
the development of each of these parcels may proceed as the Proponent, in its sole discretion 
determines is appropriate due to market conditions and other factors. The three development 
parcels consist of an approximately 13,916 SF parcel which includes the existing Franklin Union 
Building (the “Franklin Union Parcel”), an approximately 32,508 SF parcel with frontage along 
Tremont Street (the “Senior Care Parcel”), and an approximately 7,002 SF parcel with frontage 
along Appleton Street (the “Appleton Parcel”). The approximate location of the Franklin Union 
Parcel is shown as Lot A1 on the plan attached as Exhibit A-2 and the legal description of the 
Franklin Union Parcel is attached hereto as Exhibit B-2. The approximate location of the Senior 
Care Parcel is shown as Lot A2 on the plan attached as Exhibit A-2 and a legal description of the 
Senior Care Parcel is attached as Exhibit B-3. The approximate location of the Appleton Parcel 
is shown as Lot A3 on the plan attached as Exhibit A-2 and a legal description of the Appleton 
Parcel is attached hereto as Exhibit B-4. 
The Project Site is located in: (i) the Boston Center for the Arts-Franklin Institute 
Community Facilities Subdistrict of the South End Neighborhood Zoning District, the relevant 
underlying zoning controls for which are set forth in Article 64 of the Code; (ii) the Restricted 
Parking Overlay District (“RPOD”) governed by Section 3-1A(c) of the Code; (iii) the Coastal 
Flood Resilience Overlay District (“CFROD”) governed by Article 25A of the Code; and (iv) 
the Groundwater Conservation Overlay District (“GCOD”), governed by Article 32 of the Code. 
The Project Site is eligible for permitting as a Planned Development Area (“PDA”). The Project 
Site is also located within the South End Landmark District, subject to review and approval by 
the South End Landmark District Commission (“SELDC”). 
Location, Appearance and Proposed Dimensions of Structures and Proposed Density: 
The Proposed Project will consist of three buildings totaling approximately 266,460 SF each 
referred to herein as a Project “Component” for purposes of this Article 80 review. 
The various components of the Project are shown on the plans, elevations and drawings 
attached hereto as Exhibit D (collectively, the “Project Plans”), and the three elements of the 
Project are more particularly described as follows (each a “Project Component” and 
collectively, the “Project Components”), with the three components being shown on a plan 
attached hereto as Exhibit D-1: 
Project Components include: 
Senior Care Component to be developed on the Senior Care Parcel will consist of 
approximately 190,300 SF for Senior Care use, a health care use providing a care 
environment for seniors including assisted living and memory care, licensed by the 
Commonwealth of Massachusetts Executive Office of Elder Affairs with approximately 
5,300 SF of ground floor restaurant/retail use. The Senior Care Component will have 
approximately 236 beds and parking for up to approximately 60 vehicles intended to 
serve the Project as a whole. The Senior Care Component will primarily be located 
within the Senior Care Parcel, with the exception of an approximately 9,120 SF portion 
of the Senior Care Component which extends on the fifth through tenth floors into the 
Appleton Street Parcel over a portion of the Appleton Component. Parking will be 
located in a parking garage below the building accessed by an existing curb cut off 

4 
 
Appleton Street. The upper floors will include assisted living and memory care services, 
medication management, wellness, dining and amenity spaces. The main entrance to the 
facility will be on Tremont Street, and a secondary entry will be located in the middle of 
the Project Site to provide an accessible, at-grade entry to the Senior Care Component; 
Franklin Union Building Component to be developed on the Franklin Union Parcel 
will include the renovation and expansion of the existing Franklin Union Building into 
approximately 50,900 SF of residential home ownership use with approximately 2,800 
SF of ground floor retail. The historic facades and the bulk of the existing floors will be 
preserved, and a one-story vertical addition will be added. The 1980s auto-repair 
addition to the existing building will be removed, which will allow for additional 
pedestrian open space on the Project Site. 
Appleton Component to be developed on the Appleton Parcel will include the 
renovation and expansion of 4 Appleton Street into approximately 13,900 SF of income-
restricted and age-restricted residential rental use and an approximately 3,450 SF 
community room occupying the ground floor. 
The Project Components will be reviewed in a coordinated process for the purposes of 
both Article 80B and Article 80C review. As such, each individual Project Component may be 
developed by individual developers who will obtain individual certifications of compliance and 
consistency and execute on its specific plan, including development agreements, with the BRA 
and other city agencies to the extent required. 
The interior of the Project Site will be a publicly accessible landscaped courtyard passage 
providing direct pedestrian access from Berkeley Street to Tremont Street. The landscaping will 
include seating, shade trees and a public park at the corner of Appleton and Tremont streets that 
will augment the community room function. Approximately 24% of the Project Site area will be 
made open and accessible to the public. Sidewalks, street trees and streetscape amenities will be 
designed to Boston Complete Streets guidelines. The Proponent is committed to phasing 
construction to allow for BFCIT’s continued operations on the Project Site following its sale and 
prior to BFCIT’s relocation to Nubian Square. 
The Senior Care Component will have a maximum building height, as calculated 
under the Code and this Development Plan, not to exceed 110 feet. The Franklin Union 
Building Component will have a maximum building height, as calculated under the Code and 
this Development Plan, of 90 feet. The Appleton Building Component will have a maximum 
building height, as calculated under the Code and this Development Plan, of 50 feet. The 
height of each building has been measured from an elevation of 19 feet Boston City Base 
which shall constitute “Grade” as that term is understood in the Code. The Building Height 
of each of the Components are exclusive of rooftop mechanical penthouses, elevator 
penthouses and other rooftop mechanical equipment approximately as depicted per the roof 
plans and elevations in Exhibit D. 
The Floor Area Ratio (“FAR”) of the Proposed Project will not exceed 5.0 as 
calculated pursuant to the Code. All areas provided herein are described in gross floor area 
as such term is used in the definition of “Floor Area Ratio” in the Code; provided further that 

5 
 
such areas devoted to garage use, whether or not within the basement of a building, 
mechanical equipment, storage, service and loading areas, wherever located, are specifically 
excluded for the purposes of determining “Floor Area, Gross”. Furthermore, based upon the 
further division of the Project Site to enable the development of each of the Senior Care 
Component on the Senior Care Parcel, the Franklin Union Building Component on the Franklin 
Union Parcel, and the Appleton Component on the Appleton Parcel, as depicted on Exhibit D-1, 
which may be amended from time to time, the maximum FAR for the Senior Care Component is 
6.02 inclusive of the 9,120 SF which extends into the Appleton Street Parcel which shall only be 
attributable to the Senior Care Parcel; the maximum FAR for the Franklin Union Building 
Component is 3.86; and the maximum FAR for the Appleton Building Component is 2.48. 
The final square footages devoted to each of the uses within the Project Components on 
the Project Site and the mix of uses on the Project Site will vary depending on market conditions 
from time to time. The Proponent retains the right to change certain space within a Project 
Component from one use to another use, and provided such uses are permitted under the 
Development Plan, the dimensions and densities of the Proposed Project shall not exceed those 
that are permitted under the Development Plan, and Proponent obtains the necessary approvals, 
such modification to or conversion of the uses shall not require an amendment to this 
Development Plan. Without limiting the foregoing, adjustments of the boundaries of Project 
Components shall require notice to the BRA but shall not be subject to BRA approval. 
It is contemplated that each Project Component may be separately owned, constructed 
and financed or that portions or all of each Project Component may be further subdivided into 
one or more separate parcels which may be under separate ownership, or one or more of the 
Project Components may be combined to create one single parcel or a condominium ownership 
structure may be created for all or part of the Project Site, all without further BRA action. This 
Development Plan approves any zoning nonconformity created or increased by the separation of 
ownership of individual Project Components, or by the subdivision, re-subdivision, combination, 
or submission to condominium ownership or other forms of ownership of the Project 
Components, provided that (a) the use requirements of this Development Plan are met by the 
resulting parcel or parcels, (b) the Proposed Project’s Site-wide FAR does not exceed the 
maximum density permitted under this Development Plan for the Project Site as a whole, (c) the 
open space, parking and loading space requirements of this Development Plan are met with 
respect to the Project Site as a whole, and (d) the public benefit obligations required by this 
Development Plan and any other agreements entered into by the Proponent as a condition to the 
BRA’s Article 80 approval of the Proposed Project are not modified, nor their implementation 
changed, without the prior written consent of the Director of the BRA, and the scope of the 
public benefit obligations required by this Development Plan and any other agreement entered 
into by the Proponent as a condition of the BRA’s Article 80 approval of the Proposed Project 
are not diminished. Compliance of each Project Component with the requirements of this 
Development Plan shall be determined on an individual Project Component rather than a 
Proposed Project Site-wide basis, except as otherwise expressly provided in this Development 
Plan, and each Project Component will be eligible to receive its own Certification of 
Consistency. The compliance or non-compliance of any one Project Component shall not affect 
the compliance of any other Project Component. 

6 
 
The maximum square footage, maximum building height and FAR set forth above, 
together with the maximum development footprint as set forth in Section 64-29.3 of the Code, 
will be the only dimensional requirements applicable to the Proposed Project and the Project 
Site. All other dimensional requirements of the Code shall not be applicable to the Proposed 
Project and the Project Site and are superseded by this Development Plan. 
Roof Deck and Roof Terraces: The Proposed Project may include roof decks or roof 
terraces on portions of the roofs not occupied by mechanical penthouses. Access to such roof 
decks and roof terraces may be provided by one or more elevators and stairwells also serving 
mechanical penthouses. Notwithstanding the definition of “Building Height” found in Article 
2A and the provisions of Section 64-34 of the Code, any elevator penthouse, mechanical 
equipment, stairway bulkhead or any other roof structure built for the purpose of accessing a roof 
deck or roof terrace, as well as the said roof decks and roof terraces themselves, shall be 
excluded from the calculation of the building height under this Development Plan. 
Proposed Uses: It is currently anticipated that the Proposed Project will be used 
primarily for health care use (Senior Care) and Residential Uses, with ground floor 
Retail/Commercial and Not-for-Profit Affordable Cultural Uses (as described in Exhibit E 
hereto). In addition, the Proposed Project will include parking and loading as described herein. 
The uses will also include additional commercial and residential amenities such as fitness 
facilities, meeting rooms, and roof terraces and roof decks as appropriate. 
Affordable Housing: The Proposed Project will comply with Section 64-29.1(c)1 of the 
Code which requires that a minimum of ten percent (10%) of the residential dwelling units 
included within the Proposed Project will be Affordable Housing delivered on-site, as such 
Affordable Housing is defined in Section 64-41.1 of the Code within each of the Franklin Union 
Building and the Appleton Component. The Proposed Project will in fact provide more than 
twenty percent (20%) of the residential units on site as Affordable Housing as that term is 
understood in the Code and the City’s Inclusionary Development Policy (“IDP”). The Project 
will comply with the requirements of the Code and the City’s IDP and the Proponent will enter 
into an Affordable Rental Housing Agreement and Restriction or an Affordable Housing 
Agreement, depending on whether the Project includes rental or home ownership units. The 
Franklin Union Building Component is anticipated to contain 35 for-sale homeownership units, 
one of which will be affordable in compliance with the IDP and as required in Section 64- 
29.1(c)1 of the Code and the Appleton Component is anticipated to contain sixteen (16) age- 
restricted, rental units, all of which will be affordable in compliance with the IDP and Section 
64-29.1 of the Code. 
The Project has been designed consistent with the provisions of Article 80B of the Code 
which requires projects subject to Large Project Review to incorporate strategies for meeting 
Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing (“AFFH”) goals. Development which is consistent with 
the goals of AFFH ensures the creation and preservation of places for protected classes to live 
and thrive, thus contributing to the City’s planning goals for vibrant, resilient neighborhoods. 
The Project Site, a current institutional development which is not open to the public, presents a 
unique opportunity to take meaningful action to address housing disparities near the Project Site. 
The Proponent has complied with the AFFH requirements, including undertaking an AFFH 
Assessment and completing an AFFH Checklist as part of its Article 80B Large Project Review. 

7 
 
Existing or Start-Up Business & Not-for-Profit Affordable Cultural Space: The Proposed 
Project will comply with Section 64-29.1(c)2 of the Code. The Proponent will develop a 
purpose-built, multi-purpose Community Center on the ground floor of the Appleton Component 
in satisfaction of the requirement set forth in Section 64-29.1c(2) of the Code to provide an 
Affordable Cultural Space as part of the Project. The approximately 3,450 SF Community 
Center will be dedicated for Affordable Cultural Uses as defined in Section 64-41 of the Code to 
meet the City's goals for a creative economy and constitutes more than five percent (5%) of the 
total Gross Floor Area allocated to non-residential uses of any of the Project Components within 
this PDA, above that allowed as-of-right in the underlying CF Zoning Subdistrict (which 
subdistrict would otherwise have an FAR of 4.0.) This multi-purpose Community Center will be 
complemented by a generous outdoor plaza at the corner of Appleton and Tremont streets which 
will afford indoor-outdoor programming opportunities. The space will provide an affordable, 
local gathering space to accommodate small group meetings, large events, gallery and exhibit 
opportunities for local artists, as well as audio-visual connections for rehearsal and concert 
needs, all of which are supportive of the City’s creative economy. The Community Center space 
will not be dedicated to one user, but rather the Proponent will work with the BRA and the 
Mayor’s Office of Arts and Culture (“MOAC”) to identify an Operator/Lessor to manage the 
non-profit facility to meet the needs of the neighborhood. The Proponent, with input from the 
BRA and the MOAC will draft and issue a Request for Interest (“RFI”) and a Request for 
Proposal (“RFP”) to assist in the qualification and selection of the Operator/Lessor. The 
Operator/Lessor will work with the BRA and MOAC to survey, classify, select, and schedule use 
of this space so as to meet the evolving needs of the local South End community in a manner 
which services to support and advance the City’s creative economy and celebrate the 
neighborhood’s cultural assets. 
Proposed Open Spaces and Landscaping: The Proposed Project will comply with Section 
64-29.3 of the Code, and therefore the development footprint shall not cover more than 76% of 
the Project Site. The remaining 24% shall be designed and built to ensure public access or 
enhance the public realm. As an element of such public access, the Proposed Project will include 
a publicly accessible landscaped courtyard passage providing direct pedestrian access from 
Berkeley Street to Tremont Street. The courtyard passage seeks to enhance the public realm by 
connecting the Project’s assemblage of open spaces, tree-lined passages, and welcoming 
courtyards to the neighborhood, encouraging discovery within the unique community plaza 
concept. In addition to this publicly accessible landscaped open space, the Proposed Project will 
include a covered arcade through the courtyard offers shelter for all-season use, further 
encouraging an open ground floor experience with a continuance network of indoor and outdoor 
spaces designed as a destination and a boulevard. A combination of fixed benches and flexible 
furniture is planned in the courtyard to allow the public varying seating options to sit and enjoy 
the courtyard. The Proposed Project also includes an exterior open green lawn space on the 
corner of Appleton Street and Tremont Street with direct access to the Community Center. A 
small plaza including plantings and flexible furniture is included at the corner of Berkeley Street 
and Tremont Street for enjoyment and use by the public. The Ground Floor Plan included in 
Exhibit D shows these access routes through the Project Site. 
Proposed Traffic Circulation: As currently designed, vehicular access to and egress from 
the parking garage entrance will be via an existing Appleton Street curb cut. This access point 

8 
 
will be used by passenger cars and select service vehicles delivering to the Senior Care 
Component and the Franklin Union Building Component. The primary access for the Senior 
Care Component will be at the main building entry on Tremont Street, where short-term parking 
spaces will allow for the safe pick-up and drop-off of visitors to the Senior Care Component. A 
secondary service entry on Tremont Street adjacent to the Senior Care Component lobby will be 
used for food service deliveries and emergency vehicles. Lastly, another vehicular access point 
will be at the driveway off of Berkeley Street. This driveway provides access to the at-grade, 
ADA-accessible arrival court which will be used by select passenger vehicles servicing the 
Senior Care Component. The Franklin Union Building Component will utilize the existing at-
grade entries on Berkeley Street to create accessible accommodations to both the residential and 
retail entries. Drop-off and pick-up will occur on Berkeley Street, with all loading, service and 
parking for the building accessed via the rear of the Property at the service drive on Appleton 
Street. The affordable, residential units in the Appleton Component will be accessed and 
serviced from Appleton Street. The ground floor Community Center in the Appleton Component 
will be accessed via the new, landscaped passageway facing Tremont Street. An additional 
back-of-house access point will be provided off of Appleton Street to accommodate service 
functions. The Proponent will enter into a Transportation Access Plan Agreement with the 
Boston Transportation Department which will further describe the proposed traffic circulation 
patterns for the Proposed Project. 
Proposed Parking and Loading Facilities: The Project Site is located within the RPOD 
established in accordance with Section 3-1A(c) of the Code. There are no existing on-site 
parking spaces but there is an existing on-campus automotive garage. The Project proposes to 
retrofit this garage entrance and construct a garage for up to approximately 60 vehicles to be 
shared among the Senior Care Component occupants, staff and visitors and residents of the 
Franklin Union Building Component and/or visitors to the Proposed Project and, as on-site 
demand allows, made available for sale or lease to area residents. 
The Project will provide two distinct loading areas for deliveries serving the various 
residential, retail, and health care uses on the ground floor. The Tremont Street service entry in 
the Senior Care Component will be used for food service deliveries, emergency vehicles and 
occasional moving services. The service drive and garage beneath the Senior Care Component is 
expected to accommodate all other service needs, including loading for the Franklin Union 
Building Component. A dedicated receiving area for the Franklin Union Building Component 
will be located at the east side of the building, at the entry to the Proposed Project’s below-grade 
garage, directly adjacent to the service drive lane on Appleton Street. Loading and service 
(including move-in/move out) for the Appleton Building Component will occur on Appleton 
Street within the on-street parking spaces. Trash pickup will be accommodated on Appleton 
Street with dumpsters rolled out to the street. Pursuant to Section 64-36 of the Code, any parking 
and loading shall be approved in connection with the BRA’s Large Project Review under Section 
80B of the Code. This Development Plan authorizes the parking in compliance with the 
provisions of the RPOD without the need for any relief from the Board of Appeal. 
Bicycle Accommodation: In accordance with the City of Boston Bicycle Guidelines, and 
to encourage bicycling as an alternative mode of transportation, the Proponent will provide 
secure bicycle spaces at a rate of one space per residential unit, 0.5 spaces per health care unit, 
and one space per 3,000 sf of retail/cultural space. Additionally, the Project will provide outdoor 

9 
 
publicly accessible spaces for visitors at a rate of one for every five residential or health care 
units, one per 5,000 sf of retail/cultural space. In accordance with BTD guidelines as well as to 
further support the expansion of bicycle sharing, the Project will make a bike share contribution 
proportional to the size of the development by installing a new bike bay station either on-site or 
within the neighborhood, the location of which will be determined in coordination with BTD. 
Access to Public Transportation: The Proposed Project is located in close proximity to 
several MBTA bus routes and other transportation hubs, including the MBTA’s Silver Line 
along Washington Street and the Back Bay Orange Line Station. MBTA bus routes 9 and 43 
make stops at the East Berkeley Street corner of the Project Site. In addition, the Red Line 
Station at Broadway, the MBTA’s Silver Line along Washington Street and the Orange Line 
Station at Tufts Medical Center are all within walking distance. 
Signage: The signage program for the Proposed Project shall be subject to design, 
environmental and other development review by the BPDA, and any signage approved as part of 
such review shall be deemed to be in compliance with the Development Plan. 
Development Review Procedures: All design plans for the Proposed Project are subject 
to ongoing design and development review and approval by the BPDA. Such review will be 
conducted in accordance with Large Project Review under Section 80B of the Code. 
Urban and Public Benefits: The Proposed Project will generate many public benefits and 
satisfy the requirements of Section 64-13 of the Code, including by redeveloping an 
underutilized institutional site into a pedestrian-friendly environment that preserves and 
renovates the existing Franklin Union Building; provides home ownership opportunities for the 
South End neighborhood; provides a much-needed Senior Care facility; and delivers age-
restricted affordable housing to allow seniors in the community to age in place. Among its many 
other improvements, the Proposed Project will result in the following benefits: 
 Creation of up to 51 new residential units within approximately one-quarter mile of the 
MBTA Silver and Orange Lines and bus routes. 
 Increase of the City’s affordable housing stock, with a particular emphasis on providing 
housing for elderly residents. 
 Creation of not-for-profit Affordable Cultural Space, pursuant to Section 64-29.1(c)2 of 
the Code to provide a much-needed resource for the South End community. 
 Creation of approximately 500 construction jobs and up to 200 new permanent jobs. 
 Generation of additional property taxes following completion of the Proposed Project, 
given the conversion of the Project Site from tax-exempt use to a mix of residential and 
health care uses, thus resulting in a substantial increase from the historic tax revenues 
provided by the underdeveloped Project Site. 
The Proposed Project will provide a variety of urban design benefits to the surrounding 
neighborhood, including: 

10 
 
 Creating transparency and connectivity within a previously gated, underutilized parcel 
and transforming it into a vibrant mixed-use development in a key area of the South End. 
 Introduce street level activity along all street frontages, by providing ground-floor retail 
in the Senior Care Component facing Tremont Street, as well as the publicly accessible 
retail/restaurant space in the renovated Franklin Union Building Component and the 
Affordable Cultural Space in the Appleton Component. Some of the retail will wrap the 
corner onto Berkeley Street, which is a “Neighborhood Connector” street. Appleton 
Street is a “Neighborhood Residential” street and as such will retain its quieter, 
neighborhood character. 
 Providing building design and placement that complements the adjacent Atelier 505 
condominium building and the Castle Square complex by putting the tallest elements at 
the Berkeley-Tremont corner across from the Atelier 505 tower and providing a street 
wall along Tremont Street to echo the rhythmic street wall of Castle Square. The height 
of the new affordable housing along Appleton Street will match the height of the existing 
residential brownstones. 
 The assemblage of buildings on the site creates an internal passageway and courtyard 
allowing pedestrian passage from Berkeley Street through to Tremont Street. This interior 
public way will be designed to be publicly accessible with covered passages, planters, 
seating areas, green space and trees. This through block connection is a common feature 
of the South End and a key part of the planning approach to the Project. 
 Providing an improved streetscape with street trees and new lighting that will be 
activated with new retail and restaurant space, as well as providing a pedestrian friendly 
environment on both Tremont and East Berkeley Street with through block connections 
and passageways. 
 Revitalizing an underutilized urban area and reinvigorating land formerly dedicated to 
institutional uses, allowing for the optimum utilization of land which will further the 
connection of the South End Neighborhood with the Chinatown and Downtown 
Neighborhoods. 
The Proposed Project will provide a variety of transportation, streetscape and open space 
benefits to the surrounding neighborhood, including: 
 The Project proposes to support or install a BLUEbikes bicycle sharing station near or on 
the Project Site in coordination with BTD to help further expand the extensive bike share 
network in the neighborhood. 
 The Project proposes public realm improvements along Berkeley Street to improve 
pedestrian safety, increase bicycle connectivity and widen the sidewalk. A curb bump out 
in the area of Warren Avenue will allow for a larger public realm abutting the Site and 
addresses key safety concerns of the neighborhood at the unsignalized intersection 
crossing. Along the Project Site’s Berkeley frontage, a raised bicycle track and buffered 

11 
 
bicycle lane will be constructed extending the Tremont Street bicycle network now under 
construction. 
 The Project proposes to construct a curb extension at both the corners of Appleton Street 
and Tremont Street and Berkeley Street and Appleton Street to create additional areas for 
public use with landscaping, street furniture and amenities. Along Appleton Street the 
Project also proposes to create a dedicated bicycle lane. 
 On Tremont Street the Project is proposing a raised cycle track within the pick-up/drop-
off area. This public amenity will benefit the community by providing for safe pick-
up/drop-off activity for the Proposed Project and other Tremont Street users and alleviate 
congestion from Tremont Street double parking. 
 The proposed on-site courtyard and pedestrian passageway through the center of the 
Project Site will add valuable connections to the pedestrian network allowing for 
alternative quiet routes through the South End neighborhood. 
Groundwater Conservation: The Proposed Project is located within the GCOD governed 
by Article 32 of the Code. The Proposed Project will comply with the standards and 
requirements set forth in Article 32 of the Code. The Proponent shall obtain a written 
determination from the Boston Water and Sewer Commission (“BWSC”) as to whether the 
Proposed Project meets the standards and requirements of Article 32. In addition, the Proponent 
will demonstrate that the Proposed Project meets the requirements of Section 32-6 of the Code 
by obtaining a stamped certification from a Massachusetts registered engineer that the 
requirements of Section 32-6 of the Code are met. The Proponent will provide both a copy of 
the written determination from BWSC and a copy of the stamped certification from a 
Massachusetts registered engineer to the BPDA and the Boston Groundwater Trust prior to the 
issuance of a Certification of Consistency. As such, the Proposed Project will be deemed to be 
in compliance with Article 32 of the Code and will not need a conditional use permit from the 
Board of Appeal for Article 32 purposes. 
Coastal Floor Resilience Overlay District: The Project Site is located within the CFROD 
as established by Article 25A of the Code. The Project will include facilities to promote 
resiliency in accordance with the requirements of Article 25A, including elevating each of the 
Buildings. The proposed elevation of approximately 19 feet BCB meets the site-specific Sea-
Level Rise Design Flood Elevation (SLR-DFE) under Article 25A for the Senior Care 
Component and the proposed elevation of approximately 20 feet BCB is consistent in all material 
terms with the site specific SLR-DFE under Article 25A for the Franklin Union Building 
Component and the Appleton Component. To the extent relief from the provisions of Article 
25A is required to enable the design and use of the Franklin Union Building Component, it is 
eligible for consideration in accordance with the provisions of Article 25A which are applicable 
to historic structures. The required SLR-DFE for this site is equal to the Sea Level Rise Base 
Flood Elevation (SLR-BFE) of 18 ft BCB (which represents a future one percent annual chance 
coastal flood including approximately 40 inches of relative sea level rise) plus an additional 12 
inches of freeboard for the Senior Care Component and 24 inches of freeboard for the Franklin 
Union Building Component and the Appleton Component. All structures below the finished 
grade will be flood proofed to meet applicable building codes and regulations. The Project as 

12 
 
described in this Development Plan shall be in compliance with Article 25A of the Code and the 
Project shall not, except to the extent required in connection with the Franklin Union Building, 
require a conditional use permit from the Board of Appeal under Article 25A. 
Green Building Requirements: The Proposed Project is a Large Project pursuant to 
Section 80B of the Code. As such, the Proposed Project is subject to Article 37 of the Code. As 
such, the Developer shall ensure that the Proposed Project is in compliance with Article 37 of the 
Code. 
Other Approvals: The Project is subject to Large Project Review under Article 80B of 
the Code. Given the location of the Project Site within the South End Landmark District, review 
and approval of the design of the Project by the SELDC in accordance with the South End 
Landmarks Standards and Criteria is required. 
Throughout this review time, the Proponent has held additional meetings with the 
community, the Project’s Impact Advisory Group, South End neighbors, elected officials, city 
and state regulatory authorities, local non-profit organizations and other interested parties to 
discuss the Project. The Proponent has also undertaken review of the Project Design with the 
BCDC and the SELDC. 
Various other permits and approvals will also be required for the Project and will be 
obtained by the Proponent at the appropriate time, including but not limited to State Register 
Review (to the extent required) and water, wastewater and air permitting and other licensing and 
approvals. Modifications to the Project may be required as a result of these review processes. 
Minor modifications of the Project that are consistent with the dimensional limitations and public 
benefit obligations herein, will be subject to the approval of the Director under this Development 
Plan without further Authority action. 
Casualty/Reconstruction/Replacement: In addition, notwithstanding the provisions of 
underlying zoning, the reconstruction or replacement of a structure constructed pursuant to this 
Development Plan, including a Component thereof, shall be determined by the Authority to be 
consistent with this Development Plan, provided that reconstruction or replacement is for uses 
allowed within this Development Plan or otherwise in then current zoning and does not exceed 
the FAR, Height and building footprint specified for the Project Site or Component thereof. 
Minor Modifications to Plans: This Development Plan sets forth the dimensional, use 
and other zoning requirements for the Project and the Project Site, to the extent such 
requirements have been addressed in this Development Plan. Once this Development Plan is 
approved, final plans and specifications for the Project will be submitted to the BRA pursuant to 
Section 80C and 80B of the Code for final design review approval and certification as to 
consistency with this Development Plan, and to other governmental agencies and authorities for 
final approval. Accordingly, subject to consistency with the dimensional regulations set forth in 
this Development Plan, minor changes may occur to the Project’s design described in this 
Development Plan without requiring a further amendment to this Development Plan. This 
provision is in addition to and not in substitution of the provisions related to reconstruction or 
replacement set forth herein. 

13 
 
Amendment of Development Plan: Any owner of the Senior Care Component, the 
Franklin Union Building Component or the Appleton Component, or any sub-parcel or building 
within a parcel or sub-parcel covered by this Development Plan may seek a further amendment 
of this Development Plan as to such parcel, sub-parcel or building, in accordance with the 
procedures prescribed by the Code without the consent of all other owners of parcels, sub-parcel 
or building. In the event any amendment to this Development Plan proposed by the owner of a 
parcel, sub-parcel or building is approved, and such amendment affects the overall compliance of 
the Project with this Development Plan, this Development Plan shall be deemed amended with 
respect to the Project as a whole to the extent necessary for the overall Project to comply with 
this Development Plan. 
Schedule: The Proponent expects to commence development of each of the Project 
Components when the Project Site is vacant, which is expected to occur at the time BFCIT 
relocates to its new Nubian Square Campus. The construction of the Project Components is not 
planned to be phased at this time. The fit-out of tenant spaces will proceed as leases are signed. 
This schedule is subject to adjustment as necessary pending completion of BRA Design Review 
and the receipt of all applicable permits and approvals required for the Project. 
No Duty to Develop the Project: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary set forth in 
this Development Plan, under no circumstances shall the Proponent be obligated to proceed with 
the Proposed Project.

1. 
INTRODUCTION 
 
Pursuant to Article 3, Section 3-1A and Article 80, Section 80C of the Boston Zoning 
Code (the “Code”), this Master Plan constitutes a Planned Development Area Master Plan 
(“PDA Master Plan”) and sets forth a statement of the development concept for the rehabilitation 
and redevelopment of an approximately 21 acre site which is located on the west side of 
Dorchester Avenue in the South Boston section of Boston, Suffolk County, Massachusetts (the 
“Site”). This PDA Master Plan includes the planning objectives and character of the 
development, the proposed uses of the area, the range of dimensional requirements contemplated 
for each of the proposed buildings, and the proposed phasing of rehabilitation and construction 
(the “Development”). 
 
One or more PDA Development Plans for phases of the Development may be submitted 
to the Authority subsequent to the submission of this PDA Master Plan. 
 
2. 
OWNER AND DEVELOPER 
 
The owners and developer of the Site are entities affiliated with Core Investments Inc. 
(with their successors and assigns, the “Owner” or “Developer”). The Developer may include 
any affiliate or other parties (“Development Participant”) when submitting any PDA 
Development Plan for any specific phase of the Development. 
 
3. 
LOCATION AND DESCRIPTION OF THE SITE 
 
The Site consists of the approximately twelve (12) parcels in South Boston, bounded 
generally by the commuter and freight rail lines to the west, Dorchester Avenue to the east, 363 – 
365 Dorchester Avenue parcel to the north, and Southampton Street to the south. More specifically, 
the site fronts directly on Dorchester Avenue to the east, and is shown on the plan attached hereto as 
Exhibit A. 
 
The Site lies in the South Boston District and more particularly within the I-2 and M-1 
industrial zoning districts in which Planned Development Areas are allowed (the “Zoning District”). 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The Site currently consists of 12 existing buildings totaling approximately 310,222 
square feet located at 371-385 Dorchester Avenue (144,888 sf); 4 Alger Street (96,215); and 2 
Alger Street (41,978sf); 1-3 Wadleigh Place (8,127 sf), 5-7 Wadleigh Place (2,795 sf); 6-8 
Wadleigh Place (5,719 sf); 5 Ellery Street (2,823 sf); and 1 Ellery Street (615 sf), as well as a 
parcel containing approximately 9 acres with two small buildings that will be removed. The 
buildings are currently permitted for a mix of uses including light industrial, commercial, office, 
retail, and similar non-residential uses. The Site currently contains approximately 223 surface 
parking spaces. 
 
4. 
STATEMENT OF DEVELOPMENT CONCEPT 
 
 
The development concept for the site is to construct new buildings with significant open 
space and public realm components as a vibrant mixed-use extension of the neighborhood 
including ground floor retail, residential units with associated amenities, and commercial 
development including office, lab, and R&D areas with associated mechanical, accessory and 
ancillary support spaces. The development will include new public and private streets, sidewalks, 
bike paths, and accessible public realm spaces consistent with the City of Boston Complete 
Streets requirements and the Boston Transportation Department Bike Parking Guidelines. The 
project will include café areas, open spaces and recreation areas for public use and enjoyment, 
distributed throughout the Master Plan area. All daily and monthly vehicle parking will be 
created below grade or interior to the buildings so as not to be visible from the public way. 
 
Vehicle Parking is proposed to be included at ratios consistent with the City of Boston 
Transportation Department Maximum Parking Ratios policies for the respective uses. Bicycle 
parking is proposed to be included at the ratios consistent with the current City of Boston 
Transportation Department Bike Parking Guidelines. The proposed Development Concept is 
shown on the plan attached as Exhibit B. (“Site Master Plan”.) 
 
Except for the buildings existing on the date of this PDA Master Plan, as further 
discussed below, each of the buildings collectively comprising the Development contemplated in 
this PDA Master Plan (each a “Proposed Project”) will be subject to separate PDA Development 
Plans submitted to the Authority for approval in full compliance with Article 80 of the Code. It 
is contemplated that such Proposed Projects may be separately owned or leased for development 
or operation, and this may necessitate the establishment of separate zoning parcels or “lots,” one 
or more of which may be governed by a separate PDA Development Plan. 
 
The following are the Proposed Projects, each of which is shown on the Site Master Plan: 
• Six (6) new construction commercial buildings for R& D, laboratory, 21st Century 
Industrial and office uses with ground floor retail, lobbies and accessory service 
areas. 
• Five (5) new construction residential buildings with ground floor retail, lobbies 
and accessory service areas. 
• Below grade parking structures for vehicle parking, compliant with Boston 
Transportation Department (“BTD”) Maximum Parking Ratios for parking 
capacity. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Bicycle storage/parking compliant with the Bike Parking Guidelines, including a 
shared central bike pavilion at West Open Space between 65 and 75 Ellery 
Streets. 
• Open spaces provided on each block. 
• Four (4) open space / green space areas: (Refer to Exhibit D). 
o “East Open Space” located between Ellery Street and Dot Ave. containing 
approximately 30,620 sf (0.70 acres); 
o “West Open Space” located between Ellery Street and Service Road 
containing approximately 18,031 sf (0.4 acres); 
o “South Open Space” located immediately north of Southampton Street 
containing approximately 13,052 sf (0.3 acres) 
o “North Open Space” located immediately north of D Street containing 
approximately 65,400 sf (1.5 acres) 
• Parking and loading access from secondary side streets and no access is provided 
off of Ellery Street or Dorchester Avenue. 
• A central Ellery Street with appropriate pedestrian, café and planting zones. 
• East – West cross streets compliant with Complete Streets guidelines located at 
Street A, Alger Street (completing the existing City of Boston Alger Street), D 
Street Extension and the southern half of “South Street” adjacent to the abutting 
development to the north. (Refer to Exhibits C1 thru C9 illustrating proposed 
Street sections and details). 
• Smart Utilities compliant systems and infrastructure, necessary utilities and 
service infrastructure within the street rights of way, and appropriate coastal flood 
resiliency measures consistent with the City of Boston Coastal Flood Resiliency 
Overlay District Requirements. 
 
The Development initially proposes the retention of the existing industrial buildings 
reusing the existing buildings and facilities to the maximum extent feasible, coupled with interior 
tenant improvements (each, an “Existing Building”). The continued use of the Existing 
Buildings, anticipated for between five (5) and fifteen (15) years is planned while other buildings 
within the Development are constructed. This PDA Master Plan, without the need for any PDA 
Development Plan, authorizes the reuse of each Existing Building for any allowed uses. Any 
exterior modifications to an Existing Building shall be subject to ongoing design review in 
accordance with the Authority’s Development Review Procedures. However, if significant 
architectural alterations of an Existing Building is proposed that is materially different in 
character or degree from the then condition of the Existing Building, a separate PDA 
Development Plan will be required. 
 
 
5. 
PLANNING OBJECTIVES AND CHARACTER OF DEVELOPMENT 
 
Urban Design Goals: 
 
The Project is intended to generally align with the BPDA’s 2016 PLAN: Dot Ave planning 
process and seeks to develop an aspirational vision that broadly aligns with the goals of that 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
planning document. Below is both a summary of that planning process and goals as well as a 
description of the Project’s goals to further enrich and expand the intentions of PLAN: Dot Ave.: 
 
The Project presents an enormous opportunity to transform a significant void in the city’s urban 
fabric to create an active and safe 21st Century mixed-use neighborhood with gracious 
pedestrian-friendly sidewalks, verdant public open spaces, and improved bicycle infrastructure. 
 
Key findings related to the Project’s Urban Design include: 
 
• The Ellery Street boulevard as envisioned in PLAN: Dot Ave will be tree-lined linear 
open space with expansive colorful shrubs and perennial plantings and wide sidewalks, 
and lighting, for its entire length from north to south. 
 
• Evenly spaced parks and usable open space located on each block will complement the 
linear space. Each open space will have a distinct character and programs on either side 
of Ellery Street supporting varied yet complementary public uses that will be inviting to 
the neighborhood. 
› The Project includes wide sidewalks, separated raised bike lanes, and tree lined 
streets on Dorchester Avenue and within the Site boundaries. 
› The Project will include lighting along public and pedestrian ways for increased 
safety and visibility. 
› The Project creates a safe walkable pedestrian environment with 24/7 uses that 
will improve the character and safety of the Andrew Square Station environs. 
› The Project promotes public transit-oriented development as well as bicycle and 
personal mobility device commuting. 
› The Project Site will be designed to be ADA accessible. 
› The Project creates much needed public open space for the Dorchester Avenue 
corridor. 
› The Project brings a mix of commercial and R&D jobs to South Boston. 
› The Project adds to the stock of income-restricted and market rate residential units 
in South Boston proximate to public transit that are needed to create a 24/7 urban 
environment. 
› The Project brings much-needed restaurant and retail uses to the blighted and 
overlooked Andrew Square Station area. 
› The Project will improve resiliency by raising site grades and complying with 
Coastal Flood Resiliency Overlay District Requirements. 
› The Project will construct high-performance climate ready buildings with cutting-
edge levels of resiliency, sustainability and energy performance that will be 
attractive to tenants and residents. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
› The Project is generally consistent with the urban design goals of PLAN: Dot Ave 
and conforms to the Plan’s goals for open space, street rights-of-way (ROWs), 
and height limits. 
› 
The Project will activate an area currently open to undesirable conditions, creating 
a more secure environment for neighbors. 
 
• The BPDA’s PLAN: Dot Ave is a culmination of a process led by the BPDA to create a 
vision and provide guidelines for the redevelopment of a large portion of South Boston, 
including the Dorchester Avenue Corridor from Andrew Square to Broadway Station, 
anticipated to occur over a 15- to 20-year period. The 2016 publication is meant to serve as 
the basis for a living document that is adjusted over time as best practices for creating great 
urban places evolve. 
 
• PLAN: Dot Ave envisions a walkable neighborhood with improved public transportation; 
amenities such as retail, services, civic/cultural/art spaces, and new and varied open 
spaces; and a diversity of housing types including live/work opportunities, mid-rise and 
high-rise apartment buildings, and smaller housing units, while allowing preservation of 
existing character. 
 
• The goals of PLAN: Dot Ave and the proposed Master Plan PDA are to: 
› Create a framework for a new, urban, mixed-use 21st century district in Boston, 
› Form a network of new streets, blocks, connections, and open spaces forming the 
framework of a new district, 
› Create significant new housing at a variety of price points and rental rates that 
also relieves pressures on older housing stock, 
› Create a neighborhood, 
› Use planning and zoning tools to implement a coordinated, integrated new 
district consistent with the vision established by the public process, 
› Support inclusive development that improves awareness and access to funding 
resources, 
› Encourage best practices to encourage job creation and small business growth, 
› Accommodate 21st Century industrial and maker spaces in appropriate use zones 
as established in the Plan, 
› Create ground floor uses that are accessible to the public and activate street 
edges and sidewalks, and 
› Reserve ground floor and podium-level space for artist and maker space, 
according to the use zones established in the Plan. 
 
In addition to the above goals the Project design goals also include the following: 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
› Create an integrated and collaborative facility for idea generation and intellectual 
exchange, 
› Build upon the MBTA Red Line’s Life Science Corridor with a premiere life 
science and research development, 
› Create a destination for neighbors, visitors, and tenants, and continue the 
historical significance of innovation and creativity in South Boston, 
› Provide a diverse network of open space capable of small- and large-scale events 
that creates a district of distinct places and public realm experiences, and 
› Improve the streetscape, not only visually, but also addressing the need for safer 
complete streets with multi-modal routes for pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles. 
Pedestrian Circulation and Safety 
The public realm enhancements, along with the proximity to multiple modes of public 
transportation, will transform the area into an appealing, pedestrian-oriented, safe, and 
walkable neighborhood. The Site borders the MBTA Red Line Andrew Station at the south 
and is within 0.5 miles of Broadway Station to the north. Bus routes and stops along 
Dorchester Avenue and originating from Andrew Square also provide convenient 
connections to points throughout the city. 
The Site/landscape improvements establish a hierarchy of appealing, robust tree-lined streets 
and multi-modal network throughout the Site, welcoming the Andrew Square neighborhood 
westward across Dorchester Avenue. Complete streets, with separated pedestrian and bicycle 
accommodations will result in comfortable, clear, and safe routes for all modes of travel. 
Proposed streetscapes provide generous, ADA-compliant continuous paths of travel within the 
public right of way as well within the Site and to each building. In addition, multiple paths of 
circulation knit together the east and west community parks and provide for a variety of public 
open space experiences and welcome the community. 
All pedestrian and bicycle circulation zones will be appropriately lit for safe evening and 
nighttime travel, and the ground floor uses of the development have been organized to line 
the major pedestrian streets with active retail programming to provide an elevated sense of 
safety and awareness. 
ADA Accessibility 
Despite the need to raise lower portions of the Site to mitigate potential flooding due to sea 
level rise and climate change, all the buildings in the Masterplan will be ADA Accessible. 
To comply with the MA State building code and to address sea-level-rise (SLR) and climate 
change, the buildings on development parcels located immediately adjacent to Dorchester 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Avenue will have their finish floor elevations set above the sidewalk elevation. The building 
finish floor elevations are extended from the building to create an exterior raised terrace, as 
necessary. To provide ADA-compliant access between the sidewalks and the raised terrace 
outside the buildings, slope walkways with less than a 5 percent pitch slope will occur, and to 
provide accessible access coincident with stairs at various locations along the façade. The 
sidewalk cross pitches will be under 1.5 percent from the building toward the street to create 
positive drainage away from building and to maintain an accessible route continuously along 
the sidewalk. 
Bicycle Circulation and Safety 
 
The Project will include all new bicycle facilities with separated and buffered bike lanes 
throughout the Site, including on Street A, Alger Street, D Street, Service Road, Ellery Street 
and the proponents portion of South Street. 
 
There will be raised one-way cycle tracks, adequately buffered from parking and pedestrian 
uses, along the length of Dorchester Avenue and on both sides of Ellery Street as well as the 
interior east-west cross streets. At-grade, parking-protected/buffered bike lanes will be 
located on east-west cross streets. 
 
The proposed Project will provide a continuous, uninterrupted, multi-use path along its 
western edge, running parallel to Service Road at the western Site boundary. 
 
Thoughtful consideration will be given to strategically located short-term, public bike 
parking near building entries, along streetscapes adjacent to retail and community uses, and 
within open spaces. Additionally, accommodations will be made to locate Bluebikes stations 
as required by the Project’s transportation agreement. 
 
Refer to Exhibit B illustrating the proposed bike lanes, multi-use path, and bicycle 
infrastructure to be incorporated into the Master Plan development. 
 
 
 Sustainability: 
 
The Development will demonstrate practices that promote sustainability, including measures 
to increase efficiency and use of renewable resources. In addition to complying with the 
requirements of Article 37 (Green Buildings) of the Code, the Development will be based on 
a series of sustainability principles, including: 
 
• Develop all-electric, Passive House compliant residential buildings; 
• Reduce vulnerability to climate change impacts including natural hazards by 
integrating climate change adaptation into planning and project design; 
• Promote health, productivity and safety of the South Boston community through 
design and maintenance of the built environments; 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Enhance the health of South Boston ecosystems and increase the diversity of 
native species; 
• Establish indicators for sustainability that will enable monitoring, reporting and 
continuous improvement; 
• Minimize the impacts on ecosystems and water resources, and reduce drainage 
impacts of the projects; 
• Promote smart use of water, inside and out, to reduce potable water consumption; 
• Promote better building energy performance through innovative strategies; 
• Use sustainable building materials and reduce waste; 
• Promote better indoor air quality and access to daylight and views; 
• Promote walkability with efficient transportation options and open space; 
• Emphasize compact, walkable mixed-use neighborhood with good connections to 
nearby South Boston areas; 
• Reduce the environmental consequences of the construction and operation of 
buildings and infrastructure.

to the provisions of such Development Plan and the Article 80B Documents applicable to such 
Proposed Project. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, upon approval of a PDA 
Development Plan for a Proposed Project, the Development Participants as “Developer” 
thereunder shall not be chargeable with any omission, commission, default or delay by any other 
person, including without limitation the Development Participants as “Developer” of any other 
Proposed Project, in the implementation of this PDA Master Plan, or any other approved 
Development Plan, or the undertakings of the Article 80B Documents with respect to any other 
Proposed Project or any other portion of the Development. This provision to make the 
undertakings with respect to each Proposed Project severable is included in order to facilitate the 
separate ownership and/or financing of portions of the Development without concern for any so-
called cross-default or zoning non-compliance attributable to the acts of others. 
 
The issuance of any permit for the development or construction of any Proposed Project 
in accordance with this PDA Master Plan, or any PDA Development Plan previously approved 
or approved simultaneously with or subsequent to this PDA Master Plan, as the same may be 
amended from time to time, shall be deemed to be the issuance of a permit for the entire 
Development for the purpose of applying Section 5 of Chapter 665 of the Acts of 1956 as 
amended from time to time. Without limiting the foregoing sentence, the proviso of Section 5 
that construction work under the permit proceed continuously to completion shall be deemed 
satisfied so long as construction on the Development proceeds generally in accordance with the 
development schedule set forth in this PDA Master Plan. 
 
9. 
PROPOSED VEHICULAR AND PEDESTRIAN TRAFFIC CIRCULATION: 
 
The proposed Master Plan PDA and each individual block and project therein will be 
designed to meet the requirements and guidelines of the August 2021 PLAN: South Boston 
Transportation Plan adopted by the BPDA including conformance with the requirements of the 
appropriate Complete Streets guidelines and the proposed 80’ to 90’ Ellery Street boulevard 
configuration. 
 
Refer to Exhibit C1 thru C10 for proposed Complete Street sections and dimensions 
defining all streets proposed to be included within the development project. 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Refer to Exhibit G for proposed Master PDA Plan Rights of Way, Setbacks, and sections 
of each proposed street, with dimensions and details related to parking, bike lanes, travel lanes, 
furniture zones, and sidewalks. 
 
The project is not to exceed the trip generation quantities that are associated with the 
PLAN: Dorchester Avenue build out assumptions, establishing trip generation forecasting for the 
project. As proposed, the project does not exceed and is compliant with the PLAN: Dorchester 
Avenue trip generation impacts and assumptions. If the proposed land uses are altered, and trip 
generation rates are exceeded from what is proposed through this document, additional 
mitigation of impacts will be required. 
 
10. 
ACCESS TO PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION 
 
The Site is located within convenient distance of the MBTA public transportation system. 
The MBTA Red Line Andrew Square and Broadway subway stations and located within a 5–10-
minute walking distance from the Site. Andrew Station is also a major MBTA bus hub. 
 
11. 
PUBLIC BENEFITS 
 
The Development will provide substantial public benefits to the City of Boston and the 
surrounding neighborhood. These benefits will include: 
 
› Provides approximately 2.92 acres of publicly accessible, landscaped space, privately 
owned, deed restricted as public open space in perpetuity, that supports a variety of 
community uses and programming opportunities, 
› Creates a minimum of a 1.5-acre contiguous open space, privately funded and maintained, 
privately owned, deed restricted as public open space in perpetuity, north of the relocated / 
realigned D Street, 
› In accordance with the proposed density bonus provisions of the Plan, 17% of all 
residential units will be designated as IDP units under the Inclusionary Development 
Policy, an increase of 4% over current IDP requirements. 
› Creates a comfortable, safe, multimodal district through robust pedestrian, bicycle, and 
vehicle infrastructure that complies with the Complete Streets guidelines, 
› Improves pedestrian safety with new wider sidewalks and crosswalks, 
› Leverages existing nearby transit and alternative transportation choices to establish a 
transit-oriented development, 
› Targets LEED Gold to foster sustainability, 
› Improves resiliency by raising Site grades and complying with the Coastal Flood 
Resilience Overlay District requirements, 
› Remediation of toxic and hazardous materials from prior industrial uses, 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
› Provides state-of-the art space for commercial uses, which promotes employment and 
contributes to neighborhood economic health and diversity, 
› Constructs below-grade parking to minimize impervious surfaces and implement urban 
design best practices, 
› Provides activation, lighting, and security to an at-risk and transitional former industrial 
area that has been noted as potentially “unsafe” at times in community meetings, 
› Provides transportation design services as part of an overall TAPA agreement to advance 
critical priorities noted within the PLAN: South Boston Dorchester Avenue Transportation 
Planning Study (the “Transportation Plan”), 
› Provides mitigation funds, through the BPDA, to support community based and selected 
non-profit organizations, community infrastructure and service priorities, and to financially 
assist with critical social service needs within the surrounding neighborhood, 
› Identifies appropriate ground floor active retail space to be subsidized in the build out and 
ongoing operations costs and made available to community start-ups, artists needing maker 
and industrial arts workspaces, and similarly identified community, faith-based 
organizations, business and arts & culture programs in conformance with the benefits 
mitigation calculation stipulated in Plan: Dot Ave. 
› Commits to working with the future life science and technology tenants to create a 
“learning zone” space where community youth can engage with, be mentored by, and learn 
from successful professionals in the sciences, thus creating a sense of potential and 
opportunity for neighborhood young people, 
› Provides public and private bicycle storage capacity to encourage micro-mobility within 
the neighborhood by affording the ability to park and ride bikes and the MBTA Red Line, 
and 
› Improves stormwater and sewer infrastructure. 
› Creates opportunity for significant on-site income-restricted housing unit development and 
increases the available high-quality housing stock available in South Boston. 
› Measures to be undertaken to comply with the City of Boston Inclusionary Development 
Policy for all residential projects will be included in each applicable PDA Development 
Plan.

I. 
Proponent 
Core Investments, Inc. 
II. 
Project Location 
The PDA Master Plan Area comprises approximately 21 acres of land, 
bounded generally by Southampton Street to the south, the 
Southampton/Amtrak railyards to the west, private property at 365 
Dorchester Avenue to the north, and Dorchester Avenue to the east. 
III. 
Development 
Concept 
The PDA Master Plan proposes the construction of multiple buildings that 
comprise the Proposed Project, containing a total of approximately 1,940,000 
square feet and described conceptually below: 
 
Phase I 
 
• 
495 Dorchester Avenue: a residential building containing 
approximately 328,000 square feet with approximately 9,230 
square feet of retail, restaurant, and other ground floor uses, 
with 90 underground parking spaces, 
• 
65 Ellery Street: a commercial/office/research and development 
building containing approximately 495,700 square feet and 15,000 
square feet of retail, restaurant, and other ground floor uses with 525 
underground parking spaces, 
• 
75 Ellery Street: a commercial/office/research and development 
building containing approximately 374,900 square feet and 15,000 
square feet of retail, restaurant, and other ground floor uses with 225 
underground parking spaces, 
• 
505 Dorchester Avenue: a commercial/office/research and 
development building containing approximately 467,400 square feet 
and 20,000 square feet of retail, restaurant, and other ground floor 
uses with 0 underground parking spaces, and 
• 
Open space areas containing approximately48,650 square feet located 
between 505 and 495 Dorchester Avenue and between 75 and 65 
Ellery Street, with new extensions of Ellery Street, and a new Street 
A (to be named later), a new Service Drive (located along the 
Southampton/Amtrak railyards) and a significant improvement to 
Alger Street, all with new sidewalks, lighting, bicycle facilities, and 
pedestrian areas. 
 
 

 
 
Phase 2 
 
• 
A residential building containing approximately 224,200 square 
feet with approximately 11,000 square feet of retail, restaurant and 
other ground floor uses with 236 underground parking spaces, 
• 
Opens space area containing approximately 13,052 square feet, 
with improvements to Ellery Street leading to Southampton Street. 
 
 
Phase 3 
 
• 
Two a commercial/office/research and development buildings 
containing approximately 630,200 square feet in total and 22,000 
square feet of retail, restaurant, and other ground floor uses with 
660 underground parking spaces, 
• 
A residential building containing approximately 190,500 square 
feet with approximately 4,000 square feet of retail, restaurant and 
other ground floor uses with 100 underground parking spaces, 
• 
Improvements to Ellery Street and D Street, and an extension of 
Service Drive, all with new sidewalks, lighting, bicycle facilities 
and pedestrian areas. 
 
 
Phase 4 
 
• 
A commercial/office/research and development buildings 
containing approximately 345,500 square feet and 12,000 square 
feet of retail, restaurant, and other ground floor uses with 100 
underground parking spaces, 
• 
Two residential buildings containing approximately 567,000 square 
feet in total with approximately 41,000 square feet of retail, 
restaurant and other ground floor uses with 240 underground 
parking spaces, and 
• 
Open space containing approximately 65,400 square feet (1.501 
acres) fronting on Dorchester Avenue, a realigned D Street, an 
extension of Ellery Street, and an extension of Service Drive, all 
with new sidewalks, lighting, bicycle facilities and pedestrian 
areas. 
IV. 
Project Uses 
Allowed uses for the PDA Area include, among others, office, laboratory, 
residential, cultural, research and development, service, open space 
(including programmed open space), retail, restaurant, entertainment, 
together with accessory and ancillary uses thereto. Uses will also include 
below-grade, at-grade, and structured accessory parking for all types of 
uses. 

 
 
V. 
Public Benefits 
The development of the Proposed Project contemplated by the PDA Master 
Plan will provide a range of public benefits, including: 
 
• 
Remediation of EPA and MassDEP supervised toxic and hazardous 
materials disposal site. 
• 
Increased and improved publicly-accessible open space which connects 
to a broader network of open spaces. 
• 
Creation of 1.5 acre open space, deed restricted as public open space 
along Dorchester Avenue and realigned D Street. 
• 
Creates a comfortable, save, multimodal district through robust 
pedestrian, bicycle, and vehicle infrastructure that complies with 
Complete Streets guidelines. 
• 
Targets LEED Gold to foster sustainability. 
• 
Improves resiliency by raising Site grades and complying with 
Coastal Flood Resilience Overlay District requirements. 
• 
New affordable housing units in connection with any residential 
development that comply with City requirements. 
• 
Provides state-of-the-art commercial spaces to promote 
employment and contribute to neighborhood economic health 
and diversity. 
• 
Housing and job linkage payments from qualifying uses in connection 
with construction of buildings containing such uses; 
• 
New construction and permanent jobs. 
• 
Increased tax revenues for the City. 
• 
Transportation improvements, including new complete streets, in 
furtherance of PLAN: South Boston Dorchester Avenue 
Transportation Planning Study. 
 
Public benefits associated with each phase of the Proposed Project will be 
included in the PDA Development Plan for such phase.

1. 
PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA DEVELOPMENT PLAN: On October 
12, 2023, the Boston Redevelopment Authority, doing business as the Boston Planning & 
Development Agency (the “Authority”) approved the Master Plan for Planned Development 
Area No. 144 (the “PDA Master Plan”) pursuant to Article 3, Section 3-1A and Article 80, 
Section 80C of the Boston Zoning Code (the “Code”) for the parcels of land along Dorchester 
Avenue in South Boston (the “Development”). Capitalized terms used herein without definition 
which are defined in the PDA Master Plan shall have the meanings ascribed to them therein. 
 
On December 13, 2023, the Boston Zoning Commission (the “Commission”), by the 
adoption of Map Amendment No. ____, approved the PDA Master Plan and amended the series 
of maps entitled “Zoning Districts City of Boston,” dated August 15, 1962, as amended, by 
adding a “D” designation, indicating a Planned Development Area overlay district, to the 495 
Project Site. 
 
The PDA Master Plan contemplates that one or more PDA Development Plans for phases 
of the Development may be submitted either simultaneously with or subsequent to the 
submission of the PDA Master Plan. 
 
In accordance with Article 3, Section 3-1A of the Code and Article 80, Section 80C, this 
development plan sets forth information on the construction of Phase 1A of the Development 
comprising 495 Dorchester Avenue (the “495 Project”). The 495 Project is located on an 
approximately 53,791 sf portion (the “495 Project Site”) of the of the approximately 21 acre site 
described in the PDA Master Plan along Dorchester Avenue in the South Boston section of 
Boston, Suffolk County, Massachusetts. The 495 Project Site is currently vacant. It has long 
been used for industrial purposes and the 495 Project will entail substantial environmental 
remediation due to the prior industrial uses. 

 
 
 
 
This development plan includes the proposed location and appearance of structures, open 
spaces and landscaping, the proposed uses of the 495 Project, the proposed dimensions of the 
structures, the proposed densities, the proposed traffic circulation, parking and loading facilities, 
access to public transportation and other major elements of the 495 Project (the “Development 
Plan”). This Development Plan constitutes the permanent zoning for the 495 Project and 
supersedes any existing zoning requirements contained in the Code. 
 
2. 
DEVELOPER: The owners and developer of the 495 Project Site is On the Dot 
LLC and entities affiliated with Core Investments, Inc. (with their successors and assigns, the 
“Owner” or the “Developer”). 
 
3. 
LOCATION AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT SITE: The 495 
Project Site is the approximately 53,791 square foot portion of the land described as Phase IA in the 
PDA Master Plan. As of the date of this Development Plan, the 495 Project Site has not been 
subdivided into separate lots for zoning purposes. The Developer shall have the right to so 
subdivide the 495 Project Site at any time, which subdivision shall not require amendment of this 
Development Plan. 
 
The 495 Project Site lies in the South Boston District and more particularly within the I-2 
zoning district in which Planned Development Areas are allowed (the “Zoning District”). 
 
4. 
PROPOSED LOCATION AND APPEARANCE OF STRUCTURES: The 
495 Project consists of the development of one new building along with new sidewalks leading 
from Dorchester Avenue and Alger Street. The 495 Project consists of the development of one 
(1) new building containing approximately 326,000 square feet with 237 market rate units, 94 
units of affordable housing for seniors that will serve very low-income seniors with supportive 
services, two ground floor retail and commercial spaces containing a total of approximately 
8,437 square feet. There will be approximately 88 parking spaces constructed beneath the 
structure in an underground garage that will be accessed from Alger Street. 
 
The 495 Project is consistent with the criteria specified in Section 80C-4 of the Code for 
the approval of planned development areas in that the underlying zoning does not prohibit 
planned development areas, and the 495 Project Site is not located in a residential zoning district. 
Further, this Development Plan generally conforms to the plan for this area, including without 
limitation, the BPDA PLAN: Dot Ave. and PLAN South Boston Dorchester Ave. Transportation 
Plan; and on balance, nothing in this Development Plan will be injurious to the neighborhood or 
otherwise detrimental to the public welfare. This Development Plan furthers the goals of the 
neighborhood to create a vibrant, mixed-use, transit oriented development. 
 
Plans showing the architectural elements of the building comprising the 495 Project 
entitled “On the Dot Residential Plans” prepared by Utile (collectively, the “Project Plans”) are 
attached hereto as Appendix A and incorporated herein by this reference. 
 
5. 
OPEN SPACES AND LANDSCAPING: The 495 Project includes new 
sidewalks, bike lanes, new curbing, and street trees on the immediately adjacent portions of 

 
 
 
Dorchester Avenue and Alger Street, as illustrated in the attached Site Plan as Appendix B. The 
open space totals approximately 16,123 sf of which approximately 11,192 sf will be for the use 
of the residents. The public East Open space identified in the PDA Master Plan will be located 
adjacent to the 495 Project and will be further described in the PDA Development Plan that will 
be filed for Phase 1B immediately following this Development Plan.

Site may include the allowed and conditional uses set forth in the Code, including without
