Exhibit C attached hereto. This PDA Development Plan represents a stage in the planning 
process prior to the stage at which final plans and specifications for the Building B Project are 
submitted to the BRA pursuant to Section 3-1A.a and Article 80C of the Code for final design 
review approval and certification as to consistency with this PDA Development Plan. Therefore, 
the Building B Project is subject to final design, environmental, and other development review 
by the BRA and by other governmental agencies and authorities, and minor changes may occur 
to the Building B Project’s design without the need to amend this PDA Development Plan, 
provided that the Building B Project is consistent with the use and dimensional limitations 
described and shown in this PDA Development Plan. All references herein to terms set forth in 
the Code shall have the meanings set forth in the Code, as amended to the effective date hereof. 

 
2 
 
4911-7405-9075, v. 2 
This Plan is not subject to changes to the Code or zoning maps that take effect after such 
effective date. 
2. 
Project Site Description. As shown on the context map attached as Exhibit A 
hereto, the Master Plan Area is comprised of discrete City of Boston Assessing Parcels No. 
0203963050 (the “Northern Site”) and No. 0203964000 (the “Southern Site”) bordered to the 
east by a pedestrian walkway known as Millers River Littoral Way owned by the Massachusetts 
Department of Transportation (“DOT”) and an on-ramp to US Route 1; to the south by a rear 
service driveway owned by DOT; to the west by Austin Street (a City of Boston public way) 
transitioning to the Gilmore Bridge; and to the north by New Rutherford Avenue (a City of 
Boston public way). A middle access driveway owned by DOT bisects the Master Plan Area and 
connects New Rutherford Avenue to the rear service driveway. As shown on the site plan 
attached as Exhibit C hereto, the Building B Site is a portion of the Northern Site. The Master 
Plan Area, including the Building B Site, currently contains surface parking, which will be razed 
to facilitate development. 
The legal description of the Building B Site is attached as Exhibit B hereto. Upon 
approval of this PDA Development Plan, the Building B Site will be governed by this PDA 
Development Plan. No approval for any elements of the Building B Project, whether new or 
existing and remaining, shall be required from the Board of Appeal. All references herein to 
terms set forth in the Code shall have the meanings set forth in the Code, as amended to the 
effective date hereof. This PDA Development Plan is not subject to changes to the Code or 
zoning maps that take effect after the effective date of PDA No. ____. 
3. 
Proposed Project. The various components of the Building B Project are shown 
in the project materials attached hereto as Exhibits C through F, in each case for illustrative 
purposes subject to design finalization. 
(a) 
Planning Objectives and Character. Redevelopment of the Master Plan 
Area, including the Building B Project on the Building B Site, responds to the surrounding urban 
design context, placing taller building elements proximate to the I-93 viaduct that runs parallel 
with the rear service driveway and stepping down toward New Rutherford Avenue to meet the 
residential neighborhood edge. With passive and active programs, the new open spaces will be 
crafted to engage residents and neighbors in social spaces while assisting with stormwater 
management and passive cooling while also providing recreational opportunities for the 
community. The pedestrian experience along New Rutherford Avenue will be improved with a 
line of street trees where not obstructed by existing underground infrastructure, planted in a 
landscape furniture zone, and a widened sidewalk. Trees behind the back of the sidewalk act as a 
deeper filter to New Rutherford Avenue. New trees will be carefully selected to complement the 
existing tree canopy and overall building character while providing a diversity of native species 
to enhance ecological connections. New site lighting will incorporate “dark sky guidelines” and 
will be scaled to a pedestrian, residential scale. 
(b) 
Building B. Within the Northern Site, the Proponent proposes the 
construction of a new, up to 7-story building containing approximately 125 dwelling units and 
residential amenities, together with bicycle storage in accordance with City of Boston Bike 
Parking Guidelines (anticipated to be up to 125 long-term and up to 25 short-term bicycle 

 
3 
 
4911-7405-9075, v. 2 
parking spaces), an approximately 52’ x 80’ urban plaza and lawn, a new connection across the 
Northern Site between New Rutherford Avenue and the rear service driveway, up to 15 surface 
vehicle parking spaces within the said new connection, and related site and public realm 
improvements (collectively, the “Building B Project”). 
(c) 
Dimensions and Uses. This building will not exceed a height of 85 feet, 
and will contain approximately 126,000 square feet of Gross Floor Area (as defined in Article 2 
of the Code) of residential uses on an approximately 54,069 square foot area of land within the 
Northern Site. Allowed uses are listed on Exhibit G attached hereto, and the Building B Site may 
contain any of the uses described in this PDA Development Plan and/or set forth on Exhibit G. 
Any other uses on the Building B Site shall require an amendment to this PDA Development 
Plan. The placement and maintenance of rooftop wireless communications and other 
telecommunications equipment such as antennae, dishes, equipment mounting, as well as 
elevator and stair access to and fall protection for the rooftop amenity space, and rooftop 
mechanical and energy equipment such as solar panels and equipment, which may be screened, 
shall be allowed, subject only to design review by the BRA. 
Building height shall be measured from 27.5’ Boston City Base as grade, which is 
an average measurement along the back of sidewalk on New Rutherford Avenue between Austin 
Street and the on-ramp to US Route 1, and exclusive of rooftop structures. Based upon a total 
maximum Gross Floor Area of up 790,000 square feet for the four Proposed Projects and the 
approximately 221,056 square feet (approximately 5.1 acres) of land comprising the Master Plan 
Area, the Floor Area Ratio across the Master Plan Area will not exceed 3.6. At least 25% of the 
land area within the Master Plan Area shall be permeable. No Proposed Project shall be 
noncompliant with this Floor Area Ratio maximum or permeability minimum so long as the 
Master Plan Area is compliant on a master site wide basis. In the event of any conflict between 
Sections 62-20 and -21 of the Code with respect to Area PDA I and this PDA Development Plan, 
this PDA Development Plan shall govern. There are no other requirements with respect to lot 
size (other than the minimum 5 acres required for master PDA designation), lot width, lot 
frontage, usable open space per dwelling unit, parapet setback, yards, rear yard occupancy by 
accessory buildings, or the like. 
(d) 
Open Space and Landscaping. Redevelopment of the Master Plan Area, 
including the Building B Project on the Building B Site, will transform the Master Plan Area 
from a sea of asphalt into, among other things, areas where the community can gather and enjoy 
newly-available amenities. The Building B Project’s urban plaza and lawn, substantially as 
shown on Exhibit D attached hereto (notwithstanding that the Building B Project does not 
involve portions of the Master Plan Area shown in Exhibit D outside the Building B Site), will 
provide significant recreational amenities for the Charlestown community. The planting strategy 
includes a large quantity of canopy trees, which will be comprised of mostly native trees with 
some naturalized non-natives included to provide biological diversity. This strategy helps 
ameliorate the hazard of tree loss due to disease, invasive pests, and climate change. 
(e) 
Parking and Loading. The Building B Project involves no structured 
vehicle parking spaces, up to 15 surface vehicle parking spaces within the new connection across 
the Northern Site between New Rutherford Avenue and the rear service driveway, and bicycle 
storage in accordance with City of Boston Bike Parking Guidelines (anticipated to be up to 125 

 
4 
 
4911-7405-9075, v. 2 
long-term and up to 25 short-term bicycle parking spaces). Loading activities will occur within 
the rear service driveway via adequate loading facilities. The proposed site circulation is shown 
on the vehicular circulation plan and pedestrian and bicycle circulation plan attached as Exhibit 
E hereto (notwithstanding that the Building B Project does not involve portions of the Master 
Plan Area shown in Exhibit E outside the Building B Site). The Building B Site has proximate 
access to MBTA’s Orange Line Community College subway station and bus routes 92 and 93. 
The Proponent will implement Transportation Demand Management measures to encourage 
residents, employees, and visitors of the Building B Site to utilize multimodal travel modes and 
to minimize automobile usage. 
(f) 
Existing Uses. The Building A Site may continue to be used for all 
existing uses and occupied by all existing structures and improvements as they may be modified 
or removed during the construction of the Building B Project. 
4. 
Development Schedule. The Proponent currently estimates that construction of 
the Building B Project will commence in 2026 and continue for approximately 24-30 months, 
subject to market conditions and other considerations. Notwithstanding anything set forth in this 
PDA Development Plan to the contrary, under no circumstances shall the Proponent nor any 
designee thereof be obligated to proceed with the Building B Project, or any portion thereof, or, 
once the Proponent or any designee thereof does proceed with the Building B Project, or any 
portion thereof, to complete the Building B Project or such portion. Construction of the Building 
B Project on the Building B Site may proceed in subphases concurrently or independently in any 
sequence with respect to each other. 
5. 
Public Benefits. The redevelopment program for the Master Plan Area, including 
the Building B Project on the Building B Site, contemplates a wide variety of public and 
community benefits consistent with Section 62-23 of the Code. Subject to design finalization and 
approval from appropriate governmental authorities, the specific benefits to be delivered by the 
Building B Project include: 
(a) 
the revitalization of a portion of the underutilized Master Plan Area 
proximate to public transit (i.e., MBTA’s Orange Line Community 
College subway station and bus routes 92 and 93); 
(b) 
an increase in Charlestown’s housing supply, including income-restricted 
dwelling units that comply with or exceed the applicable 13% income-
restricted requirement of the City of Boston’s Inclusionary Development 
Policy under the Mayor’s Order Relative to Inclusionary Development 
dated December 9, 2015, such that up to 60% of the dwelling units on a 
master sitewide basis at full build out will be income-restricted; 
(c) 
significant open space providing recreational amenities for the 
Charlestown community; 
(d) 
enhanced public realm elements with improved pedestrian and bicycle 
connectivity; 

 
5 
 
4911-7405-9075, v. 2 
(e) 
sustainability features such as LEED Gold certifiability, energy-efficient 
building systems, improved site permeability and stormwater treatment, 
reduced urban heat island impacts, and flood resiliency measures, all in 
accordance with Articles 25A and 37 of the Code; 
(f) 
bicycle storage in accordance with City of Boston Bike Parking 
Guidelines; 
(g) 
Transportation Demand Management measures to minimize automobile 
usage; and 
(h) 
additional property tax revenue for the City of Boston. 
7. 
Other Approvals. The Building B Project will be subject to review by the 
Boston Civic Design Commission, and to further review by the BRA of the schematic design, 
design development and construction drawings, pursuant to the BRA’s Development Review 
Guidelines and Article 80B of the Code. Signs shall be permitted as approved from time to time 
through such BRA review in accordance with Article 11 of the Code. Aspects of the Building B 
Project may also require other City of Boston approvals, such as from the Public Improvement 
Commission regarding public ways. 
8. 
Applicability. The Building B Project or each subphase thereof shall be subject 
to BPDA design review approval and eligible for its own full or partial Certification of 
Compliance and Consistency pursuant to Sections 80B-6 and 80C-8 of the Code. Upon issuance 
of such certification, the improvements subject to the same shall be deemed to be in compliance 
with this PDA Development Plan’s requirements applicable to such phase or subphase, and with 
the requirements of the Code to the extent such requirements have been addressed in this Plan in 
accordance with Section 80C-9 of the Code. 
Any noncompliance of a phase or subphase of the redevelopment of the Master Plan Area 
shall not affect compliance of any other phase or subphase, nor the right to construct 
improvements on the Building B Site as contemplated by this PDA Development Plan. In 
addition, this PDA Development Plan approves any zoning nonconformity created or increased 
solely as a result of (i) any separation of ownership of individual phases or subphases, (ii) any 
subdivision or combination of the assessor’s lots that comprise the subject land, and/or (iii) the 
submission of the subject land or any phases or subphases to a condominium regime. If the 
phases or subphases are separately owned or conveyed, including by one or more ground leases, 
then each owner shall be the Proponent with respect to its phase or subphase and shall bear no 
obligation or liability regarding zoning compliance with respect to any other phase or subphase. 
Any owner of all or a portion of the Building B Project may seek an amendment of this 
PDA Development Plan as to such owned portion in accordance with the procedures prescribed 
by the Code, without the consent of any other phase or subphase owners across the Master Plan 
Area, provided that such amendment does not change any obligations or requirements applicable 
to such other phases or subphases, nor cause noncompliance with the master sitewide Floor Area 
Ratio maximum or permeability minimum, except as allowed herein. The provisions of this PDA 

 
6 
 
4911-7405-9075, v. 2 
Development Plan applicable to all or a portion of the Building B Project may be amended only 
with the consent of the owner of such portion. 
9. 
Definitions. Unless otherwise set forth herein, capitalized terms used herein but 
not defined shall have the meanings specified in Article 2 of the Code, as amended to the 
effective date hereof, and not as the same may be amended hereafter.

FACT SHEET 
MASTER PLAN 
FOR PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA NO. ____ 
AUSTIN STREET LOTS REDEVLOPMENT, CHARLESTOWN 
I. 
Board Action 
The Proponent is requesting approval of the Boston Redevelopment 
Authority d/b/a the Boston Planning & Development Agency of a Master 
Plan for a Planned Development Area (“PDA”) in connection with the 
Austin Street Lots Redevelopment. 
II. 
Proponent 
Trinity Acquisitions LLC, a Massachusetts limited liability company, an 
affiliate of Trinity Financial, Inc., and its affiliates 
III. Location of 
Proposed 
Projects 
The PDA (the “Master Plan Area”) is comprised of discrete City of 
Boston Assessing Parcels No. 0203963050 (the “Northern Site”) and No. 
0203964000 (the “Southern Site”) located generally at the southwestern 
corner of the Austin Street/New Rutherford Avenue intersection in 
Boston’s Charlestown neighborhood. A middle access driveway bisects 
the Master Plan Area and connects New Rutherford Avenue to a rear 
service driveway. The Master Plan Area currently contains surface 
parking, which will be razed to facilitate development. 
IV. Proposed 
Projects 
The redevelopment program contemplates four new mixed-use buildings 
collectively containing up to 790,000 sf of Gross Floor Area (as defined 
in Article 2 of the Boston Zoning Code) and delivering up to 705 new 
dwelling units and residential amenities, arts and culture space, early 
childhood education space, indoor recreation space, and structured and/or 
surface vehicle parking spaces, together with an urban plaza and lawn and 
athletic/multipurpose fields, and related site and public realm 
improvements. The new buildings are anticipated to proceed in phases 
(with or without subphases) with PDA Development Plans under this 
Master Plan. 
V. 
Public Benefits 
The redevelopment program contemplates a wide variety of public and 
community benefits, subject to design finalization and approval from 
appropriate governmental authorities. These benefits include revitalization 
of an underutilized site proximate to public transit (i.e., MBTA’s Orange 
Line Community College subway station and bus routes 92 and 93); an 
increase in Charlestown’s housing supply, including income-restricted 
dwelling units; significant open space providing recreational amenities for 
the Charlestown community; enhanced public realm elements with 
improved pedestrian and bicycle connectivity; sustainability features such 
as energy-efficient building systems, improved site permeability and 
stormwater treatment, reduced urban heat island impacts, and flood 
resiliency measures; and additional property tax revenue for the City of 

 
2 
 
4925-9953-5932, v. 3 
Boston. 
VI. Existing Zoning 
The Master Plan Area is located within the Mixed Use 1 Subdistrict and 
Area PDA I of the Charlestown Neighborhood District governed by 
Article 62 and Map 2E of the Boston Zoning Code. Portions of the Master 
Plan Area are located within the Flood Hazard District governed by 
Article 25 and the Coastal Flood Overlay District governed by Article 
25A. The Master Plan Area contains more than 5 acres of land area and is 
PDA-eligible due to its inclusion within Area PDA I. 

 
 
 
BOSTON REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
MASTER PLAN 
FOR PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA NO. ____ 
AUSTIN STREET LOTS REDEVLOPMENT, CHARLESTOWN 
Dated: _____________, 2025 
1. 
Master Plan. Pursuant to Section 3-1A.a and Article 80C of the Boston Zoning 
Code (the “Code”), this plan constitutes a Master Plan (this “Master Plan”) for Planned 
Development Area No. ____ for the development of approximately 221,056 square feet 
(approximately 5.1 acres) of land (the “Master Plan Area”) located generally at the southwestern 
corner of the Austin Street/New Rutherford Avenue intersection in Boston’s Charlestown 
neighborhood. The Master Plan Area is described in more detail below, and the legal description 
is attached as Exhibit B hereto and shown on the site plan attached as Exhibit C hereto. The 
Master Plan Area is owned by the Boston Redevelopment Authority (the “BRA”). Trinity 
Acquisitions LLC, a Massachusetts limited liability company, or another affiliate of Trinity 
Financial, Inc. (the “Proponent”), expects to enter into one or more long-term ground leases with 
the BRA as the landowner. This Master Plan contemplates that one or more Planned 
Development Area Development Plans (each, a “PDA Development Plan”) will be submitted for 
the phases or subphases of the redevelopment program for the Master Plan Area in accordance 
with Section 80C of the Code, therein providing more specific information about each such 
phase or subphase. 
This Master Plan sets forth a statement of the redevelopment program concept, including 
the planning objectives and character, the proposed uses, the range of dimensional requirements 
contemplated for each of the proposed uses, the proposed phasing of construction, and the 
anticipated public benefits. This Master Plan consists of six pages of text, plus the attachments 
designated as Exhibits A through F. A conceptual site plan of the Proposed Projects, as defined 
below, is shown on Exhibit C attached hereto. 
 This Master Plan describes four new projects (each a “Proposed Project”) to be located 
on the Master Plan Area to be developed in phases (with or without sub-phases) with PDA 
Development Plans under this Master Plan, collectively containing up to 790,000 sf of Gross 
Floor Area (as defined in Article 2 of the Code) and delivering up to 705 new dwelling units and 
residential amenities, arts and culture space, early childhood education space, indoor recreation 
space, and structured and/or surface vehicle parking spaces, together with an urban plaza and 
lawn and athletic/multipurpose fields, and related site and public realm improvements. Each of 
the Proposed Projects is discussed in more detail below. 
2. 
Master Plan Area Description. As shown on the context map attached as 
Exhibit A hereto and on the site plan attached as Exhibit C hereto, the Master Plan Area is 
comprised of discrete City of Boston Assessing Parcels No. 0203963050 (the “Northern Site”) 
and No. 0203964000 (the “Southern Site”) bordered to the east by a pedestrian walkway known 
as Millers River Littoral Way owned by the Massachusetts Department of Transportation 

 
2 
 
4925-9953-5932, v. 3 
(“DOT”) and an on-ramp to US Route 1; to the south by a rear service driveway owned by DOT; 
to the west by Austin Street (a City of Boston public way) transitioning to the Gilmore Bridge; 
and to the north by New Rutherford Avenue (a City of Boston public way). A middle access 
driveway owned by DOT bisects the Master Plan Area and connects New Rutherford Avenue to 
the rear service driveway. The Master Plan Area currently contains surface parking, which will 
be razed to facilitate development. 
The legal description of the Master Plan Area is attached as Exhibit B hereto. Following 
approval of this Master Plan and the associated map amendment, the Master Plan Area will be 
governed by the PDA Development Plans proceeding under this Master Plan. No approval for 
any elements of the Proposed Projects, whether new or existing and remaining, shall be required 
from the Board of Appeal. All references herein to terms set forth in the Code shall have the 
meanings set forth in the Code, as amended to the effective date hereof. This Master Plan and 
each PDA Development Plan under this Master Plan is not subject to changes to the Code or 
zoning maps that take effect after such effective date. This Master Plan represents a conceptual 
design at an early stage in the planning process. Changes may occur to each Proposed Project’s 
design without the need to amend this Master Plan, provided that the Project is consistent with 
the approved PDA Development Plan providing zoning parameters for such Proposed Project. 
3. 
Planning Objectives and Character of the Master Plan Area. The Proposed 
Projects respond to the surrounding urban design context, placing taller building elements 
proximate to the I-93 viaduct that runs parallel with the rear service driveway and stepping down 
toward New Rutherford Avenue to meet the residential neighborhood edge. For residents of the 
new buildings, the up to 13-, 7-, 9- and 9-story buildings are designed to capitalize on views in 
all directions. The buildings wrap broad open spaces edged by lower building volumes toward 
New Rutherford Avenue. With passive and active programs, the new open spaces will be crafted 
to engage residents and neighbors in social spaces while assisting with stormwater management 
and passive cooling while also providing recreational opportunities for the community. 
The pedestrian experience along New Rutherford Avenue will be improved with a line of 
street trees where not obstructed by existing underground infrastructure, planted in a landscape 
furniture zone, and a widened sidewalk. Trees behind the back of the sidewalk act as a deeper 
filter to New Rutherford Avenue. New trees will be carefully selected to complement the 
existing tree canopy and overall building character while providing a diversity of native species 
to enhance ecological connections. New site lighting will incorporate “dark sky guidelines” and 
will be scaled to a pedestrian, residential scale. 
4. 
Proposed Projects. Each of the four Proposed Projects is described conceptually 
below and will be the subject of a separate PDA Development Plan. The various components are 
preliminarily shown in the project materials attached hereto as Exhibits C through E, in each case 
for illustrative purposes subject to design finalization. It is anticipated that the Proposed Projects 
will be phased, concurrently or independently in any order, subject to market considerations, as 
preliminarily indicated in Exhibit F attached hereto. 
(a) 
Building A. Within the Northern Site, construction of a new, up to 13-
story building containing approximately 250 dwelling units and residential amenities, up to 2,000 
square feet of Gross Floor Area of community gallery/art space or other non-residential use, 

 
3 
 
4925-9953-5932, v. 3 
together with up to 120 structured vehicle parking spaces, bicycle storage in accordance with 
City of Boston Bike Parking Guidelines (anticipated to be up to 251 long-term and up to 51 
short-term bicycle parking spaces), and related site and public realm improvements. 
(b) 
Building B. Within the Northern Site, construction of a new, up to 7-story 
building containing approximately 125 dwelling units and residential amenities, together with 
bicycle storage in accordance with City of Boston Bike Parking Guidelines (anticipated to be up 
to 125 long-term and up to 25 short-term bicycle parking spaces), an approximately 52’ x 80’ 
urban plaza and lawn, a new connection across the Northern Site between New Rutherford 
Avenue and the rear service driveway, and related site and public realm improvements. 
(c) 
Building C. Within the Southern Site, construction of a new, up to 9-story 
building containing approximately 160 dwelling units and residential amenities, up to 14,000 
square feet of Gross Floor Area of early childhood education or other non-residential use, 
together with up to 60 structured vehicle parking spaces, bicycle storage in accordance with City 
of Boston Bike Parking Guidelines (anticipated to be up to 165 long-term and up to 38 short-
term bicycle parking spaces), and related site and public realm improvements. 
(d) 
Building D. Within the Southern Site, construction of a new, up to 9-story 
building containing approximately 170 dwelling units and residential amenities, up to 46,000 
square feet of Gross Floor Area of community recreation or other non-residential use, together 
with up to 60 structured vehicle parking spaces, bicycle storage in accordance with City of 
Boston Bike Parking Guidelines (anticipated to be up to 189 long-term and up to 53 short-term 
bicycle parking spaces), three approximately 90’ x 90’ athletic/multipurpose fields, and related 
site and public realm improvements. 
Additional redevelopment program components include a new connection across the 
Southern Site between New Rutherford Avenue and the rear service driveway to be delivered 
with the first to proceed of Building C or Building D, and shared pedestrian/bicycle path 
improvements along the Southern Site’s frontage on New Rutherford Avenue, and up to 30 
surface vehicle parking spaces within the aforementioned new connections across the Northern 
Site and the Southern Site. 
5. 
Existing Zoning. The Master Plan Area is located within the Mixed Use 1 
Subdistrict and Area PDA I of the Charlestown Neighborhood District governed by Article 62 
and Map 2E of the Code. Portions of the Master Plan Area are located within the Flood Hazard 
District governed by Article 25 of the Code and the Coastal Flood Overlay District governed by 
Article 25A of the Code. The Master Plan Area contains more than 5 acres of land area and is 
PDA-eligible due to its inclusion within Area PDA I. Each of the Proposed Projects will undergo 
review and approval under Articles 80B and 80C of the Code, together with additional 
anticipated approvals described below. 
6. 
Range of Density and Dimensions, and Proposed Uses, of Proposed Projects. 
The range of density and dimensions and proposed uses of the Proposed Projects are as follows, 
as shall be more particularly described in and made effective for each Proposed Project in its 
respective PDA Development Plan under this Master Plan: 

 
4 
 
4925-9953-5932, v. 3 
(a) 
Building A. This building will contain approximately 268,000 square feet 
of Gross Floor Area of residential uses and up to 2,000 square feet of non-residential uses, with 
parking and loading as determined through Article 80B Large Project Review, on an 
approximately 44,969 square foot area of land within the Northern Site. This building will not 
exceed a height of 150 feet. 
(b) 
Building B. This building will contain approximately 126,000 square feet 
of Gross Floor Area of residential uses, with parking and loading as determined through Article 
80B Large Project Review, as more particularly described in the applicable PDA Development 
Plan under this Master Plan, on an approximately 54,069 square foot area of land within the 
Northern Site. This building will not exceed a height of 85 feet. 
(c) 
Building C. This building will contain approximately 157,000 square feet 
of Gross Floor Area of residential uses and up to 14,000 square feet of non-residential uses, with 
parking and loading as determined through Article 80B Large Project Review, as more 
particularly described in the applicable PDA Development Plan under this Master Plan, on an 
approximately 33,771 square foot area of land within the Southern Site. This building will not 
exceed a height of 110 feet. 
(d) 
Building D. This building will contain approximately 177,000 square feet 
of Gross Floor Area of residential uses and up to 46,000 square feet of non-residential uses, with 
parking and loading as determined through Article 80B Large Project Review, as more 
particularly described in the applicable PDA Development Plan under this Master Plan, on an 
approximately 73,590 square foot area of land within the Southern Site. This building will not 
exceed a height of 115 feet. 
Building height shall be measured from 27.5’ Boston City Base as grade, which is an 
average measurement along the back of sidewalk on New Rutherford Avenue between Austin 
Street and the on-ramp to US Route 1, and exclusive of rooftop structures. Based upon a total 
maximum Gross Floor Area of up 790,000 square feet for the four Proposed Projects and the 
approximately 221,056 square feet (approximately 5.1 acres) of land comprising the Master Plan 
Area, the Floor Area Ratio across the Master Plan Area will not exceed 3.6. At least 25% of the 
land area within the Master Plan Area shall be permeable. No Proposed Project shall be 
noncompliant with this Floor Area Ratio maximum or permeability minimum so long as the 
Master Plan Area is compliant on a master site wide basis, the land area for such calculations 
being the land area shown on Exhibit B attached hereto. In the event of any conflict between 
Sections 62-20 and -21 of the Code with respect to Area PDA I and the applicable PDA 
Development Plan under this Master Plan, such PDA Development Plan shall govern. 
7. 
Open Space and Landscaping. The Proposed Projects will transform the Master 
Plan Area from a sea of asphalt into, among other things, areas where the community can gather 
and enjoy newly-available amenities. The urban plaza and lawn and athletic/multipurpose fields, 
substantially as shown on Exhibit D attached hereto, will provide significant recreational 
amenities for the Charlestown community. The planting strategy includes a large quantity of 
canopy trees, which will be comprised of mostly native trees with some naturalized non-natives 
included to provide biological diversity. This strategy helps ameliorate the hazard of tree loss 
due to disease, invasive pests, and climate change. 

 
5 
 
4925-9953-5932, v. 3 
8. 
Range of Parking and Loading Facilities. The number and location of the 
parking and loading components will be determined as part of each Proposed Project’s Article 
80B Large Project Review. It is anticipated that there will be up to 240 structured vehicle 
parking spaces within Buildings A, C, and D, as well as up to 30 surface vehicle parking spaces 
within the new connections across the Northern Site and the Southern Site between New 
Rutherford Avenue and the rear service driveway, and loading activities will occur within the 
rear service driveway via adequate loading facilities. 
9. 
Public Benefits. The redevelopment program contemplates a wide variety of 
public and community benefits consistent with Section 62-23 of the Code. Subject to design 
finalization and approval from appropriate governmental authorities, the specific benefits to be 
delivered by the Proposed Projects collectively, as may be allocated in each PDA Development 
Plan as appropriate, include: 
(a) 
the revitalization of an underutilized site proximate to public transit (i.e., 
MBTA’s Orange Line Community College subway station and bus routes 
92 and 93); 
(b) 
an increase in Charlestown’s housing supply, including income-restricted 
dwelling units that comply with or exceed the applicable 13% income-
restricted requirement of the City of Boston’s Inclusionary Development 
Policy under the Mayor’s Order Relative to Inclusionary Development 
dated December 9, 2015, such that up to 60% of the dwelling units on a 
master sitewide basis at full build out will be income-restricted; 
(c) 
significant open space providing recreational amenities for the 
Charlestown community; 
(d) 
enhanced public realm elements with improved pedestrian and bicycle 
connectivity; 
(e) 
sustainability features such as LEED Gold certifiability, energy-efficient 
building systems, improved site permeability and stormwater treatment, 
reduced urban heat island impacts, and flood resiliency measures, all in 
accordance with Articles 25A and 37 of the Code; 
(f) 
bicycle storage in accordance with City of Boston Bike Parking 
Guidelines; 
(g) 
a new Bluebike station onsite at the corner of New Rutherford Avenue and 
Millers River Littoral Way to support ridership throughout the 
neighborhood; 
(h) 
Transportation Demand Management measures to minimize automobile 
usage; and 
(i) 
additional property tax revenue for the City of Boston. 

 
6 
 
4925-9953-5932, v. 3 
10. 
Other Approvals. Each Proposed Project will be subject to review by the Boston 
Civic Design Commission, and to further review by the BRA of the schematic design, design 
development and construction drawings, pursuant to the BRA’s Development Review Guidelines 
and Article 80B of the Code. Signs shall be permitted as approved from time to time through 
such BRA review in accordance with Article 11 of the Code. Each Proposed Project, subject to 
phasing, will enter into a separate Cooperation Agreement with the BRA, as well as other 
agreements required as a result of such Proposed Project’s Article 80B Large Project Review. 
Aspects of the Proposed Projects may also require other City of Boston approvals, such as from 
the Public Improvement Commission regarding public ways, and the Boston Public Safety 
Commission Committee on Licenses regarding garages and storage of inflammables. Each of the 
Proposed Projects shall be the subject of a PDA Development Plan submitted for Boston Zoning 
Commission and mayoral approval in accordance with Article 80C of the Code. 
11. 
Effect of PDA Master Plan. This Master Plan sets forth the anticipated plan of 
redevelopment and the zoning compliance pathway for the Proposed Projects on the Master Plan 
Area. Upon approval of this Master Plan and any PDA Development Plan for a Proposed Project 
by the BRA and the Boston Zoning Commission, and issuance of one or more Certifications of 
Consistency or Partial Certifications of Consistency, such Proposed Project shall be deemed to 
be in compliance with the requirements of underlying zoning to the extent that such requirements 
have been addressed in the applicable PDA Development Plan. 
A Certification of Consistency or Partial Certification of Consistency may be issued 
separately for each Proposed Project, or subphase thereof, in accordance with Section 80C-8 of 
the Code; provided that the non-compliance of any Proposed Project, or subphase thereof, with 
the terms of this Master Plan and such Proposed Project’s PDA Development Plan shall not 
affect the compliance of any other Proposed Project, or subphase thereof, for which a 
Certification of Consistency has been issued, or affect the right to construct any other Proposed 
Project, or subphase of a Proposed Project, contemplated by this Master Plan. The provisions of 
any PDA Development Plan applicable to a specific Proposed Project, or subphase thereof, may 
only be amended with the consent of the owner of such phase or subphase. 
12. 
Definitions. Unless otherwise set forth herein, capitalized terms used herein but 
not defined shall have the meanings specified in Article 2 of the Code, as amended to the 
effective date hereof, and not as the same may be amended hereafter.

“Code”), this amendment constitutes Amendment No. 6 to Development Plan and Development 
Impact Project Plan for Planned Development Area No. 37 (“Amendment No. 6”). 
I. 
THE EXISTING PDA DEVELOPMENT PLAN FOR PDA NO. 37 
1. 
Procedural History for Planned Development Area No. 37. 
A. The Original Development Plan 
Pursuant to Section 3-1A of the Zoning Code, the Boston Redevelopment Authority (now 
known as Boston Planning and Development Agency, the “Agency”) by a vote taken on January 
18, 1990 approved the Development Plan and Development Impact Project Plan (the “Original 
Development Plan”) for Planned Development Area No. 37 (“PDA No. 37”) in connection with 
the redevelopment (the “Project”) of Prudential Center (the “Prudential Center”). On March 20, 
1990, the Boston Zoning Code was amended by inserting Article 41, “Huntington 
Avenue/Prudential Center District”. On February 22, 1990, the Boston Zoning Commission (the 
“Commission”) approved the Original Development Plan and Map Amendment No. 236 (the 
“1990 Map Amendment”) establishing PDA No. 37, which Original Development Plan and 
associated Map Amendment were effective March 20, 1990. 
B. Development Plan Amendments 1 through 5 
By a vote taken on December 8, 1994 the Agency approved an Amendment to the Original 
Development Plan (“Amendment No. 1”) in connection with the sale of the Sheraton Hotel. On 
December 14, 1994, the Commission approved Amendment No. 1, which Amendment No. 1 was 
effective December 19, 1994. On September 29, 1998, the Agency approved a Second Amendment 
to the Original Development Plan (“Amendment No. 2”) in connection with the sale of Prudential 
Center and with extension of the development schedule. On October 21, 1998, the Commission 
approved Amendment No. 2, which Amendment No. 2 was effective October 23, 1998. By a vote 
taken on May 9, 2002, the Agency approved a Third Amendment to the Original Development 
Plan (“Amendment No. 3”), in connection with the modification of Phases 4b and 5 of the 
Development Plan and the approval of a Master Plan for Phase 6. On July 24, 2002, the 
Commission amended Article 41 by adopting Text Amendment No. 286 and approved 
Amendment No. 3 and Map Amendment No. 406 (“2002 Map Amendment”), which Text

Development Plan. On January 7, 2009, the Commission approved Amendment No. 4, which 
Amendment No. 4 was effective January 7, 2009. By vote taken on December 4, 2008, the Agency 
approved a Fifth Amendment to the Original Development Plan (“Amendment No. 5”), in 
connection with the modification of Phase 6 of the Development Plan. On January 7, 2009, the 
Commission approved Amendment No. 5, which Amendment No. 5 was effective January 7, 2009.

Development Plan or the Code as in effect as of the date of the Development Plan, without giving

2. 
Overview of the Site and Project. 
The Development Plan area encompasses approximately 1,116,222 square feet known as 
the Prudential Center (the “Site”) bounded by Boylston Street, Exeter Street, Huntington Avenue, 
Belvidere Street and the Hynes Convention Center. The Site has been severed into several parcels, 
including the Hotel Site (defined in Amendment No. 1). 
Implementation of the Development Plan began in the early 1990s by The Prudential 
Insurance Company of America (“Prudential”). Pursuant to the terms of Amendment No. 1, on 
December 29, 1994, Sheraton purchased the Hotel Site from Prudential and became owner of the 
Hotel Site by virtue of a deed filed with the Suffolk County Registry of Deeds District of the Land 
Court (the “Land Court”) as Document No. 522046 on Certificate of Title No. 109190. The 
current owner of the Hotel Site is 39 Dalton Owner, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company 
(the “Hotel Site Owner”) by virtue of a deed dated as of February 2, 2022 and filed with the Land 
Court as Document No. 931599 on Certificate of Title No. 138466. The Hotel Site includes, among 
other features, an existing two hundred fifty thousand (250,000) square foot south tower (the 
“South Tower”) as shown on Exhibit A attached hereto.

1.0 
Introduction 
In accordance with Section 3-1A(a), Section 80C-2 and Section 80C-3 of the Boston Zoning 
Code (the “Code”), this document constitutes the Planned Development Area Master Plan 
(the “PDA Master Plan”) for the development of approximately 20 new buildings (each a 
“Building”, and collectively, the “Buildings”) containing in the aggregate, approximately 
5,744,600 square feet (“SF”) of Gross Floor Area (“GFA”) as defined in the Code, on 
multiple land parcels in the South Boston neighborhood of Boston (the “Proposed Project”). 
Refer to Exhibit A for the site location. Upon adoption of an amendment to the Boston 
Zoning Map concurrently with approval of this PDA Master Plan by the Boston Zoning 
Commission (the “Zoning Commission”), these land parcels will comprise a Planned 
Development Area (“PDA”) established pursuant to the provisions of Section 3-1A(a), 
Section 80C-2 and Section 80C-3 of the Code. 
The area of the PDA overlay (the “PDA Overlay Area”), which includes the area below the 
mean high tide line, measures 1,366,789 SF (31.38 acres) and is shown on the PDA Overlay 
Area plan attached hereto as Exhibit B-1 (the “PDA Overlay Area Plan”). A full legal 
description of the PDA Overlay Area Plan is included as Exhibit B-2. It presently is 
anticipated that the entirety of the Proposed Project will be located within the PDA Overlay 
Area. 
The Gillette Company, a Delaware limited liability company that is a wholly owned 
subsidiary of The Procter & Gamble Company, an Ohio corporation (“Gillette”), presently 
plans to construct the Proposed Project (as defined in Section 3.0 below) on parcels of land 
located in South Boston which collectively comprise approximately 1,345,402 SF (30.89 
acres) of uplands (the “Project Site”). The Project Site, which is entirely within the PDA 
Overlay Area, is shown on the plan attached hereto as Exhibit C. 
The Proposed Project involves planning the future of Gillette’s existing approximately 
31.38-acre campus, which currently includes approximately 1,500,000 SF of GFA utilized 
for office, manufacturing, laboratory and warehouse uses, as well as various accessory and 
ancillary uses. A portion of the Project Site includes filled tidelands that are subject to 
licensing under M.G.L. c. 91 and its implementing regulations. 
The Project Site as set forth in the PDA Master Plan is presently owned by Gillette. Gillette 
is the current proponent of this PDA Master Plan, but it is anticipated that at some point 
other entities will become proponents for this PDA Master Plan, or for individual Project 
Components (as defined in Section 8.0 below). The term “Proponent” as used herein is 
intended to apply to Gillette as to any portions of the Project Site which it may own from

time to time, and to such other entity or entities which may own all or portions of the Project 
Site in the future. 
A. Redevelopment Vision & Goals 
Redevelopment of the Project Site provides a unique opportunity to: 
1. Deliver one of the largest public waterfront parks on private land ever created in this 
part of the City of Boston (the “City”). This Waterfront Park (as defined in Section 
3.0.C.1).a) below) will be resilient to the projected 2070 sea level rise in the adjacent 
Fort Point Channel. 
2. Provide public access to the Project Site, which has been inaccessible to the public for 
more than 60 years and connect the Project Site (including the Waterfront Park) to 
surrounding neighborhoods, open spaces, the waterfront and public transportation. 
3. Transform the existing industrial-oriented commercial uses into a vibrant mixed-use 
community by introducing residential uses and density that, combined with the existing 
commercial density, will activate ground floors and result in welcoming view corridors. 
4. Create a forward-thinking climate-resilient development that supports the City’s 
environmental goals, includes green infrastructure to address district stormwater 
concerns, and promotes coastal resilience by protecting much of the Project Site and the 
neighborhood beyond. 
5. Develop a transit-oriented, sustainable neighborhood that improves circulation in the 
area, and contributes to a City that is welcoming, accessible, and inclusive. 
6. Generate a significant number of construction and permanent jobs. Each phase of the 
Proposed Project will unlock new property tax revenues for the City, while also 
contributing linkage fees towards the creation of housing and job training. Other project 
mitigation elements and public benefits will be identified as part of the project review 
process with the City and community. 
Existing zoning allows for primarily commercial and industrial uses. Adoption of this PDA 
Master Plan will also allow residential uses along with increased density. The current vision 
allows for the construction of approximately 20 Buildings with a blend of residential and 
commercial uses to be built out over time. A floor area ratio (“FAR”) of approximately 4.3 
will be achieved as measured across the Project Site (not at each developable parcel). It is 
further anticipated that the Proposed Project will support the Project Site’s transition from 
uses consistent with a Manufacturing District, where allowed uses are primarily commercial 
and industrial, to a Project Site with a mix of uses, with a minimum of 30% of the total GFA 
to be dedicated to residential uses. 
The Proposed Project proposes a thoughtful layout that is seamlessly integrated with the 
surrounding transportation network. It will accommodate a wide variety of modalities with 
a mix of pedestrian friendly streets and vehicle-free corridors providing access directly to 
the waterfront. The Proposed Project is anticipated to include contiguous, usable public 
open space for over approximately 50% of the Project Site, including a dynamic, publicly 
accessible multi-acre Waterfront Park (as defined in Section 3.0.C.1).a) below), linked to 

 
 
3 – Gillette Fort Point Redevelopment 
adjacent public realm improvements. The Project Site will feature a varied and distinctive 
skyline with Buildings that step down to create a comfortable scale along the waterfront. 
The circulation pattern envisioned for the Project Site will include a major street running 
generally northeast-southwest extending Necco Street in a southerly direction through much 
of the Project Site to Richards Street. The circulation pattern will also include Richards 
Street, a major street running generally east/west through the Project Site connecting A 
Street and Dorchester Avenue, and a second street in the location of former West First Street 
(a/k/a Gillette Park), also connecting A Street and Dorchester Avenue. There also will be a 
variety of minor private or public streets on the Project Site that will enable future parking 
and loading needs of the Buildings to be erected on the Project Site, as well as provide 
additional pedestrian connections from A Street and West Second Street to the major open 
space along Fort Point Channel. 
This PDA Master Plan is intended to provide flexibility to allow for future approval 
processes to dictate specific uses within each Development Plan (as defined in Section 
1.0.C. below). The conceptual plans and imagery included in the attached exhibits illustrate 
a potential configuration wherein the residential Buildings are clustered into two 
neighborhoods, both of which face toward the primary open space adjacent to Fort Point 
Channel. One neighborhood is configured along Necco Street north of Richards Street, and 
the other is configured along Richards Street and Dorchester Avenue in the southwesterly 
portion of the Project Site. The commercial Buildings are clustered generally into two areas: 
one adjacent to A Street in the northeasterly portion of the Project Site, and the other located 
south of Richards Street along A Street and West Second Street in the southerly portion of 
the Project Site. The conceptual plans and imagery included in the exhibits attached to this 
Master Plan are likely to evolve following the approval of this PDA Master Plan, so as to 
be responsive to the design review process associated with the ultimate approval of each 
Development Plan. 
B. Existing Site Uses & Operations 
The majority of the Project Site is currently used as Gillette’s South Boston Manufacturing 
Center (“SBMC”), the existing home of its headquarters, as well as for large research and 
development, manufacturing, warehouse, electric power generation uses and various 
accessory and ancillary uses. These facilities together comprise about 1,500,000 SF of GFA. 
There also are several parking areas. Under the South Boston Parking Freeze enforced by 
the Boston Air Pollution Control Commission (the “BAPCC”), the Project Site was 
inventoried as containing 1,798 parking spaces; however, over time, the Project Site has 
come to have fewer parking spaces due to additional construction and other constraints, so 
that the maximum number of off-street parking spaces that can be presently accommodated 
on the Project Site without lifters is approximately 1,550. 
Gillette intends to transition its operations from the Project Site to other locations as they 
become available. Gillette’s innovative manufacturing operations will be relocated to 
Gillette’s new manufacturing facilities in Andover, MA. Once that relocation occurs, 
Gillette will be in a position to commence demolition of certain elements of the SBMC and 
begin certain additional enabling work that will allow for the implementation of the vision 
set forth in this PDA Master Plan.

C. PDA Master Plan 
Consistent with the requirements of Article 80C and Section 3-1A(a) of the Code, this PDA 
Master Plan sets forth the proposed development concept, including, without limitation, the 
planning objectives and character of the Proposed Project, the location of the sub-districts 
(the “Sub-Districts”) to accommodate future Buildings, the proposed public realm 
improvements to be constructed in connection therewith, the proposed open space areas to 
be created within the PDA Overlay Area, the proposed uses in and around the Buildings, 
the proposed dimensions and densities of the Buildings, the proposed traffic circulation 
around and through the Project Site, the general locations of proposed parking and loading 
accommodations, a description of access to nearby public transportation services, utility 
information and phasing information regarding the Proposed Project. 
This PDA Master Plan also includes conceptual plans for the new public realm 
improvements to be constructed, addresses relevant planning history and the neighborhood 
context within which the Proposed Project will be developed, and contains an overview of 
the public benefits, public realm improvements and potential mitigation concepts associated 
with the Proposed Project. As set forth below, more definitive plans articulating the ultimate 
public benefits, public realm improvements and potential mitigation concepts will be 
brought forward by the Proponent in the Development Plans that will be associated with the 
Article 80B process as applied to the various Buildings within the Proposed Project. 
This PDA Master Plan consists of 30 pages of text and the attachments designated as 
Exhibits A through N. All references herein to “this PDA Master Plan” or “the PDA 
Master Plan” pertain only to these 30 pages of text and Exhibits A through N. 
This PDA Master Plan sets forth all of the zoning parameters for the Proposed Project within 
the PDA Overlay Area. However, this PDA Master Plan contemplates that multiple 
Development Plans, as such term is referenced in Section 3-1A(a) of the Code (each, a 
“Development Plan” and collectively, the “Development Plans”), will be submitted to the 
Boston Redevelopment Authority, acting through the Boston Planning Department (the 
“Planning Department”), in accordance with the provisions of Articles 80B and 80C of the 
Code, and Section 3-1A(a) of the Code, in connection with the development of one or more 
specific Buildings at the Project Site and any public realm improvements and/or new open 
space area(s) related thereto. 
The design plans for each Building and related improvements will be more granular and 
subject to future review by the Boston Civic Design Commission (“BCDC”) and the 
Planning Department. Hence, the design of the Buildings, the conceptual design plans for 
the open spaces and public realm improvements referenced herein, the proposed vehicular, 
pedestrian and bicycle circulation around and through the Project Site, the proposed parking 
and loading accommodations, as well as the conceptual site plan for the Proposed Project 
included in this PDA Master Plan, will be subject to further design refinement and will 
evolve during the course of the design review process pursuant to Article 80B and 80C of 
the Code. In this way, the actual Buildings constructed and their related improvements will 
be better attuned to the neighborhood context as the PDA Master Plan is implemented 
through the design review process.

D. Chapter 91 Jurisdiction 
Based upon Gillette’s examination of various historical plans and documents, Gillette has 
determined that the PDA Overlay Area includes approximately 1,365,461 SF of Tidelands as 
defined in M.G.L. c. 91 and accompanying regulations at 310 CMR 9.00 et seq. (“Chapter 91”). 
Approximately 1,010,339 SF of these Tidelands are considered to be Private Tidelands that 
are not Landlocked Tidelands. The Filled Private Tidelands that are not Landlocked 
Tidelands constitute approximately 994,048 SF of the Project Site. Flowed Private 
Tidelands constitute approximately 16,291 SF but are not part of the Project Site. 
A smaller portion of the Tidelands in the PDA Overlay Area (approximately 24,101 SF) 
constitutes Commonwealth Tidelands by virtue of being land formerly below the historic 
mean low water mark; that determination is primarily based upon the U.S. Coast Survey 
map of Boston Harbor conducted in 1847. Of these known Commonwealth Tidelands, 
approximately 19,035 SF are Filled Commonwealth Tidelands and are part of the Project 

 
 
12 – Gillette Fort Point Redevelopment 
Site. Approximately 5,066 SF of the Commonwealth Tidelands in the PDA Overlay Area 
are Flowed Commonwealth Tidelands but are not part of the Project Site. 
Further, a Determination of Applicability was issued by the Massachusetts Department of 
Environmental Protection (“MassDEP”) Waterways Regulation Program in 2021 recorded 
with the Suffolk Registry of Deeds (the “Suffolk Registry”) in Book 66845, Page 209, 
which found that certain portions of the Private Tidelands on the Project Site constitute 
Landlocked Tidelands; that determination affected approximately 331,021 SF of the Project 
Site. The Chapter 91 jurisdiction plan that is included as Exhibit E-3 illustrates the 
Commonwealth Tidelands, the Landlocked Tidelands, and the Private Tidelands that are 
part of the PDA Overlay Area and the Project Site. 
Pursuant to the provisions of 310 CMR 9.00 et seq., the primary implications of the presence 
of Filled Commonwealth Tidelands on the Project Site are as follows: 
1. Pursuant to Section 9.53(1), the developer of nonwater-dependent uses on Filled 
Commonwealth Tidelands must not interfere with possible water-dependent uses on 
such land. 
2. Pursuant to Section 9.53(2)(a), if a project includes a water-dependent use zone, the 
developer must provide at least one facility utilizing the shoreline that promotes water-
based public activity. 
3. Pursuant to Section 9.53(2)(b), the project must include exterior open spaces for active 
or passive recreation, which spaces must be equivalent to the square footage of Filled 
Commonwealth Tidelands on the project site that is landward of a project shoreline and 
not within the footprint of buildings. 
4. Pursuant to Section 9.53(2)(c), the project must provide interior space for facilities of 
public accommodation, at least equivalent to the square footage of all Commonwealth 
tidelands on the project site within the footprint of buildings containing nonwater-
dependent facilities of private tenancy. 
5. Pursuant to Section 9.53(2)(d), the project shall include a management plan for all on-
site facilities offering water-related benefits to the public. 
In regard to the relatively small area (19,035 SF) of Filled Commonwealth Tidelands which 
have been determined to exist on the Project Site, Gillette is prepared to meet applicable 
MassDEP requirements over the course of construction of the Proposed Project. In regard 
to any additional portions of the Project Site which may yet be similarly determined to be 
Filled Commonwealth Tidelands, Gillette also intend to meet such MassDEP obligations 
over the course of construction of the Proposed Project. In addition, Gillette is prepared to 
meet all MassDEP requirements pertaining to Private Tidelands under 310 CMR 9.00 et 
seq., and to Landlocked Tidelands pursuant to 301 CMR 13.00 et seq. Exhibit E-3 depicts 
all the Tidelands within the PDA Overlay Area as presently determined.

F. Climate Change and Resiliency 
1) Coastal Flooding 
The Project Site will be designed to protect most of the PDA Overlay Area and adjacent 
areas from projected flooding associated with the 1% annual chance event in 2070. The 
area of the existing Harborwalk and areas below the seawall will not be made resilient to 
this standard, but, assuming that federal funding is forthcoming, the balance of the Project 
Site will accommodate the Resilient Fort Point Channel Infrastructure (“RFPCI”) project. 
Separate and apart from that RFPCI project, the Proponent will design and construct the 
grading of the Project Site so that such protection is provided, effectively creating a 
resiliency system upland of the RFPCI project that will complement the RFPCI project. 
Buildings will comply with Article 25A of the Code pertaining to the Coastal Flood 
Resilience Overlay District, as applicable, to protect persons and structures from the adverse 
effects of sea level rise and storm surge associated with climate change. Project Components 
(as defined in Section 8.0) will also comply with the Article 37 Green Building and Climate 
Resiliency Guidelines in order to minimize adverse environmental impacts, conserve 
natural resources, foster resilience to climate change, promote a more sustainable City, and 
enhance the quality of life in the City. Exhibit L presents the proposed site elevations across 
the Project Site as presently contemplated. 
2) Precipitation Flooding 
According to the Boston Water and Sewer Commission (“BWSC”), there is a significant 
probability that the 10-year, 24-hour design storm precipitation level will increase to at least 
6 inches by the end of the century. The Proposed Project will comply with the City’s Smart 
Utilities requirements and the BWSC’s regulations, policies and guidelines related to 
stormwater management to prepare for the effects of climate change. 

 
 
15 – Gillette Fort Point Redevelopment 
3) Extreme Heat 
According to the Heat Resilience Solutions for Boston report (the “Heat Report”), if 
greenhouse gas emissions continue at the current rate, it is likely that by the 2050s the City 
will have up to 25 to 42 days above 90°F each year and up to 1 to 6 days above 100°F. The 
current lack of vegetation on the Project Site contributes to above-average temperatures in 
this location. Consistent with the goals identified in the Heat Report, the Proposed Project 
will aim to reduce heat exposure for site users, adapt to heat, and help foster healthy, 
connected communities. Further recommendations from the Heat Report will be evaluated 
for potential implementation as design progresses.

A. Enabling Phase 
The enabling phase of the Proposed Project includes pre-construction and construction 
activities to prepare the PDA Overlay Area for future Building development, and may 
involve demolition of existing building structures, remediation of past reportable releases 
to soil, site resiliency measures, new onsite roadways, utility and other infrastructure, 
publicly accessible open space and public realm improvements (the “Enabling Phase”). 
Future Building development sites will be prepared to a defined delivery condition in the 
Enabling Phase, including temporary measures for soil stabilization, drainage, public safety, 
and security. The Enabling Phase will also include temporary construction to accommodate 
interim land uses, such as parking. 
The Enabling Phase is expected to commence once all permits and entitlements are obtained 
and when Gillette has relocated various existing operations from the PDA Overlay Area 
that otherwise would interfere with the Enabling Phase. The Enabling Phase activities will 
be conducted in two distinct work zones: Enabling Zone 1 is defined as the land north of 
(and including) Richards Street; and Enabling Zone 2 is the land south of Richards Street. 
Refer to Exhibit M for the conceptual enabling phasing diagram. It is expected that the 
Enabling Phase will begin in Enabling Zone 1 and that most of the Enabling Phase activities 
in Enabling Zone 2 will occur following the completion of the Enabling Phase activities in 
Enabling Zone 1. While it is possible that all existing Gillette operations in a given Enabling 
Zone will have been relocated prior to the start of the Enabling Phase activities in that 

 
 
20 – Gillette Fort Point Redevelopment 
Enabling Zone, Gillette will require flexibility to retain some operations in a given Enabling 
Zone while conducting such Enabling Phase activities in that Enabling Zone as can be 
undertaken without ceasing all operations. 
Section 9.0.E. of this PDA Master Plan describes the known soil contamination documented 
in existing Release Tracking Number (“RTN”) filings and Exhibit J shows associated RTN 
locations. Clean fill material will be imported to raise the land elevation of portions of the 
Project Site in support of the Proposed Project’s resilience objectives. Enabling Zone 1 is 
adjacent to the Fort Point Channel and therefore key to the City’s long-term resilience 
planning efforts. The elevation of the land located between Richards Street and Necco 
Street to the Harborwalk will be raised by as much as seven feet (7’). If not earlier achieved 
by the RFPCI project, the Proposed Project will achieve the City’s 2070 resilience 
objectives for much of the PDA Overlay Area upon completion of the Enabling Zone 1 
earthwork operations; at which point, finish grades for the extension of both Necco Street 
and Richards Street will be established (Exhibit M). Stormwater infiltration and detention 
infrastructure to support district-wide requirements will be studied for landscape 
implementation in and/or beneath designated public Open Spaces. It is also anticipated that 
the Proposed Project will crush and repurpose acceptable concrete construction material 
salvaged from building demolition for use as fill material beneath new streets. Recycled 
concrete material will reduce the need for virgin materials, while also reducing landfill 
waste and related transportation impacts. A Beneficial Use Determination (“BUD”) may be 
required by the MassDEP for this purpose. 
Construction of Necco and Richards Streets, including related utility infrastructure, in the 
PDA Overlay Area will begin once building demolition and soil remediation efforts allow 
and the associated Sub-Districts development begins that will require the street 
infrastructure. The portions of Necco Street and Richards Streets adjacent to future Building 
sites will be delivered with temporary sidewalks and surface improvements until such time 
as the adjacent Building development occurs. Public roadway improvements will be 
designed and constructed in accordance with City of Boston entitlements, Boston Complete 
Streets Design Guidelines, the Americans with Disabilities Act, and Massachusetts 
Architectural Access Board requirements. Substantial completion of Necco Street and 
Richards Street will denote the completion of the Enabling Phase activities within Enabling 
Zone 1 (Exhibit M). 
The Waterfront Park in Enabling Zone 1 represents a significant future amenity to the local 
community and to the City. It is important to the Proposed Project that the public be 
provided with access to this waterfront amenity as soon as practicable. However, most of 
the Enabling Phase activities within Enabling Zone 1 must be substantially completed for 
this Waterfront Park to take shape. It may be possible for portions of the Waterfront Park 
to be made available to the public initially in a temporary state of completion at the 
completion of the Enabling Phase work in Enabling Zone 1. Development of Open Spaces 
OS-A through OS-G will occur incrementally as future/adjacent Building development 
occurs. Public Open Spaces will be constructed in accordance with Section 3.0.C.1).a) of 
this PDA Master Plan and City entitlements.

Site preparation and stabilization measures will be undertaken in SD-1 and SD-2 as part of 
the Enabling Phase to provide a safe, durable condition that can be reasonably maintained 
until future building development is entitled. Site preparation and stabilization will include 
temporary site drainage infrastructure, topsoil and seeding, and/or asphalt pavement (if for 
temporary parking), and security fencing, if appropriate. SD-5 will be finished as an 
extension of OS-A until a civic project is designated for the site. 
Completion of the Enabling Phase activities in Enabling Zone 1 represents a point at which 
further development of the Proposed Project can reasonably pause for several years, 
allowing SD-1 and SD-2 development to align with real estate market demand. Existing 
building structures in Enabling Zone 2 may remain occupied, or be temporarily leased, until 
demand for land in Enabling Zone 2 is realized. Subject to real estate market conditions, it 
is possible for the Enabling Phase activities in Enabling Zone 2 to progress immediately 
after, or concurrently with, the Enabling Phase activities in Enabling Zone 1. 
The Enabling Phase activities in Enabling Zone 2 are similar in scope to Enabling Zone 1, 
including demolition, remediation of contamination within existing RTN boundaries, site 
infill and grading, roadway construction, and development site preparation. In Enabling Zone 
2, public roadway construction will involve the construction of West First Street from A Street 
to Dorchester Avenue. Site preparation and stabilization measures will be undertaken in SD-
3 and SD-4 in the final stages of the Enabling Zone 2 Enabling Phase work. 
B. Development Phase 
Similar to the Enabling Phase work outlined above, it is anticipated that building (vertical) 
development will be enabled to commence in two distinct zones: Enabling Zone 1 being

Building development in Enabling Zone 1 will occur in Sub-Districts SD-1 and SD-2,

A. Site Remediation

Urban Design & Public Realm 
The Proposed Project will create one of the largest waterfront open spaces on private land 
ever created in this part of the City, which open space will be adjacent to Fort Point Channel, 
contribute to resiliency against sea level rise of the Project Site and its surrounding 
neighborhoods, and be both accessible by and inclusive of all City residents. The Proposed 
Project will open a Project Site that has been inaccessible to the public for more than 60 
years, and connect it to surrounding neighborhoods, open spaces, the waterfront and public 
transportation. It will transform the existing industrial-oriented uses into a vibrant mixed-
use community that includes both residential and commercial uses, with active ground 
floors and welcoming view corridors. 
1) Streets

and landscaping as described below. New public streets will include: 
 Richards Street, from A Street to Dorchester Avenue. This street will feature a 
dedicated one-way bus lane, two-way vehicular traffic lanes, dedicated two-way bike lanes, 
and significant public sidewalks, including planting and furnishings.

street will feature two-way vehicular travel lanes, two parking lanes, dedicated two-way 
bike lanes, and significant public sidewalks, including planting and furnishings. 
• West First Street, from A Street to Dorchester Avenue. This street will feature a 
dedicated one-way bus lane, two-way vehicular travel lanes, dedicated two-way bike 
lanes and public sidewalks, including planting and furnishings. 
During the period prior to the construction of West First Street, two-way bus lanes on 
Richards Street are contemplated.

As described in Section 3.0.C.3) above, the Proposed Project includes seven dedicated Open 
Spaces, comprising a total of approximately 8.0 acres. Those Open Space areas are 
identified on Exhibit E-2.

C. Sustainable and Climate Change Resilient Development 
The Proposed Project will advance the City’s carbon neutral and climate ready goals by 
incorporating a variety of sustainable design and resilient building strategies designed to 
reduce carbon emissions, improve water quality, reduce the urban heat island effect, 
maximize the conservation of energy and water, and reduce the risk of flooding due to sea

applicable future sustainable development and resiliency standards that may be set forth in 
amendments to Article 37, as well as all future applicable requirements under the BERDO 
and the Massachusetts State Building Code as in effect in the City.

Green infrastructure will be used to address the Proposed Project stormwater. 
D. Transportation 
The Proposed Project will be a transit-oriented development that will improve circulation 
in the area, and contribute to a City that is welcoming, accessible, and equitable. The 
Proposed Project will also include transportation mitigation consistent with commitments 
to be made by the Proponent prior to the approval of this PDA Master Plan. 
E. Infrastructure/Smart Utilities 
Each Building within the Proposed Project will employ Smart Utilities compliant systems 
and infrastructure, necessary utilities and service infrastructure within the street rights of 
way, and appropriate coastal flood resiliency measures consistent with the RFPCI project, 
as applicable. Buildings will be subject to Smart Utilities review during the applicable 
Article 80 development review process. 
F. Socioeconomic 
Affordable housing will be created in connection with the Proposed Project, so as to increase 
the affordable housing supply in the South Boston neighborhood. The Proposed Project will 
generate numerous construction and permanent jobs at the Project Site over many years, 
while yielding important Housing Exactions and Jobs Contributions Exactions. 
The Proposed Project will provide City residents with apprenticeships and employment 
opportunities associated with project construction. Such apprenticeship and employment 
opportunities shall commence upon issuance of the first demolition permit for the Proposed 
Project and shall continue during construction of the Proposed Project. 
The Proposed Project also will provide permanent employment opportunities associated with 
the non-residential and residential uses ultimately in place as part of the Proposed Project.

A. Comprehensive Transportation Study 
A transportation study (Attachment 1) has been developed to quantify the transportation 
impacts generated by the Proposed Project and to devise a comprehensive transportation 
mitigation and improvement plan that supports future operations of the Proposed Project 
and provides area-wide transportation improvements to South Boston’s Fort Point 
neighborhood. A major emphasis of this proposed redevelopment effort focuses on area 
urban mobility, including improved access and circulation to support the Project Site and 
abutting properties, access to key transit nodes, and significant pedestrian and bicycle 
infrastructure improvements. 
 The purpose of these analyses is to: 
• Define and quantify existing transportation conditions in the Project Study Area; 
• Estimate the transportation demand that may be generated under future conditions based 
on the proposed program for the Proposed Project; 
• Assess potential impacts of the added Proposed Project travel demand and develop a set 
of mitigation strategies and improvement measures that will help lessen the 
transportation impacts of the Proposed Project; 
• Demonstrate that these improvement measures and transportation mitigation efforts will 
meet or exceed Planning Department and BTD requirements and will serve as 
exceptional public benefits; and 
• Illustrate the Proposed Project’s prioritization of transit, pedestrian and bicycle modes 
as part of the overall Transportation Demand Management (“TDM”) strategy and 
commitment to modern urban mobility. 
This study finds that the Proposed Project will result in additional trips generated by all 
modes to and from the Project Site, which are expected to produce localized impacts to the 
surrounding transportation infrastructure. These impacts will be mitigated through various 
actions ranging from significant infrastructure and operational improvements to proactive 
TDM measures. 
Exhibits G-1 through G-5 illustrate the proposed transportation facilities and 
improvements for the Proposed Project. 
B. Historic Resources 
VHB identified properties within and in the vicinity of the Project Site that are listed in the 
National and/or State Registers of Historic Places, included in the Massachusetts Historical 
Commission’s (“MHC”) Inventory of Historic and Archaeological Assets of the 
Commonwealth (the “Inventory”), and Massachusetts Department of Transportation’s 
(“MassDOT”) South Station Expansion Project Historic Architectural Resources Technical 
Report, updated March 2017. 
The on-site Gillette complex (MHC # not available) consists of 20 extant buildings on 
approximately 31 acres of land, constructed between circa 1910 and circa 2000. Several of 
the buildings, especially at the south end, were constructed prior to Gillette’s acquisition of 
the property and were subsumed into the developing complex. The complex was determined

Refer to Attachment 2 for the complete list of historic resources within the vicinity of the

E. Environmental Site Contamination 
In 1905, Gillette relocated from Atlantic Avenue in Boston to its present location on West 
First Street in South Boston. Over the years, Gillette acquired adjoining properties, and 
constructed new buildings for offices, research and development and the manufacturing of 
razor blades. 
There are three origins to impacts in soil and groundwater at the Project Site: 
• Historic filling of tidelands in the mid-1800s with various sources of material, resulting 
in trace levels of metals and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in soil (this is ubiquitous 
in areas of made land in the City and pre-dates Gillette’s ownership); 
• Releases from prior owners/operators of land ultimately subsequently purchased by 
Gillette; and 
• Releases from Gillette’s operations. 
Exhibit J includes a map of all releases within the Project Site. Refer to Attachment 5 for 
further details of the on-site releases.

PUBLIC OPEN SPACE
PROJECT SITE BOUNDARY LINE

Created by the project for fee transfer to public

PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE OPEN SPACE 
[or POPS]
[ 339,104 sf proposed = 25% of total sf ]
Created by the project to be accessible by the 
general public without a fee; privately-owned and 
maintained by the fee-holding private development/institution
in perpetuity (not protected open space, 
privately-owned public space).
PUBLIC REALM
[ 182,300 sf proposed = 14% of total sf ]
Can include:
• Buffers (transitional/interstitial spaces) such as 
rain gardens, shy zones, furnishing zones, 
expanded sidewalks (beyond what exists in the 
established adjacent right-of-way). The private 
development/institution is responsible for maintenance.
• Connections - walkways/bikeways through a 
private parcel site that provide connection to 
amenities available to the public, or a through 
block connection; may be open to public use. 
The private development/institution is responsible for 
maintenance of these types of connections. 
Driveway and loading zones should not be 
counted in the calculation of Open Space. 
• Publicly-owned sidewalks in an established 
right-of-way will count as open space if the 
development/institution is improving and maintaining them 
through a LMI; privately-owned sidewalks 
associated with established private 
rights-of-ways. The private development/institution is 
responsible for maintenance.
• Bike lanes and areas that serve pedestrian and 
bicycle transportation that are not necessarily 
associated with established rights-of-way. The 
private development/institution is responsible for 
maintenance. 
GROUND FLOOR
AMENITY SPACE
[ 18,000 sf proposed = 1% of total sf ]
Outdoor amenity space that is for the exclusive use 
of the project--typically ground floor retail space; 
open to public use for a fee (but can be made 
available for free); retail-associated space (can be 
designated in a retail lease, but does not 
necessarily have to be assigned in a lease or to a 
retail use). The private development/institutional entity or the 
current leaseholder is responsible for maintenance.
PRIVATE AMENITY SPACE
[ ##,### sf proposed = ##.#% of total sf ]
Privately-owned, exterior spaces used only by 
building/development users (owners and tenants), 
such as balconies and roof decks. The private 
development/institution or private user (owner or tenant) is 
responsible for maintenance.
PUBLIC REALM - PUBLIC ROAD
[ 112,700 sf proposed = 8% of total sf ]
Establishment of a new public highway easement counts 
 toward open space if it is designated as a new public road.
BUILDING SPACE
Space that is not open to the sky, including all building 
interiors, and thus does not qualify as “open space”.
