1. 
PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA DEVELOPMENT PLAN. On March 
14, 2019, the Boston Redevelopment Authority, doing business as the Boston Planning & 
Development Agency (the “Authority”) approved an Amended and Restated Planned 
Development Area Master Plan for Planned Development Area No. 51 pursuant to Article 3, 
Section 3-1A and Article 80, Section 80C of the Boston Zoning Code (the “Code”) for the Hood 
Park in Charlestown (the “Development”), which Master Plan was amended by First 
Amendment to Amended and Restated Master Plan approved by the Authority on December 12, 
2019, and by Second Amendment to Amended and Restated Master Plan approved by the 
Authority on _________________, 2025 (as amended, the “PDA Master Plan”). Capitalized 
terms used herein without definition which are defined in the PDA Master Plan shall have the 
meanings ascribed to them therein. 
 
On October 20, 2000 the Boston Zoning Commission (the “Commission”), by the 
adoption of Map Amendment No. 382, approved the PDA Master Plan and amended the series of 
maps entitled “Zoning Districts City of Boston,” dated August 15, 1962, as amended, by adding 
a “D” designation, indicating a Planned Development Area overlay district, to the Site. 
 
The PDA Master Plan contemplates that one or more PDA Development Plans for phases 
of the Development may be submitted either simultaneously with or subsequent to the 
submission of the PDA Master Plan. 
 
In accordance with Article 3, Section 3-1A of the Code and Article 80, Section 80C, this 
development plan sets forth information on the construction of a building to contain up to 18 
residential units, with approximately 24,500 square feet of ground floor retail space, along with 
below grade parking areas, which parking areas will be shared with 25 Supertest Street (as set 
forth in the Development Plan for 25 Supertest Street approved by the Authority), along with the 
construction of a portion of Supertest Street and a portion of a fifteen (15) foot wide multi-use 
bicycle and pedestrian path along the northern property boundary (collectively, the “Project”). 

2 
The Project is located on a portion of an approximately twenty-acre site which is the former 
Hood Dairy Plant located on the west side of Rutherford Avenue in the Charlestown section of 
Boston, Suffolk County, Massachusetts (the “Site”) within a Special Purpose Overlay District 
Planned Development Area (“PDA”). The Project will be located on a vacant portion of the site 
that was most recently used for surface parking. 
 
This development plan includes the proposed location and appearance of structures, open 
spaces and landscaping, the proposed uses of the Project, the proposed dimensions of the 
structure, the proposed density, the proposed traffic circulation, parking and loading facilities, 
access to public transportation and other major elements of the Project (the “Development 
Plan”). 
 
2. 
DEVELOPER. The owner and developer of the portion of the Site on which the 
Project will be undertaken (the “Project Site”) is Hood Park, LLC, a Massachusetts limited 
liability company (the “Owner”). 
 
3. 
LOCATION AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT SITE. The Project 
Site is the approximately 57,725 square foot portion of the Site as referenced in the Project Plans, as 
hereinafter defined. As of the date of this Development Plan, the Project Site has not been 
subdivided into a separate lot for zoning purposes. The Developer shall have the right to so 
subdivide the Project Site at any time, which subdivision shall not require amendment of this 
Development Plan. 
 
The Project Site lies in the Charlestown Neighborhood District established by Article 62 of 
the Code, and more particularly within a Mixed-Use Subdistrict in which Planned Development 
Areas are allowed (the “Zoning District”). 
 
4. 
PROPOSED LOCATION AND APPEARANCE OF STRUCTURE. The 
Project consists of the development of a new structure that will be approximately 45 feet high 
(which height includes mechanical equipment) that will contain approximately 49,800 square 
feet with approximately 83 below grade parking spaces that will be shared with 25 Supertest 
Street. 
 
The Project is consistent with the criteria specified in Article 62, Section 62-23 of the 
Code for the approval of planned development areas in the Zoning District. These include the 
“diversification and expansion of Charlestown’s economy and job opportunities through 
economic activity,” as well as “significant mobility improvements through the addition of, but 
not limited to, streets, sidewalks, and bike lanes” and “provision of affordable housing.” 
 
Plans showing the architectural elements of the Project entitled “15 Supertest Street, 
Charlestown, Massachusetts” prepared by Elkus Manfredi Architects (the “Project Plans”) are 
attached hereto as Appendix A and incorporated herein by this reference. 
 
5. 
OPEN SPACES AND LANDSCAPING. The Project also includes pedestrian 
improvements to Rutherford Avenue as shown on the Landscape Plan attached hereto as part of 
the Project Plans. 

3 
 
6. 
PROPOSED USES OF THE SITE AND STRUCTURE. In accordance with 
Article 80, Section 80C of the Code, the uses of the Site may include the allowed and conditional 
uses set forth in Article 62 of the Code, including without limitation the uses set forth in the PDA 
Master Plan, and described by reference to the definitions set forth in Article 2 of the Code as in 
effect on the date of approval of the PDA Master Plan, except as otherwise noted, all of which 
uses, notwithstanding any classification to the contrary in Article 62 of the Code, are expressly 
allowed within the Project Site. A description of the major use components for the Project is set 
forth on Appendix B attached hereto

(3) levels, including the mechanical penthouse, plus rooftop mechanical equipment, rooftop solar 
panels, penthouses and screen walls for a total maximum height of 45 feet. The loading area will 
be accessed off of Supertest Street, as will the ramp to the underground parking area. The gross 
floor area of the Project will be approximately 49,800 square feet. For purposes of determining 
gross floor area in accordance with the Code, storage areas, parking garage areas, solar, 
mechanical and electrical spaces, both within the Project and on the penthouse, shall not be 
included.

9. 
PROPOSED VEHICULAR AND PEDESTRIAN TRAFFIC 
CIRCULATION. 
 
Traffic Circulation: 
 
Currently, the Site has access from Rutherford Avenue on a driveway from the northern 
portion of the Site to Rutherford Avenue. As described in the PDA Master Plan, Supertest Street 
will be constructed in the northern portion of the Site to connect with Rutherford Avenue and 
Stack Street. There is also access from the Site onto D Street leading to Spice Street, Cambridge 
Street and Sullivan Square. This driveway primarily serves traffic coming from or heading 
toward Spice Street. As described in the PDA Master Plan, Stack Street will lead from Hood 
Park Drive to D Street and will replace the current driveway near this location. 
 
The Site is located on the west side of Rutherford Avenue (Route 99) and just east of 
Interstate Route 93 (I-93), which runs parallel to Route 99. The Route 99 underpass is adjacent 
to the Site, with two travel lanes in each direction. The I-93 overpass adjacent to the Site 
connects Charlestown with I-93 North, with two travel lanes in each direction. Rutherford 
Avenue itself near the Site is divided into a one-way pair by the Route 99 underpass and I-93 
overpass. 
 
The Site can be directly accessed by entering traffic from the I-93 overpass via Spice 
Street and Rutherford Avenue. Traffic from the Route 99 underpass, however, cannot access the 
Site directly. Traffic leaving the Site toward the north can utilize D Street to Spice Street to 
Cambridge Street. Spice Street has one travel lane in each direction with parking on both sides 
of the street. 
 
 
Pedestrian Circulation: 
 
The major pedestrian route to the Site is Hood Park Drive, Stack Street and the to be 
constructed Supertest Street leading off of Rutherford Avenue. Hood Park Drive includes 
landscaping and sidewalks leading from the Project Site to other buildings within the 
Development and to Rutherford Avenue. Stack Street, Supertest Street and pedestrian and 
bicycle pathways will be constructed to improve the pedestrian and bicycle access to the northern 
part of the Site as further described in the PDA Master Plan.

Development. The garage parking spaces included in the Project need not comply with any

11. 
ACCESS TO PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION. The Project Site is located 
within convenient distance of the MBTA public transportation system. The Orange Line 
Sullivan Station is located to the north, at a 5-10 minute walking distance from the Site. Sullivan 
Station is also a major MBTA bus hub.

14. 
PUBLIC BENEFITS. The Project, as a part of the Development, will provide 
substantial public benefits to the City of Boston and the surrounding neighborhood. These 
benefits will include: 
 
Constructive Reuse of an Industrial Site. The Project continues the transformation of 
the former Hood Dairy plant from an obsolete industrial plant to a state-of-the-art 21st 
century mixed-use development. 
 
The significant new retail space planned for grocery use will increase the community’s 
access to quality, affordable, food options by bringing a second grocery store to 
Charlestown and providing a food option at the northern end of the neighborhood. 
 

6 
The proposed uses of the Development will result in a reduction in traffic impacts (i.e., 
noise, road infrastructure damages, air quality) by the elimination of uses relying upon 
trucks and other heavy vehicles that currently service the Site. 
 
Construction Employment. Construction of the Project will create approximately 450 
construction jobs and will be subject to a Boston Residents Construction Employment 
Plan. 
 
Permanent Employment. The Project will result in approximately 45 permanent jobs. 
 
Redirected Growth. The Development will enhance the City’s goals of providing mixed-
use developments for residential, commercial and retail close to major transit hubs. 
 
Affordable Housing Creation. The Project will result in the creation of eighteen (18) off-
site two, three and four bedroom family affordable housing units in the West Rutherford 
area of the Charlestown neighborhood. 
 
Enhanced Pedestrian & Bicycle Network. The Development will result in the creation of 
a fifteen (15) foot wide multi-use pedestrian and bicycle path extending along the 
Project’s northerly property line from Rutherford Avenue to Stack Street. 
 
Hood Green. The Development will coordinate with the adjacent hotel/residential tower 
project at 25 Supertest Street in its creation of a new approximately one (1) acre publicly 
accessible open space on top of the below-grade parking structure, between Supertest 
Street and the northern property boundary, including soft and hardscape finishes, 
plantings, trees, recreational components, and public access accommodations, referred to 
as “Hood Green”. 
 
PLAN: Charlestown. The Development will foster and enhance the development goals 
of the PLAN: Charlestown planning initiative approved by the Authority in 2023 by 
providing affordable housing, open space areas, and improved connectivity in 
Charlestown. 
 
15. 
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW PROCEDURES. All design plans for the Project 
are subject to the on-going development review and approval of the Authority. Such review is to 
be conducted in accordance with Article 80 of the Code and the Authority’s Development 
Review Procedures, dated 2006. 
 
 
16. 
CONSISTENCY WITH THE PDA MASTER PLAN. The Project described in 
this Development Plan is consistent with the overall planning objectives and character of the 
Development described in the PDA Master Plan. The dimensional provisions, allowed uses, 
parking, loading and other provisions described in this Development Plan shall be controlling for 
the Project and are consistent with and in compliance with the provisions in PDA Master Plan 
No. 51.

a Certification of Consistency (or partial Certification of Consistency) for the Project or 
portion(s) thereof. Upon the issuance of a Certification of Consistency (or partial Certification 
of Consistency if applicable) such Project or portion thereof shall be deemed to comply with any

18. 
OWNERSHIP OF SITE AND PROJECT. Although the Site is currently a 
single lot, it is contemplated that the Project may be separately owned and financed including, 
without limitation, by the creation of separate parcels, condominium ownership, ground leases, 
or otherwise. The compliance or non-compliance of any other project described in the PDA 
Master Plan shall not affect the compliance of the Project with the requirements of this 
Development Plan. The Project will be eligible to receive its own Certification of Consistency or 
Partial Certification of Consistency if, and only if, the Director of the Authority makes the 
findings set forth in Article 80C-8 of the Code. If the Project is separately owned, the owner of 
the Project may seek an amendment of this Development Plan as to the Project, provided that 
such amendment does not change any obligation or requirement of the PDA Master Plan or any 
other project built in accordance with a separate development plan pursuant to the PDA Master

the Developer under this Development Plan, is to adhere to the provisions of this Development 
Plan, the PDA Master Plan, and the Article 80B Documents applicable to the Project. Without 
limiting the generality of the foregoing, upon approval of this Development Plan for the Project, 
the Developer hereunder shall not be chargeable with any omission, commission, default or 
delay by any other person, including without limitation the developers of any other Proposed 
Project, in the implementation of the PDA Master Plan, or any other approved Development 
Plan, or the undertakings of the Article 80B Documents with respect to any other Proposed 
Project or any other portion of the Development. This provision to make the undertakings with 
respect to each Proposed Project severable is included in order to facilitate the separate 
ownership and/or financing of portions of the Project without concern for any so-called cross-
default or zoning non-compliance attributable to the acts of others.

“Project”) of the Mary Ellen McCormack public housing site located at 10 Kemp Street, South 
Boston, including the proposed location and appearance of structures, open spaces and 
landscaping, proposed uses of the area, densities, proposed traffic circulation, parking and loading 
facilities, access to public transportation and proposed dimensions of structures. 
 
This Development Plan approves zoning for the Project. The Project is also undergoing 
Large Project Review under Section 80B of the Code. A Project Notification Form for the Project 
was filed with the Boston Redevelopment Authority (doing business as the Boston Planning & 
Development Agency, the “BPDA”) on October 29, 2021, and the BPDA issued a request for 
Supplemental Information for the Project under Section 80B of the Code on August 12, 2022, in 
response to which the Proponent filed a Supplemental Information Document on August 25, 2023. 
The Project has undergone review by the Boston Civic Design Commission (“BCDC”) in

2. 
Proponent. The Proponent of the Project is Transform Mary Ellen McCormack 
LLC, a Massachusetts limited liability company (collectively with its respective successors and 
assigns, as applicable, the “Proponent”). The Proponent is an affiliate of WinnDevelopment, a 
Massachusetts profit corporation. The Project is anticipated to involve the disposition of the Site 
(as defined herein) via one or more 99-year ground leases from the Boston Housing Authority 
(“BHA”), which owns the Project site, to the Proponent (or its affiliates). 
3. 
Project Site. The Project is located at 10 Kemp Street in the South Boston 
neighborhood of Boston and consists of approximately 784,080 square feet (approximately 18 
acres) of land comprising the northern portion of the 31-acre Mary Ellen McCormack Housing 
Development (the “McCormack Development”), as more specifically described on Exhibit A 
attached hereto and depicted on Exhibit B attached hereto (the “Project Site”). The remaining 
approximately thirteen (13) acres of the McCormack Development will be redeveloped under a 
separate Planned Development Area Development Plan as part of a future second phase (the 
“Phase 2 Project”, and together with the Project comprise the “Master Project”). The Project 
Site is bounded by Old Colony Avenue to the east, the Massachusetts Bay Transportation 
Authority (“MBTA”) right-of-way to the south, Dorchester Avenue and O’Connor Way to the 
west, and Devine Way to the north. The Project Site is adjacent to Moakley Park, which is an 
approximately 58-acre urban waterfront park featuring multiple sports fields, a playground, and a 
splash pad. The City of Boston is currently in the process of developing the Moakley Park Vision 
Plan with an eye toward balancing recreational needs with the need for community gathering 
spaces and flood protection. The Proponent is actively participating in the Moakley Park 
development process to ensure as much coordination and alignment as possible is taken into 
consideration. 
The McCormack Development was developed under the United States Housing Act of 
1937. Completed in 1938, it is one of the largest public housing developments in New England 
and currently consists of 1,016 deeply subsidized public housing apartments in eighteen (18) mid-
rise buildings and sixteen (16) townhome buildings. The Project Site suffers from outdated utility, 
roadway, bicycle, and pedestrian infrastructure and lacks overall connectivity with the surrounding 
neighborhood. 
The Project Site is located within the H-1 Apartment Residential subdistrict of South 
Boston (the “District”) and is governed by the underlying base provisions of the Code. It is also 
located within a Restricted Parking Overlay District (“RPOD”) and the Coastal Flood Resilience 
Overlay District (“CFROD”). The regulations set forth in this Development Plan shall apply to 
the entire PDA Overlay District in lieu of any zoning district or subdistrict requirements that would 
otherwise be applicable at the time of permitting, excluding current zoning overlays or other 
applicable regulatory requirements as specified in this document. All dimensional, use, and design 
requirements of underlying zoning shall not be applicable to the Project and the Project Site and 

 
3 
 
are superseded by this Development Plan. It is contemplated that portions of the Project Site and 
the buildings and other improvements located thereon from time to time may be reconfigured into 
a number of smaller parcels or sub-areas, including, without limitation, through one or more 
subdivisions, ground leases, subleases, condominium regimes, or otherwise, which parcels or sub-
areas may be under common or separate ownership, developed sequentially or simultaneously, 
and/or separately developed and/or financed (each such parcel or sub-area is referred to herein as 
a “Project Component”). As of the date of this Development Plan, the Project Site is anticipated 
to be comprised of three (3) Project Components: (a) “Phase 1.1”; (b) “Phase 1.2”; and (c) “Phase 
1.3”. The Project Components may be combined, divided or otherwise changed and additional 
Project Component(s) may be created within the Project Site, and shall be deemed consistent with 
this Development Plan. The minimum number of BHA Replacement Units (as defined in 
Paragraph 4 of this Development Plan) in the Project will be 529 (40% of the units), a one-for-one 
replacement of BHA units. 
Notwithstanding anything set forth herein or in the Code to the contrary, for purposes of 
this Development Plan, compliance of the individual Project Components with the requirements 
of this Development Plan will be determined as if the entire Project Site were one Lot, even if it is 
comprised at any time of more than one Lot, including Lots that have been subdivided, re-
subdivided or combined or submitted to a condominium regime or other form of ownership. This 
Development Plan approves any zoning nonconformity created or increased by the separation of 
ownership of individual Project Components, or by the subdivision, re-subdivision, combination, 
or submission to condominium ownership or other forms of ownership of Project Components, 
provided that (a) the use provisions of this Development Plan are not violated by the resulting Lot 
or Lots, (b) the Project’s floor area ratio (“FAR”) and gross floor area (“GFA”) do not exceed the 
maximum permitted (as defined below) under this Development Plan for the Project as a whole, 
(c) the open space, parking and loading space requirements of this Development Plan are met with 
respect to the Project Site as a whole, and (d) the public benefit obligations set forth in this

receive its own Certification of Consistency or Partial Certification of Consistency.

Proposed Appearance and Dimensions of Structures and Proposed Density. As 
currently envisioned, the Project will consist of the phased redevelopment of the northern-most 18 
acres of the 31-acre McCormack Development in South Boston, one of the oldest and largest public 
housing developments in New England, into a mixed-use, mixed-income community. The Project 
will comprise eight (8) new buildings, the substantial renovation of an existing structure (the 
“Boiler Building”) and will include up to 1,478,000 square feet of GFA of residential, retail, 
community, above-grade parking garages, and open space uses, and uses accessory and ancillary 
thereto. Building heights will range from low and mid-rise structures to a high-rise tower with the 
maximum height not to exceed 19 stories (199 feet). The maximum FAR for the Project shall not 
exceed 3.10.1Conceptual plans and renderings of the Project showing anticipated massing, 
building heights, and other details are attached to this Development Plan as Exhibit C.

The following concepts have informed the Project’s height and massing strategy: (i) the 
location of Old Colony Avenue adjacent to Moakley Park supports mid-rise buildings designed 
to play a supporting role as a “background” urban edge; (ii) lower buildings are appropriate 
along the Project Site’s north and west sides where it abuts existing lower-scale neighborhoods; 
and (iii) taller buildings are appropriate for the interior of the Project Site, where they can benefit 
from the adjacency of new community open spaces. The buildings along Logan Way will have a 
consistent street frontage with lower-scale massing that will clearly define the two retail blocks 
and identify this street as different from the others. The buildings along Old Colony Avenue will 
be purposely indented and provided with a visible raised courtyard to connect the development 
with Moakley Park. Buildings located within the Project Site’s interior will rise with a series of 
setbacks to allow open views of the sky from adjacent open spaces.

and the Mohawk Street extension and will have a maximum building height of six (6) stories (70 
feet) and a maximum GFA of up to 109,000 square feet. It will contain up to 94 residential units, 
100% of which will be permanently deeply subsidized housing units for households currently 
living in the McCormack Development and for future low-income households from BHA’s 
subsidized housing waiting list (“BHA Replacement Units”) Building A will also include up to 
4,300 square feet of amenity space including a 1,000 square-foot property management office. 
Buildings B1 and B2 will be located between Logan Way and Devine Way, with Old

building height of thirteen (13) stories (150 feet) and Building B2 will have a maximum building 
height of six (6) stories (70 feet). Combined, Buildings B1 and B2 will have a maximum GFA of 
up to 294,000 square feet and will contain up to 300 residential units, at least 20% of which will 
be BHA Replacement Units. Building B1 will also include approximately 8,000 square feet of 
retail space. 
Buildings C1 and C2 will be located along Logan Way and Devine Way in between 
Gavin Way and Wendeller Street. Building C1 will have a maximum building height of seven (7)

Proposed Phasing of Construction: Construction of the Project is anticipated to be 
phased over several years. The Project includes the demolition of existing on-site buildings (with 
the exception of the Boiler Building) and construction of eight new buildings anticipated over three 
phases starting in 2024, with all construction anticipated to be complete in approximately 8-10 
years. The development schedule for the Project, construction schedule for each of the buildings, 
and the order in which each of the buildings is developed, will depend on availability of funds and 
market conditions. New and relocated streets and underground utilities will be developed 
concurrently with adjacent parcels. Open space will similarly keep pace with redevelopment by 
first constructing Veterans Park, the Community Green, and Town Square (each as described 
herein). It is expected that development will be phased generally as depicted on Exhibit F and in 
the following sequence: 
● Phase 1.1: Building A, Building B, Building C1 & C2, Building D, & Billy 
McGonagle Community Center (Building X) 
● Phase 1.2: Building E & Building F 
● Phase 1.3: Building G 
 
7. 
Proposed Open Spaces and Landscaping: The Project will include the establishment 
of significant areas of open space on the Project Site. Well-designed, new open spaces, attention 
to existing trees, and a new web of streetscapes will help establish an inviting community setting. 
Approximately eleven (11) percent of the Project Site will be comprised of publicly accessible 
open space which will be provided in a variety of configurations, with active and passive areas and 
hardscaped and planted areas. As currently designed, the Project will create approximately 2.05 
acres of publicly accessible open space, as depicted on Exhibit G attached hereto, approximately 
3.6 acres of new public realm improvements including new streetscapes, sidewalks and plazas, as 
well as rebuilding another 2.0 acres of existing public realm. The public realm improvements will 
total approximately 5.6 acres. The publicly accessible open spaces will be constructed and 
maintained by the Proponent pursuant to one or more ground leases from the BHA which will also 
require the Proponent to ensure public access to the open spaces and to maintain them in perpetuity. 
The ribbon of open spaces will link Dorchester Avenue to Old Colony Avenue thoughtfully 
integrating the surrounding neighborhood and the Project into the proposed redevelopment of 
Moakley Park being undertaken by the City of Boston. The open spaces will provide areas for 
community functions, active recreation, children’s play, exercise, gardening, rest and relaxation. 
They will also include important green infrastructure elements including subsurface infiltration 
chambers for stormwater management at the site. 
The distinctive open spaces will include: 
● Veterans Park – The memorial at Veterans Park will be relocated in conjunction 
with the development of the first new building on the Project Site (Building A). 
The commemorative pavers, plaques, medallions, and sculptures will be salvaged 
and sensitively integrated into a new park, approximately 8,800 square feet in 
size, which will re-establish a place of contemplation. The space will also include 
space for flexible outdoor seating, and a universally accessible tot lot. 
● Town Square – This approximately 36,900 square foot open space will form the 
gateway to the Project Site along Old Colony Avenue at the pedestrian crossing to 

 
9 
 
Moakley Park. It will be located at the terminus of the Logan Way retail street 
leading in from Andrew Square and the eastern end of the Kemp Street corridor 
from Dorchester Avenue. It will be surrounded on three sides by active public 
uses and will be a natural meeting place for residents of the Project, visitors to 
Moakley Park, and the surrounding neighborhoods. It incorporates the principles 
of selectively preserving the tree canopy, providing usable open spaces, and 
providing a strong connection to Moakley Park. It will also be designed to help 
absorb any flooding on the site. 
Town Square will be most actively programmed as a meeting space for the larger 
surrounding community. It will feature festivals and activities related to the 
changing seasons, activities in the park, food trucks on the weekend, opportunities 
to host farmers’ markets during the week, and a recurring crafts fair during the 
summer. Its implementation will be phased, with a temporary space constructed 
with Building B1, and fully completed with Building G. 
● Community Green – The Community Green, an approximately 38,700 square 
foot open space, will provide a western anchor to the linked parks along Kemp 
Street as well as a destination at the southern end of O’Connor Way. The 
basketball and tennis courts that currently exist between Devine and O’Connor 
Ways will be re-established at the Community Green with the redevelopment of 
the existing Boiler Building into the Billy McGonagle Community Center. In 
addition to the sports courts, the Community Green will feature a broad open lawn 
that will be designed to welcome neighborhood and community gatherings, such 
as neighborhood picnics, outdoor movie nights, morning Tai Chi or Yoga, and 
social or instructional activities in conjunction with programs offered by the Billy 
McGonagle Community Center. 
● Small Open Spaces - Additionally, smaller pocket parks will be provided 
throughout the Project Site. These spaces will provide more intimate open space 
opportunities for programming such as a dog park, tot lots, and senior gardens. 
These open spaces will punctuate a vibrant, urban mixed-use development while 
also helping to mitigate stormwater and to make the development more resilient to 
future climate change impacts. 
● Networked Open Space - The open spaces will be linked together via 
streetscapes, site lines, and pedestrian safety features. The internal network will 
have clear connections to the larger open space network beyond the boundaries of 
the Project Site. Moakley Park will be deliberately connected at Town Square, 
and discussions are underway to redevelop Moakley Park to meet this connection 
in a mutually beneficial way. Elements of the open space network reach Devine 
Way with easy pedestrian connections to Preble Street and the Andrew Square 
neighborhood. The Project proposes a dedicated bicycle connection along Kemp 
Street, connecting the bikeways on Old Colony Avenue with bikeways on 
Dorchester Avenue north and south. The Project will provide a safe connection 
through the Site between these major corridors and an excellent connection for 
bicyclists to the wider community.

 The streets will be developed in accordance with the Boston Transportation 
Department’s (“BTD”) Complete Streets Guidelines. In addition to the publicly accessible open 
space, the total public realm improvements (new and improved) will include approximately 5.6 
acres of streetscape enhancements. Clear and accessible paths for pedestrian and bicycle travel 
will be constructed, and newly planted and existing mature trees will buffer pedestrians and 
bicyclists from vehicles, beautify the neighborhood and provide shade to help mitigate extreme 
heat. The Project’s open space program shall be subject to design review by the BPDA, and any 
open space or landscaping approved as part of such review shall be deemed in compliance with

Transportation and Site Circulation: A network of streets already exists on the Site. 
Nevertheless, new internal and external connections will be established to knit the Project Site into 
the surrounding community. The Project Site includes two new cross-site east/west connections 
from Dorchester Avenue to Old Colony Avenue via Logan Way and the extension of Kemp Street. 
Logan Way will also include a separated cycle track from Dorchester Avenue to Moakley Park. 
These connections will include an improved intersection, as well as bicycle and pedestrian 
crossings at Old Colony Avenue. While Logan Way is a pedestrian-oriented street with retail 
outlets and community facilities, Kemp Street serves to connect the public recreation and passive 
open spaces such as the proposed Community Green, Sterling Square, and Town Square. Existing 
north/south connections will be enhanced along Gavin Way. A relocated and extended Gavin Way 
will create an enhanced connection to Devine Way. Wendeller Street will connect Logan Way and 
Kemp Street, with a pedestrian connection to Devine Way, creating a north/south connection. 
O’Connor Way will connect Logan Way to Kemp Street. Mohawk Street will be extended into the 
Project Site and connect to the realigned Logan Way. 
Refer generally to Exhibit D for proposed rights-of-way and sections of each proposed 
street, with minimum dimensions and details related to parking, bike lanes, travel lanes, furniture 
zones and sidewalks. The new internal east/west and north/south connections radiate outward to 
connect to the adjacent neighborhoods, drawing people into and through the Project Site. Kemp 
Street and Logan Way both connect to the Town Square, which provides an active civic portal into 
the Project Site and an important identity marker along Old Colony Avenue. Town Square also 
focuses on pedestrian and bicycle crossing at a new signalized crossing to provide safe and 
convenient access to and from Moakley Park. The north/south routes provide connection to the 
Andrew Square neighborhood across Preble Street to the north, while the east/west routes connect 
to Dorchester Avenue and the Savin Hill neighborhood. Andrew Square will be connected to 
Moakley Park with the transformation of Logan Way into a main retail street. Old Colony Avenue 
will be made into a stronger urban edge to Moakley Park through the construction of appropriately 
scaled residential buildings that are set back from the street and step back as they rise. The park 
will benefit from framing by and visual connection to the community it serves. Roadway 
circulation throughout the Project Site and street classifications will be generally as depicted on 
Exhibit H.

Proposed Motor Vehicle Parking and Loading Facilities and Bicycle Parking: On-
street parking will continue to be provided along the streets within the Project Site. The Project 
Site will create a maximum of 508 off-street parking spaces located both on the surface and in 
above- and below-grade facilities. 
The Proponent will provide one thousand two hundred forty-five (1,245) interior covered 
and secure bike parking spaces and a minimum of two hundred forty-eight (248) exterior visitor 
post and ring bike parking spaces on site in compliance with the city’s Bike Parking Guidelines 
(revised January 2021). All bike parking is subject to design review by BPDA Transportation 
staff and BTD. Short-term bike parking within the public right of way will be subject to PIC 
review. 
 The Proponent will comply with BTD’s 2020 Bike Parking Guidelines for on-site bike 
parking space requirements and proportional monetary contribution to the Bluebikes bike share 
system at the discretion of BTD and the BPDA, all as provided in the TAPA. As currently 
contemplated and detailed in Exhibit I, the Proponent will provide space for two (2) nineteen (19) 
dock bike share stations. One station will be delivered near Town Square at the intersection of Old 
Colony Avenue and Logan Way and one station will be delivered at the Community Green Space. 
The stations will be delivered prior to issuance of Certificate of Occupancy for Buildings B1/ B2 
and X respectively. The Proponent will also comply with the short-term bike parking requirements. 
As currently contemplated, the Proponent will provide some off-site short-term bike parking 
throughout the neighborhood. 
The Project’s on-site parking and loading facilities shall be subject to design, 
environmental and other development review by the BPDA, and the aspects of the Project 
approved as part of such review shall be and are hereby deemed to be the required parking and 
loading applicable to the Project and hereby incorporated in this Development Plan.

Access to Public Transportation: The Project Site is near several public 
transportation opportunities including the MBTA Red Line, the Commuter Rail and several bus 
lines. The Project Site is located between Andrew Square Station to the north and JFK/UMass 
Station to the south. Andrew Square Station provides connections to six different bus lines 
including the CT3, 9, 10, 16, 17 and 171 buses. JFK/Umass Station provides connections to the 
three different bus lines including the 8, 16, and 41 buses, and three different Commuter Rail lines, 
including the Green Bush line, the Kingston/Plymouth line, and the Middleborough/Lakeville line. 
The Red Line branch of the MBTA subway system stops at Andrew Square Station and 
JFK/Umass Station. The Red Line provides access between Alewife Station to the north and 
Ashmont and Braintree Stations to the south. The Red Line provides convenient access to 
downtown Boston, as well as Dorchester, Mattapan, Cambridge, Quincy, and Braintree. It also 

 
12 
 
provides access to South Station, which provides a connection to bus terminals, Commuter Rail 
lines, regional rail lines, and Logan Airport via the MBTA Silver Line. Approximate walking and 
cycling distances from public transportation sources are depicted in Exhibit I. 
10. 
Housing: The Project will provide one-for-one replacement of the existing, deeply 
subsidized, affordable public housing units on-site. As an inclusive, mixed-use, mixed-income 
project with residential units being affordable to a range of incomes, the Project will provide a 
public benefit due to the need for additional housing in Boston. The Project contemplates 
approximately 1,310 residential units within eight new buildings that will range from 
approximately 20 to 300 residential units each. Of the 1,310 units, 529 will be affordable, BHA 
Replacement Units (the remaining 487 replacement affordable units will be constructed pursuant 
to a future Development Plan so that 100 percent of all existing affordable housing units are 
replaced). At least 20% of the residential units in each building will be BHA Replacement Units. 
The market-rate units will help fund the capital costs for the replacement units and provide for 
sustainable, long-term and ongoing maintenance, operations, and community programming. The 
Project will showcase new, high-quality design and neighborhood amenities, while maintaining 
affordable housing restrictions currently existing at the site today. The phasing of the Project is 
designed to limit off-site, temporary relocation of existing households and maximize one-time 
moves from existing units into new units. 
11. 
Signage: The signage program for the Project shall be subject to design, 
environmental and other development review by the BPDA, and any “Sign” approved as part of 
such review shall be deemed to be in compliance with this Development Plan. 
12. 
Green Buildings: The Project shall comply with Article 37, Green Buildings, of the 
Code, with the latest version of the Building Emissions Reduction and Disclosure Ordinance, and 
with the BHA’s Fossil Fuel Free policy on new construction. 
The buildings will be sustainable, LEED Gold certifiable, fossil-fuel-free Passive House 
certified buildings employing ultra-low carbon design solutions (Building 2035 pCEI ranging 
from 0.79 kg to 1.06 kg CO2e/sf-yr) that include on-site and off-site renewable energy sources, 
thereby contributing to the Boston Housing Authority’s goal of going Fossil Fuel Free by 2030 
and the City of Boston’s goal of making Boston carbon neutral by 2050. Buildings will employ 
low embodied carbon construction materials and products such as mass timber, which will be 
piloted at Building B1/B2 and considered throughout the rest of the development. 
13. 
Development Review Procedures: Building A, Building B, and Building C1 & C2 
have been reviewed and approved by the BCDC and are subject to ongoing design review by the 
BPDA. Building A, Building B, and Building C1 & C2 are subject to further sustainable and 
resilience design review and approval of the individual buildings by the Interagency Green 
Building Committee (“IGBC”) in accordance with Articles 25A and 37. The further design of 
individual buildings are subject to design review according the BPDA’s Development Review 
Guidelines and by the BCDC and the IGBC in accordance with Article 28 and Article 37, 
respectively, of the Code. Each individual building shall meet the City’s requirements in effect at 
the time of submission of the individual building design review filing respecting updates to Article 
37, USGBC’s LEED Rating Systems, with the latest version of the Building Emissions Reduction 
and Disclosure Ordinance, with the BHA’s Fossil Fuel Free policy on new construction, and 

 
13 
 
Boston Climate Resiliency and Sea Level Rise Base Flood Elevation Requirements, Climate 
Action Plan or their successors. 
At the time of review and approval of plans and specifications for Buildings D, E, F, G, 
and X, if deemed necessary and appropriate by the Director of the BPDA, the Proponent shall 
provide updates to the noise, wind, and shadow studies included in the PNF for review by the 
BPDA. If such updated studies require different or additional mitigation based on net new impacts 
that result from Buildings D, E, F, G, and X as compared to those studies provided in the PNF, as 
determined by the Director of the BPDA, such mitigation shall be included in the Cooperation 
Agreement to be entered into for such Building. 
Aspects of the Project may also require approvals of other governmental agencies, such as 
the City of Boston’s Public Improvement Commission (“PIC”) and the Boston Conservation 
Commission. No permits for any elements of the Project included in the Development Plan, as the 
same may be amended, shall be required from the Zoning Board of Appeal. 
The BPDA shall not approve the issuance for a Certification of Consistency and 
Certification of Compliance for any building requesting such Certifications until the following 
process has been completed: 
● Review of the building by the BCDC as applicable 
● Review of schematic design, design development and construction drawings by the 
BPDA pursuant to the Development Review Guidelines and Article 80B of the Code 
● Review and approval of the building by the IGBC. 
● Execution of all Article 80 documents 
The BPDA’s approval of final plans and specifications shall confirm their consistency 
with this Development Plan. 
14. 
Public Benefits: The Project will advance the City of Boston’s housing production 
goals by creating a variety of affordable, middle-income (if funding is available), and market-rate 
housing in a highly convenient, transit-oriented location, providing deeply affordable housing 
opportunities in close proximity to public transit, job centers, healthcare providers, and other 
important community amenities. Some of the primary public benefits are summarized below. 
a) The creation of approximately 1,310 mixed-income, residential units on-site 
including the replacement of 529 deeply subsidized affordable housing units. 
b) Construction of a new “Billy McGonagle Community Center” (named in honor of 
the late former BHA administrator who grew up at the site) which will make a 
measurable impact in six key outcome areas that fuel individual and collective 
quality of life: Housing, Employment, Education, Community Engagement, 
Health and Economic Mobility. The Center will connect residents and neighbors 
with their broader surroundings and resources, reduce neighborhood crime and 

 
14 
 
violence, and cultivate a safe, secure, and vibrant community for the current and 
future residents. 
c) Contribution to the Transportation Mitigation Bank which is a fund that is in the 
purview of MassDot, DCR, and relevant City agencies (including the BPDA) that 
supports area infrastructure improvements ("TMB"). The Proponent has 
committed to a contribution of $6 per square foot of Gross Floor Area for market 
rate residential and market rate retail space which shall be paid into the TMB to 
support area infrastructure improvements. This payment will be made at the time 
of issuance of a building permit and calculated proportionally for each phase of 
the Project. The total payment to the TMB for the Project is estimated to be 
approximately Four Million Three Hundred Thirty-Three Thousand Dollars 
($4,330,000.00). However, the relevant entities that administer TMB including 
MassDOT, DCR, the MBTA and relevant City of Boston agencies (including the 
BPDA), have not finalized certain ancillary agreements which shall determine the 
final payment owed. Consideration shall be provided for the cost of permanent 
offsite improvements constructed by the Proponent be deducted from the TMB 
payment owed. The BPDA and the Proponent shall finalize that total contribution 
number in the Cooperation Agreement and based on further discussion and 
approvals among the relevant agencies. Further, the Cooperation Agreement will 
memorialize that it is expected that those state and city agencies will enter into a 
Memorandum of Agreement to govern the establishment of the TMB as a force 
account at MassDOT and decision making around priority investments of the 
TMB funds. 
d) Provision of 2.05 acres of new landscaping, pedestrian connections, gathering 
areas, and spaces open to public use. 
e) Implementation of stormwater management strategies that will significantly 
improve the quality and decrease the quantity of stormwater generated by the 
Project Site when compared with existing conditions. 
f) Creation of new temporary and permanent jobs during both construction and 
operation phases. 
g) Provision of 1,245 interior covered and secure bike parking spaces and 248 
exterior visitor post-and-ring bike parking spaces in compliance with the City’s 
Bike Parking Guidelines. 
h) Two-time “bikeshare” contribution of $364,480.00 to Boston Transportation 
Department (“BTD”) per the City’s Bike Parking Guidelines, all as provided in 
the Transportation Access Plan Agreement (“TAPA”). The first payment will be 
made at the time of Building B1/ B2’s full building permit and will be at a rate of 
$75,000.00. The second payment will be the remaining $289,480.00 at full 
building permit for Building X. 

 
15 
 
i) Design and implementation of six (6) raised intersections throughout the Project 
Site with three (3) located on Logan Way at Wendeller Street, Gavin Way, and 
Mohawk Street and three located on Kemp Street at Gavin Way, Wendeller 
Street, and O’Callaghan Way. 
j) Installation of raised crossings on O’Connor Way at Kemp Street and Logan 
Way. Pedestrian crossings will be evaluated for raised crossings at Kemp Street 
and Logan Way at Dorchester Avenue, at Mohawk Street and Gavin Way at 
Devine Way, and at Logan Way at Old Colony Avenue. 
 
k) Provision of space for two (2) nineteen (19) dock bike share stations onsite upon 
issuance of Certificate of Occupancy. The Proponent will work with BTD and the 
BPDA to site the station appropriately. Bike share stations may require 
Administrative Review by PIC. Generally, one (1) station will be delivered with 
Building B1/ B2 on Old Colony Avenue and Logan Way and one (1) station will 
be delivered with Building X at the Community Green Space. 
l) Enable sustainable, multimodal transportation and access through adequate, 
adaptable parking, pedestrian permeability, bicycle accommodations, and 
enhanced transit access. 
m) The Proponent will provide a trash receptacle on its property for each building, 
located adjacent to the building entry within the bounds of the proposed sidewalk 
setback (not on the public right-of-way) and will maintain it in perpetuity. 
n) Installation of a full-build separated two-way bike facility at sidewalk level on 
Logan Way between O’Connor Way and Old Colony Avenue. At O’Connor 
Way, as currently contemplated, the bike facilities will transition to roadway 
grade, separated by a mountable island in order to provide a minimum 20’ curb to 
curb for emergency access along O’Connor Way. This will make the street more 
predictable, and shorter pedestrian crossings, which means people crossing are 
less exposed to traffic. The construction of additional separated bike facilities in 
the Phase 2 Project will be required if: travel distance to separate bike facility 
exceeds 3-minute walk, the Phase 2 Project exceeds 30,000 square feet in ground 
floor retail representing a significant increase, or roadway Bicycle Level of 
Traffic Stress (“LTS”) (as measured by Bicycle Level of Traffic Street Technical 
Documentation December 2020, Version 1.0) is LTS 3 or higher. 
o) The Proponent will make necessary upgrades and enhancements to the existing 
public rights-of-way to improve accessibility and foster connectivity. These 
proposed improvements shall be completed before building permit issuance for 
the Project and are subject to design review and approval by BTD, Public Works 
Department (“PWD”), PIC, and the BPDA. The rights-of-way in the future will 
be contain minimum dimensions of: 
a. Kemp Street will have a typical minimum public right-of-way dimension 
of 62’, and a typical minimum curb-to-curb dimension of 38’. The street 

 
16 
 
will transition from the western terminus of the Project Site to Dorchester 
Avenue to be a maximum of 22’ curb-to-curb to provide two-way 
vehicular circulation and 8’ and 7’ sidewalks. 
b. Logan Way will have a typical minimum right-of-way dimension of 75’, 
and a typical minimum curb-to-curb dimension of 38’. The street will 
transition from the western terminus of the Project Site to Dorchester 
Avenue to be a maximum of 25.5’ curb-to-curb to provide 12.5’ one-way 
vehicular circulation, 3’ mountable curb/buffer, 10’ two-way bike facility 
and 7’ and 5.5’ sidewalks. 
c. Gavin Way, Wendeller Street, and Mohawk Street will have typical 
minimum right-of-way dimensions of 62’, and typical minimum curb-to-
curb dimensions of 38’. 
d. O’Connor Way will have typical minimum right-of-way dimensions of 
54.4’, and typical minimum curb-to-curb dimensions of 30’. 
e. Devine Way will have a typical minimum right-of-way dimension of 40’ 
and will maintain the existing typical minimum curb-to-curb dimension of 
26’ plus a 7’ sidewalk, which will extend into the development site. 
f. The Proponent, on the western edge of Old Colony Avenue from Devine 
Way to the southern boundary of Town Square, will relocate the western 
curb and reconstruct a pedestrian zone, greenscape & furnishing zone on 
the western edge of Old Colony Avenue from Devine Way to the southern 
boundary of Town Square. The sidewalk widening will bring the bike 
facility to sidewalk level and provide an expanded sidewalk. The 
Proponent will restripe Old Colony Avenue southbound to adjust for these 
changes. The restriping will extend from Preble Circle to approximately 
505 Old Colony Avenue. 
p) The Proponent will design and implement alterations to the existing signal at the 
issuance of full building permit of Building B1/B2 at Old Colony Avenue and 
Logan Way to benefit pedestrians, cyclists, and motorists. Signal adjustments can 
slow speeds, enhance safety, and separate modes. 
q) Support locally focused and responsive retail space, including a grocery retailer, 
to activate the streetscape and encourage greater connectivity with the rest of the 
neighborhood. The ground floor activation strategy will ensure that retail uses are 
both attractive and accessible to all residents across all income levels, including 
current residents of Mary Ellen McCormack. A minimum of 25% of retail spaces 
in the Project will be offered with below-market rents.

Language Access Plan: In connection with the development of the Project in 
accordance with this Development Plan, the Proponent has worked closely with the BPDA to 
develop a Language Access Plan (the “LAP”) for the Project. Based on the BPDA’s Limited 

 
17 
 
English Proficiency Assessment, Spanish and Chinese have been identified by the BPDA as 
threshold languages of the South Boston neighborhood. The LAP addresses requirements for

Restricted Parking Overlay District: The Project Site is located within the RPOD 
as governed by Article 3-1A.c of the Code. Approval of this Development Plan shall constitute 
compliance with any and all applicable RPOD requirements, including approval of parking for all 
non-residential uses of the Project from time to time. 
17. 
Coastal Flood Resilience Overlay District: The Project Site is located within the 
CFROD. Approval of this Development Plan shall constitute compliance with any and all 
applicable CFROD requirements, including use, dimensional and resilience review requirements. 
18. 
Effect of PDA: In accordance with Section 80C-9 of the Code, consistency of the 
Project with this Development Plan constitutes compliance with the dimensional, use, design, and 
all other requirements of the Code to the extent such requirements have been addressed in this 
Development Plan. All open space, landscaping, roadways and circulation, and parking, traffic and 
loading zoning requirements not specified in this Development Plan shall not be applicable to the 
Project and the Project Site. A Certification of Consistency (or Partial Certification of Consistency 
for the applicable Project Component) shall be required for the Project. To the extent that any 
aspect of the uses and/or structures complying with this Development Plan are in conflict with any 
requirement of the Code not expressly enumerated in this Development Plan, such requirements 
shall be deemed to be waived upon approval of this Development Plan. In accordance with Section 
80C-9 of the Code, issuance of a Certification of Consistency (or a Partial Certification of 
Consistency for the applicable Project Component) confirms consistency of the Project with this 
Development Plan. Noncompliance of any building shall not affect compliance of any other 
building for which a Certification of Consistency has been issued, or the right to construct any 
other building contemplated by this Development Plan. 
19. 
Amendment of Development Plan: Any owner of an individual lot within the 
Project Site may seek amendment of this Development Plan only as to such lot in accordance with 
the procedures prescribed by the Code without the consent of any other owner of land within the 
Project Site; provided, however, that no such amendment shall affect the rights or obligations of 
any other owner of land in the Project Site under this Development Plan or any agreements between 
the Proponent and the BPDA or other city agencies. Given the scope of the Project, and in light of 
the various reviews necessary to secure all required permits and approvals, the Proponent may 
seek to make modifications to the buildings and site improvements included in the Project. 
Proposed minor modifications to individual buildings and site improvements may be approved by 
the BPDA as part of a staff-level review process, without requiring an amendment to this 
Development Plan. 
20. 
No Obligation to Proceed with Project: Notwithstanding anything set forth herein 
to the contrary, under no circumstances shall the Proponent or any other party be obligated to 
proceed with all or any portion of the Project.

FOURTH AMENDMENT TO DEVELOPMENT PLAN 
 
FOR 
 
PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA NO. 67 
 
OLMSTED GREEN 
 
American Legion Highway, Morton Street and Harvard Street 
 
BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS 
 
Dated: October 05, 2022 
 
 
 
Pursuant to Section 3-1 A and Article 80, Section 80C of the Zoning Code of the City of Boston 
(“Code”), this amendment constitutes the Fourth Amendment to Development Plan for Planned 
Development Area No. 67, Olmsted Green (“Fourth PDA Amendment”). 
 
 On January 26, 2006, the Boston Planning & Development Authority, then known as the Boston 
Redevelopment Authority (the “BPDA”), approved a zoning Map Amendment Application to establish 
Planned Development Area No. 67 and a Development Plan for Planned Development Area No. 67, 
Olmsted Green (the “Original PDA Plan”). On February 15, 2006, the Boston Zoning Commission 
adopted said Map Amendment and approved the Original PDA Plan. 
 
The Original PDA Plan encompasses an approximately 42.5-acre site in the Mattapan section of 
Boston, comprising three parcels of land (the “Site”). Two of the parcels are former Boston State Hospital 
campus parcels which abut the east and west sides of Morton Street, (designated as the “East Campus” 
and “West Campus”, respectively). The third parcel is an approximately four-acre parcel formerly owned 
by Lena Park Community Development Corporation (the “Lena Park Parcel”) and is adjacent to the East 
Campus. The Original PDA Plan provided for the construction of a mixed-use development, including 
residential, senior housing, community facilities, mental health program space, urban farming, retail, open 
space, accessory parking and recreational facilities known as the Olmsted Green Project. As set forth in 
the Original PDA Plan, the Olmsted Green Project involved the development on the Site of multiple 
buildings and facilities containing a total combined Gross Floor Area of approximately 851,000 square 
feet. 
 

 
KH 817360.3 
First Amendment to the Original PDA Plan 
 
A First Amendment to the Original PDA Plan (“First PDA Amendment”) amended the Original 
PDA Plan by reducing the Senior Housing Component on the East Campus from 83 Units and 
approximately 76,000 square feet of Gross Floor Area to 59 Units and approximately 59,049 square feet 
of Gross Floor Area. The First PDA Amendment also decreased the total Gross Floor Area for the 
Olmsted Green Project from approximately 851,000 square feet to approximately 834,000 square feet. 
The First PDA Amendment was approved by the BPDA on November 16, 2010, adopted by the Boston 
Zoning Commission on November 17, 2010, and approved by the Mayor on November 19, 2010. 
 
Second Amendment to PDA Plan 
 
A Second Amendment to the Original PDA Plan (“Second PDA Amendment”) further amended 
the Original PDA Plan by approving the permitted uses for the Lena Park Parcel to include a school and 
by reducing the Gross Floor Area for the Project Component on the Lena Park Parcel from 80,000 square 
feet to 61,000 square feet. The Second PDA Amendment also further decreased the total Gross Floor 
Area for the Olmsted Green Project from approximately 834,000 square feet to approximately 815,000 
square feet. The Second PDA Amendment was approved by the BPDA on November 15, 2012, adopted 
by the Boston Zoning Commission on December 12, 2012 and approved by the Mayor on December 20, 
2012. 
 
Third Amendment to PDA Plan 
 
The Third Amendment to the PDA Plan (“Third PDA Amendment”) further amended the 
Original PDA Plan with respect to the uses, dimensions and parking requirements for uses for the Vinfen 
and Heritage House parcels on the East Campus. The Third PDA Amendment amended the PDA Plan to 
change the intended development to delete the Heritage House and Vinfen Nursing and Rehab Facility 
uses on Parcels E2 and E3 of the East Campus and insert in their stead a new school use having a Gross 
Floor Area of approximately 95,000 square feet (the “High School Component”), and to allow the parking 
requirements for the High School Component to be determined through Large Project Review under 
Article 80 of the Code. The Third PDA Amendment was approved by the BPDA on March 16, 2017, 
adopted by the Boston Zoning Commission on April 12, 2017, and approved by the Mayor on April 20, 
2017. Collectively, the Original PDA Plan, the First PDA Amendment, the Second PDA Amendment and 
the Third PDA Amendment are hereinafter referred to as the “PDA Plan”. 
 
Fourth Amendment to PDA Plan 
 
 
This Fourth Amendment to the PDA Plan (“Fourth PDA Amendment”), as set forth below, 
amends the PDA Plan only with respect to the square footage for the Project Component on the Lena Park 
Parcel, and the total Gross Floor Area for the Olmsted Green Project. This Fourth PDA Amendment 

 
KH 817360.3

Gross Floor Area for the Olmsted Green Project to approximately [853,600] square feet from 
approximately 841,049. Capitalized terms in this Fourth PDA Amendment, unless otherwise defined 
herein, shall have the meaning set forth in the PDA Plan and the Code.

FIFTH AMENDMENT TO DEVELOPMENT PLAN 
 
FOR 
 
PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA NO. 67 
 
OLMSTED GREEN 
 
American Legion Highway, Morton Street and Harvard Street 
 
BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS 
 
Dated: November 28, 2022 
 
 
 
Pursuant to Section 3-1 A and Article 80, Section 80C of the Zoning Code of the City of Boston 
(“Code”), this amendment constitutes the Fifth Amendment to Development Plan for Planned 
Development Area No. 67, Olmsted Green (“Fifth PDA Amendment”). 
 
 On January 26, 2006, the Boston Planning & Development Authority, then known as the Boston 
Redevelopment Authority (the “BPDA”), approved a zoning Map Amendment Application to establish 
Planned Development Area No. 67 and a Development Plan for Planned Development Area No. 67, 
Olmsted Green (the “Original PDA Plan”). On February 15, 2006, the Boston Zoning Commission 
adopted said Map Amendment and approved the Original PDA Plan. 
 
The Original PDA Plan encompasses an approximately 42.5-acre site in the Mattapan section of 
Boston, comprising three parcels of land (the “Site”). Two of the parcels are former Boston State Hospital 
campus parcels which abut the east and west sides of Morton Street, (designated as the “East Campus” 
and “West Campus”, respectively). The third parcel is an approximately four-acre parcel formerly owned 
by Lena Park Community Development Corporation (the “Lena Park Parcel”) and is adjacent to the East 
Campus. The Original PDA Plan provided for the construction of a mixed-use development, including 
residential, senior housing, community facilities, mental health program space, urban farming, retail, open 
space, accessory parking and recreational facilities known as the Olmsted Green Project. As set forth in 
the Original PDA Plan, the Olmsted Green Project involved the development on the Site of multiple 
buildings and facilities containing a total combined Gross Floor Area of approximately 851,000 square 
feet. 
 

KH 817360.5 
First Amendment to the Original PDA Plan 
 
A First Amendment to the Original PDA Plan (“First PDA Amendment”) amended the Original 
PDA Plan by reducing the Senior Housing Component on the East Campus from 83 Units and 
approximately 76,000 square feet of Gross Floor Area to 59 Units and approximately 59,049 square feet 
of Gross Floor Area. The First PDA Amendment also decreased the total Gross Floor Area for the 
Olmsted Green Project from approximately 851,000 square feet to approximately 834,000 square feet. 
The First PDA Amendment was approved by the BPDA on November 16, 2010, adopted by the Boston 
Zoning Commission on November 17, 2010, and approved by the Mayor on November 19, 2010. 
 
Second Amendment to PDA Plan 
 
A Second Amendment to the Original PDA Plan (“Second PDA Amendment”) further amended 
the Original PDA Plan by approving the permitted uses for the Lena Park Parcel to include a school and 
by reducing the Gross Floor Area for the Project Component on the Lena Park Parcel from 80,000 square 
feet to 61,000 square feet. The Second PDA Amendment also further decreased the total Gross Floor 
Area for the Olmsted Green Project from approximately 834,000 square feet to approximately 815,000 
square feet. The Second PDA Amendment was approved by the BPDA on November 15, 2012, adopted 
by the Boston Zoning Commission on December 12, 2012 and approved by the Mayor on December 20, 
2012. 
 
Third Amendment to PDA Plan 
 
The Third Amendment to the PDA Plan (“Third PDA Amendment”) further amended the 
Original PDA Plan with respect to the uses, dimensions and parking requirements for uses for the Vinfen 
and Heritage House parcels on the East Campus. The Third PDA Amendment amended the PDA Plan to 
change the intended development to delete the Heritage House and Vinfen Nursing and Rehab Facility 
uses on Parcels E2 and E3 of the East Campus and insert in their stead a new school use having a Gross 
Floor Area of approximately 95,000 square feet (the “High School Component”), and to allow the parking 
requirements for the High School Component to be determined through Large Project Review under 
Article 80 of the Code. The Third PDA Amendment was approved by the BPDA on March 16, 2017, 
adopted by the Boston Zoning Commission on April 12, 2017, and approved by the Mayor on April 20, 
2017. 
 
Fourth Amendment to PDA Plan 
 
 
The Fourth Amendment to the PDA Plan (“Fourth PDA Amendment”) further amended the 
Original PDA Plan with respect to the uses, dimensions and parking requirements for the urban farm and 
food retail components on the East Campus. The Fourth PDA Amendment amended the Original PDA 
Plan to allow for the development of an open space and active and passive recreational component in 

KH 817360.5 
place of the urban farm and food retail components. The Fourth PDA Amendment allowed for open 
space/recreational uses with an approximate gross floor area of 789,000 square feet. The Fourth PDA 
Amendment was approved by the BPDA on March 12, 2020, adopted by the Boston Zoning Commission 
on May 13, 2020, and approved by the Mayor on May 29, 2020. Collectively, the Original PDA Plan, the 
First PDA Amendment, the Second PDA Amendment, the Third PDA Amendment, and the Fourth PDA 
Amendment are hereinafter referred to as the “PDA Plan”. 
 
Fifth Amendment to PDA Plan 
 
 
This Fifth Amendment to the PDA Plan (“Fifth PDA Amendment”), as set forth below, amends 
the PDA Plan only with respect to the square footage for the Project Component on the Lena Park Parcel, 
and the total Gross Floor Area for the Olmsted Green Project. This Fifth PDA Amendment amends the 
provision that the school use on the Lena Park Parcel may be up to approximately 73,600 square feet from 
approximately 61,000 square feet. This Fifth PDA Amendment also revises the total Gross Floor Area 
for the Olmsted Green Project to approximately [853,600] square feet from approximately 841,049. 
Capitalized terms in this Fifth PDA Amendment, unless otherwise defined herein, shall have the meaning 
set forth in the PDA Plan and the Code. 
 
The Fifth PDA Amendment hereby amends the PDA Plan as follows:
