FACT SHEET 
Development Plan for 
Planned Development Area No. ___ (“PDA Plan”) 
1 Mystic Avenue 
Charlestown, Boston, Massachusetts 
I.
Proponent
One Mystic Owner, LLC. 
II.
Project Location: 
The proposed Planned Development Area Overlay District (the
“PDA Overlay Area”) is an approximately 1.68-acre area
(approximately 73,348 square feet) encompassing the parcel of 
land in the Charlestown neighborhood of Boston that is known as 
and numbered 1 Mystic Avenue (the “Site”). The Site is bounded 
by Sherman Street to the west, the 3 Sherman Street lot and 
Temple Street (a private way) to the north, Dorrance Street to the 
East, and Mystic Avenue to the South. The Site currently contains 
a dilapidated 4,800-square-foot residential/commercial building 
previously occupied partially by Flynn’s Auto Salvage (located at 
1-3 Mystic Avenue), an 8,600-square-foot commercial building 
that was recently vacated by the wholesale HVAC Bell/Simons 
Company (aka The Simons Co.), a plumbing and refrigeration 
business
(located at 3 Sherman Street), a transformer building, a cell tower, 
and associated parking and access drives.
III.
Project Description: The proposed project (the “Project”) is a 25-story, high-rise mixed-
IV.
Project Uses:
V.
Public Benefits:
use residential building consisting of approximately 636 
residential units supported by approximately 11,000 square feet of 
ground-floor retail/restaurant and community space, and 
approximately 171 off-street parking spaces located in a two-level, 
below-grade garage, and incorporating a variety of supporting 
amenities and new landscaped open spaces. 
The Project’s gross floor area will be principally devoted to 
multifamily residential use, and this mixed-use development will 
also incorporate other residential, community, and accessory uses, 
including parking and loading uses. 
The public benefits of the Project include the following: 

Adding substantially to the city’s housing stock during a period
of rapidly-escalating demand for rental units by supplying a
total of 636 new market rate and income-restricted apartments
to serve the needs of the area’s growing employer base and

 
 
2
contribute meaningfully towards meeting the City’s goal of 
creating 69,000 new housing units in Boston by 2030; 
 Complying with and exceeding the City’s Inclusionary 
Development Policy, by creating approximately 127 new 
affordable rental units for Boston residents; 
 Creating an anticipated 1,500 construction jobs as well as 60 
permanent, full-time employment positions for retail and 
residential program staff; 
 Providing an architecturally-distinguished structure of a 
quality, scale, and massing appropriate to the Site and its 
general context; 
 Incorporating environmentally-sustainable construction 
approaches and building systems into a major new residential 
tower; 
 Locating a transit-oriented, mixed-use development in an area 
supported by extensive transportation and utility infrastructure, 
thereby minimizing effects on the environment and helping 
maximize the effectiveness of investments in public 
transportation and other infrastructure in the area; 
 Designing and implementing an improved pedestrian 
connection from the Site to the Sullivan Square MBTA station; 
 Improving pedestrian and bicycle safety through enhanced 
connections to the Sullivan Square MBTA station; 
 Joining a Charlestown / Sullivan Square TMA and leading the 
creation of an area shuttle bus program; 
 Providing public and visitor accessible bike parking; 
 Initiating community programs including Charlestown resident 
employment opportunities and Charlestown resident internship 
opportunities; 
 Participating in an apprenticeship Program for professional 
development of Union Workers; 
 Making available significant subcontractor opportunities for 
small, diverse MWBE businesses and start-ups; 
 Creating Charlestown business incubator opportunities, which 
will include providing rent subsidies for approved small 
businesses; 
 Creating a new highly visible gateway to the Charlestown 
neighborhood and the City of Boston at a site currently 
characterized by undesirable, dilapidated conditions; 

 
 
3
 Designing and implementing a large and vibrant public realm 
with activated outdoor and indoor space permeable to the 
public and the immediate neighborhood; and 
 Generating significant increased real estate and sales tax 
revenues for the City of Boston. 
VI. 
Existing Zoning: 
Map 2B/2C of the series of Boston Zoning Maps indicates that the 
PDA Overlay Area is located within the Charlestown General 
Industrial Subdistrict, Article 42B of the Code. Land within this 
zoning article is designated as PDA-eligible. 
 
VII. 
Changes to Zoning: As set fourth in the PDA Plan, the PDA Plan will supersede the 
dimensional, density, use, parking, and loading requirements of the 
underlying zoning. 
 

- 1 -
DEVELOPMENT PLAN FOR 
PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA NO. ___ 
1 Mystic Avenue 
Charlestown, Massachusetts 
Dated: March 31, 2023 
Plan. Pursuant to Section 3-1A and Articles 51 and 80C of the Boston Zoning Code (the 
“Code”), this plan constitutes a Planned Development Area (“PDA”) Development Plan (the 
“Plan”) for the development of an approximately 1.4-acre (60,089 square foot) site in the 
Charlestown neighborhood of Boston that is known as and numbered 1 Mystic Avenue (the 
“Site”). The Site is bounded by Sherman Street to the west, the 3 Sherman Street lot and 
Temple Street (a private way) to the north, Dorrance Street to the East, and Mystic Avenue to 
the South. The Site currently contains a dilapidated 4,800-square-foot residential/commercial 
building previously occupied partially by Flynn’s Auto Salvage (located at 1-3 Mystic Avenue), 
an 8,600-square-foot commercial building that was recently vacated by the wholesale HVAC 
Bell/Simons Company (aka The Simons Co.), a plumbing and refrigeration business (located at 
3 Sherman Street), a transformer building, a cell tower, and associated parking and access 
drives. The Site is described in Exhibit A attached hereto and is shown on that certain “ALTA/
ASCM Land Title Survey in Boston, Massachusetts, 1 / 1A / 3 Mystic Avenue, Sherman 
Square, Charlestown, Massachusetts,” dated February 20, 2020, and prepared by Peter Nolan & 
Associates LLC, Land Surveyors, a copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit B. 
The Proponent (as hereinafter defined) proposes to redevelop the Site to create a 
distinctive, 25-story, high-rise mixed-use residential building in the rapidly redeveloping 
Sullivan Square area consisting of approximately 636 residential units supported by 
approximately 11,000 square feet of ground-floor retail/restaurant and community space, and 
approximately 171 off-street parking spaces located in a two-level, below-grade garage, and 
incorporating a variety of supporting amenities and new landscaped open spaces, all as more 
fully described below (the “Project”). This Plan is consistent with the approvals of the Project 
that have been granted pursuant to Section 80B of the Code. 
This Plan sets forth the proposed location and appearance of structures, open spaces and 
landscaping, proposed uses of the Site, densities, proposed traffic circulation, parking and 
loading facilities, access to public transportation, and proposed dimensions of structures with 
respect to the Project. Upon approval, this Plan will constitute permanent zoning for the Site in 
accordance with Section 3-1A and Article 80C of the Code. The Project is subject to ongoing 
urban design, environmental, and other development review by the Boston Redevelopment 
Authority, doing business as the Boston Planning & Development Agency (the “BPDA”) and by 
other governmental agencies and authorities, and the design of the Project may evolve in the 
course of such review, to the extent consistent with the use and dimensional limitations of this 
Plan. In accordance with Section 80C-8 of the Code, a building, use, or occupancy permit for 
the Project or for any Project Component (as hereinafter defined) will not be issued until the 
BPDA has issued a Certification of Consistency pursuant to Code Article 80C-8 for such Project 

2 
or such Project Component. To the extent that the Director of the BPDA (the “Director”) 
certifies that the Project or any Project Component is consistent with this Plan, the Project or 
Project Component will be deemed to be in compliance with the requirements of the Code, in 
accordance with Code Section 80C-9. 
This Plan consists of 9 pages of text, plus attachments designated Exhibits A through G. 
All references to this Plan contained herein pertain to such pages and exhibits. Capitalized terms 
used, but not defined, herein will have the meanings assigned to such terms in the Code as in 
effect as of the date hereof, without giving effect to any subsequent amendments to the Code. 
Proponent. One Mystic Owner, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the 
“Proponent”), has an address of c/o Fulcrum Global Investors, LLC, 1280 Centre Street, 
Newton Center, Massachusetts 02201. Members of the Project team are identified on Exhibit C. 
Planned Development Area Overlay District. The proposed Planned Development 
Area Overlay District (the “PDA Overlay Area”) consists of approximately 1.68 acres (73,348 
square feet) in the Charlestown neighborhood of Boston. The PDA Overlay Area, shown on 
Exhibit D, attached hereto, is located at the intersection of Mystic Avenue and Dorrance Street. 
Following approval of the Plan and associated zoning map amendment by the Boston Zoning 
Commission, the PDA Overlay Area will be located entirely within a zoning district designated 
“D.” 
Map 2B/2C of the series of Boston Zoning Maps indicates that the PDA Overlay Area is 
located within the Harborpark District: Charlestown Waterfront, Article 42B of the Code, and 
more specifically the Charlestown General Industrial Subdistrict. The Land within this zoning 
article is designated as PDA-eligible. 
The ongoing City of Boston Planning process for the Charlestown neighborhood, entitled 
PLAN: Charlestown, has generated draft findings related to height and density, open space, 
transit access, amenity space, and buffering. The Project is generally consistent with these 
recommendations, as follows: 
Height and Density. The Project proposes high density residential development with 
ground floor retail, which is consistent with the preferences expressed through the PLAN: 
Charlestown process to date. 
Open Space. As of this filing, the only consolidated open space in the vicinity of the 
Project Site shown on PLAN: Charlestown materials is located at the intersection of Maffa Way, 
Beacham Street, and Cambridge Street. Potential green corridors are also identified along 
Mystic Avenue and adjacent to the MBTA right-of-way via Sherman Street. This concept is 
consistent with the Rutherford Avenue Road Improvement Plans, which are currently at 25% 
complete design. The Project is consistent with these proposals and will provide on-site open 
space in excess of the regulatory requirements. Subject to approvals from the pertinent 
governing bodies, the Project has further committed to landscaping and maintaining two 
publicly-owned triangular land parcels located within the public roadways between the site and 
Sullivan Station. 
Transit Access. PLAN: Charlestown’s proposed transit improvements include a modified 
MBTA 92 bus line and a Charlestown Link route on Mystic Avenue adjacent to the Project Site. 

3 
The Project is consistent with this modification, and in fact supports it by providing 636 units of 
potential riders, with a transit rider subsidy for tenants, directly adjacent to the proposed routes. 
Further, Plan Charlestown has proposed a shuttle bus route implemented by the TMA that the 
Proponent has agreed with the BPDA to join and implement. 
Amenity Space. The PLAN: Charlestown materials that are currently available identify 
neighborhood amenities such as schools, community centers, stores, parks, and roads as a key 
component of the redevelopment of existing industrial areas, including the Project Site. The 
Project supports this approach by providing 11,000 square feet of retail space, two dog parks 
and plazas, and improvements to Sherman and Temple Streets, all of which will be open to the 
public. 
Buffering. Participants in the PLAN: Charlestown process noted that tall buildings 
adjacent to the highway and rail line can buffer the interior neighborhood from noise. The 
Project will reduce noise and air emissions within the adjacent area and will at the same time be 
designed and constructed to minimize those same impacts within the building interior. 
It is also noteworthy that the PLAN: Charlestown Scenarios recognize that placing 
housing in the areas around the Sullivan Square MBTA station will support new residents using 
public transit for a majority of their commuting, thereby creating less traffic. 
As further detailed below, the Project in addition exceeds the applicable BPDA policy 
standards relating to the creation of inclusionary housing. 
Therefore, and as more particularly set forth below, this Plan adequately and sufficiently 
satisfies all criteria for the establishment of a PDA under Section 80C-4 and all other applicable 
provisions of the Code. 
Project Description. The proposed development of the Site includes the construction of 
an up to 279-foot-high, 25-story multifamily residential building containing (i) approximately 
636 dwelling units; (ii) ground-floor retail/restaurant and community space; (iii) accessory 
below-grade parking for approximately 171 cars; and (iv) other typical supporting uses and 
facilities for a multifamily residential apartment project, such as off-street loading for building 
service and trash removal. In total, the Project will include up to 478,880 square feet of gross 
floor area,1 including approximately 11,000 square feet of supporting ground-floor lobby, retail / 
service / restaurant space, and shared-use amenity space distributed throughout the building. 
The final design of the Project will incorporate a variety of sustainability measures, 
potentially including those relating to conservation of energy, water, and other resources, 
transportation, efficient lighting and building energy management systems, recycling, indoor air 
quality, use of clean construction vehicles, and employment of locally-produced building 
materials. The Project will comply with Article 37 of the Code, Green Buildings. 
Proposed Location and Appearance of Structures. The Project will make an 
important architectural contribution to the developing Sullivan Square neighborhood. The “H-
shaped” building includes a taller (25-story) portion set back toward Temple Street, with a

shorter (19-story) portion located along Mystic Avenue. It employs a distinctly vertical language 
achieved with a curtain wall façade establishing a rhythm of 2-story openings consisting of 
extruded vertical mullions against beige precast concrete panel cladding. 
The Project’s building height and design are consistent with other high-rise buildings in 
the area, including approved buildings at the nearby Hood Park and the Encore Casino. Given its 
location, its height and profile will provide the secondary benefit of providing a landmark point 
of entry into Boston from the north. 
 
The site plan/ground floor plan attached hereto as Exhibit E shows the Project and its 
approximate location within the Site, and the elevations and floor plans attached hereto as 
Exhibit F (collectively with Exhibit E, the “Schematic Plans”) illustrate the Project’s general 
appearance as currently envisioned. 
 
Open Space and Landscaping. The Project proposes an urban landscaping scheme 
appropriate to its setting. It includes a publicly accessible plaza at the Site’s southeast corner 
fronting on Mystic Avenue and Dorrance Street. This open space will have southern solar 
exposure that will support vegetation and trees that will provide shading throughout the day and 
bring a sense of nature to that space. The Project will also make significant use of hardscape 
elements, including broad sidewalks and decorative pavers. In addition to the plaza, the Project 
will provide additional public and private on-site open spaces to serve residents and the 
community, including a dog park as well as a rooftop deck, pool deck, outdoor seating, and an 
herb garden for residents. The proposed Project landscaping is shown on Exhibit E. 
 
In addition, in conjunction with the Project, and in close coordination with the MBTA, 
the Proponent has proposed to landscape and maintain the adjacent plaza area to be created 
should the MBTA pursue its planned relocation of Dorrance Street to the south. 
 
The Project’s open space and landscaping elements will be deemed to comply with all 
pertinent requirements of the Code. 
 
Approved Uses. The Project may be used for the uses described in this Plan, which uses 
will be deemed to comply with the Code, including the Multifamily Residential, Retail / Service 
/ Restaurant, Parking and Loading, and Accessory uses set forth in Exhibit G attached hereto. 
 
Densities and Proposed Dimensions of Structures. The only dimensional regulations 
applicable to the Project will be those of building height and floor-area ratio (“FAR”), and those 
set forth in this Plan. The Project therefore may be a zero-lot-line development, approved to be 
built to its surrounding sidewalks without any mandatory setbacks or stepbacks, which 
requirements will be deemed to comply with the Code. 
 
Building Height. The Project’s height and massing are appropriate to its urban location 
in the Sullivan Square area and comparable to existing and planned area high-rise buildings. The 
maximum building height of the Project will be 279 feet, and it will contain up to 25 stories. All 
references to “building height” refer to this term’s definition in the Code. For purposes of this 
Plan, rooftop mechanical equipment, whether or not screened, penthouses normally built above 
the roof and not used or designed to be used for human occupancy, and structures and facilities 

5 
providing access to rooftop space, will not be included in calculating building height, provided 
that such structures and equipment do not exceed in the aggregate one-third of the floor area of 
all building rooftops. 
Proposed Density. The Project will include up to 478,880 square feet of gross floor 
area, and the maximum FAR for the Project will be 8.0. 
Parking and Loading Facilities. The Project proposes a new, below-grade parking 
garage with parking for approximately 171 cars on two levels. It also includes 774 bike parking 
spaces. To facilitate the achievement of its intended capacity, the garage may include compact 
parking spaces sized to meet site constraints, tandem spaces, and stackers. The Proponent will 
explore the feasibility of allocating a portion of the garage parking spaces to an internal car-
sharing service for the benefit of the Project’s residents, and this Plan approves such use of the 
Project’s parking spaces, as well as any number of spaces allocated to a commercial car-sharing 
service such as ZipCar. 
This Plan approves the number, location, dimensions, and design of the proposed parking 
spaces as described herein and as depicted on the Schematic Plans (which plans may be 
amended, consistently with this Plan, through the BPDA design review process), and such spaces 
will be deemed to meet the requirements of the Code. In addition, notwithstanding any parking-
related requirements of the Code to the contrary, this Plan approves parking accessory to any 
Project use approved by this Plan, including without limitation: (a) proposed parking accessory 
to Project uses; (b) the use of proposed parking by residents of, customers of, employees at, and 
visitors to the Project, whether or not such parking is an accessory use under the Code; and (c) 
possible future re-allocations of accessory parking among Project uses notwithstanding the 
provisions of the Code governing the Restricted Parking District. 
The Project will also include one dedicated loading bay, to be accessed from Temple 
Street via the Project’s ground-floor internal circulation pattern, which will accommodate trash 
dumpsters as needed and any associated vehicular parking. Loading facilities having the 
locations, dimensions and design shown on the final Schematic Plans will be deemed to meet the 
requirements of the Code and this Plan. 
Proposed Traffic Circulation. To minimize parking and loading impacts on the 
adjacent public ways, access to and egress from the Project’s garage will be provided via Temple 
Street, an abutting private way. 
Access to Public Transportation. The Site is an ideal location for housing due to its 
adjacency to the Sullivan Station multimodal transit hub, which is located within approximately 
500 feet of the Site. Sullivan Station is served by the Orange Line and is a major transfer point 
for 12 bus routes connecting the Site to key areas of Boston, Cambridge, Somerville, Medford, 
Everett, and beyond. The Site therefore will afford its residents exceptional connections to 
employment options. It is also within 0.25 miles of Ryan Playground, Schrafft’s City Center, 
and the East Somerville Neighborhood. In addition, we note that the MBTA has proposed a 
revised transit network as part of the Better Bus Project Bus Network Redesign that will further 

 
6 
 
strengthen transit access to Sullivan Square with high frequency connections to surrounding 
communities, including new routes with direct connections to Harvard Square and Lechmere to 
facilitate transfers to connecting subway lines. 
 
In consultation with the Boston Transportation Department (“BTD”), the Proponent will 
promote transportation demand management strategies designed to reduce auto dependency of 
people who will travel to and from the Project. These strategies may include encouraging 
residents to utilize the public transit options near to the Site. The Proponent will also join a local 
Transportation Management Association. Specifics of traffic circulation and transportation 
demand management will be developed in consultation with BTD and will be included in a 
Transportation Access Plan Agreement (“TAPA”) for the Project.

 Adding substantially to the city’s housing stock during a period of rapidly-escalating 
demand for rental units by supplying a total of 636 new market rate and income-
restricted apartments to serve the needs of the area’s growing employer base and 
contribute meaningfully towards meeting the City’s goal of creating 69,000 new 
housing units in Boston by 2030; 
 Complying with and exceeding the City’s Inclusionary Development Policy, by 
creating approximately 127 new affordable rental units for Boston residents; 
 Creating an anticipated 1,500 construction jobs as well as 60 permanent, full-time 
employment positions for retail and residential program staff; 
 Providing an architecturally-distinguished structure of a quality, scale, and massing 
appropriate to the Site and its general context; 
 Incorporating environmentally-sustainable construction approaches and building 
systems into a major new residential tower; 
 Locating a transit-oriented, mixed-use development in an area supported by extensive 
transportation and utility infrastructure, thereby minimizing effects on the 
environment and helping maximize the effectiveness of investments in public 
transportation and other infrastructure in the area; 
 Designing and implementing an improved pedestrian connection from the Site to the 
Sullivan Square MBTA station; 
 Improving pedestrian and bicycle safety through enhanced connections to the 
Sullivan Square MBTA station; 
 Joining a Charlestown / Sullivan Square TMA and leading the creation of an area

FIRST AMENDMENT TO 
DEVELOPMENT PLAN FOR 
PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA NO. 100 
PARCEL 25/PARCEL 25B 
MISSION HILL NEIGHBORHOOD, BOSTON 
 
Dated: September ____, 2023 
 
 
Pursuant to Section 3-lA and Article 80C of the City Boston Zoning Code (the “Zoning 
Code”), this amendment constitutes the First Amendment to the Development Plan for Planned 
Development Area (“PDA”) No. 100 dated September 18, 2014 (the “Original Plan”; and this 
amendment is the “First Amendment”). 
 
The Original Plan and the accompanying map amendment were approved by the Boston 
Redevelopment Authority (the “BRA”) on September 18, 2014. On October 15, 2014, the Boston 
Zoning Commission approved the Original Plan and the accompanying map amendment. 
 
The Original Plan encompassed approximately 1.89 acres of land in the Mission Hill 
neighborhood of Boston at Tremont and Gurney Streets, as described in Exhibit A to the Original 
Plan. It is comprised of two (2) former MBTA-owned parcels, the first bounded by Tremont, Gurney, 
and Stations Streets, an MBTA pumping station and the MBTA tracks/Southwest Corridor (“Parcel 
25”), and a second smaller parcel located on the northeast corner of Gurney Street in Mission Hill 
(“Parcel 25B”). The larger parcel known as Parcel 25 contained approximately 76,703 square feet 
and the smaller parcel, known as Parcel 25B, contained approximately 5,500 square feet for a total 
of approximately 82,203 square feet of land area (collectively, the “Site” or “PDA Area”). There are 
no proposed changes to the Site or PDA Area as part of the First Amendment. 
 
 The Original Plan provided for development of a mixed-use residential, retail, and 
commercial development of up to 305,750 gross square feet to be developed in multiple phases: Phase 
1 to consist of two (2) buildings – Building 1A of approximately 76,250 gross square feet and 
Building 1B of approximately 12,000 gross square feet; Phase 2 of approximately 56,000 gross square 
feet in Building 2; and Phase 3 of approximately 161,500 gross square feet in Building 3 (collectively, 
the “Project”). 
 
This First Amendment to the Original Plan proposes changes which only involve Building 1B 
of Phase 1 and Phase 3 of the Project and their related land area as shown herein. No changes are 
proposed to the other approved or constructed buildings or portions of the Site. Under the Original 
Plan, Building 1B of Phase 1 (the “Parcel 25 Phase 1B Project”) was to consist of approximately 12,000 
gross square feet with retail and non-profit office space, but will no longer be constructed and will 
instead be included as frontage as part of the revised Phase 3 in Building 3, as detailed herein below. 
Under the Original Plan, Building 3 in Phase 3 was approved as a 10-story, up to 160 foot tall 
building, with 161,500 gross square feet of office uses and including several trays of below grade 
parking totaling 185 vehicular spaces (the “Approved Phase 3 Project”). 
 

The Parcel 25 Phase 1A project for Building 1A was completed and occupied on a subdivided 
Parcel 25D of approximately 22,803 square feet and the Parcel 25 Phase 1A project includes 40 Low 
Income Housing Tax Credit (“LIHTC”) affordable rental apartments, with 16 surface parking spaces, 
approximately 26,753 square feet of non-profit office space, and 4,577 square feet of retail spaces 
(the “Parcel 25 Phase 1A Project”). 
Building 2 under the Original Plan is currently under construction and consists of a 100% 
affordable 46-unit LIHTC residential housing building with 29 below grade parking spaces (the 
“Parcel 25 Phase 2 Project”). The Parcel 25 Phase 2 Project is located on subdivided Parcel 25G, a 
site of approximately 21,755 square feet. 
The Original Plan, as amended by the First Amendment, sets forth the proposed location and 
appearance of structures, open spaces and landscaping, uses, densities and dimensions of structures, 
traffic circulation, parking and loading facilities, access to public transportation and other zoning 
requirements applicable to the Project. 
Amendments to the Original Plan 
As set forth below, this First Amendment modifies the Original Plan to amend certain of its 
provisions, in order to now allow for the construction of much needed affordable residences in place 
of the Approved Phase 3 Project’s previously contemplated and approved 10-story, 161,500 gsf office 
building at a height of 160 feet with several trays of below grade parking totaling 185 spaces. This 
First Amendment will replace the Approved Phase 3 Project office building instead with a new six 
(6) story, approximately 120,000 gsf building with up to 94 affordable rental residences and 33 above 
ground parking spaces, including eight (8) spaces for the sole use of NPC Phase 3 Project residents 
and the remaining 25 spaces as ancillary parking for the adjacent Parcel 25 Phase 1A project, 
including residential, office and retail spaces (the “NPC Phase 3 Project”). 
Additionally, this First Amendment removes the Building 1B of Phase 1 under the Original 
Plan, which was to consist of approximately 12,000 gross square feet of retail and non-profit office 
space which will not be built; instead, this site area will be included as frontage for the NPC Phase 3 
Project.

Capitalized terms in this First Amendment, unless otherwise defined herein, shall be 
defined as set forth in the Original Plan. The Original Plan is hereby amended as follows: 
 
Proposed Project Location, Phasing and Appearance of Structures 
 
 The Original Plan sets forth the Proposed Project Location, Phasing and Appearance of 
Structures to include a total development of up to 305,750 gross square feet with 
approximately 98,000 gross square feet of residential space (88 apartments), approximately 
10,000 gross square feet of retail space, approximately 196,500 gross square feet of office 
space, and approximately 1,250 gross square feet of community space, including a Building 
1B of approximately 12,000 square feet and 36 feet in height, and a Phase 3 of approximately 
161,500 gross square feet in Building 3 and up to 160 feet in height. The Original Plan also 
states a maximum of 201 parking spaces will be provided in a combination of surface parking 
and a below-grade parking garage. 
 This First Amendment hereby revises this section by removing Building 1B of Phase 1 under 
the Original Plan altogether and revising the Phase 3/Building 3 portion of the project to a 
new six (6) story building of approximately 69 feet 11 inches with approximately 120,000 
gsf and up to 94 affordable rental residences and 33 above ground parking spaces, including 
eight (8) spaces for the sole use of NPC Phase 3 Project residents and the remaining 25 spaces 
as ancillary parking for the adjacent Parcel 25 Phase 1A project, including residential, office 
and retail spaces. 
 This First Amendment also revises this section to provide for the following overall project 
description of a total development of up to 251,170 gross square feet with approximately 
219,840 gross square feet of residential space (180 units), approximately 4,577 gross square 
feet of retail space, and approximately 26,753 gross square feet of office space. 
 This First Amendment also revises the parking programming in the Original Plan to now 
include in the NPC Phase 3 Project a total of 33 above ground parking spaces, including 
eight (8) spaces for the sole use of NPC Phase 3 Project residents and the remaining 25 spaces 

as ancillary parking for the adjacent Parcel 25 Phase 1A project, equaling an overall total of 
16 surface parking spaces and 62 garage spaces and a total of 78 parking spaces overall for 
the Project. 
 The location and appearance of the Proposed Project Location, Phasing and Appearance of 
Structures was included in schematic plans included with the Original Plan within Exhibit 
C. 
 This First Amendment hereby amends Exhibit C – PDA Conceptual Plans with regard to 
Building 1B of Phase 1 and Phase 3 and replaces those with the attached new Exhibit C 
hereto which provides updated schematic plans, renderings and elevations for the NPC Phase 
3 Project for Phase 3 in comparison to the Approved Phase 3 Project. 
 
Open Space and Landscaping 
 
 The Original Plan sets forth the Open Space and Landscaping for the Project to include a 
plaza of approximately 40 feet by 60 feet between Building 1B and Building 2, and 
approximately 120 feet by 35 feet during full completion of all phases between Building 2 
and Building 3. 
 
 This First Amendment hereby revises this section by connecting the previously proposed 
spaces into one larger contiguous space located between the Parcel 25 Phase 1A Project, the 
Parcel 25 Phase 2 Project, and the NPC Phase 3 Project. 
 
Commercial Subdistrict 
 
 
No changes. 
 
Proposed Uses 
 
 The Original Plan sets forth the Proposed Uses for the Project to include residential, office, 
retail, and community space and accessory uses thereto, and, at full build-out, to contain up 
to 201 parking spaces in both surface and a below-grade garage made available on a phased 
basis as the Project is developed. 
 This First Amendment hereby revises this section by revising the overall parking space 
number from 201 parking spaces to a total of 78 parking spaces overall for the Project. The 
Proposed Uses remain the same other than to add Ancillary Parking as an Allowed Use 
under this First Amendment in order to allow for six (6) parking spaces at the Parcel 25 
Phase 2 Project to be utilized for the Parcel 25 Phase 1A Project, and 25 spaces on the Phase 
3 building site as part of the NPC Phase 3 Project (once the various parcels are subdivided) 
as ancillary parking for the adjacent Parcel 25 Phase 1A project. 
Densities 
 
 The Original Plan sets forth the Densities for the Project as anticipated FAR of 
approximately 1.07 for proposed Phase 1 and approximately 4.0 for the fully phased Project, 
but not to exceed an FAR of 5.0. 
 This First Amendment hereby revises this section by providing an as built FAR of 

approximately 3.40 for Phase 1 (on its now subdivided lot), an as built FAR of 
approximately 2.47 for Phase 2 (on its now subdivided lot), and a proposed FAR of 
approximately 3.73 for Phase 3 as part of the NPC Phase 3 Project (on its now subdivided 
lot), for an overall FAR of approximately 3.06 for the fully phased Project on the Site, still 
not to exceed the approved allowable FAR of 4.00 under the Original Plan or the allowable 
FAR of 5.00 under the CC-2 Subdistrict for a PDA. 
 
Proposed Traffic Circulation, Parking, and Loading Facilities 
 
 The Original Plan sets forth the Proposed Traffic Circulation, Parking, and Loading 
Facilities for the Project to include up to 201 spaces within a surface lot (accessible from 
Gurney Street) and underground garage (accessible from Station Street). The Original Plan 
also details that as part of Phase 3 of the Project, the surface parking for the first two phases 
will be reconfigured and supplemented with a parking garage below grade and below the 
Phase 3 office building. The Original Plan states that in Phase 1, approximately 56 spaces 
will be provided on a surface lot on the Site and that Phase 2 will be served with 
approximately 24 surface parking spaces. 
 This First Amendment hereby revises this section by amending the overall parking space 
number from 201 total parking spaces to 78 total overall parking spaces for the overall 
Project, to include 16 surface parking spaces at the Parcel 25 Phase 1A Project on Parcel 
25B, 29 parking spaces at the Parcel 25 Phase 2 Project, and 33 above ground parking 
spaces at the NPC Phase 3 Project, including eight (8) spaces for the sole use of NPC Phase 
3 Project residents and the remaining 25 spaces as ancillary parking for the adjacent Parcel 
25 Phase 1A project. This First Amendment now provides for an overall total of 16 surface

 This First Amendment also notes that the NPC Phase 3 Project is an all-affordable

FACT SHEET 
DEVELOPMENT PLAN FOR PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA NO. 93 
500 Huntington Avenue 
MISSION HILL, BOSTON 
(As Amended) 
Proponent: 
Huntington Development Group LLC (the “Proponent”). The Proponent is a 50% 
minority-owned development joint venture among affiliates of the Owens 
Companies, Inc., the oldest minority-owned and operated company in New 
England, Waldwin Development Group LLC, a longtime Boston-based, minority-
owned business, and The Fallon Company LLC, a multi-generational Boston-
based real estate developer. 
Site: 
The Project Site is located at Huntington Avenue, Parker Street and Ruggles 
Street, Boston and contains approximately 132,130 square feet of land (3.033 
acres) as shown on the plan entitled “Compiled Plot Plan, Wentworth Sweeney 
Field, Huntington Avenue in Boston, MA” prepared by Feldman Professional 
Land Surveyors, dated February 1, 2013. 
Proposed Project: 
The Project Site is currently subject to PDA No. 93, which was approved in 
2013 following an in-depth public process undertaken by Wentworth Institute 
of Technology. PDA No. 93 permits development of 640,000 square feet of gross 
floor area on the Project Site, comprised of office/R&D space and other 
commercial uses with ground floor retail and below-grade parking. The 
Proponent proposes to amend PDA No. 93 to refine the design and scope of the 
Project to improve its overall feasibility. Notably, the Proposed Project is 
consistent with the height, density, and parking limitations set forth in the 
previously approved PDA No. 93. The Proposed Project consists of a total of 
up to 640,000 square feet of gross floor area, comprised of life 
sciences/office/research and development space and other commercial or 
activated uses, first floor retail/restaurant/commercial/activated space; and up to 
410 parking spaces in a below-grade garage. It is currently anticipated that the 
Proposed Project will consist of two buildings built in one or more phases: 
Building One will be up to 18 stories high and front on Huntington Avenue and 
Building Two will be up to 18 stories high and front on Parker Street and 
Ruggles Street. 
Proposed Uses: 
Consistent with PDA No. 93, the Proposed Project is currently anticipated to 
contain life sciences/office/research and development space and other 
commercial uses, first floor retail/restaurant/commercial/activated space and 
parking 
Proposed Densities: 
PDA No. 93 provides for an overall maximum Floor Area Ratio of 5.0 and a 
maximum gross floor area of 640,000 square feet. The Proposed Project does 
not propose any changes to these maximums. 
 
Height: 
PDA No. 93 provides that the height of the buildings will be a maximum of 253 
feet to the top of the roof and 280 feet to the top of the mechanical equipment 
screens. The Proposed Project does not propose any changes to these 
maximums. 

 
 
Construction Timetable: 
The construction period for the first phase will be approximately 30 months 
following completion of the regulatory approvals process and commencement of 
construction. 
Public Benefits: 
The approval of the Proposed Project will result in expanded public benefits for 
the Project, including: 
 
♦ Fulfills the vision and needs of Wentworth Institute of Technology by providing 
critical economic benefits and synergies between (i) the Wentworth campus 
and students, and (ii) the Project’s vibrant public realm and commercial users. 
Among other things, the Project will strengthen Wentworth’s presence on 
Huntington Avenue, generate experiential opportunities and beneficial 
partnerships for its students, and produce critical financial support for its unique 
educational mission to serve a diverse community of learners. 
♦ Creates unique workforce development opportunities and career ladders for a 
variety of roles through innovative partnerships, most notably including with 
Wentworth, its students and the local community. 
♦ Introduces, by virtue of the Proponent, an innovative 50% minority-owned 
development partnership to the Boston development landscape. 
♦ Fills a key void on Huntington Avenue Corridor, a void that has long been 
contemplated for redevelopment with a project similar to the Project, as noted 
in the City’s Avenue of the Arts design guidelines and PDA No. 93. 
♦ Maximizes the public realm on a site that was previously fenced off to the public 
by providing approximately 70,000 sf of publicly-accessible open space, a 
significant increase from PDA No. 93. 
♦ Includes ground floor retail, restaurant, commercial space, or other activated 
uses, to activate the new publicly accessible open space and Huntington 
Avenue. 
♦ Creates new outdoor spaces for gatherings and place-making for neighborhood 
use. 
♦ Opens the Project to students in the Real Estate Entrepreneurship Youth 
Program founded by The Fallon Company and Street2Ivy, which seeks to equip 
community youth with the skills, knowledge, and mentors needed to participate 
in real estate investing, and set them on a path to help eliminate the income 
and wealth disparity in Boston. 
♦ Partners with Wentworth’s RAMP program, which provides unique solutions for 
closing the opportunity gap in the construction industry by engaging with Boston 
youth early and often throughout their educational journey. 
♦ Significantly enhances neighborhood pedestrian and bike connectivity by 
providing publicly accessible paths through and around the site, improving 
connection among the Ruggles and Museum of Fine Arts MBTA stations, the 
neighboring institutions, the Southwest Corridor, and the Emerald Necklace.
